Title: Intern in the Science Operations Department - Discovering Astronomical Anomalies with AnomalyMatch
description_html:
Location
ESAC, Villanueva de la Cañada, Spain  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of D/SCI, the Head of the Science Operations Department is responsible for the development of the science operations infrastructure under the Directorate responsibility, the operation of the Directorate’s missions once successfully commissioned, and the curation of all scientific data in the missions’ legacy phase. These responsibilities are discharged in full coordination with the Directorate’s Departments and Offices and as appropriate, with the Directorate of Operations (D/OPS).

 

In implementing their duties, SCI-S is supported by the: 

  • Mission Management and Science Operations Division (SCI-SO);
  • Science Operations Development Division (SCI-SD);
  • Data Science and Archives Division (SCI-SA).

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Beyond Images: Discovering Astronomical Anomalies in Light Curves and Spectra with AnomalyMatch.

 

Astronomical archives contain vast collections of spectra and light curves that may hide rare objects, unusual variability, and unexpected physical phenomena. This project will extend AnomalyMatch, a semi-supervised and active-learning framework for finding scientifically interesting anomalies from only a few labelled examples, to support such one-dimensional data.

 

AnomalyMatch recently received global press attention after discovering hundreds of previously unknown anomalies in the Hubble archive and has demonstrated the capacity to trawl hundreds of millions of astronomical cutouts. It is also integrated into ESA Datalabs, allowing researchers to apply the tool directly to large astronomical datasets and scalable computing resources.

 

So far, AnomalyMatch has been limited to image data. You will adapt its machine-learning methodology and software for spectra and/or light curves and validate the resulting approach on real astronomical datasets. The project may also explore combining measurements from different telescopes or instruments, opening new possibilities for discovering objects that appear ordinary in one dataset but unusual when multiple observations are considered together.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • strong Python programming skills;
  • background in machine learning and neural networks;
  • experience with PyTorch or a similar deep-learning framework;
  • familiarity with astronomical spectra, light curves, or scientific data analysis would be advantageous.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Future Missions Department - Astrophysics Section of the Prodex Office
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Future Missions Department is responsible for preparing future missions, as well as defining and implementing Small/Fast missions within the Directorate of Science (e.g. SMILE and Comet-Interceptor, ARRAKHIS).


Within Future Missions Department, PRODEX is an optional programme dedicated to the development of scientific instruments and experiments for space science missions. In PRODEX Office, the Astrophysics and International Collaboration Missions Section (SCI-FEA) is responsible for addressing a subset of PRODEX activities, in particular the implementation and monitoring of activities and developments related to astrophysics and fundamental physics science missions (e.g. ATHENA, LISA, SMILE and ARIEL), as well as those involving international external partners, some of them with export control constraints. Developments in other domains of activities handled by the Office may also be entrusted to the section (e.g. Earth observation-related developments).

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

This internship position in PRODEX offers an opportunity to contribute to the preparatory work for nuANCESTOR (frequency ANchor for Cross-calibration of Extreme preciSion asTronOmical spectRographs) mission. This Swiss-led mission uses a space-based Laser Frequency Comb for absolute calibration and cross-calibration of extreme-precision radial velocity ground-based spectrographs. The industrial development for this project has already started in the field of opto-electronics, telescope design and GNSS. As an intern, you will work on the mission definition and will also have the opportunity to get involved in any one or more of these industrial developments based on your education, background and aptitude. 
 

Your role within this project will include the following tasks:

  • work on mission definition for nuANCESTOR with the institute and industrial partners;
  • interface with ESA technical experts on various sub-system developments;
  • support the monitoring of an industrial activity related to nuANCESTOR.

 

During the course of this project, you will learn about exoplanet detection and characterisation, astronomical spectroscopy, space optical and opto-electronic instruments design and development, Technological Readiness Levels of space mission and trade-offs involved in the sub-system design for a successful mission.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in astronomical space instrumentation including optics, detectors, thermal and electronics is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Commercialisation Department - Innovation Services Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Within the Commercialisation Department and under the direct authority of the Head of ScaleUp Programme Division, the Innovation Services Section follows three main objectives:  

 

  1. nurturing innovation and de-risking projects through dedicated environment, expertise and funding;
  2. brokering innovative (space) solutions to ESA programmes or European industry;
  3. diversifying space as a business (New Space).
     

Among other tasks, the Innovation Services Section is in charge of the following business lines: 

 

  • ESA Phi-Lab NET, whose mission is to bring research closer to commercialisation by bridging disruptive research and commercial needs;  
  • ESA Technology Brokers Network, whose mission is bridging the gap between space and terrestrial markets.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will support the ESA Innovation Services Section in developing digital tools for supporting the monitoring of innovation activities, and the innovation process itself. 

 

Following a requirement and feasibility assessment, you will select one or more projects, for the development and prototyping of the following tools: 

 

  • dashboard for monitoring technology transfer activities;
  • tool for discovering existing knowledge and technologies to solve problems (e.g. lessons learnt from past R&D projects and analogous solutions to similar problems), leveraging existing databases and AI agentic capabilities.
  • tool for expert forecasting on technical questions, to efficiently inject collective intelligence into the design process.

 

Learning Objectives:

 

  • apply your software engineering or data science skills to develop and refine tools supporting ESA’s innovation services;
  • gain practical experience in translating conceptual frameworks into operational software;
  • contribute to ESA’s efforts to provide technology intelligence and support technical innovation;
  • develop skills in AI and agentic systems, RAG, semantic search, knowledge engineering, and the analysis of structured and unstructured data.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

You are a technically capable and curious problem-solver, able to design and prototype digital tools.

You should be familiar with AI techniques, software development, data visualisation, Microsoft digital tools and stakeholder-oriented innovation work. 

 

Useful competencies include knowledge, skills and/or experience with: 

 

  • AI and data science fundamentals, including GenAI, agents, RAG, Natural Language Processing (NLP), semantic search and embeddings;
  • python, APIs, data processing, technical architecture and rapid proof-of-concepts;
  • structured and unstructured data modelling, analysis, abstraction and cross-domain problem-solving;
  • Microsoft Power Platform, dashboards, data visualisation and user-centered interfaces.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics.

The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Title: Intern in the Infrastructure Department - Propulsion Tests and Services
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

The Propulsion Test Facilities and Services team (STS-IF), part of the Infrastructure Department, is responsible for the stewardship of ESA-owned propulsion test facilities. 

 

The team ensures that these facilities, operated by industry and public-sector partners, remain fully operational and available to support current and future propulsion development activities. It is also responsible for setting up, managing and monitoring the contractual framework with the different facility operators. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose between the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Maintenance and Enhancement of Pre-Engineering and Programme Management Tools

You will contribute to the maintenance, enhancement and deployment of internal STS-IF pre-engineering and programme management tools by: 

 

  • ​maintaining and upgrading STS-IF internal engineering and programme management tools; 
  • ensuring that tools can be easily installed and operated on ESA workstations and, where appropriate, made accessible through web-based interfaces; 
  • improving tool robustness and compatibility with evolving Windows, Python and Streamlit environments;  
  • ​developing new functionalities and enhancing existing features/functions based on user needs; 
  • ​facilitating access to the tools for other ESA users; 
  • ​preparing and delivering demonstrations and presentations of new functionalities; 
  • ​assessing the feasibility of long-term maintenance of these tools by ESA IT services. 

​ 

​2) Topic 2: Identification of Artificial Intelligence Applications to streamline STS-IF activities

You will analyse STS-IF activities and develop proposals for the use of AI to improve efficiency and reduce administrative workload in areas such as:

 

  • action tracking and follow-up;
  • preparation of presentations and briefing materials; 
  • ​equipment price monitoring and market intelligence; 
  • ​automated generation of status reports. 

​ 

3) ​Topic 3: Development of a Maintenance Planning and Prioritisation Tool for Test Facilities 

​You will design and develop a tool to support the management of propulsion test facility maintenance activities, including:

 

  • ​recording main maintenance tasks and related cost estimates; 
  • ​prioritising activities based on operational needs and available resources; 
  • ​generating summaries and management reporting to support decision-making.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Following skills are considered an advantage: 

  • Python programming; 
  • knowledge of Streamlit; 
  • knowledge of AI; 
  • knowledge of project management; 
  • knowledge of fluid dynamics. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Science Operations Department - Mission Management and Science Operations Division
description_html:
Location
ESAC, Villanueva de la Cañada, Spain  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of D/SCI, the Head of the Science Operations Department is responsible for the development of the science operations infrastructure under the Directorate responsibility, the operation of the Directorate’s missions once successfully commissioned, and the curation of all scientific data in the missions’ legacy phase. These responsibilities are discharged in full coordination with the Directorate’s Departments and Offices and as appropriate, with the Directorate of Operations (D/OPS).

 

In implementing their duties, SCI-S is supported by the: 

  • Mission Management and Science Operations Division (SCI-SO);
  • Science Operations Development Division (SCI-SD);
  • Data Science and Archives Division (SCI-SA).

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Future-proofing access to Gaia’s treasure trove

 

Gaia is one of the most scientifically productive space science missions ever undertaken. Its highly successful data releases - DR1, DR2, DR3 and, in December 2026, DR4 - are the most visible products of a complex data processing system involving several major processing centres and expert groups across Europe. These public releases, however, represent only part of Gaia’s scientific data legacy.

 

At the foundation of the processing system lies the Gaia Main Database (MDB), hosted at one of Gaia’s main data-processing centres at ESAC near Madrid. The MDB contains the basic input and intermediate data used throughout the Gaia processing chain. Its underlying storage format, known as GBin, was developed specifically for the Java-based processing systems. While this solution has served the mission well, it is closely tied to a particular programming language and was not designed primarily with long-term accessibility and preservation in mind.

 

Following the conclusion of Gaia in 2030, the mission will enter its legacy phase. The MDB is expected to be preserved so that it may remain accessible for future scientific investigations, reprocessing activities and other uses that cannot yet be anticipated. To facilitate such access, it would be desirable to represent the data in a well-supported, programming-language-independent and durable format, such as Parquet, HDF5, Zarr or another suitable technology.

 

The objective of this internship is to investigate and compare possible approaches for converting the MDB from GBin into a modern, long-lived data format. It is expected that prototype conversion and validation tools/concepts are developed. You will work closely with Gaia mission and data-processing experts at ESAC and across Europe in a technically challenging and collaborative environment.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • solid background in computer science, software engineering, data science;
  • good programming skills, preferably in Python, Java or both;
  • understanding of structured data, data models and serialisation concepts.

 

Desirable:

  • experience with scientific data formats or storage technologies such as Parquet, HDF5, Zarr, FITS;
  • familiarity with large-scale data processing, distributed computing or database systems.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Galileo and EGNOS Programme Department - Hybrid and Resilient PNT Systems Evolution
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The team, GNSS Evolution Upstream R&D Implementation Office, is responsible for defining, consolidating and implementing innovative technologies and supporting research and development for the next generations of operational systems for the European Union (EU PNT satellite systems).

EU satellite navigation systems are undergoing a paradigm shift towards multi-layered system concepts and architectures (e.g. GEO, MEO, LEO), while also leveraging synergies with other components of the EU Space Programme (e.g. IRISS, so-called Fused PNT concepts leveraging governmental satellite communications signals for PNT) to enhance the performance and resilience of PNT solutions.

If selected for the role, you will have the opportunity to directly contribute to shaping the future evolution of EU PNT satellite systems (e.g., future generations of Galileo, Egnos, and EU LEO-PNT). This role features unique opportunities to develop your expertise and take initiative while addressing cutting-edge concepts and technologies. It will give you the opportunity to develop your expertise in System of PNT systems, apportionment of performances among layers, components and systems contributing to EU’s future System of PNT Systems concepts, and the exploration of synergies with other components of the EU Space Programme to ehance future PNT capabilities.

It will also involve cooperation with diverse teams of the Directorate, involved in PNT evolutions at various levels (system, space and ground segments, future concepts, in-orbit demonstrations and user segments technologies, synergies with satellite communication systems), as well as with the Directorate of Technology, Engineering and Quality, with access to world-class laboratories for PNT and satellite communications.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

During this internship, you will contribute to a defined technical work package on hybrid, fused and resilient positioning, navigation and timing (PNT), selected according to your academic background, available laboratory equipment and the team’s priorities. Under the guidance of your tutor, you will have the following tasks:

 

  • reviewing the state of the art in GNSS evolution, multi-layer, fused and hybrid PNT, including relevant ESA field-trial results, and identifying performance trends and improvement opportunities, particularly for indoor, deep-urban, canopy, obstructed, jamming and spoofing conditions;
  • defining or refining PNT concepts combining multiple orbital layers, GNSS, satellite communications, terrestrial and non-terrestrial 5G/6G networks, synthetic aperture radar signals and complementary sensors (e.g. vision);
  • developing simulations, receiver models, processing algorithms and performance-apportionment methods, exploring artificial intelligence and field-trial datasets to improve modelling accuracy and analysis of overall system performance;
  • implementing and improving user-receiver algorithms that fuse GNSS with signals from telecommunication or radar satellites, wireless networks, cameras, inertial sensors and other advanced sensors;
  • setting up and conducting simulations and laboratory tests using generated, recorded or live signals, then processing the measurements and assessing positioning accuracy, availability, continuity, robustness and resilience;
  • comparing the investigated techniques, documenting the software, models, test configurations and results, and presenting your main findings, limitations and recommendations to the team.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

The following are considered assets:

 

  • a university background in electrical engineering, telecommunications engineering, aerospace engineering, applied mathematics, computer science, physics or another relevant discipline;
  • basic knowledge of satellite navigation, signal processing, estimation, telecommunications or sensor fusion;
  • experience gained through university courses or academic projects with Python, MATLAB or a comparable scientific programming environment;
  • a proactive and curious mindset, with an interest in exploring evolutions in space systems and an appetite for new concepts and technologies relevant to European space systems. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Commercialisation Department - Ventures and Finance Office
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France

Our team and mission

The Access to Finance, Ventures and Analytics Office is responsible for developing measures to encourage, assist and ease access to finance for space entities and commercial projects, including support to venture capital investment and support to secure debt or loans. In addition, the office provides expertise in business analytics and automation, supporting both the operation and impact assessment of the CIP programmes and support schemes (including financing activities). It also contributes to the development of a comprehensive and effective commercial and institutional market intelligence, making full use of and coordinating with relevant areas across ESA.

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Process Automation and Digital Tools

  • identify opportunities to automate repetitive or manual processes within market research, financial assessments, and application tracking;
  • contribute to the design and development of simple internal tools (e.g., dashboards, templates, or scripts) to streamline data analysis and reporting;
  • support integration and upkeep of document repositories, or shared databases used in engagement and tracking efforts;
  • work with the team to pilot and evaluate automation tools to enhance operational efficiency.

 

2) Topic 2: Communication and Relationship with Industry

  • provide hands-on support to companies during their application process, offering clear guidance and responsive assistance;
  • collaborate with internal teams to create effective marketing materials, case studies, and outreach content tailored to different industry segments;
  • assist in organising and supporting industry events, webinars, and matchmaking activities that foster ecosystem engagement. 

 

3) Topic 3: Space Market Research and Business Analysis

  • conduct research to identify and evaluate potential candidate companies within the space sector, supporting the development of a comprehensive and up-to-date ecosystem map;
  • analyse business plans submitted by applicant companies, assessing their viability, innovation potential, and alignment with evolving space industry trends;
  • support internal efforts to refine financial assessment processes, including data collection, scoring frameworks, and benchmarking practices;
  • monitor and report on emerging industry trends, contributing insights for future thematic programme campaigns and strategic focus areas. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

You are proactive and autonomous with strong analytical and organisational skills. You are able to identify inefficiencies and propose automation solutions within existing workflows using Microsoft-based platforms.

You have knowledge of the financial ecosystem and an understanding of the investment lifecycle of a company, as well as knowledge of the European space ecosystem and space economy.

 

The following are considered assets:

 

  • experience with Microsoft 365 tools, particularly advanced Excel functions and macros, Power BI and Power Automate for process optimisation and reporting;
  • a demonstrated interest in space technologies and start-ups; practical experience gained in a space start-up;
  • knowledge and background in economics, finance or business administration;
  • knowledge and background in marketing and communication.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in Space Applications for the Mobility Sector
description_html:
Location
ECSAT, Harwell, United Kingdom  

Due to the location of ECSAT and current UK legislation, only UK citizens, students enrolled in a UK university, or those with pre-settled status (right to study) in the UK are eligible to apply for this internship.

Our team and mission

ESA Business Applications and Space Solutions (BASS) aims to demonstrate that space is open for business and has the power to improve our everyday lives on Earth. This is done by helping companies in ESA’s member states develop innovative services and products that utilise data from existing space assets, such as satellite communication, earth observation, satellite navigation and human spaceflight technologies, in combination with terrestrial technologies, to deliver sustainable services for the benefit of user communities. 

Operating at the intersection of innovation and business, the programme helps stakeholders address commercial and technical risks throughout the development lifecycle, transforming commercially promising space‐based application concepts into operational, profitable and self‐sustaining applications. Acting as a trusted mediator between user communities, the space industry, and service providers, ESA BASS is committed to demonstrating the transformative power of space technology in improving everyday life on Earth.

Mobility is one of the sectors with significant potential for innovative services that integrate space technologies. The green transition currently under way, together with the digitalisation and automation of transport, brings countless opportunities for innovation across the entire chain.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Through this internship, you will gain, particularly in the context of the automotive and micro-mobility sectors:

 

  1. a comprehensive overview of innovative services based on integrated space-based data and terrestrial technologies;
  2. an in depth understanding of future trends in the automotive industry and the emerging role of the space industry in the automotive value chain;
  3. experience in business development and an understanding of business models.

 

You will aim to build a comprehensive understanding of the market opportunities in the mobility sector for downstream space applications to support the development of sustainable, green and innovative applications. The emphasis will be on the automotive and micro-mobility industries, where ESA has a number of working groups and initiatives with external partners.

 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks:

 

  • identifying and characterising commercial opportunities for innovative services and applications in the mobility sector exploiting space assets such as satellite communications, satellite navigation, and earth observation;
  • supporting the identification of and engagement with champion industry stakeholders and public entities that may become potential customers and users of the mobility services identified;
  • supporting the characterisation, documentation and organisation of relevant industrial contacts and stakeholders;
  • identifying gaps in existing technologies and services and supporting the identification of new developments in both terrestrial and space-based technologies, including emerging technologies.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

The following are considered assets:

 

  • knowledge of the automotive sector;
  • knowledge of business development and commercial topics;
  • an interest in new and emerging technologies.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Strategy Department - Strategy, Sustainability, and Strategic Foresight Tracks
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

Strategy Department (SLE-S)  

The European Space Agency's Strategy Department is at the centre of the action when it comes to shaping the future of Europe in space. Its mission is to transform Strategy 2040 from a vision into reality, ensuring ESA not only anticipates global challenges but also leads in addressing them. 

 
The Strategy Department defines, coordinates and implements the Agency's strategic framework, including the ESA-wide strategy, working with all stakeholders. It runs the relevant processes and the Inter-Directorate Programme Strategy Group (IDPSG), and provides the foresight, strategic intelligence, tools and frameworks needed to translate long-term ambitions into action. It delivers strategic analysis to support decision-making and to keep the Agency's long-term objectives aligned with its short-, mid- and long-term planning cycles, while enabling ESA to set long-term priorities, prepare bold initiatives and align resources so that Europe remains a space leader on the world stage. 


The Department also represents the Agency in relations with external strategy and policy organisations relevant to ESA's long-term positioning. 


As an intern, you will be directly involved in this effort and gain unique insight into how strategic decisions are made at the highest level. You will have the chance to follow one of three paths, each playing a vital role in Europe's space future. 

 

Strategic Initiatives (SLE-SC) 

Within the ESA Strategy Department, the Strategic Initiatives Team supports the implementation of ESA’s Strategy 2040. The Team is responsible for identifying, defining and coordinating new, cross-cutting initiatives that advance ESA’s strategic goals and priorities between Council Meetings at Ministerial level. The Team analyses strategic gaps and opportunities for the European space sector and accelerates the definition and early implementation of high-impact initiatives to address them. For this purpose, the Team works in close cooperation with ESA Directorates and strategic partners through collaborative frameworks, processes and campaigns. 

 

In addition, the Team leads the development of new concepts, methodologies and tools for strategic innovation, and organises collaborative and competitive events, such as innovation sprints, to support the development of strategic initiatives. Finally, the Team supports the broader work of the Strategy Department and contributes to high-level engagements with ESA Member States, as required.

Strategic Coordination (SLE-SA)

Under the direct authority of the Head of Department, the Strategy Coordination Division coordinates the implementation and evolution of the Agency’s strategic framework, supporting ESA’s mission and objectives by maintaining the Long-Term Plan (LTP), monitoring Agency performance, and overseeing the Basic Activities (BA) programme. The Division ensures coherence across ESA’s short-, medium- and long-term planning cycles and coordinates closely with relevant Directorates and services. 

 

1. Long-Term Plan & Strategy Coordination 

  • coordinating the implementation and evolution of the Agency’s strategic framework;
  • maintaining and defining the ESA Long-Term Plan (LTP) in line with the Agency’s strategic framework and across all programmes and activities;
  • ensuring coherence across ESA’s short-, medium- and long-term planning cycles;
  • integrating strategic foresight into Agency decision-making processes;
  • coordinating strategic analysis and financial planning, including preparation for Council Meetings at Ministerial level;
  • defining, monitoring and overseeing the evolution of the Agency’s key performance indicators (KPIs);
  • contributing to the Agency-wide implementation of strategy-related recommendations and measures;
  • preparing the ESA Annual Report to Council;
  • analysing the strategic evolution of ESA’s footprint in Member States;
  • preparing space-related background and strategic policy papers. 

 

2. Basic Activities Programme / Basic Activities Office 

The BA constitute the Agency’s corporate, mandatory programme foundation, providing the capabilities, infrastructure, knowledge management, education programmes and early-stage R&D that underpin ESA’s programmes and prepare future missions and activities across all domains.

The Division oversees the programmatic and budgetary planning, geographical return, preparation, implementation and continuous evolution of the Basic Activities programme framework, ensuring consistency across the Agency and effective coordination with all relevant Directorates and services. It provides the governance, monitoring and strategic oversight required to ensure that BA activities remain coherent, affordable and aligned with the Agency’s strategic objectives.

A key responsibility of the Division is the preparation of the Director General’s Proposal on the Level of Resources (LoR) proposal, which is decided at Ministerial Council level, consolidating programmatic needs, financial requirements, strategic priorities and Member State considerations into a coherent and evidence-based proposal. The Division supports the process from early priority-setting and internal coordination through to Member State engagement and negotiation, ensuring that the BA package is strategically justified, financially sustainable and clearly articulated in terms of its value in enabling ESA’s programmes and future missions.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Interns in the Strategy Department will contribute to the implementation of Strategy 2040, at the heart of ESA’s efforts to shape the future of Europe in space. Depending on their path, interns may support activities in Strategic Initiatives and Strategic Coordinations. 

 

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Strategic Initiatives (SLE-SC)  

Within the Strategic Initiatives Team, you will be involved in the practical activities behind new strategic initiatives, helping turn ideas, inputs and discussions into clear actions and useful material. You will support the preparation, coordination and follow-up of activities, helping the team organise information, prepare concise inputs for internal discussions, monitor ongoing work and keep workshops, Strategy Forums and competitive Innovation Sprints running smoothly. 

 

You will contribute to: 

  • exploring strategic themes, emerging trends and relevant space-sector activities, then turning your findings into clear and useful summaries; 
  • bringing structure to information on innovation-related activities, helping the team track progress, spot connections and prepare internal reporting;
  • shaping practical material for meetings, workshops and management discussions, including briefing notes, slide decks and short summaries;
  • keeping collaborative activities moving by consolidating inputs, updating trackers, preparing agendas, capturing key points and following up on agreed actions;
  • helping develop new tools and dashboards that make activities easier to monitor, analyse and communicate;
  • engaging with colleagues from different teams and, where relevant, external partners by preparing practical material and helping turn collaborative inputs into usable outputs;
  • supporting the organisation of lively strategy and innovation events, such as strategy forums, innovation sprints and innovation-focused workshops;
  • supporting communication activities by helping to develop clear messaging, simple visual material and short articles.

2) Topic 2: Strategic Coordination (SLE-SA)

1. Long-Term Plan & Strategy Coordination  

During your internship, you will contribute to strategic planning and organisational transformation activities at the heart of ESA's Strategy Coordination function. In a highly international and multicultural environment, you will support the delivery of ESA's Long-Term Plan (LTP), a key Agency strategic document defining the pathways for the next decade.

You will support the development, deployment and operational implementation of a digital tool designed to monitor and facilitate this delivery.

You will collaborate closely with stakeholders across ESA directorates to collect, analyse and consolidate strategic data, helping to translate long-term ambitions into measurable actions and results.

The internship will also provide opportunities to support strategic analyses and evaluations of ESA's legal framework, administrative structures, programmes and financial planning contributing to the continuous evolution of the Agency.

In addition, you will support internal and external reporting and presentations of results and achievements for senior management and Member States. 

 

2. Basic Activities Programme / Basic Activities Office 

​​Joining the Strategy Coordination Division within the Basic Activities team will allow you to gain first-hand experience in the management of ESA’s core mandatory programme framework and acquire an in-depth understanding of a number of activities considered the foundations of the Agency, while advancing the Agency's long-term goals. 

In an international and multicultural environment, you will support the delivery of strategic analysis, helping to define the pathways for the next decades. During this internship, you will contribute to strategic planning and organisational transformation activities and gain unique insight into how strategic decisions are made at the highest level. 

 

More specifically, you will have the chance to support the team by: 

  • ​analysing Member States' strategic positions, economic outlook and political policies to inform documents tabled at different committees;  
  • ​supporting the preparation of reports and documents on BA activity lines, including associated research and analysis; 
  • ​preparing intelligence briefings for key decision-makers, synthesising information on programmatic, political and industrial developments; 
  • ​contributing to the update of ESA’s programmatic roadmaps in coordination with Programme Directorates. 

​ 

​As part of the Strategy Department, you may also contribute to wider strategy-related activities, gaining insight into ESA’s institutional framework, programmes, policies and decision-making processes. In a multicultural and collaborative environment, you will interact with experts across different areas, develop a broader understanding of the European and international space sector and contribute directly to ESA’s strategic objectives and change. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Strategic analysis and research

  • interest in strategic planning, public policy or international affairs;
  • knowledge of innovation management or a related field;
  • ability to analyse and synthesise information from multiple source;
  • good written and verbal English communication skills;
  • ability to prepare clear and structured reports and presentations.

 

Digital tools and data analysis 

  • interest in digital transformation and data-driven decision-making;
  • knowledge of software development is an asset.

 

Personal skills 

  • proactive attitude and willingness to learn;
  • curiosity, initiative, and the ability to work both independently and as part of a multicultural team;
  • strong organisational skills and attention to detail;
  • ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

The Team analyses strategic gaps and opportunities for the European space sector and accelerates the definition and early implementation of high-impact initiatives to address them. For this purpose, the Team works in close cooperation with ESA Directorates and strategic partners through collaborative frameworks, processes and campaigns. In addition, the Team leads the development of new concepts, methodologies and tools for strategic innovation, and organises collaborative and competitive events, such as innovation sprints, to support the development of strategic initiatives. Finally, the Team supports the broader work of the Strategy Department and contributes to high-level engagements with ESA Member States, as required. Strategic Coordination (SLE-SA) Under the direct authority of the Head of Department, the Strategy Coordination Division coordinates the implementation and evolution of the Agency’s strategic framework, supporting ESA’s mission and objectives by maintaining the Long-Term Plan (LTP), monitoring Agency performance, and overseeing the Basic Activities (BA) programme. The Division ensures coherence across ESA’s short-, medium- and long-term planning cycles and coordinates closely with relevant Directorates and services. 1. Long-Term Plan & Strategy Coordination coordinating the implementation and evolution of the Agency’s strategic framework; maintaining and defining the ESA Long-Term Plan (LTP) in line with the Agency’s strategic framework and across all programmes and activities; ensuring coherence across ESA’s short-, medium- and long-term planning cycles; integrating strategic foresight into Agency decision-making processes; coordinating strategic analysis and financial planning, including preparation for Council Meetings at Ministerial level; defining, monitoring and overseeing the evolution of the Agency’s key performance indicators (KPIs); contributing to the Agency-wide implementation of strategy-related recommendations and measures; preparing the ESA Annual Report to Council; analysing the strategic evolution of ESA’s footprint in Member States; preparing space-related background and strategic policy papers. 2. Basic Activities Programme / Basic Activities Office The BA constitute the Agency’s corporate, mandatory programme foundation, providing the capabilities, infrastructure, knowledge management, education programmes and early-stage R&D that underpin ESA’s programmes and prepare future missions and activities across all domains. The Division oversees the programmatic and budgetary planning, geographical return, preparation, implementation and continuous evolution of the Basic Activities programme framework, ensuring consistency across the Agency and effective coordination with all relevant Directorates and services. It provides the governance, monitoring and strategic oversight required to ensure that BA activities remain coherent, affordable and aligned with the Agency’s strategic objectives. A key responsibility of the Division is the preparation of the Director General’s Proposal on the Level of Resources (LoR) proposal, which is decided at Ministerial Council level, consolidating programmatic needs, financial requirements, strategic priorities and Member State considerations into a coherent and evidence-based proposal. The Division supports the process from early priority-setting and internal coordination through to Member State engagement and negotiation, ensuring that the BA package is strategically justified, financially sustainable and clearly articulated in terms of its value in enabling ESA’s programmes and future missions. You will contribute to: exploring strategic themes, emerging trends and relevant space-sector activities, then turning your findings into clear and useful summaries; bringing structure to information on innovation-related activities, helping the team track progress, spot connections and prepare internal reporting; shaping practical material for meetings, workshops and management discussions, including briefing notes, slide decks and short summaries; keeping collaborative activities moving by consolidating inputs, updating trackers, preparing agendas, capturing key points and following up on agreed actions; helping develop new tools and dashboards that make activities easier to monitor, analyse and communicate; engaging with colleagues from different teams and, where relevant, external partners by preparing practical material and helping turn collaborative inputs into usable outputs; supporting the organisation of lively strategy and innovation events, such as strategy forums, innovation sprints and innovation-focused workshops; supporting communication activities by helping to develop clear messaging, simple visual material and short articles. 2) Topic 2: Strategic Coordination (SLE-SA) 1. Long-Term Plan & Strategy Coordination During your internship, you will contribute to strategic planning and organisational transformation activities at the heart of ESA's Strategy Coordination function. In a highly international and multicultural environment, you will support the delivery of ESA's Long-Term Plan (LTP), a key Agency strategic document defining the pathways for the next decade. You will support the development, deployment and operational implementation of a digital tool designed to monitor and facilitate this delivery. You will collaborate closely with stakeholders across ESA directorates to collect, analyse and consolidate strategic data, helping to translate long-term ambitions into measurable actions and results. The internship will also provide opportunities to support strategic analyses and evaluations of ESA's legal framework, administrative structures, programmes and financial planning contributing to the continuous evolution of the Agency. In addition, you will support internal and external reporting and presentations of results and achievements for senior management and Member States. 2. Basic Activities Programme / Basic Activities Office ​​Joining the Strategy Coordination Division within the Basic Activities team will allow you to gain first-hand experience in the management of ESA’s core mandatory programme framework and acquire an in-depth understanding of a number of activities considered the foundations of the Agency, while advancing the Agency's long-term goals. Title: Intern in the Future Space Transportation Preparation Department - Project Support
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

As part of the ESA Directorate of Space Transportation (STS), the Future Space Transportation team (STS-F, including the Future Launchers Preparatory Programme - FLPP) is leading the maturation of the required technologies, demonstrators and enabling capabilities for future space transportation systems. It is therefore responsible for:  

 

  • conducting system studies and establishing Technology Roadmaps based on strategy-driven guidelines; 
  • supporting the assessment of the overall coherence of all technologies related to space transportation systems and products, including technology policy and harmonisation; 
  • preparing new elements and follow-on activities of the Future Launchers Preparatory Programme (FLPP); 
  • leading the implementation of the FLPP Technology Roadmaps, including the maturation of key technologies for future space transportation (Avionics & GNC, Structures, Materials and Processes, Propulsion and Modelling & Simulation) and the development of demonstrators (such as Prometheus and Themis).

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Providing project support in the Future Launchers Preparatory Programme, which leads the maturation of the required technologies, demonstrators and enabling capabilities for future space transportation systems. This includes:  

 

  • ​supporting the FIRST! Propulsion Initiative, including the project management of ongoing projects; supporting open OSIP calls (not necessarily limited to Propulsion but potentially also linked to other launcher technologies); supporting the preparation of the specific open competition procurement process for the next FIRST! Propulsion call including the preparation and review of procurement documents, organisation of internal meetings, evaluation of proposals, support to negotiation and project kick-off and subsequent management of projects;  
  • ​supporting the THRUST! Initiative, including the finalisation of the procurement of the next THRUST! phase including organisation of internal meetings, evaluation of proposals, support to negotiation, and project kick-off (as necessary);   
  • ​supporting the Future Access to Space Club - organisation of online and in-person events as needed; maintaining the contact database; performance/follow-up of specific actions identified during club meetings (as necessary); 
  • ​identifying best practices and improvements in Future Launchers Preparatory Programme (FLPP) open competition procurement actions, with a focus on improving the connection between technology providers and primes;  
  • conducting ​technical analysis of proposals according to FLPP criteria and procedures, with a strong focus on liquid propulsion; 
  • ​managing and regularly updating FLPP databases, namely of technology evaluation/roadmapping and European space companies intelligence gathering, with a focus on new space companies in Europe with a significant activity in propulsion; 
  • supporting FLPP knowledge management processes; standardisation, simplification, and optimisation of project management processes including use development and use of efficient tools for management and reporting; 
  • ​participating in and reporting on launcher technology and research meetings and workshops in order to assess potential technologies and identify potential providers.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in space, specifically space transportation vehicles, propulsion is a strong asset.  

Knowledge of Technology Readiness levels and project life cycles is a strong asset. 

Knowledge of the European Space Transportation industry is an asset. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Commercial Partnerships Department - AI and Robotics - Space for 5G/6G
description_html:
Location
ECSAT, Harwell, United Kingdom  

Due to the location of ECSAT and current UK legislation, only UK citizens, students enrolled in a UK university, or those with pre-settled status (right to study) in the UK are eligible to apply for this internship.

Our team and mission

ESA’s Space for 5G/6G & Sustainable Connectivity strategic programme line is advancing 5G and 6G technologies to support Europe’s digital transformation through the integration of satellite and terrestrial communication networks. This convergence of terrestrial (TN) and non-terrestrial networks (NTN) is expected to revolutionise how people live, work and communicate by enhancing mobile coverage, smart mobility, security and network resilience. The programme aims to promote the standardisation of seamless global connectivity for various industries and applications, including telemedicine, autonomous vehicles, aviation and maritime services. 
As an intern, you will work in a dynamic and multidisciplinary environment at ESA's European Centre for Space Applications and Telecommunications (ECSAT) in the United Kingdom. You will engage with experts in satellite communications, artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and emerging digital technologies through activities associated with the AI Hub and the 5G/6G Hub. These centres provide facilities for innovation, experimentation and demonstration activities aimed at enabling seamless global connectivity.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an intern, you will contribute to activities at the forefront of future communication networks, satellite communications, AI and robotics, supporting technical studies, experiments and collaborative projects that explore how integrated satellite and terrestrial networks can enable intelligent systems and new digital services. Depending on your interests and background, your activities may include:

 

  • supporting technical studies on future communication network architectures, services and applications;
  • developing and evaluating AI models for communication systems and network management;
  • experimenting with mixed reality technologies, robotics and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) as part of use-case development;
  • assisting with the preparation, execution and analysis of trials and technology demonstrations;
  • contributing to the development and operation of the AI Hub and the 5G/6G Hub;
  • supporting workshops, demonstrations and engagement activities involving industry and academic partners.

 

You will also have the flexibility to define and pursue your own research project within the team's areas of activity. Through this internship, you will gain practical experience in satellite-enabled connectivity, future networks and AI, while developing skills in research, experimentation, systems engineering and stakeholder engagement in an international and multidisciplinary environment.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

You should have good interpersonal and communication skills and should be able to work in a multicultural environment, both independently and as part of a team. 

 

Knowledge and background in the following areas is an asset:

 

  • satellite and terrestrial communication networks, including 5G and 6G;
  • network modelling, simulation, experimentation or testbeds;
  • AI/ML applied to communication systems, network management, or autonomous networks;
  • immersive technologies (AR, VR and XR), robotics and UAVs;
  • programming and software development, particularly in Python;
  • familiarity with AI and data analysis frameworks;
  • experience in conducting technical research projects;
  • previous experience working in international teams.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.
