Title: Intern in the Science Operations Department - Solar Orbiter App Development
description_html:
Location
ESAC, Villanueva de la Cañada, Spain  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of D/SCI, the Head of the Science Operations Department is responsible for the development of the science operations infrastructure under the Directorate responsibility, the operation of the Directorate’s missions once successfully commissioned, and the curation of all scientific data in the missions’ legacy phase. These responsibilities are discharged in full coordination with the Directorate’s Departments and Offices and as appropriate, with the Directorate of Operations (D/OPS).

 

In implementing their duties, SCI-S is supported by the: 

  • Mission Management and Science Operations Division (SCI-SO);
  • Science Operations Development Division (SCI-SD);
  • Data Science and Archives Division (SCI-SA).

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Developing the Solar Orbiter App in ESA Datalabs

 

Solar Orbiter is an ESA-led flagship mission in heliophysics to observe the Sun and the heliosphere. The respective Solar Orbiter ARchive (SOAR) at ESAC contains more than 5 million unique science files measured by ten instruments aboard the spacecraft. These data include high-resolution remote-sensing observations - such as the closest images of the Sun ever taken and the world-first observations of the solar poles. In addition, the data contain state-of-the-art in-situ measurements of solar particles and the electromagnetic field at the spacecraft site, which allow phenomena on the Sun to be linked with their impact on the inner solar system. 

 

The goal of this project is to make key-science datasets from Solar Orbiter more accessible to the scientific community by developing a new application within the ESA Datalabs (EDL) environment. EDL serves as a primary computational platform for accessing and analysing ESA's astronomical datasets and is currently being expanded towards planetary and heliophysics datasets. One central aspect of EDL is that users can run their own code directly on the archived mission data volume instead of downloading all these data. Taking advantage of this infrastructure, we aim to integrate a comprehensive “starter package” for scientific data analysis within one single “Solar Orbiter App” in EDL. 

 

The scientific analysis code with examples for each Solar Orbiter instrument is currently available as individual Jupiter notebooks that demonstrate important steps for the analysis of key-datasets. You will work together with experts from ESA archives and Datalabs on the full implementation cycle of the application up to its public release, including the design of its architecture, the integration of code and access to the archive data, and finally the systematic testing of the application with implementation of necessary improvements. In the end, the Solar Orbiter App shall allow new users a kickstart for their science projects and for experienced users it shall demonstrate the added value of EDL by containing code applications based on clear scientific use cases to run on the mission data for one or several instruments datasets.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • strong background in physics, computer science, or software engineering;
  • proficiency in Python (at least 1 year's experience in scientific or software development projects);
  • solid knowledge of astrophysics, space physics, or plasma physics (completed at least one university course on one of these topics).

 

Highly valued: 

  • experience with cloud platforms, containerisation (Docker), and distributed computing;
  • experience in scientific data analysis with Python (ideally space physics remote-sensing or in-situ data).

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Science Engagement and Oversight Office - CESAR Telescope Operations and Education
description_html:
Location
ESAC, Villanueva de la Cañada, Spain  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of D/SCI, the Head of the Science Engagement and Oversight Office is responsible for overseeing the scientific content of the Programme, interfacing with the scientific community and providing scientific expertise to studies, projects and missions, also in other Directorates as needed.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

CESAR (Cooperation through Education in Science and Astronomy Research) is a joint educational programme developed by the European Space Agency (ESA), the Spanish National Institute for Aerospace Technology (INTA) and the public company ISDEFE. It is based at ESA’s European Space Astronomy Centre (ESAC) in Villanueva de la Cañada, Madrid, Spain. Its main goal is to provide students and teachers from European schools with hands-on educational materials and resources about Astrophysics and Space Sciences, to be carried out in the classroom, as well as easy access to ESA´s data archive and to optical and radio telescopes. 

 

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Support in the pedagogical development of CESAR’s educational activities, with a special focus on the educational campaign for the upcoming solar eclipses.

 

The CESAR team carries out continuous work on transforming its activities and educational materials, adapting them to new formats and pedagogical strategies that are more engaging for students. Some examples include the development of new activities such as online labs, VR applications, and e-learning platforms. In this context, we follow the principles and guidelines already established by our colleagues at ESA Education, with whom the CESAR team is in regular contact. These updates are also carried out with the aim of making the materials progressively more accessible, inclusive, and diverse.
In addition to continuing our usual educational activities, in 2026 the CESAR project launched a specific educational campaign in preparation for the total and annular solar eclipses that were going to be visible from Europe over the next three years. After a successful first phase related to the total solar eclipse of August 2026, we are now continuing the development of this campaign in preparation for the total solar eclipse of August 2027 and the annular solar eclipse of January 2028. 

 

The goal of this internship would be:

  • to collaborate in the development and revision of CESAR’s educational resources, with a particular focus on inclusion;
  • to take part specifically in the design and implementation of CESAR’s educational campaign related to the solar eclipses visible from Europe in 2027 and 2028;
  • to design and develop new multimedia material for the educational activities of the CESAR project, as well as its publication and impact monitoring on the project’s website and social media channels. 


2) Topic 2: Support for the operation and educational implementation of CESAR’s telescopes


The CESAR Project comprises three observatories: a solar observatory with three telescopes, currently operational; a 0.5 m optical telescope at the Cebreros Observatory, fully refurbished and operational since summer 2026; and two smaller optical telescopes. These telescopes serve as resources for the CESAR project's educational activities.

 

The main objectives of this internship are:

  • support for the educational implementation of the 0.5 m optical telescope at the Cebreros Observatory, by creating observational cases and developing the system that will allow educational institutions to request and carry out their own observations;
  • support for the operation of the solar and Cebreros telescopes, as well as the development of software to manage the acquired data. This includes the support in the design of a CESAR data archive, with data curation and search tools.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Technical and/or scientific competences

 

Topic 1

Required:

  • good understanding of astronomical concepts;
  • interest in Planetary Science, Space Science and Communications;
  • fluency in English and Spanish (reading and writing);
  • pedagogical skills and experience working with primary- and secondary-school students;
  • familiarity with inclusive and diverse environments;
  • creativity and ability to work both independently and in international teams;
  • good communication skills;
  • general multimedia and social media knowledge.

 

Desired:

  • experience designing educational materials for inclusive and diverse audiences;
  • experience in the design of AR/VR tools and/or mechanical experiments;
  • knowledge of graphic design and basic HTML;
  • good level of editing pictures and videos;
  • experience and/or knowledge in UX Design.

 

Topic 2

Required:

  • good understanding of astronomical concepts;
  • interest in Planetary Science, Space Science and Communications;
  • familiarity with the use of telescopes;
  • programming skills in astronomical software, such as Python and ASCOM;
  • familiarity with computer hardware and ability to add new components when required;
  • pedagogical skills applicable to school observations;
  • capable of working in international teams;
  • fluency in English (required) and Spanish (desired) (reading and writing);
  • creative, capable of meeting milestones within schedules.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Ariane 6 Department - Ariane Mission and System Engineering Division
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

The Ariane 6 team supports the ramp-up of the Ariane 6 launch system. This includes improving the performance of the launcher, the launch complex and the Guiana Space Centre launch range, with the aim of ensuring affordable and continuous access to space for European institutional missions. 

 

The team provides engineering support in the following areas: 

 

  • complementary developments to enhance Ariane 6 launch system capabilities for specific missions, including science, exploration, Earth observation and navigation;
  • adaptations to improve quality, cost, availability and performance; 
  • monitoring of Ariane 6 exploitation, including production and launch campaign activities; 
  • maintenance of the Ariane 6 launch system in operational condition, including anomaly correction and obsolescence management. 

  

Working closely with the launcher system prime contractor (ArianeGroup) and the launch base design authority (CNES), the team assesses industrial capability, operational performance and Guiana Space Centre resources. This includes monitoring prime contractor factories and the supply chain, launch campaign operations, launch complex maintenance, operational tools, payload preparation facilities and readiness to support Ariane 6 launches. Performance is assessed by tracking the on-time delivery of flight hardware and Ariane 6 launches and by comparing expected performance, such as production rate and launch cadence, with actual delivery, including flight hardware delivery dates and key launch campaign milestones.  

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​You will support the A6 Launch System operational performance modelisation team in the following tasks: 

​ 

  • ​acting as key point of contact for OPERA users, ensuring effective support and coordination within the STS Directorate; 
  • ​managing reference models, including their creation and updates; 
  • ​updating the means database; 
  • ​providing methodological support to ESA users developing new models; 
  • ​preparing and running operational performance calculations to support use-case evaluations; 
  • ​coding and testing new models, from process analysis and model design to the creation of sequences, operations and test scenarios. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should demonstrate a genuine interest in space transportation systems, together with the motivation to contribute to the analysis of production flows and launch campaign activities. 

Experience with calculation tools would be an advantage.  

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

Title: Intern in the Commercialisation Acceleration Dept. - Entrepreneurship & Business Incubation Office
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Entrepreneurship & Business Incubation Office (CIP-ASB) represents a visible contribution to ESA’s entrepreneurial effort to boost green and digital commercialisation. By tapping into Europe’s enterprising communities, the Office is expeditiously extending the reach of European commercial space into the global economy and society at large. 

In particular, the ESA Business Incubation Centre (ESA BIC) Network focuses on supporting entrepreneurs and early-stage start-ups using space related technologies and/or data. 

The ESA BICs focus on three main objectives: 

 

  1. Addressing real customer needs;
  2. Diversifying space as a business (New Space);
  3. Focusing on the acceleration of commercial growth. 

 

The first ESA BIC was launched in the Netherlands in 2004, which has grown into a pan-European network of 40 ESA BICs in 23 Participating States by mid-2026. The Office additionally manages the ESRIC Start-up Support Programme in Luxembourg.

The Entrepreneurship & Business Incubation Office (CIP-ASB) represents the best place for students to engage with decision-makers in industry and aspiring entrepreneurs for future engagements beyond their internships. It will also be an exciting time to join as we are implementing the new ACCESS programme adopted at the 2025 Ministerial Council.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

The European Space Agency (ESA) has a network of ESA Business Incubation Centres (ESA BICs) across Europe. Each year over 250 start-ups with a space-related business idea are selected for incubation, while over 2200 start-ups have been supported altogether. The ESA BICs help these start-ups to develop and grow their businesses. ESA routinely collects information about the incubatees and alumni of ESA BICs. This has been done to evaluate the socioeconomic impact of the ESA BIC supported start-ups in terms of revenue, employment and investments.  
 
As an intern, you will have the following tasks: 

 

  • process and analyse data from start-ups on a portfolio level;
  • create and manage databases related to business incubation activities;
  • identify opportunities for further automation of ESA BIC data collection, processing and visualisation, including developing new approaches and dashboards;
  • prepare presentations and reports on findings;
  • perform other assignments based on operational needs of the team, for example activity coordination, supporting on-site events, conducting business research.  

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and skills in one or several of the following areas are required:

 

  • statistics;
  • data analysis;
  • economic Key Performance Indicators for high-tech start-ups;
  • MS Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint;
  • statistical software (e.g. R, PowerBI); 
  • data automation and dashboards.

 

The following are considered assets:

 

  • programming languages (e.g. Python);
  • experience with AI prompting.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Director General's Cabinet - Translation and Terminology
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

The Language Services and Minute-Writing Division is in charge of translating and editing official documents, correspondence and miscellaneous texts relating to the Agency’s work with a particular emphasis on scientific, technical, legal, financial and administrative subjects, as well as of drafting minutes of the meetings of ESA’s different bodies.

The main languages from and into which texts are translated are English, French and German.

The Division maintains a trilingual terminology database with over 30,000 terms and uses computer-assisted translation (CAT) tools and neural machine translation to support the translation process.

It consists of 24 team members and comprises the following three sections: The English Translation, Editing and Support Section, the French Translation Section and the German Translation Section.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an intern, you will support the work of the Language Services by carrying out the following tasks:

 

  • translation – from English into French – of a wide variety of texts relating to the Agency’s activities and processes, with some emphasis on scientific and technical subjects but also including legal, financial and administrative matters;
  • terminological research and extracting terminology from Agency documents and other reliable sources in French, German and English;
  • maintaining and drafting terminology records for the ESA Termbase, the Agency’s multilingual terminology database covering most areas of ESA activity.

 

In performing these tasks, you will make use of the tools and resources available to the team.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. Due to the nature of this position, native proficiency in French and a thorough knowledge of English and German are required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Experience in translation work and knowledge of CAT tools and other language technologies is a pre-requisite.
 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Legal Services Department - New Initiatives and Commercialisation Division
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The European Space Agency is an international organisation and the European gateway to space. Together with its Member States, the Agency expands the boundaries of discovery and exploration and provides space applications for the benefit of citizens on Earth.

 

The Legal Services Department provides the full range of legal services across ESA’s programmes and legal disciplines, such as public international law, European law and the national law of ESA’s Member States.

 

The Legal Services Department provides authoritative legal advice to the Director General, the Directorates, but also to Council and other organs of the Agency, to achieve the objectives set up in the ESA Convention. As such the Legal Services Department participates to the decision-making among Member States, formulating legal opinions and bringing new ideas to formalise space policies and programmes in Europe.

 

You will be part of a team of highly motivated, skilled lawyers working in an inspirational, interdisciplinary and multicultural environment.

 

 http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Law_at_ESA/ESA_Legal_Services_Department

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Legal support to new initiatives, commercialisation and programmes

 

You will support the Division of New Initiatives and Commercialisation in addressing legal matters arising in the preparation and implementation of ESA programmes and activities. Topics may include:

 

  • legal questions linked to the commercialisation of space activities and the development of new services and business models, and innovative forms of cooperation with industry;
  • programme-related matters, including the preparation and implementation of contractual and cooperation frameworks;
  • issues relating to procurement, funding, intellectual property, data, liability, governance and the allocation of risks and responsibilities;
  • interpretation and application of the Agency’s internal rules, policies and legal instruments;
  • legal research, analysis and drafting in support of the Division’s advisory work.

 

Through these activities, you will gain practical knowledge of institutional law and strengthen your legal research, analytical and drafting skills.

 
As an intern, you will have the following tasks:

 

  • carry out legal research and analysis on public international law, including ESA’s legal framework and European Union law, and the relevant national laws of the jurisdictions in which the Agency operates;
  • prepare and contribute to the drafting, review and processing of a variety of legal instruments (agreements, memoranda, etc.) and other documents;
  • monitor and review developments in international law, including the evolution of legal doctrine and its practical application in international organisations;
  • contribute to the Department’s daily operations by supporting the work of legal officers. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in public international law, including European Union law, and the relevant national laws of the jurisdictions in which the Agency operates, demonstrated through both study and experience, is an asset. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the P120/P160C Team - Rocket Propulsion Indicators and Applications of Energetic Materials
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

​​The ESA Directorate of Space Transportation (STS) is responsible for ensuring Europe’s independent access to space through the development, qualification and exploitation of launch systems such as Ariane 6, Vega-C and future transportation systems. Within STS, the solid propulsion team focuses primarly on the development, qualification and performance monitoring of Europe’s solid rocket motors: the P120C serves as both the first stage of Vega-C and the booster of Ariane 6, while the P160C is its enhanced evolution aimed at increasing launcher performance and payload capacity. The team supports test campaigns, data analysis, post-flight assessments and the continuous improvement of these strategic systems. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​Solid rocket motors and energetic materials are key components of current and future space systems. In a context of continuous performance improvement and the emergence of new applications, this internship aims to assess solid rocket motor indicators while exploring potential new uses of energetic materials.  

​ 

​During this internship, you will contribute to the following activities: 

​ 

​1. Solid rocket motors:

  • ​become familiar with solid propulsion;
  • ​process and analyse available data from ground tests and flights and assess the dispersion of key performance parameters;
  • ​propose relevant monitoring indicators and develop related dashboards to support performance analysis and monitoring;
  • ​analyse trends;
  • ​support the identification of improvements or future developments for Ariane and Vega.

​ 

​2. Other uses of energetic materials: 

  • ​conduct literature reviews on the use of energetic materials in space applications (including launch escape towers);
  • ​map current applications and use cases;
  • ​benchmark existing and emerging alternative technologies/systems;  
  • ​analyse potential applications. 

​

​Skills you will develop:

  • ​data analysis;
  • ​solid rocket motor knowledge;
  • ​development of technical indicators and monitoring dashboards;
  • ​technology intelligence and benchmarking;
  • ​knowledge of energetic materials and their space applications;
  • ​technical reporting and presentation of results in an international environment. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Your profile:  

You should have a strong interest in research and development, space technologies and innovation. You should be curious, proactive and eager to explore multidisciplinary topics, with the ability to work both independently and as part of an international team. You should also have strong analytical, communication and reporting skills.

 

The following would be considered assets:

  • being enrolled in the second year of a Master's degree in Engineering, or an equivalent programme, with a specialisation in mechanics, materials, or energetics; 
  • familiarity with scientific data analysis and programming tools such as Python or equivalent.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Projects Department - EnVision Project:Venus Atmospheric Variability and Gravity Waves
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

EnVision was selected by ESA’s Science Programme Committee as the fifth Medium-class mission in the Agency’s Cosmic Vision plan, with a launch in the early 2030s from ESA’s Spaceport in Kourou. EnVision will be the first mission to investigate Venus from its inner core to its upper atmosphere, characterising the interaction between its different envelopes: its atmosphere, surface/subsurface and interior. It aims to provide a holistic view of Venus, studying the planet’s history, activity, and climate.

 

EnVision’s science payload consists of VeraSAR, a dual polarisation S-band radar also operating as microwave radiometer and altimeter, which will map the surface of Venus; three optical spectrometers (VenSpec-M, VenSpec-U and VenSpec-H) designed to observe the surface and atmosphere of Venus; and the Subsurface Radar Sounder (VeSper), a High Frequency (HF) sounding radar to probe the top kilometres of subsurface. These are complemented by a Radio Science investigation exploiting the spacecraft Telemetry Tracking and Command (TT&C) system to map the planet’s gravity field and constrain its internal structure, and to measure the composition and structure of Venus’ atmosphere.

 

The EnVision project team is responsible for implementing the EnVision mission, composed of all its elements (Spacecraft, Instruments, Ground Segment). 

 

The role of the Mission and Performance team within the EnVision project is to ensure that the mission will fulfil its mission requirements by rigorous requirements apportioning, defining and controlling interfaces between elements, and verifying the requirements by establishing end-to-end performance budgets, supported as needed by mission performance simulations. The team is directly interfacing with all stakeholders of the mission (industry, the mission operations centre at ESOC in Germany, the Science Operations centre at ESAC in Spain, the launcher provider, the science team and the instrument teams).

 

The mission and performance team develops and maintains mission-level tools and budgets (e.g. Delta V budget, aerobraking scenarios), including mission performance simulators for both the aerobraking and scientific parts of the mission, perform relevant mission-level analyses and lead mission-level trade-offs.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Representation of Venus atmospheric variability and gravity-wave activity

 

The internship will exploit accelerometer measurements acquired during the Venus Express aerobraking campaign to constrain the representation of atmospheric variability and gravity-wave activity used in EnVision aerobraking simulations. Following the reconstruction of atmospheric-density profiles from the VEX measurements, Venus Climate Database simulations will be generated for conditions representative of the corresponding VEX passes. The simulations will be compared with the observed density levels, variability and spectral content.

 

You will develop a parametric representation of the measured density perturbations—for example, based on a superposition of wave trains—and derive distributions for the associated amplitudes, wavelengths and phases. The ability of both the Venus Climate Database and the parametric model to reproduce the flight observations and their resulting aerodynamic effects will be assessed.

 

The resulting modelling approach will then be applied to representative EnVision trajectories to generate reference atmospheric-density disturbance scenarios. These scenarios will support, in particular, Attitude and Orbit Control System simulations and thermo-mechanical fatigue analyses of spacecraft appendages, including the solar arrays. Time permitting, you will also contribute to relevant EnVision aerobraking Monte Carlo analyses.

 

Throughout the internship, you will collaborate closely with the mission analysis, system engineering, payload and science teams, as well as environment experts of the technical directorate. The internship offers a unique opportunity to gain end-to-end insight into planetary mission design and to make a meaningful contribution to the preparation of a major European planetary exploration mission.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in Python is an asset, as well as the ability to work autonomously.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality

Title: Intern in the Science Engagement and Oversight Office - A Logarithmic Map of the Gaia DR4 Universe
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of D/SCI, the Head of the Science Engagement and Oversight Office is responsible for overseeing the scientific content of the Programme, interfacing with the scientific community and providing scientific expertise to studies, projects and missions, also in other Directorates as needed.

 

You will work within the Gaia mission scientists’ team in the Astrophysics Section of the Office. The Gaia mission has been built and operated to map our home Galaxy in many dimensions with unprecedented precision and has brought a golden age for astronomy. Its data cover more than two billion sources, extending from the Solar System through the Milky Way to remote galaxies and quasars. The next data release, Gaia DR4, takes place on 2 December 2026 and consists of a huge and revolutionary catalogue with diverse data products on stars, exoplanets, black holes, double stars, variable stars, galaxies, quasars, asteroids, moons of planets, comets, and much more.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship:  A logarithmic map of the Gaia DR4 universe

 

The logarithm map of the Universe, originally devised by Richard Gott and Mario Jurić in the early 2000s (www.astro.princeton.edu/universe, A Map of the Universe), is a powerful tool to display the entire range of astronomical scales in the Universe, from the Earth's neighbourhood to the cosmic microwave background. Although the map was primarily devised to visualise the distribution of quasars in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey in the high-redshift Universe, the latest (fourth) Gaia data release (www.cosmos.esa.int/web/gaia/data-release-4) calls for a Gaia-dedicated update of the map. Due to its logarithmic nature, the map will provide exemplary proof of the full scientific reach of Gaia, ranging from asteroids, comets, and Kuiper Belt Objects in the Solar System, through nearby stars (and exoplanets and black holes), star clusters, spiral arms, and the Milky Way as a whole (including halo streams), to the Local Group (including the Magellanic Clouds, M31, and nearby dwarf galaxies), and unresolved galaxies and distant quasars that make up the Gaia Celestial Reference Frame.

 

You will work on creating such an updated map, using the 100+ data products in the latest data release to visualise the Gaia Universe. Extensions to three dimensions (two sky coordinates and logarithmic distance) can be considered. You will also add selected structures described in the peer-reviewed literature, for example halo streams and star clusters. Depending on your interest, the internship can also involve other aspects, for example additional Python coding to make the map interactive or story writing for associated outreach and education based on the map.

 

Objectives of the internship are:

  • learn how ESA runs its revolutionary Gaia mission in a highly multi-cultural environment;
  • enhance Python coding skills;
  • gain hands-on experience with the Gaia archive and Gaia data products;
  • broaden astronomical knowledge of Gaia’s latest data release;
  • exercise creative thinking and problem solving;
  • work in a team.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

The internship is suitable for candidates with a broad interest in astronomy.

Some experience with Python is an asset but the internship offers ample opportunity to improve programming skills.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics.

If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.

Title: Intern in the Galileo and EGNOS Programme Department - Digital Transformation
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Galileo is the European Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), providing highly accurate and autonomous Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) services under civilian control. It includes multiple services such as the classic Open Service, High Accuracy Service, Search and Rescue Service and new development such as the Emergency Warning Satellite System, Return Link Service, and the Timing Service Message. The programme is overseen by the European Commission, with ESA responsible for development, deployment, and system design.

The Galileo ground segment is the network of facilities and systems on Earth that enable the operation, control, and maintenance of the satellite constellation and its services. It includes the mission control infrastructure responsible for managing satellite operations and ensuring precise orbit and timing determination, as well as the system that processes navigation signals and generates data for user positioning. The ground segment also comprises a global network of sensor stations that continuously monitor the signals transmitted by the satellites, uplink stations that send updated navigation data and commands to the spacecraft, and additional facilities that provide security, system integrity, and service performance monitoring. Together, these elements ensure the reliability, accuracy, and availability of Galileo services worldwide.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will join an engineering team working at the heart of one of Europe's most advanced satellite navigation ground infrastructures. 
This internship offers a unique opportunity to immerse yourself in agile task management and information exchange within a dynamic, multifaceted system. You will focus on adapting Jira, a robust task management tool, to optimise task management, enhance team collaboration, and streamline communication across various projects and teams.

 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks:  

 

  • analysing existing processes with their users to identify user problems and needs;
  • defining and refining processes;
  • creating and customising Jira, Confluence and other tool projects for those processes;
  • exploring the use of AI in these processes;
  • developing tools in very close collaboration with our stakeholders;
  • making process information available through dashboards;
  • continuously updating the projects and tools to improve them;
  • providing direct assistance to process stakeholders.

 

During your internship, you will gain practical experience in:

 

  • streamlining processes for the management of large and complex systems;
  • optimising a essential tools for real-world applications, including JIRA and Confluence
  • project management methodologies, including Agile and Kanban;
  • effective communication strategies across multidisciplinary teams;
  • AI-assisted software development. 

 

Moreover, this role will help you develop problem-solving and analytical abilities as you navigate the challenges of managing a multi-project, multi-team environment while collaborating with experienced engineers.

This position is ideal for candidates looking to apply theoretical knowledge to practical, agile development environments and information systems.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

  • Python 3 language;
  • Web Application development;
  • Large Language Models usage, i.e. ChatGPT, Claude, Mistral;
  • Knowledge and background in Jira and Confluence are assets.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Galileo and EGNOS Programme Department - Resilient Navigation Systems
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

You will be joining the system security unit of the Galileo programme, which forms part of the Directorate of Resilience, Navigation and Connectivity. Our team is responsible for managing security activities throughout the programme, addressing both civil and governmental services to maintain robust end-to-end security standards.
We facilitate the definition of mission requirements and their subsequent evolution, integrating these into the system design while considering both performance and security. Furthermore, our unit assists in prototyping user segment receivers and system validation tools, enabling us to verify system capabilities and performance levels in advance and ensure compliance with mission, system and security specifications.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Your internship will look at how future positioning, navigation and timing systems could become more resilient by making better use of the space segment and reducing their dependence on ground infrastructure.

Today, the generation and maintenance of high-accuracy navigation information rely heavily on ground infrastructure. Precise satellite orbits and clocks are determined and monitored from the ground, while information such as Earth orientation parameters is also generated through ground-based processing and observations. This creates a strong dependency between the space and ground segments and can represent a vulnerability to the resilience of the overall service. A disruption or loss of access to critical ground infrastructure could affect the ability to maintain accurate positioning, navigation and timing services.

At the same time, a number of new space-based capabilities are becoming available. Galileo provides a global navigation infrastructure, while new concepts involving low Earth orbit satellites, distributed navigation payloads and missions such as Genesis could provide additional measurements, precise timing and orbit determination capabilities. The question is whether these different capabilities could be brought together as a system of systems, with the space segment itself providing a much larger part of the information currently generated on the ground.

 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks:

 

  • investigating what such an architecture could look like and, more importantly, what would be needed to make it work and improve the resilience of the overall system;
  • looking firstly at the functions currently performed by the ground segment and assessing which of them could potentially be moved into space or supported by information exchanged between space-based assets, including orbit and clock determination, time and frequency synchronisation, Earth orientation information, navigation data generation and integrity monitoring;
  • investigating then how different space assets could work together, including the measurements available from different types of satellites, the information that would need to be exchanged, possible inter-satellite links, distributed processing, the use of different orbital regimes, and how a common time and reference frame could be maintained across the system;
  • identifying, as a key part of the internship, what is still missing to make the system sufficiently autonomous and resilient, including assessing gaps that may require new technologies, additional measurements or a different system architecture, and evaluating their impact on the ability of the system to continue providing positioning, navigation and timing services when parts of the ground infrastructure are unavailable or degraded;
  • developing, as final objective, a possible roadmap towards a more autonomous and resilient space-based positioning, navigation and timing system, proposing how existing and future capabilities could complement each other, identifying the main technical and architectural challenges, and determining which developments would be needed to move from today's predominantly ground-supported architecture towards a system in which the space segment can increasingly determine, maintain and distribute its own navigation and timing information, even in the presence of disruptions to the ground segment.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. Title: Intern in the Galileo and EGNOS Programme Department - Artificial Intelligence
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Galileo is the European Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), providing highly accurate and autonomous Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) services under civilian control. It includes multiple services such as the classic Open Service, High Accuracy Service, Search and Rescue Service and new development such as the Emergency Warning Satellite System, Return Link Service, and the Timing Service Message. The programme is overseen by the European Commission, with ESA responsible for development, deployment, and system design.

The Galileo ground segment is the network of facilities and systems on Earth that enable the operation, control, and maintenance of the satellite constellation and its services. It includes the mission control infrastructure responsible for managing satellite operations and ensuring precise orbit and timing determination, as well as the system that processes navigation signals and generates data for user positioning. The ground segment also comprises a global network of sensor stations that continuously monitor the signals transmitted by the satellites, uplink stations that send updated navigation data and commands to the spacecraft, and additional facilities that provide security, system integrity, and service performance monitoring. Together, these elements ensure the reliability, accuracy, and availability of Galileo services worldwide.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will join an engineering team working at the heart of one of Europe's most advanced satellite navigation ground infrastructures. 
As an intern, you will contribute to the adoption of artificial intelligence technologies within a real engineering environment. You will investigate how artificial intelligence can improve software validation activities, enhance engineering efficiency and support better decision-making across the team.

 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks:  

 

  • developing artificial intelligence applications to support the review of software deliveries, including software quality assessment, source code analysis and security checks;
  • evaluating emerging artificial intelligence models, tools and techniques to determine their suitability and performance;
  • identifying opportunities to improve ways of working through intelligent assistants and autonomous software agents, and proposing innovative approaches to increase team productivity.

 

During your internship, you will gain practical experience in:

 

  • applying artificial intelligence technologies in a professional engineering environment;
  • secure software development and deployment practices;
  • evaluating emerging artificial intelligence models and technologies;
  • communicating technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.

 

This internship offers a unique opportunity to engage with cutting-edge technologies while contributing to the future adoption of artificial intelligence in a large-scale operational environment. You will collaborate with experienced engineers, gain exposure to real-world challenges and help shape innovative ways of working through the responsible use of artificial intelligence.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in software engineering and agentic artificial intelligence are assets.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Galileo and Egnos Programme Department - AI for Galileo System Engineering and MBSE
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The internship opportunity is within the Galileo System Engineering Unit, Galileo System Engineering Service, Galileo Project Office, in the Galileo and EGNOS Programme Department. ESA is the design authority of Galileo in support of the EU and the System Development Prime.

Galileo is Europe’s own global navigation satellite system, providing a highly accurate, guaranteed global positioning service under civilian control. Galileo is already the most precise satellite navigation system in the world, with more than four billion users.

Our team oversees the definition and specification of the Galileo System releases, known as System Builds, responding to increasing mission needs in terms of position accuracy, availability, integrity, assurance, robustness and emergency response. This encompasses the definition of the new Galileo Second Generation satellites (with the first batch under development), the updates of the current Galileo (1st Generation) fleet, the necessary updates of the Ground Segment, and the interface with service facilities and external entities.

We are a multidisciplinary, enthusiastic and diverse team and work hand-in-hand with other Galileo and ESA discliplines, from radionavigation and security engineers to ground and space segment engineers.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Galileo is a large and complex system with hundreds of functions, thousands of requirements, and an infrastructure distributed across the whole world. Galileo has new system releases and updates coming on a yearly basis. Implementation of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning tools at System Level is a priority for the Galileo Programme in order to ensure knowledge transfer, modelling of current and future evolutions of the Galileo System and fast data access for decision-making processes (design, qualification and anomaly resolution).

As a means to manage this complexity, the Galileo System Engineering team has put in place a Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) approach linking those functions to one another in a graphical manner. The MBSE system model is available to the full Project team: from engineers and testers to security accreditors and managers. This system model opens up new opportunities to link all the design elements and artefacts with their verification and validation across the whole lifecycle. Linking all design aspects will improve the system design and behavioural understanding by our Project team, and will maximise the success of its deployment.

Elements to be linked with the system model range from requirements, analyses and simulations, to performance prediction and early validation and finally, to real measurements. 

It is a massive amount of data to connect and we believe that artificial intelligence/machine learning can help in this endeavour. This is part of a growing trend in Systems Engineering known as AI-for-Systems Engineering, or AI4SE.

 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks:

 

  • exploring the AI4SE (AI-for-Systems Engineering) approach in the context of the Galileo MBSE system model;
  • defining and implementing practical use cases in which artificial intelligence and machine learning enable the MBSE system model to be queried, expanded and connected to other databases (requirements, simulations, test results, configuration, field measurements) in a better, and more efficient way;
  • developing Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning tools, methodologies, scripts and digital threads to support these capabilities.

 

In these tasks, you will engage with state-of-the-art Galileo professionals from ESA and industry. This would allow our Project team to digitally navigate through the system design seamlessly and minimise the risks associated with developing and deploying new Galileo system releases.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in Satellite Radionavigation, data science and artificial intelligence are assets.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.
