ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The TEC-R Team : 

  • define and maintain ESA’s technology strategy, ensuring alignment with Agency objectives and future programme needs;
  • identify, assess and prioritise technology development opportunities across all domains of space activities;
  • monitor emerging technologies, technology trends and critical technologies relevant to European competitiveness and non-dependence;
  • prepare future missions, programmes and capabilities through studies, concept maturation and technology foresight activities;
  • develop and maintain technology roadmaps that guide long-term investments and technology evolution;
  • manage ESA’s technology R&D programmes and oversee the full technology lifecycle from early research to demonstration and application;
  • coordinate technology development activities across ESA programmes, Directorates and stakeholders;
  • interface with Member States, the European Commission, industry, academia and institutional partners on technology matters;
  • monitor the execution, performance and impact of technology development activities and programmes;
  • communicate technology achievements, results and strategic directions to stakeholders and decision-making bodies;
  • promote the transfer, exploitation and industrial uptake of technology developments across the European space sector;
  • accelerate innovation through digitalisation, automation, knowledge management and continuous process improvement;
  • enable data-driven decision making by integrating technology, programme and performance information across the R&D ecosystem;
  • foster innovation, advanced concepts and new ways of working to prepare ESA for future technological challenges and opportunities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Your main task will be to support the preparation of the next Technology Strategy at Directorate Level:

  • prepare supporting material (data tables, visuals, briefing notes) for TEC management in the context of strategy preparation discussions;
  • collect, consolidate, and analyse quantitative and qualitative data from ESA’s technology programmes, Technology domains, and application domains;
  • support the creation of guidelines and recommendations to harmonise the use of digital tools (SharePoint, Teams, and IT tools) across the TEC Directorate.

 

You will belong to the Accelerate and Innovation team:

  • supporting initiatives to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of technology R&D activities through digitalisation, process optimisation, automation and continuous improvement;
  • ensuring the integration of data, knowledge and digital tools across technology strategy, roadmaps, R&D activities and reporting processes to support informed decision-making and organisational learning;
  • exploring opportunities for process automation and digitalisation, including the use of AI, with a focus on management reporting and knowledge-sharing tools.

 

At the end of the Internship, you will: 

  • gain hands-on experience in the analysis of a large-scale technology strategy, including the collection and synthesis of data across multiple programmes and domains;
  • gain hands-on experience in harmonising digital management tools (SharePoint, Teams, dashboards, AI-based reporting) within a large international organisation;
  • develop proficiency in structuring and managing technical repositories, including content migration and collaboration with the ESTEC/TEC Communication team;
  • acquire skills in data visualisation and smart reporting;
  • understand the role of digital tools in supporting strategic and operational decision-making;
  • learn how to support high-level strategic activities, such as contributing to ESA’s Technology Strategy;
  • build familiarity with knowledge management practices and the integration of automation and AI;
  • gain experience in cross-directorate collaboration, working closely with both technical and communication teams across ESTEC and TEC.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Title: Intern in the Secure Connectivity Department - Payload Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The ESA Programme Related to EU Secure Connectivity, hereinafter referred to as "Secure Connectivity", is intended to support the effective development and validation of the EU Secure Connectivity governmental infrastructure and the services provided through it, as well as the validation and demonstration of services based on the commercial infrastructure developed by the contractor(s) delivering the EU Secure Connectivity governmental infrastructure. 

The Secure Connectivity programme has been established by the EU and ESA, with the objective of deploying an EU-owned satellite constellation for secure communications, called IRIS² (Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity and Security by Satellite). 

Within the Space Segment Office, the Secure Connectivity Payload Section is responsible for all engineering tasks related to the design, development and deployment of the payloads of the secure connectivity space segment.

 

To find out more about our activities and how they fit within the wider context and future of ESA, visit: ESA Programme Related to EU Secure Connectivity – IRIS²

Moreover, candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1)    Topic 1: Efficient Techniques for Area-Beam Beamforming
The objective of this topic is to investigate and evaluate advanced beamforming techniques for area-beam satellite communications systems. The study will focus on methods that improve coverage flexibility, spectral efficiency, and power utilization while minimizing implementation complexity and resource consumption.
The project is expected to provide a comparative assessment of efficient area-beam beamforming techniques and identify trade-offs between performance, flexibility, implementation complexity and compatibility with the available technology in the currently developed secure communication satellites.

 

2)    Topic 2: Multibeam Nulling Techniques for Resilient Satellite Communications
The objective of this topic is to investigate advanced multibeam nulling techniques for mitigating interference and jamming in satellite communication systems. The project is expected to assess the applicability of digital beamforming and adaptive antenna processing methods to resilient satellite payloads and implement and evaluate the trade-offs between interference suppression performance, system capacity, coverage preservation, and implementation complexity, through modelling and benchmarking.

 

3)    Topic 3:  Modelling of Telecom On-board Processing & Active Antenna
The objective of this topic is to model a telecommunications payload architecture comprising an active antenna and an on-board processor at block level, to support performance analysis, e.g. power consumption, heat dissipation, process efficiency. The tasks envisaged encompass the survey of active antenna and on-board processor architectures, identification of major blocks and interfaces, definition of a modelling architecture, modelling of blocks and implementation of use cases for model validation, including relevant waveforms. Correlation with hardware may also be included.

 

This internship offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the development of next-generation satellite communication payloads supporting the European Union Secure Connectivity programme (IRIS²).

You will gain hands-on experience in payload engineering, system performance analysis and advanced satellite communication technologies that enable secure and resilient connectivity services across Europe.

You will have the opportunity to contribute to one of the above topics, depending on your background and interests.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in Satellite Communications and/or Radio Frequency subsystems are assets.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.

Title: Intern in the Electrical Department - Data Handling Systems Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Avionics and EEE Division plays a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability and advancement of spacecraft avionics and component technologies. Its mission spans design assurance, qualification, and testing of EEE components, as well as radiation hardness assurance for space systems in its domain of responsibility. The division operates specialised laboratories and provides expertise to ESA projects, industry, and research partners. It actively disseminates knowledge through internal and external training, conference participation, and tutoring of PhD students, ESA Graduate Trainees (EGTs), and National Trainees, fostering innovation and professional growth.

 

Components
The Section is responsible for ensuring that all EEEE Components (passive & active) flown on ESA missions are suitable for their application and the environment for which they are intended, lead the development of EEEE Components and their qualification. European Space Component Coordination (ESCC) executives and actively supporting European Cooperation for Space Standardisation (ECSS) standardisation activities. The section conducts Research and Development (R&D) activities in their domain of responsibility. 


Radiation & Component Reliability
The Section is responsible for assessing all aspects of EEEE Component Radiation Effects to ensure EEEE Components flown on ESA Missions are suitable for the Radiation Environment and their assigned application for the duration of the mission. It is also responsible for all EEEE Component laboratory Test and Analysis activities. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the EEEE Component Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ESCC/ECSS standardisation activities.

 

Microelectronics 
The section is responsible for development and verification of all Microelectronic devices flown on ESA missions such as AI Accelerators, FPGAs, ASICs, Microprocessors, microelectronic processes, Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), radiation-aware design, prototyping and test for space‑grade microelectronics. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the Microelectronics Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ECSS standardisation activities.

 

Avionic Architecture 
Responsible for supporting all ESA missions in the area of Avionics Sub-System development, their verification and validation, and their qualification within the framework of the agency's strategic objectives. 

 

Data Handling
Responsible for on-board data handling sub-systems (Platform and Payload). Responsible for developing and qualifying equipment for data acquisition, processing, and distribution (buses, interfaces, mass‑memory, data‑processing chains, remote interface units, etc.). on-Board data processing is an important focus of the section including development of turn-key AI HW solutions for ESA Missions. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the Data Handling Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ECSS/CCSDS standardisation activities.

 

Flight Software
This section designs and maintains flight software for spacecraft control and payload management. It addresses real-time operating systems, fault detection and recovery, and software validation frameworks. The team also explores advanced concepts such as AI-assisted on-board processing, ensuring adaptability and resilience in increasingly complex missions. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the Flight Software Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ECSS/CCSDS standardisation activities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Utilisation of neuromorphic for efficient AI implementation for space on-board Data Handling System applications. 

 

Recent AI developments have primarily relied on large-scale GPU-based cloud infrastructures, but this approach faces challenges with latency, power consumption, and data privacy. To address these issues, there is an increasing shift toward edge AI. Upcoming ESA missions will require greater on-board autonomy, utilising smart sensors AI powered. However, SWaP constraints may require energy efficient solutions, particularly when deployed on rovers, probes, or landers. The proposed activity shall highlight how event-based processing, neuromorphic technology, could effectively address these limitations, enabling efficient object detection, classification, and tracking.

 

The proposed activity will identify use cases in which event-based, or neuromorphic, computing can outperform or complement artificial neural networks deployed on conventional FPGA, GPU, or TPU platforms. Key advantages include lower power consumption and reduced latency, particularly when event-based sensors, such as cameras, are paired with event processors. Whereas conventional frame cameras typically operate at 25–100 Hz, event-based cameras can achieve sampling rates of up to 1 MHz. Combining an event-based camera with an event processor can therefore significantly improve the tracking of fast-moving objects and operation in low-signal-to-noise conditions, such as low-light environments.

 

Relevant datasets will then be identified or, if real data are unavailable, generated using a digital twin. This approach is particularly suitable for debris detection, landing, and proximity operations such as docking, servicing, and capture.

 

Finally, a testbed based on Neuromorphyx boards will be deployed for laboratory demonstration. It will integrate a NeuroSight event-based camera (Prophesee GenX320) with a NeuroCore event inference engine (BrainChip AKD 1500).

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in the following areas is an asset:

  • AI knowledge;
  • electronics.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Quality Department - Human Spaceflight Safety
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The TEC-QI Independent Safety Office is responsible for overseeing the development, implementation, and maintenance of ESA policies, requirements, standards, and for providing functional support to ESA projects in the areas of: 

  • Human Spaceflight Safety;
  • Space Debris Mitigation;
  • Re-entry Safety;
  • Nuclear Safety for applications in space.

 

The mission of the TEC-QI is to ensure the highest safety standards for ESA missions by enforcing clear safety processes, reducing risks, and protecting space assets, environment and general public. TEC-QI aims to make sure all ESA activities are carried out with a strong commitment to safety.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Under the supervision of the assigned tutor in the Independent Safety Office, you will: 

  • familiarise yourself with the recently updated safety requirements and the safety certification process applicable to the International Space Station (ISS), the Lunar Gateway habitation modules and, more generally, human spaceflight exploration, including crewed vehicles;
  • participate in ESA safety review activities for the certification of system and payload hardware developed by European industry;
  • review already certified system and payload hardware for lessons learnt compilation;
  • participate in the definition of new safety requirements, their implementation and verification approach;
  • compile safety guidelines for transportation and operations of simple payloads/experiments on-board the ISS;
  • support the preparation of drafts, presentations and tools aimed at improving the efficiency of the ESA Safety Review Panel.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness

Title: Intern in the Electrical Department - Wave Interaction and Propagation Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Wave Interaction and Propagation Section covers the understanding of the behaviour of electromagnetic waves (from a few megahertz to optical wavelengths) in a variety of media - both natural and man-made - and environmental conditions, and the application of this understanding to the development and exploitation of space systems. This includes modelling, data analysis and algorithmic development, as well as experimental validation of models and algorithms. It contributes to the performance assessment of space missions.

 

More specifically this includes:

  • wave propagation relevant to space communications, navigation and remote sensing;
  • wave interaction for active, passive and combined remote sensing of ocean, land and atmosphere of the Earth and other planets;
  • in-situ characterisation of the interaction/propagation environment;
  • payload data processing and data science techniques, simulation and performance evaluation tools.

 

For what concerns:

  • theoretical modelling and experimental validation;
  • associated processing, mitigation, retrieval, correction and calibration algorithms for product generation. For remote sensing this includes algorithmic developments relevant to the generation of Lvl1 (physical observable) and Lvl2 (geophysical quantity) data products;
  • for remote sensing, design and validation of on-board processing functions/algorithms for payload data products, image processing and optical payload data compression;
  • contribution to mission performance assessment and to data products quality monitoring and improvement.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

FORUM is the Far-infrared, Outgoing Radiation Understanding and Monitoring mission, a research mission of the Earth Observation Directorate. It will be the first mission to take global measurements of Earth’s outgoing spectrum in the far-infrared at unprecedented resolution. These data will be used to investigate climate feedback from water vapour and clouds and ultimately improve climate models. FORUM will embark two payloads; The FORUM Sounding Imager (FSI) which is a Fourier Transform Interferometer working in the 100 to 1600 cm-1 spectral region and the FORUM embedded Imager (FEI).
ESA - FORUM 

 

The Wave Interaction and Propagation Section provides expert support to the FORUM project on aspects related to instruments performances, Level 1 (from raw data to calibrated signal) and Level 2 (from calibrated signals to geophysical parameters) processors development, and mission performances evaluation.

 

In this position you will be involved in FORUM performance assessment activities:

  • ingesting the outcome of the on-ground characterisation tests of the instrument as parametrisation of the FORUM end-to-end simulator, to assess expected performances of the mission. You will run several sensitivity studies as a function of geophysical scene, or settings of the ground processing algorithms, to assess the impact on the Level 1 products (calibrated signals);
  • using the FORUM end-to-end simulator, you will generate reference datasets to support: (a) the assessment of the performances at Level 2 (geophysical retrievals), (b) further scientific activities and (c) the development of the operational ground segment;
  • you could be involved in the prototyping of calibration algorithms for FORUM.

Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

Title: Intern in the Electrical Department - Power Systems Architecture Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Power Systems Architecture Section supports space missions and technology research and development activities by defining and optimising spacecraft power system architectures. The team contributes to the sizing and design of power generation, power conditioning and power distribution systems that safely regulate and deliver electrical power to spacecraft equipment.
As an intern, you will work in a multidisciplinary engineering environment, collaborating with specialists in power electronics and spacecraft systems. You will use advanced engineering tools and simulation techniques to assess electrical performance, analyse system dynamics and investigate failure modes under different space mission conditions. This provides a unique opportunity to contribute to innovative technologies that support future space missions.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: AI for Advanced Digital Control and Failure Prediction of DC/DC Converters


This topic will be hosted in the Power Systems Architecture section in the TEC-EP Division. 
The objective is to investigate how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can enhance the performance, robustness, and autonomy of digitally controlled DC/DC converters for space applications. The work may include AI-assisted control strategies, adaptive tuning of control parameters, anomaly detection, health monitoring, and predictive failure analysis based on telemetry and operational data. You will explore techniques such as machine learning, neural networks, and digital twins to improve converter efficiency, stability, reliability, and fault tolerance while supporting future intelligent power management architectures.

 
2) Topic 2: AI assisted Design of DC/DC converters


This topic will be hosted in the Power Systems Architecture section in the TEC-EP Division. 
The objective is to explore the application of Artificial Intelligence to support and accelerate the design of DC/DC converters. Areas of investigation may include topology selection, semiconductor sizing and loss estimation, magnetic component design, control system development, and multi-objective optimisation. The work will assess how specialised AI agents, combined with engineering design tools, can automate design tasks, improve design quality, reduce development time, and support engineers throughout the converter design process. The study will focus on creating efficient AI-driven workflows for power electronics engineering.

Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in DC/DC power conversion, power converter control and FPGA programming is an asset.

Title: Intern in the Electrical Department - Energy Storage Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Electric energy storage is crucial for all space applications. Batteries are used in launchers as well as in Low-Earth Orbit (LEO), Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) and science spacecraft when energy from sunlight is unavailable. The most important characteristic of a space battery is specific energy, measured in Wh/kg. Since most lithium-ion battery developments are currently happening for terrestrial applications, spin-in into the space sector is of utmost importance. Current developments aim to further improve the specific energy of new lithium-ion space batteries.

 

The Energy Storage Section covers all aspects of energy storage for space applications, typically primary and secondary batteries, fuel cells and supercapacitors. The Section is at the forefront of these developments, leading R&D activities, supporting space missions, and performing independent testing of novel battery technologies in our own battery test facility.
To assess the sizing and performance of batteries for different missions, an independent battery model has been developed and validated. This model will be utilized to simulate different cases, which can occur on the battery during different mission phases.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

The aim of this opportunity is to perform battery simulations using our independent battery model in close cooperation with the energy storage engineers and the power management engineers in the team. Different mission scenarios including the launch phase, failure cases, abusive conditions as well as end-of-life performance shall be simulated. 

A further task will be to advance the battery models of the Energy Storage Section. Existing models shall be refined and optimised and new models for new cell types or battery configurations may have to be developed. These model developments will be supported by experimental testing at our own test facility.

You will draw up test plans and work closely with all the Section members and the test facility team to implement the tests.

The data will be assessed and the models built based on the experimental results.

 

During your internship, you will work on the following core activities:

  • simulation of Li-ion space batteries performance during different space mission scenarios;
  • modelling of Li-ion batteries for space applications;
  • refinement of cell and battery models and related documentation;
  • definition and testing of battery cells and batteries;
  • evaluation of test results and extraction of test parameters;
  • writing a comprehensive report and presenting the work at the end of the project.

 

The scope of work could be expanded to cover the following:

  • developing new Li-Ion cell model;
  • Li-ion battery abuse testing in space-relevant conditions.

description_text: Location ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands Our team and mission Electric energy storage is crucial for all space applications. Batteries are used in launchers as well as in Low-Earth Orbit (LEO), Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) and science spacecraft when energy from sunlight is unavailable. The most important characteristic of a space battery is specific energy, measured in Wh/kg. Since most lithium-ion battery developments are currently happening for terrestrial applications, spin-in into the space sector is of utmost importance. Current developments aim to further improve the specific energy of new lithium-ion space batteries. The Energy Storage Section covers all aspects of energy storage for space applications, typically primary and secondary batteries, fuel cells and supercapacitors. The Section is at the forefront of these developments, leading R&D activities, supporting space missions, and performing independent testing of novel battery technologies in our own battery test facility. To assess the sizing and performance of batteries for different missions, an independent battery model has been developed and validated. This model will be utilized to simulate different cases, which can occur on the battery during different mission phases. Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int Field(s) of activity for the internship The aim of this opportunity is to perform battery simulations using our independent battery model in close cooperation with the energy storage engineers and the power management engineers in the team. Different mission scenarios including the launch phase, failure cases, abusive conditions as well as end-of-life performance shall be simulated. A further task will be to advance the battery models of the Energy Storage Section. Existing models shall be refined and optimised and new models for new cell types or battery configurations may have to be developed. These model developments will be supported by experimental testing at our own test facility. You will draw up test plans and work closely with all the Section members and the test facility team to implement the tests. The data will be assessed and the models built based on the experimental results. During your internship, you will work on the following core activities: simulation of Li-ion space batteries performance during different space mission scenarios; modelling of Li-ion batteries for space applications; refinement of cell and battery models and related documentation; definition and testing of battery cells and batteries; evaluation of test results and extraction of test parameters; writing a comprehensive report and presenting the work at the end of the project. Title: Intern in Visual Communication, Presentation Design and Event Coordination
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The TEC and ESTEC Communication Team is a dedicated, supportive, and service-minded team that helps translate ESA's Technology and ESTEC's key messages to the employees, partners, visitors, stakeholders, and the general public.

 

The team is known for:

  • working well together and supporting each other;
  • building strong relationships with colleagues and stakeholders;
  • translating complex topics in a clear and understandable way;
  • being professional, reliable, and approachable;
  • finding practical solutions and adapting to changing priorities;
  • organising high-quality events, visits, and outreach activities;
  • promoting an inclusive and welcoming environment for all audiences.

 

The team helps strengthen the visibility of TEC, and ESTEC and supports positive engagement with internal and external stakeholders.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

The ESTEC/TEC Communications Team at the European Space Agency (ESA) in Noordwijk, the Netherlands, is offering a six-month internship focused on visual communication, graphic design, presentations, and communication support for events and outreach activities for the Technology Programmes.

 

This internship provides an opportunity to learn about and contribute to the communication activities of ESA's technical directorate through visual storytelling, design, presentations, and stakeholder engagement.

 

Visual Communication & Graphic Design:

  • learn about ESA's branding guidelines and visual identity;
  • assist in the creation and adaptation of communication materials for digital platforms, reports, exhibitions, and events in order to communicate the key messages of the Technology Programmes;
  • support the development of graphics that help communicate ESA technologies, projects, and activities.

 

Infographics & Presentation Design:

  • gain experience in creating and updating infographics that communicate complex technical information in a clear and engaging way;
  • assist in the preparation of presentations using Microsoft PowerPoint and other design tools;
  • learn how visual storytelling supports effective communication with diverse audiences.

 

Event & Communication Support:

  • support communication activities related to events, workshops, visits, and outreach initiatives;
  • assist with communication materials, participant information, and visitor engagement activities;
  • gain insight into how communications and events contribute to stakeholder engagement within ESA.

 

Further Opportunities Within the Team:

  • participate in editorial, multimedia, and digital communication activities;
  • collaborate with colleagues from across ESA's technical and communication communities;
  • contribute to projects that showcase ESA's technologies, missions, and people.

 

By the end of the internship, you will:

  • gain practical experience in applying ESA branding and communication standards in collaboration with Corporate Communication;
  • develop skills in graphic design, infographic creation, and presentation development;
  • understand how visual communication supports a large international technical organisation;
  • gain exposure to events, outreach activities, and stakeholder engagement;
  • experience working within a multidisciplinary communications team in an international environment.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the RNC Projects Department - LEO-PNT Payload, Signal and Frequencies Team
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Intern in LEO-PNT Signal Engineering & RF Compatibility, within the LEO-PNT Payload, Signal and Frequencies Team, Celeste Programme, Projects Department, Directorate of Resilience, Navigation and Connectivity. 

Celeste is the Component 1 LEO-PNT within the FutureNAV programme. It represents the ESA contribution towards establishing a European Low Earth Orbit Positioning, Navigation and Timing (LEO-PNT) capability as part of a multilayer system-of-systems PNT architecture. The component aims to complement existing GNSS services by leveraging a constellation of LEO satellites to deliver enhanced resilience, improved accuracy and innovative features for emerging applications.

The LEO-PNT Payload, Signal and Frequency Team is responsible for all aspects related to the satellite payload and associated technology building blocks, signal-in-space engineering, as well as frequency management within the following LEO-PNT activities managed by ESA: 

 

  • the implementation of the Component 1 of the FutureNAV programme, including:
    • the Celeste In-Orbit Demonstrator (IOD) phase, through an end-to-end system showcasing the feasibility and benefits of using low Earth orbits, novel signals and frequency bands;
    • the Celeste In-Orbit Preparatory (IOP) phase, to prepare for a future LEO-PNT operational system for the European Union and to unlock potential global commercial opportunities.
  • the preparation of the future operational phase of the EU LEO-PNT system.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Signal Engineering & Radio-Frequency Compatibility of LEO-PNT Systems

The growing interest in Low Earth Orbit Positioning, Navigation and Timing (LEO-PNT) systems creates new challenges in terms of radio-frequency (RF) spectrum usage and compatibility with existing GNSS/RNSS services.


As an intern, you will have the following tasks:

 

  • contributing to the analysis of the RF compatibility of potential LEO-PNT signals;
  • characterising, under the guidance of experienced engineers, navigation signals in the frequency domain; assessing potential interference mechanisms and evaluating the impact of system parameters such as signal bandwidth, power, spectral shaping, antenna patterns and orbital geometry;
  • developing and using simulation tools in MATLAB and/or Python to generate and analyse signals, calculate spectral and interference metrics and investigate compatibility scenarios.

 

By the end of the internship, you will have gained hands-on experience in satellite navigation signal design, RF interference and compatibility analysis, numerical modelling and engineering assessment, while developing the ability to independently formulate and investigate technical questions relevant to future LEO-PNT systems.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

  • good understanding of GNSS fundamentals, digital communications and signal processing, including modulation schemes, signal spectra, Doppler effects, correlation and receiver acquisition/tracking concepts;
  • basic knowledge of RF systems, antennas, propagation and link budgets;
  • experience with MATLAB and/or Python for signal generation, spectral analysis and numerical simulations; ability to analyse PSDs, interference levels and receiver-performance impacts is desirable.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.

Title: Intern in the Technology Department - Advanced Concepts Team
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

This internship will take place within ESA's Advanced Concepts Team (ACT). The ACT is a team of scientists who originate from a broad variety of academic fields and are aiming for an academic career. Its task is to monitor, perform and foster research on advanced space systems, innovative concepts and working methods. It interacts externally almost exclusively with academia and operates as a truly interdisciplinary team bound to high scientific standards. Through its research, the team acts as a pathfinder to explore novel, potentially promising areas for ESA and the space sector, ranging from applied to fundamental research topics. An important task of the team is to communicate scientific trends and results, as input to the strategic planning of the Agency. Visit our webpages at Advanced Concepts Team of ESA.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Autodiscovery of search strategies for large Keplerian Travelling Salesperson Problem instances and variants


The Keplerian Traveling Salesperson Problem (KTSP) is a combinatorial optimisation problem arising in spacecraft trajectory design, where a spacecraft must visit targets moving on Keplerian orbits. In contrast to the classical TSP, transfer costs are time-dependent and asymmetric. The KTSP is relevant to applications including active debris removal, in-orbit servicing, and multi-rendezvous mission planning [1–3].

 

Existing approaches use metaheuristics such as Ant Colony Optimisation (ACO), beam search, and Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS). Hybrid methods, for example Beam P-ACO, combine probabilistic solution construction with bounded tree search and have shown promising results for multi-rendezvous trajectory optimisation [3]. However, their performance depends on manually designed elements such as beam-width policies, rollout rules, pheromone updates, and local-search procedures.

 

Recent work in automated heuristic design combines evolutionary computation and language models to generate and refine optimisation heuristics. This internship will investigate whether an open framework based on evolutionary search and compact open-source language models (e.g. CHATOSS) can automatically discover effective search strategies for large KTSP instances and variants [4–6].

 

Objectives:
The goal of this internship is to develop and evaluate an LLM based framework for the automatic discovery of search strategies for large KTSP instances.

 

The objectives of this internship include:

  • a survey of KTSP, related spacecraft trajectory optimisation problems, and the development of new large instances of KTSP and a few useful variants;
  • development of a modular representation of heuristic components, including ACO rules, beam-search policies, MCTS rollout strategies, and hybrid approaches;
  • implementation of an agentic framework that generates, evaluates, selects, and refines heuristic variants;
  • benchmarking on KTSP instances in terms of solution quality, runtime, robustness, and scalability;
  • comparison of automatically discovered strategies with manually designed ACO, beam search, MCTS, and hybrid baselines.

 

References:
[1] M. Bannach, G. Acciarini, and D. Izzo, The Keplerian Traveling Salesperson Problem, arXiv:2605.00010, 2026.
[2] D. Izzo, I. Getzner, D. Hennes, and L. F. Simões, Evolving solutions to TSP variants for active space debris removal, Proceedings of GECCO, 2015.
[3] L. F. Simões, D. Izzo, E. Haasdijk, and A. E. Eiben, Multi-rendezvous spacecraft trajectory optimization with beam P-ACO, Evolutionary Computation in Combinatorial Optimization, 2017.
[4] M. Schmidt and H. Lipson, Distilling free-form natural laws from experimental data, Science, 324(5923), 81–85, 2009.
[5] F. Liu, X. Tong, M. Yuan, X. Lin, F. Luo, Z. Wang, Z. Lu, and Q. Zhang, Evolution of Heuristics: Towards Efficient Automatic Algorithm Design Using Large Language Model, Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 32201–32223, 2024. 
[6] H. Ye, J. Wang, Z. Cao, F. Berto, C. Hua, H. Kim, J. Park, and G. Song, ReEvo: Large Language Models as Hyper-Heuristics with Reflective Evolution, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37, 43571–43608, 2024.

2) Topic 2: Informing Guidance and Control Networks through Physics

 

Guidance and Control Networks (G&CNETs) are neural architectures that map the current state of a system directly to control actions, combining guidance and control in a single inference step. They are commonly trained using behavioural cloning: large datasets of optimal trajectories are generated offline and used to learn state-action mappings. This approach has been successfully demonstrated for spacecraft landing as well as low-thrust interplanetary transfers, where neural policies can reproduce near-optimal guidance in real time [1–3].

 

However, supervised learning alone does not explicitly enforce the optimality principles that generated the training data, such as Pontryagin’s Maximum Principle, the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation, Hamiltonian minimisation, and costate dynamics. Recent work has highlighted the potential of embedding these principles directly into neural guidance architectures, while physics-informed and Pontryagin neural networks have been applied to low-thrust transfers and planetary landing problems [4–5].

 

Objectives:
The goal of this internship is to develop the next generation of G&CNETs architecture combining behavioural cloning with optimal-control constraints during training in a PINN-like architecture.

 

The objectives of this internship include:

  • a survey of G&CNETs, physics-informed neural networks, and neural methods based on the HJB equation and Pontryagin’s Maximum Principle;
  • development and test of composite training losses combining supervised control imitation with HJB residuals, Hamiltonian minimisation, and costate-consistency constraints;
  • validation on benchmark spacecraft guidance problems, such as planetary landing or low-thrust interplanetary transfers;
  • comparison with standard supervised G&CNETs in terms of accuracy, robustness, closed-loop performance, and propellant optimality.

 

References:
[1] C. Sánchez-Sánchez and D. Izzo, Real-Time Optimal Control via Deep Neural Networks: Study on Landing Problems, Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics, 41(5), 2018.
[2] D. Izzo and E. Öztürk, Real-Time Optimal Guidance and Control for Interplanetary Transfers Using Deep Networks, Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics, 44(2), 315–327, 2021.
[3] D. Izzo, E. Blazquez, R. Ferede, S. Origer, C. De Wagter, and G. C. H. E. de Croon, Optimality Principles in Spacecraft Neural Guidance and Control, Science Robotics, 9(91), 2024.
[4] D. Izzo, E. Öztürk, and M. Märtens, Interplanetary Transfers via Deep Representations of the Optimal Policy and/or of the Value Function, 2019.
[5] A. Addario et al., Learning Fuel-Optimal Trajectories for Space Applications via Pontryagin Neural Networks, Aerospace, 11(3), 228, 2024.

3) Topic 3: Low-discrepancy deployment heuristics for competitive mega-constellations

 

Mega-constellations in low Earth orbit (LEO) are progressively deployed and replenished as multiple operators launch, insert, and replace satellites over several years. During this growth phase, the geometry of individual constellations and of the shared orbital environment changes continuously, generating close approaches both within and between satellite systems. Studies of large constellations have shown that self-induced conjunctions can represent an important component of the overall collision risk [3,4]. Conventional Walker constellations provide simple and structured final configurations [2], but their phasing rules do not directly prescribe how available orbital slots should be filled safely as a populated environment evolves.

 

This internship will develop and evaluate greedy deployment heuristics to determine where a new operator should place its next N satellites within an already populated LEO environment. The approach will treat conjunctions as a quantifiable operational cost and seek insertion rules that preserve a well-spread population in orbital-element space. Low-discrepancy sequences, such as Halton and Sobol' sequences, will provide one possible class of space-filling rules [5]; alternative maximin, greedy-packing, or risk-aware heuristics will also be considered.

 

The focus will be on the assignment of orbital phases, primarily mean anomaly and, where relevant, right ascension of the ascending node (RAAN). Satellites will be introduced one at a time or in small batches, and each candidate placement will be evaluated against the existing population in terms of close approaches, minimum separation, and collision-risk indicators. Large orbital populations will be propagated and analysed using ESA's cascade library [1].

 

Objectives:

  • survey conjunction risk, self-induced collision risk, orbital slotting, and deployment strategies for growing LEO mega-constellations [3,4];
  • develop greedy insertion rules for selecting orbital slots in mean anomaly and RAAN in the presence of an existing multi-operator background population;
  • investigate low-discrepancy sequences as incremental space-filling rules [5], alongside alternative maximin and conjunction-aware placement heuristics;
  • simulate progressive deployment scenarios using ESA's cascade library [1] and evaluate close-approach statistics, minimum-distance distributions, and collision-risk indicators at successive growth stages;
  • compare the proposed heuristics with Walker-type [2] and random-deployment baselines in terms of conjunction frequency, risk, coverage, and operational practicality;
  • formulate preliminary guidelines for safer incremental deployment in shared, multi-operator LEO environments.

References:

[1] F. Biscani and D. Izzo, "cascade: A C++/Python library for the propagation of large orbital populations and collision detection," European Space Agency, Advanced Concepts Team, 2023. Available at: cascade — cascade 0.1.10 documentation 
[2] J. G. Walker, "Satellite Constellations," Journal of the British Interplanetary Society, vol. 37, no. 12, pp. 559–572, 1984.
[3] H. G. Lewis, J. Radtke, J. Beck, B. Bastida Virgili, and H. Krag, "Self-induced collision risk analysis for large constellations," Proceedings of the 7th European Conference on Space Debris, Darmstadt, Germany, 2017. Available at: Self-induced collision risk analysis for large constellations | ESA Proceedings Database 
[4] N. Reiland, A. J. Rosengren, R. Malhotra, and C. Bombardelli, "Assessing and Minimizing Collisions in Satellite Mega-Constellations," Advances in Space Research, vol. 67, no. 6, pp. 2013–2025, 2021. doi: 10.1016/j.asr.2021.01.004
[5] J. Dick and F. Pillichshammer, Digital Nets and Sequences: Discrepancy Theory and Quasi-Monte Carlo Integration, Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, 2010. doi: 10.1017/CBO9780511761188.

 

4) Topic 4: Differentiable simulation and orbital control of shape-changing spacecraft in generic spacetimes
 
A spacecraft with movable internal masses can function as a form of propellantless propulsion when it interacts with a non-uniform gravitational field. By changing its internal geometry at different points along the orbit, the spacecraft modifies its gravitational coupling to the local tidal field. 

 

A simple example is a dumbbell spacecraft or a variable-length tether with masses at its ends. Extending and contracting the dumbbell at selected orbital positions can exchange energy and angular momentum with the orbit without expelling propellant.

Harte and collaborators developed a generic description of this mechanism based on the spacecraft’s mass quadrupole tensor [1–2]. Instead of modelling every movable mass or tether element, the spacecraft is represented by a time-dependent symmetric quadrupole tensor. 

Its eigenvalues describe the principal distribution of mass, while its eigenvectors describe the corresponding principal directions. 

The formalism has been developed for a general class of spacetimes, where forces and torques in Kerr and Schwarzschild metrics are known in closed form, though the practical orbital consequences remain unsolved for rotating black holes. 

Quadrupole modulation can influence orbital energy, eccentricity, apsidal orientation, and orbital stability [1–3]. Jupiter provides an interesting initial test case because of its strong gravity, large tidal gradients, rapid rotation, and significant oblateness. 

 

The project will investigate whether quadrupole modulation can produce useful secular changes in orbital energy, eccentricity, apsidal orientation, nodal precession, or inclination in strong gravitational regimes including Kerr and Schwarzschild metrics.

Objectives:

  • developing a differentiable simulator in heyoka [3] for a shape-changing spacecraft implementing Harte’s formalism for Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes;
  • validating the simulator by reproducing published results on eccentricity control, circularisation, apsidal motion, and orbital stabilisation;
  • applying automatic differentiation and gradient-based optimisation to identify effective deformation amplitudes, frequencies, phases, and switching conditions;
  • testing on Jupiter’s gravity and then reproducing and looking for pure GR effects in a representative Kerr Black Hole.

 

The project will combine general relativity, analytical mechanics and automatic differentiation. The final outcome will be a reproducible computational framework for studying shape-controlled orbital dynamics and evaluating unconventional orbital-control scenarios around exotic gravitational regimes.
 

References:
[1] M. Harte and M. Gaffney, “Extended-body effects and rocket-free orbital manoeuvring,” Acta Astronautica, vol. 178, pp. 625–633, 2021.
[2] M. Harte and M. Gaffney, “Extended-body motion in black hole spacetimes: What is possible?”, Physical Review D, vol. 102, 124075, 2020.
[3] F. Biscani and D. Izzo, “Revisiting high-order Taylor methods for astrodynamics and celestial mechanics,” Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, vol. 504, no. 2, pp. 2614–2628, 2021.

Title: Intern in the RNC Projects Department - Genesis Project Team
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Genesis is a mission in the ESA Resilience, Navigation and Connectivity Directorate, planned for launch in 2029 and currently under development. The Genesis satellite will combine the main geodetic techniques, namely VLBI (Very-Long-Baseline Interferometry), SLR (Satellite Laser Ranging), GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite Systems), and DORIS (Doppler Orbitography and Radiopositioning Integrated by Satellite). By flying the four geodetic techniques a single well-calibrated satellite, individual biases of the techniques can be removed. As a result, the mission will enable the generation of an updated global model of Earth – the International Terrestrial Reference Frame, employed for everything from land surveying to measuring sea-level rise, with an accuracy down to 1 mm, while tracking ground motion of just 0.1 mm per year. This improvement will have a major impact on multiple navigation and Earth science applications, including enhancing the precision of the Galileo navigation system. See ESA - Genesis for more information.

The ESA project team is small and supported by experts as required and will be working closely with industry and the scientific community to develop the mission in a ‘New Space’ approach wherever feasible. Both the space and ground segments will be under design during the internship, providing an opportunity to gain first-hand experience of system-level space mission design alongside seasoned experts.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Reporting to the Genesis System and Operations Manager, you will carry out tasks and grow your knowledge in the system engineering and payload/system performance domain, while supporting the development of the mission. In a ‘New Space’ mission framework, you will support the execution of Genesis mission engineering-related activities within the Project and industrial consortium and be part of the work during the critical design phase of the mission.

 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks:

 

  • GNSS Simulation activities, including testing with hardware-in-the-loop, including but not limited to:
    • consolidation of the Genesis reference scenario using available test equipment in the ESA lab (GNSS simulators and prototype receivers);
    • assessment of GNSS performance in the Genesis orbit.
  • GNSS/VLBI/SLR/DORIS performance simulations and assessment:
    • review and analysis of key performance parameters of the four Genesis instruments and their combination to achieve the Genesis mission goals;
    • preparation of Genesis operational scenarios and exploitation of scientific data.

 

This will be an opportunity to be part of the system engineering team of a small mission currently in its design phase, where several interesting topics need to be addressed. You will have access access to experienced team members who will support the further development of the engineering skills acquired at university, while providing opportunities to demonstrate your ability to independently handle selected tasks.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

You should be able to demonstrate your ability to work autonomously, effectively and cooperatively in a diverse, international team environment. You should also be results-oriented and capable of presenting practical solutions both verbally and in writing.

You should have a good technical background from university, together with analytical, organisational and reporting skills. You should also have a proactive approach to problem-solving and an interest in innovative technologies and methodologies.

You should have good interpersonal and communication skills and be able to work effectively in a multicultural environment, both independently and as part of a team. Previous experience working in international teams would be considered an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Future Missions Department - NoovaMoon Project
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

As part of the Future PNT Projects Division (RNC-FF), we lead the coordination of all Position, Navigation, and Timing contributions in the context of future lunar, Martian and Solar System exploration. 

This is currently implemented through various programmes: Lunar Pathfinder satellite (which includes a GNSS demonstration payload), Moonlight Programme (which involves the development of a GNSS-like lunar constellation, in addition to communication services), NovaMoon Mission (which aims to deploy a lunar station at the south pole of the Moon to monitor and augment GNSS-like lunar constellations, provide timing services and perform scientific experiments) and the planned future MARCONI Mars-dedicated communication and navigation system (currently under assessment). 

To support ESA's internal capability to follow up on these activities, the Division has established an ESA-internal R&D team fully dedicated to lunar and Martian navigation system engineering and performance analysis. This includes the development of specialised advanced exploration simulation models and tools, carried out in close collaboration with the ESA Technical Directorate.

As part of this internship, you will join this internal R&D group contributing to the analysis of on-going program activities and the development of future advanced PNT concepts for planetary exploration with a focus on the NovaMoon mission.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

This internship offers the opportunity to contribute to the NovaMoon mission, with a focus on three key areas of the payload: navigation signal monitoring, time transfer, and the generation of differential corrections.

 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks:

 

  • reviewing state-of-the-art time-transfer techniques, navigation signal monitoring strategies, and differential correction methods for lunar navigation missions such as NovaMoon;
  • contributing to the development of ESA software tools and simulation capabilities used to assess candidate models and processing approaches, including software-defined radio receivers for signal processing and positioning, navigation, and timing engines;
  • taking part in hands-on laboratory activities to design and set up a representative testbed aligned with the simulation environment;
  • planning and conducting a test campaign to evaluate system performance under representative laboratory conditions;
  • documenting the test approach and results, and presenting the key findings and recommendations to the engineering team.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

The following are considered assets:

 

  • knowledge and background in satellite radio-navigation systems;
  • knowledge and background in position estimation and/or sensor fusion;
  • knowledge and background in signal processing, GNSS receivers and software-defined radio;
  • good knowledge of and experience with Python.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in Real Estate and Facilities Management
description_html:
Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

The Real Estate and Facility Management team at the European Astronaut Centre in Cologne is responsible for creating, maintaining and continuously enhancing a safe, efficient and attractive working environment.

 

The team coordinates facility management services, workplace and accommodation activities, building-related projects and interfaces with a wide range of internal and external partners. The European Astronaut Centre provides a dynamic and international working environment that supports human spaceflight activities, astronaut operations, training, and research.


As part of the team, you will gain valuable insight into the day-to-day management and ongoing development of an operational European Space Agency site. You will collaborate closely with the Site Manager, facility management service providers, building users and a variety of technical and organisational stakeholders, contributing to the effective operation and continuous improvement of the Centre.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

During your internship, you will support the day-to-day facility, workplace and site management activities at the European Astronaut Centre.

 

Your responsibilities may include:

 

  • supporting the coordination and follow-up of facility management services and service providers;
  • assisting with workplace and accommodation management activities, including workplace allocation, occupancy planning and implementation measures;
  • contributing to the coordination and monitoring of minor works, maintenance activities and site improvement projects;
  • supporting the preparation and follow-up of meetings, action items, inspections and other operational site management activities;
  • assisting in the collection, monitoring and analysis of workplace and facility management data;
  • supporting communication and coordination with building users, service providers and other internal and external stakeholders;
  • contributing to site development activities and continuous improvement initiatives aimed at enhancing the workplace environment and operational efficiency.

 
Through this internship, you will gain practical experience in facility, workplace and site management within an international organisation. You will develop an understanding of how a complex operational site is managed, how diverse stakeholders are coordinated and how workplace needs are translated into effective and sustainable solutions. In addition, you will gain insight into the relationship between day-to-day operational activities and the planning and delivery of larger site development projects.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

A background or academic knowledge in facility management, real estate management, architecture, civil engineering, industrial engineering, workplace management, or a related discipline would be considered an asset.

Strong organisational and communication skills, combined with an interest in working in an international and operational environment, would be advantageous.

Proficiency in standard office software applications, together with an interest in data analysis, digital workplace solutions and facility management technologies, would be beneficial.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).
