Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Robotics Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Robotics Section provides functional support to ESA projects and carries out technological research and development (R&D) in the field of space robotics systems (from manipulators to autonomous vehicles) and laboratories supporting automation and robotics in crewed and uncrewed missions.

 

As part of our team of mechanical, electrical, control, and software engineers, you will contribute to the work of the Robotics Section at ESTEC, and in particular to the Automation and Robotics Laboratories (ARL), which consist of three areas:

  • the Planetary Robotics Laboratory where the work focuses on the design of rovers for planetary exploration;
  • the Human Interaction Laboratory which focuses on the collaboration of robotic systems and operators;
  • the Orbital Robotics Laboratory which focuses on activities such as Active Debris Removal and In-Orbit Servicing.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

The laboratory you will be working in and the tasks you will be given will depend on your final qualification, interests and needs of the Section but will be in the form of the following:

  • support industrial activities;
  • the laboratory is hosting third parties for tests: the preparation of the facilities and the support provided by the section personnel are vital for this;
  • research and development on novel robotics and autonomous systems: you are expected to maintain the knowledge in the field of the current robotics developments. Furthermore, you will conduct independent research and development on robotics concepts coming from internal ideas of the section. Such work includes concept designing, prototyping, testing to prove the idea viable;
  • collaboration with third parties companies in the frame of hardware development and procurement: the ARL has a constant need to upgrade and adjust its inventory in order to support new activities. You will be intimately involved in this process by directly interacting with third parties to discuss concepts, and trade-off solutions in order to procure equipment or software;
  • support relevant R&D activities or CDF studies when necessary: the section staff supervises a number of industrial R&D activities in all fields related to space robotics. You will have the opportunity to participate in reviews and otherwise support the activities as required.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in prototyping robotic systems is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Opto-Electronics Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Optoelectronics Section deals with the specification, development and characterisation of photonic component subsystems and active optical instruments, such as detectors and lasers operating in the UV to FIR wavelength ranges, fibre-optic sensors, lidars, optical communication systems and quantum technologies.

 

In these areas, the section provides functional support to ESA projects and carries out technological research.

 

The section is also developing and operating laboratory test setups and simulation tools.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Depending on your interests, technical competences and project constraints in 2026, you will support one or more of our laboratory activities for example by:

  • development of simulation tools for free-space optical communications systems;
  • testbed development of advanced spaceborne optoelectronic applications (for optical communication, optical detectors and/or lasers);
  • integration and commissioning of upgraded laser induced contamination characterisation setup;
  • assembly and commissioning of an optoelectronics test bench for the characterisation of scientific digital CMOS image sensors;
  • calibration and validation of Lidar terminals for Guidance, Navigation and Control and In-Orbit Servicing applications.

Behavioural competencies

Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

Knowledge and background in working with optical laboratory setups (including lasers, detectors, free-space or fibre based optics), real-time data acquisition or experience in programming and modelling (e.g. Python, MATLAB, LabView) or CAD is an asset.

Title: Intern in the Systems Department - Strategic Materials and Chemicals Regulatory Risk Analysis
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Sustainability Engineering & Standards Section (TEC-SFS), part of ESA's Future Engineering Division (TEC-SF), supports the development and implementation of sustainable engineering approaches across ESA programmes and projects. The section works at the intersection of system engineering, sustainability and innovation, helping to ensure that future space systems are designed, developed and operated in a more sustainable, efficient and responsible manner.
 

The team supports ESA projects from the earliest mission definition phases through technology development and implementation, helping projects integrate sustainability objectives into system design, engineering trades, verification approaches and operational concepts.

 

The Section also encompasses activities related to the EU/UK REACH regulation for environmental safety. The Section supports all ESA programmes in regulatory compliance, mapping the use of materials and chemicals, advocating for their continued use where necessary, and mitigating emerging risks of premature obsolescence.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Strategic Materials and Chemicals Regulatory Risk Analysis

 

During this internship, you will support activities aimed at improving the resilience of the supply of materials for the European space sector. You will investigate strategic raw materials, chemicals and advanced materials used in space applications and map their supply chains and key European and non-European dependencies.

 

You will assess factors that could affect their future availability, including regulatory developments, industrial changes and geopolitical risks. You will contribute to identifying emerging vulnerabilities and possible measures to reduce supply risks and strengthen European capabilities.

 

Through this work, you will learn how materials and space-specific manufacturing processes are used across the sector; how the complexity of industrial supply chains is assessed; and how regulatory, industrial and geopolitical developments can affect the availability of critical technologies.

 

You will work closely with specialists in sustainable engineering, standardisation and chemicals regulation, and help translate your findings into improvements to internal materials and regulatory databases and tools.

 

One of the objectives will be to develop a risk measurement approach to combine technology maturity, regulatory, geopolitical and potentially other relevant aspects.

Title: Intern in the Engineering Services Section - Metrology Laboratory
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

ESA operates a Test Centre at ESTEC, Noordwijk, The Netherlands, a unique place in Europe which is geared to perform environmental tests on large spacecraft and aerospace structures. The Test Centre includes the complete portfolio of test facilities to simulate the environmental conditions which are experienced by a spacecraft during its launch and early operation phase. This includes hydraulic and electrodynamic vibration test systems, shock test facilities, mass properties measurement facilities, electro-magnetic compatibility test facilities. Besides Europe’s largest space simulation chamber LSS and Europe’s largest reverberant acoustic noise test chamber, the Test Centre is equipped with a 6 degree of freedom hydraulic vibration test stand, a 320kN horizontal and a 640kN vertical electrodynamic shaker system and a large EMC test chamber. The set of facilities is complemented by a medium sized thermal vacuum chamber (Phenix), a small vacuum chamber with high solar flux simulation (VTC 1.5), a 80kN vibrations system and shock test benches for subsystem and equipment testing.  
For more information please refer to: ESTEC Test Centre 
 

Part of the Test Centre is the Engineering Services Section. The group encompasses multidisciplinary engineering domains, ranging from mechanical, electrical and electronic design up to metrology. Calibrations of electrical equipment and manufacturing are also areas covered by the Engineering Services Section, whose mission is to support the Test Centre and its customers, the ESTEC laboratories as well as the ESA programmes. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Investigation of Point Cloud Post-Processing Methodologies for Space-Grade Materials with Application to Satellite Mock-Up Reverse Engineering

 

As part of the measurements done by the metrology team, point clouds are generated and need to be processed, depending on the final application. The point clouds are generated from different sources, ranging from photogrammetry cameras to laser tracker or Coordinate Measurement Machines (CMM). The density of the point clouds varies clearly based on their source. Whereas in some cases, “simple” plane fittings are required, in other applications, more is required to be extracted from the collected point clouds.

The topic of the internship is the processing of the point clouds. It will consist of a theoretical part and a practical part. 

 

Theoretical Part
Conduct a comprehensive literature review of existing methodologies for point cloud processing, including filtering, classification, segmentation, feature extraction, and other relevant post-processing techniques.

 

Practical Part
Investigate the performance of point cloud post-processing methods on a range of space-grade materials through experimental testing. Reference measurements will be acquired using a Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) and compared with data obtained from laser scanning technologies, such as a CMM scanner probe, laser tracker scanner probe and/or laser radar. Test materials may include mesh, multi-layer insulation (MLI), carbon fibre composites, aluminium, and steel.

 

Finally, apply the acquired theoretical knowledge and practical experience to reverse engineering the Robotics Laboratory satellite mock-up, producing the most accurate and complete digital representation possible.


Keywords:
Point clouds
Data processing
3D scanning
3D models
Laboratory hands-on
Metrology

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in the use of metrological tools, as well as hands-on experience in a laboratory, are assets.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Quality Department - Space Debris Mitigation
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Independent Safety Office is responsible for providing ESA with independent safety authority in the fields of Human Spaceflight Safety, Space Debris Mitigation and Re-entry Safety, Planetary Protection and Curation, and Nuclear Power Sources Safety.

 

For what concerns the field of Space Debris Mitigation and Re-entry Safety, the main functions of the Independent Safety Office include:

  • defining and maintaining the ESA Space Debris Mitigation Policy, requirements, technical guidance and independent safety assessment processes;
  • performing independent review and compliance assessment of ESA Projects with Space Debris Mitigation requirements;
  • processing of waivers for non-compliances with the Space Debris Mitigation requirements;
  • reporting on the status of implementation of Space Debris Mitigation policy for the ESA Projects;
  • representing ESA in different international working groups on Space Debris Mitigation.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

The amount of space debris is increasing in such a way that, if current behaviours and trends in orbit continue, crucial orbital regions may become unusable. In response to this, ESA introduced its ‘Zero Debris approach’ to significantly limit the production of debris in Earth and Lunar orbits by 2030. As a first step, ESA's Space Debris Mitigation Policy and Requirements were updated in 2023, introducing stricter mitigation measures.

 

As ESA’s Technical Authority on Space Debris Mitigation, the Independent Safety Office is involved in the review of the space debris mitigation strategies for all missions at ESA. Therefore, we can evaluate the adoption of the requirements and the alignment of ESA projects with the ambitious Zero Debris goals. For each review, we prepare a detailed assessment of the status of compliance and issue recommendations to the projects on how to improve the safety and sustainability of their missions. With the introduction of the ‘Zero Debris Approach’, we have modernised such compliance analysis, with four objectives:

  1. highlight driving requirements for different classes of missions;
  2. improve traceability of the recommendations to the missions;
  3. inform policy makers on the most critical requirements that require technology developments;
  4. evaluate options for the evolution of the requirements in 2030.

 

As an intern, you will contribute to the evolution of a suite of digital tools, in Python, to reach such objectives by leveraging  the extensive dataset of reviews conducted by our team. Thanks to the database built in the previous step, you will assess the feasibility of automating the monitoring of the space debris environment impact of the ESA fleet and of ESA projects, with the objective of developing an informative dashboard on the space debris risk profile of ESA projects.

 

As an intern, you will also support the work on the evolution of the requirements considering:

  • trends in compliance as extracted from the computational pipeline above;
  • lessons learnt from ESA research and development activities related to Zero Debris;
  • emerging interest in sustainability initiatives in lunar orbit;
  • initiatives on space debris mitigation on-going beyond ESA;
  • formulation of future scenarios incorporating technology roadmaps (e.g. ESA Vision 2040) and other technology breakthroughs.

 

In performing your work, you will have the occasion to acquire:

  • a multi-disciplinary, system perspective on how to tackle the space debris issue;
  • hands-on experience in the use of ESA’s tools and data resources;
  • familiarity with emerging concepts in the field of space sustainability.

 

You will also be exposed to agile approaches for software development and involved in relevant tasks related to the normal work of the office.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Familiarity and proven experience with Python is an asset.

Title: Intern in the Electrical Department - Microelectronics Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Avionics and EEE Division plays a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability and advancement of spacecraft avionics and component technologies. Its mission spans design assurance, qualification, and testing of EEE components, as well as radiation hardness assurance for space systems in its domain of responsibility. The division operates specialised laboratories and provides expertise to ESA projects, industry, and research partners. It actively disseminates knowledge through internal and external training, conference participation, and tutoring of PhD students, ESA Graduate Trainees (EGTs), and National Trainees, fostering innovation and professional growth.

 

Components
The Section is responsible for ensuring that all EEEE Components (passive & active) flown on ESA missions are suitable for their application and the environment for which they are intended, lead the development of EEEE Components and their qualification. European Space Component Coordination (ESCC) executives and actively supporting European Cooperation for Space Standardisation (ECSS) standardisation activities. The section conducts Research and Development (R&D) activities in their domain of responsibility. 


Radiation & Component Reliability
The Section is responsible for assessing all aspects of EEEE Component Radiation Effects to ensure EEEE Components flown on ESA Missions are suitable for the Radiation Environment and their assigned application for the duration of the mission. It is also responsible for all EEEE Component laboratory Test and Analysis activities. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the EEEE Component Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ESCC/ECSS standardisation activities.

 

Microelectronics 
The section is responsible for development and verification of all Microelectronic devices flown on ESA missions such as AI Accelerators, FPGAs, ASICs, Microprocessors, microelectronic processes, Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), radiation-aware design, prototyping and test for space‑grade microelectronics. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the Microelectronics Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ECSS standardisation activities.

 

Avionic Architecture 
Responsible for supporting all ESA missions in the area of Avionics Sub-System development, their verification and validation, and their qualification within the framework of the agency's strategic objectives. 

 

Data Handling
Responsible for on-board data handling sub-systems (Platform and Payload). Responsible for developing and qualifying equipment for data acquisition, processing, and distribution (buses, interfaces, mass‑memory, data‑processing chains, remote interface units, etc.). on-Board data processing is an important focus of the section including development of turn-key AI HW solutions for ESA Missions. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the Data Handling Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ECSS/CCSDS standardisation activities.

 

Flight Software
This section designs and maintains flight software for spacecraft control and payload management. It addresses real-time operating systems, fault detection and recovery, and software validation frameworks. The team also explores advanced concepts such as AI-assisted on-board processing, ensuring adaptability and resilience in increasingly complex missions. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the Flight Software Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ECSS/CCSDS standardisation activities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Smarter Verification for Space Systems: Evaluating AI Approaches for FPGA Design Validation

 

The increasing complexity of FPGA and ASIC developments for space applications makes digital design verification one of the most resource-intensive phases of the development cycle. At the same time, recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), offer new opportunities to automate verification activities and improve engineering productivity.

 

This internship will investigate the applicability of AI tools to support the verification of digital designs used in future space systems. The work will evaluate how AI can assist engineers in creating and maintaining verification environments using modern frameworks such as UVVM and cocotb. Representative case studies may include RISC-V processors, communication interfaces, digital signal-processing functions, and hardware accelerators.

 

The study will compare traditional and AI-assisted verification approaches, focusing on tasks such as testbench generation, test creation, debugging, coverage analysis, and documentation. Particular attention will be given to the trade-offs between UVVM's VHDL-based methodology and cocotb's Python-based flexibility. The outcome will be a set of recommendations for the adoption of AI-assisted verification techniques in future ESA microelectronics developments.

 

2) Topic 2: Towards fast FPGA Demonstrators: AI-Assisted IP Integration and Automated System Assembly for ESA Microelectronics

 

ESA and European developments have produced a growing portfolio of reusable FPGA and ASIC Intellectual Property (IP) cores. However, integrating these assets into complete systems often requires significant manual effort, limiting reuse and increasing development time.

 

This internship will investigate how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can support the integration and reuse of digital IP cores for FPGA-based demonstrators. The work will explore how AI can help engineers understand IP capabilities, identify compatible interfaces, generate integration artefacts, propose system architectures, detect integration issues, and produce technical documentation.

 

Particular attention will be given to the role of machine-readable IP descriptions, including the feasibility of using standards such as IP-XACT and tools such as Kactus2 to enable AI-assisted design assembly. Representative case studies may include communication interfaces, processor subsystems, digital signal-processing functions, and other ESA-developed IP blocks; with special focus on European FPGAs design flows.

 

The resulting workflows will be evaluated through the creation and deployment of FPGA demonstrators on the TEC-EDM FPGA Farm. The outcome will be recommendations for future ESA digital engineering practices, enabling faster IP reuse, automated demonstrator generation, and more efficient validation of microelectronics developments.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Electrical Department - AOCS and Pointing Architecture Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Attitude and Orbit Control System (AOCS) & Pointing Architecture Section provides functional support to ESA projects in the technical field of AOCS & pointing systems for ESA missions on the following applicative directorates: Earth Observation, Science, Resilience, Navigation & Connectivity.
 
The AOCS & Pointing Architecture Section carries out technological research, harmonisation and standardisation in the field of AOCS and Pointing systems, with a focus on subsystem competitiveness, and innovation for performance, robustness and process improvements.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an intern in the AOCS & Pointing Architecture Section, you will develop an AOCS & pointing performance assessment tool and its time-domain simulator with a robust tuning pipeline to enable early mission feasibility assessment and architecture trade-offs. 

 

The objectives are:

  • to model and document the main performance drivers with focus on gyroless architectures and Star Tracker accommodation (including fusion of non-orthogonal Star tracker Optical Heads, dynamic-stellar estimator, and tachometer-stellar estimator);
  • to consolidate the controller tuning optimisation (already implemented in the tool) with robust control synthesis & analysis for further optimised performance, with a generic design & tuning pipeline and the documentation of the process (including of the comparison with respect to the initial optimised tuning);
  • to consolidate the architecture trade-off capacities (already implemented in the tool) by performing and documenting systematic performance evaluations over sets of Hardware suites (sensors and actuators) for architecture trade-offs, for different missions;
  • to consolidate the early micro-vibrations impact assessment (already implemented in the tool) with improved Reaction Wheel disturbance spectrum (waterfall plots catalogue) & high frequency dynamics envelope and the documentation of the models & process (how to set the dynamics envelope without a full satellite Finite Element Model);
  • to consolidate the verification & validation of the tool & simulator with built-in verification tests and documentation;
  • to consolidate the tool & simulator documentation, with a user manual & hands-on training (setting of the tool, configuration for a new satellite mission, running early performance assessment and performing architecture trade-offs, controller optimised tuning, and running consolidated performance assessment with further improved robust tuning).

 

This updated version of our tool will be used for early definition of future Earth Observation and Science missions during the internship.

Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Thermal Analysis and Verification Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Thermal Analysis and Verification Section (TEC-MTV): The section is responsible for providing the means of analysis and verification, and for performing predevelopment and verification tests in the field of thermal environment and mechanical systems. It is the centre of competence within the Agency for thermal analysis tools and verification, including testing. The Section is also responsible for the maintenance and operation of the Division’s technical infrastructure.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Space Thermal Analysis and Verification, covering one or several of the activities below:

 

  1. Mechanical Systems Laboratory: Participation in the testing activities of the laboratory including evaluation of test data. Participate in the development and acceptance of new test facilities, e.g. thermal cycling, Coefficient of Thermal Expansion;
  2. Thermal Analysis methods: Research and development in the area of computational methods for space thermal analysis or multi-disciplinary analysis e.g.:
    a. methods and tools for exchange of thermal analysis data with other disciplines such as structures (e.g. development of SINAS);
    b. co-simulation of thermal analysis models with other domains such as power or fluidics;
    c. next generation methods for radiative, fluidic or thermal analysis.
  3. Analysis methods in support of testing activities: real time model correlation or identification of discrepancies between model and test data, analysis methods for new test instrumentation such as infra-red cameras, data fusion of thermal analysis and test data, modelling of gas convection for cleanroom testing;
  4. Thermal Analysis: Perform thermal analyses, including steady state/transient analyses of instrument and satellites following familiarisation with project requirements and Agency’s tools (ESATAN-TMS). This may also include in-flight correlation of thermal analysis models for ESA projects. This task is often carried out in collaboration with the Thermal Control Section (responsible for design aspects).

Title: Intern in the Elecrical Department - Space Environments and Effects Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Space Environments and Effects Section (TEC-EPS) supports the development of ESA missions and programmes by investigating the space environments within which they will operate, assessing likely effects and defining mitigation methods. Environments addressed include high-energy radiation from radiation belts; solar particle events and cosmic rays; plasmas encountered in planetary magnetospheres; the solar wind and artificially generated charges and fields on spacecraft; micro-meteoroids and non trackable debris; planetary and lunar dust; and planetary atmospheres. The Section also initiates and manages a wide range of related modelling, software and hardware R&D activities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

With an increasing worldwide interest in Lunar Exploration, ESA is engaged in the study of several surface missions, including major undertakings such as the Argonaut mission and the deployment of surface payloads, planned to operate from 2030 on. In this context, mission preparation relies on meaningful evaluation of the detrimental effects of the near surface environment on surface assets, as well as impact on payloads response, including near surface plasma and lunar dust.

The internship will focus on supporting the team work on numerical modelling of the variability of near surface environments (plasma, transported dust and regolith behavior) along the Lunar orbit and their interactions with systems of interest, in the context of missions currently under study. You are expected to learn the basic physics associated with the processes at play and run simulations using state-of-the-art diagnostic software tools used in the Agency, Academia and Industry. Applicability of the approach is expected to be generalised to other airless bodies of interest for ESA science and exploration programmes.

Title: Intern in the Quality Department - RAMS Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of the Director of Technology, Engineering and Quality, the Head of the Quality Department is responsible for the establishment and implementation of the ESA policy, requirements, and standards with respect to quality. TEC-Q is responsible for the provision of required expertise and support services to ESA projects, support Directorates and research activities in the Product Assurance and Safety disciplines, applied to all elements of space systems (ground and on-board), including hardware, software, and humans. Product Assurance and Safety disciplines comprise Product Assurance management, technical risk management, reliability, availability, maintainability, safety, quality assurance, with support from the other TEC engineering Departments, expertise, and laboratories.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

The Probabilistic Risk Assessment (PRA) is a systematic and exhaustive methodology for qualitative and quantitative assessment of risks in complex space systems. It estimates the probability of major undesired outcomes such as Loss of Mission (LOM) and Loss of Crew (LOC), providing quantitative, traceable risk metrics to support design and Programme-level decisions.

 

ESA needs to develop its own PRA methodology. At present, no dedicated ESA/ECSS standard or handbook defines PRA principles, processes, or implementation guidance. Current PRA activities rely primarily on external standards and project-specific approaches, creating a risk of inconsistencies in modelling assumptions, analysis scope, and interfaces with Reliability, Availability, Maintainability and Safety (RAMS) activities.

 

As ESA increases its independent application of PRA for future ESA-led missions, the need for harmonised guidance becomes increasingly important. Establishing an ESA PRA methodology would promote consistency across projects and provide a solid foundation for an integrated RAMS framework, encompassing FMEA, Reliability and Availability Analyses, Hazard Analyses, and Fault Tree Analyses.

 

The main objectives of this initiative are to:

  • collect and review documentation, standards, guidance material, and software tools related to PRA methodologies used by other space agencies and organisations, including NASA;
  • analyse the collected material and produce a comprehensive assessment of existing methodologies, tools, requirements, best practices, and lessons learnt, identifying gaps, challenges, and key elements that should be addressed in the early stages of developing an ESA PRA methodology;
  • provide recommendations for the definition of a harmonised ESA PRA framework and its integration within the broader Dependability and Safety engineering processes.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You must have knowledge of risk assessment. Familiarity with Fault Tree Analysis and Reliability Analysis, as well as knowledge of Space Systems would be an asset. 

 

You must have good interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to work in a multi-cultural environment, both independently and as part of a team. You must also be thorough and meticulous.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Space Safety Programme - Mission Implementation Division (RISE)
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The ESA Space Safety Department takes care of all potential hazards and threats from space or in space, which can impact human activities, infrastructure, or related applications. The spectrum of tasks ranges from gathering the basic understanding of space hazards originating from our Sun, from human space debris, or from asteroids potentially colliding with the Earth. It also addresses basic approaches to mitigate these hazards and to implement space systems end-to-end in a sustainable and eco-compatible way. Moreover, several corner stone missions are underway to demonstrate basic methods of space weather forecasting, asteroid deflection and active space debris removal from orbit. 

 

In execution of these tasks, the Space Safety Department has the following entities: 

  • Mission Implementation Division (OPS-SM); 
  • COSMIC Project Management Office (OPS-SC); 
  • Space Weather Office (OPS-SW);
  • Planetary Defence Office (OPS-SP); 
  • Space Debris Office (OPS-SD); 
  • Clean Space & Circular Economy Office (OPS-SY); 
  • Frequency Management Office (OPS-SF);
  • Programme Coordination Office (OPS-SX). 

 

Within the Space Safety Missions Implementation Division, you will operate in a dynamic, international environment where new mission concepts become real spacecraft and you will contribute to missions in their detailed design, development, integration and operational preparation phases (Phase B2/C/D). The focus is on active debris removal and in-orbit servicing—two fast-growing fields that are redefining how spacecraft are maintained and how crowded orbits are managed. 

 

These missions develop and demonstrate technologies for rendezvous, inspection, capture, life extension, relocation, de-orbiting and repair. You will collaborate with experienced ESA specialists and innovative European companies, gaining a close-up view of both cutting-edge engineering and the emerging commercial market for sustainable space services. 

 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​RISE: Help prepare an ambitious in-orbit servicing mission that will autonomously rendezvous with and capture an active satellite in geostationary orbit. The spacecraft will temporarily take over the satellite’s attitude and orbit control before moving on to service its first commercial customer—demonstrating how satellite life can be extended in practice. 

​  

​Throughout the internship, you will learn how a complex space mission is developed end to end, how systems engineers turn mission goals into coherent technical solutions, and how multidisciplinary teams make decisions under real programme constraints. You will strengthen your ability to communicate technical information clearly, work collaboratively and apply system thinking to an operational space project. 

​ 

​This is an opportunity to make a visible contribution to a real mission while learning from experts at the forefront of sustainable spaceflight.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You will thrive in this internship if you are curious about debris removal and in-orbit servicing, enjoy working with others and are ready to take initiative. We welcome students who are eager to learn, ask thoughtful questions and contribute ideas. 

A background in space systems engineering would be an asset, but enthusiasm for complex space missions and a strong willingness to learn are equally important. 

Due to the nature of the post, a commitment of six months is preferred, depending on the candidate’s availability. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Quality Department - Software Product Assurance Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Software Product Assurance Section provides support to ESA programmes and missions ensuring that software related requirements defined in the missions baseline are met. The Section ensures that appropriate processes, methods and tools used for software development are deployed through the entire development lifecycle. 

 

The Section also offers services for software product evaluation for conformity, software safety and dependability and software process assessment.

 

The team in ESTEC consists of 14 people supporting the Software Product Assurance activities for projects across multiple domains, including Science, Human and Robotic Exploration and Earth Observation.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

This topic of the internship is to update the knowledge base and training material from the Software Product Assurance section, including the internal wiki page. The knowledge base defining key aspects used by our team for our day-to-day activities needs to be updated based on new standards and feedback from the team. The section offers training courses to a variety of audiences. The training material needs to be updated to reflect the new activities in the domain and to adapt it to the new format.

 

Learning objective: Overall knowledge about the Software Product Assurance domain for space missions, based on the proposed activity.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Background in software engineering or computer science is essential. 
Knowledge about software standards and tools is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Galileo and EGNOS Programme Department - System Engineering Section
description_html:
Location
EGNOS Project Office, Toulouse, France

Our team and mission

The EGNOS and SBAS Programme Division is responsible for the development of the EGNOS system and its qualification, in its role as Design and Procurement Agent, under the programme management of the European Commission (EC). Version 3 of the EGNOS system is currently under development and qualification.

The Division is also managing several research and development activities under the Horizon Europe and NAVISP Programmes and is supporting ASECNA in the procurement of the African SBAS.

 

The System Engineering Section of the GNSS Regional Augmentation System Division is responsible, in particular, for the following activities: 

 

  • ensuring the compliance of the system design with upper-level requirements (Mission & Performance, security, operations);
  • developing and maintaining system engineering tools and associated databases;
  • managing the corresponding industrial activities and ensuring that system engineering activities are performed according to agreed development plans, in compliance with the applicable system requirements, standards and system engineering requirements.

 

The Security Service of the EGNOS and SBAS Programme Division is responsible, in particular, for the following activities: 

 

  • establishing and maintaining the security baseline and security requirements for all releases procured by ESA;
  • identifying and managing security issues;
  • preparing security accreditation files for the ground segment;
  • managing security activities within the EGNOS Project Office.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

The EGNOS V3 System is composed of 39 Remote reference stations, 2 Main Control Centres (hosting in particular the central processing facilities) and 6 Uplink Stations connected to 3 EGNOS geostationary satellites, all interconnected through a dedicated real-time wide-area network.
EGNOS V3 design is the result of a complex multidisciplinary exercise implementing stringent performance, safety, security and operability requirements across several interconnected subsystems.

 

Based on this first EGNOS V3 version, an enhanced engineering approach is being implemented for the definition of EGNOS evolutions, typically including:

 

  • enhanced modularity of the system design through a system-of-segments approach;
  • parallel engineering of evolutions across different EGNOS system releases;
  • multidisciplinary consolidation within and across segments;
  • interactive incremental validation and report generation using AI.

 

You will be integrated into the System Engineering Section of the EGNOS and SBAS Division and will interact closely with the Security Service. You will also interact with other teams/disciplines (Product and Safety, Development and IVQ, Operations). You will develop, integrate and validate an EGNOS Engineering ToolKit aimig at demonstrating and providing an initial engineering capability in an integrated and shared environment including:

 

  • a requirements engineering COTS tool;
  • a Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) COTS tool;
  • upgrading Internal AI agents and tools from previous activities to provide engineering support capabilities exploiting the current document-centric engineering approach (engineering artefact consistency checks, cybersecurity analysis, vulnerability and security patch identification, etc.) and extending these capabilities to cover standard security inventories;
  • import/export functionalities to interface with external stakeholders.

 

To this goal, you will:

 

  • consolidate the System Engineering Team and Security Team user needs;
  • analyse available technical documentation and identify relevant information; 
  • select and justify the choice of OSS/COTS tools complementing the current selected System Engineering tools;
  • design, develop, integrate and validate the EGNOS Engineering ToolKit;
  • demonstrate the capability of the EGNOS Engineering ToolKit to conduct security and system engineering activities;
  • document the user manual.


At the end of the internship, you will have contributed to an AI-assisted proof of concept demonstrating the capability to support security and system engineering activities.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

  • software engineering with AI Agent;
  • cloud computing;
  • system Engineering tools and processes.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Digital, Data and Information Technology Department - Data and Apps Factory
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

You would join the Data & Apps Factory team, part of the Data & AI Office, working on the ESA Data Factory: the data platform that powers data-driven decisions and the integration of artificial intelligence across the organisation. Our mission is to make the organisation's data discoverable, trustworthy and ready for use by both people and intelligent systems. 

 

Alongside the core platform, we are building new initiatives that extend it beyond traditional structured data: a store that makes the knowledge held in written documents readable by intelligent systems and a context layer that captures the relationships and meaning between different data sources. You would be part of a collaborative, curious environment, contributing to real, ongoing activities and seeing your results used across the organisation. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​As an intern, you would collaborate with experienced colleagues on innovative topics within the data platform, contributing to real, ongoing activities. Your tasks may include: 

​ 

  • ​contributing to the development of a store that makes the knowledge held in written documents readable by intelligent systems, with the correct access controls; 
  • ​helping to build the context layer that captures the relationships and meaning between different data sources; 
  • ​supporting the design and development of the interfaces through which colleagues explore and understand the organisation's data; 
  • ​exploring and testing new tools and techniques in applied artificial intelligence related to data systems;
  • ​documenting approaches so they can be understood and reused by others. 

​ 

​Through this internship, you would: 

​ 

  • ​gain hands-on experience of how a modern data platform is designed and operated; 
  • ​develop practical skills in applied artificial intelligence, including how written information is made usable by intelligent systems; 
  • ​learn how meaning, relationships and access control are applied to data in a complex organisation; 
  • ​strengthen your ability to document and communicate technical information clearly.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in data systems and applied artificial intelligence is an asset. 

It is also useful if you have experience in the following areas, including through university or school projects: 

 

  • databases and structured data; 
  • cloud services, particularly Microsoft Azure, or on-premise environments such as virtual machines; 
  • vector stores or retrieval-based systems that make documents usable by intelligent systems; 
  • programming, data handling, or building small applications or interfaces; 
  • a general interest in applied artificial intelligence and how it is used with real data. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - ExoMars Time Correlation Evolution Data Analysis
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

The Mars Orbiting Mission Operations Unit (OPS-OPM) is a team of 10 engineers responsible for the operations of the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter and the Mars Express spacecraft in-orbit around Mars. This includes monitoring, control and mission planning of the spacecrafts and related ground systems (e.g. data systems, ground stations). 

 

For more information about Mars Express operations: https://www.esa.int/Enabling_Support/Operations/Mars_Express_operations

 

For more information about ExoMars/TGO operations: https://www.esa.int/Enabling_Support/Operations/ExoMars_TGO_operations

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​You will report to the Head of the Mars Orbiting Missions Operations Unit. While integrated in the Trace Gas Orbiter and Mars Express Flight Control Team, your primary activity will be data analysis. 

 

​ExoMars observes variations in its time correlation evolution. Sometimes the “spacecraft clock value to [UTC] ground time correlation” is stable for weeks while at other times the correlation drifts quickly out of limits within a few days.  

 

​Since the time correlation can be influenced by many factors (temperature, orbital geometry, one-way-light-time, ground station clock stability, etc) you shall analyse what exactly causes the observed variations in the time correlation evolution.  

 

​You will collaborate closely with the Flight Control Team (FCT) operating spacecraft at Mars and gain an understanding of interplanetary spacecraft operation. In dialogue with the FCT, you will learn how time correlation is performed and how deviations influence spacecraft operations.  

​ 

​The learning objective is to get familiar with spacecraft operations, tools for data analysis, visualisation and interpretation of the results. 

​ 

​Other analysis projects related to the shadowing of the Mars Express solar panels and its influence on energy production might be assigned if time allows.​ 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should be proficient in data analysis. 

Experience in programming/scripting in Python would be an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Title: Intern in the Lunar Science Office - Landing Site Assessment for Future Robotic Exploration Missions
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Within the Exploration Science Office, the Lunar Science Office Team (HRE-SL) is responsible for scientific activities at the Moon in ESA’s Human and Robotic Exploration Directorate.  

​ 

​These activities emphasise:

  • ​understanding lunar resources and their potential for the future;
  • ​understanding the lunar environment, its effects on human activities and the impact of human activities on the environment;
  • ​preparing for future habitation at the Moon;
  • ​working with other teams to support research into crew health and performance;
  • ​preparing opportunities to utilise the Moon as a unique location for scientific research and an archive of Solar System history.

​ 

​The team provides expert support to projects in areas relating to landing sites and the lunar environment and how these affect exploration missions.  

​ 

​Our activities operate across the missions and platforms of ESA, international partners, and new commercial actors.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

The Lunar Science Office at the European Space Agency's European Space Research and Technology Centre in Noordwijk, the Netherlands, is offering an internship opportunity focused on the assessment of candidate landing sites for future robotic exploration missions to the Moon. The work will support ongoing activities related to the PROSPECT mission, which aims to investigate water and other volatile materials near the lunar poles, and Argonaut, Europe's lunar lander programme. These activities contribute to the preparation of future scientific and exploration missions on the lunar surface. 

 

During this internship, you will contribute to the characterization of potential landing sites and surface operations areas through the analysis of lunar remote sensing data and terrain information. You will work with a variety of datasets to identify and assess landing and mobility hazards, investigate geological and geomorphological features, and support mission planning activities. 

 

Depending on your background and interests, your work may include:

  • identification and mapping of landing hazards such as impact craters, boulders, steep slopes, and rough terrain;
  • geological and geomorphological mapping of candidate exploration regions;
  • analysis and interpretation of lunar remote sensing datasets;
  • surface mobility studies and rover traverse planning using Geographic Information System software;
  • development of machine learning or deep learning approaches for automated feature detection and classification;
  • numerical modelling of surface conditions relevant to landing site safety and mission operations;
  • support to the generation of scientific and operational products used in mission planning and decision making. 

 

Through this internship, you will:

  • gain an understanding of lunar geology and the processes that have shaped the lunar surface;
  • become familiar with lunar remote sensing datasets and planetary mapping techniques;
  • learn methods for detecting and characterising surface features such as craters, boulders, and roughness elements;
  • develop practical experience with Geographic Information System tools for planetary exploration applications;
  • acquire skills in scientific data analysis, machine learning, or numerical modelling, depending on the selected project;
  • understand how scientific observations are translated into mission requirements and operational constraints for robotic exploration missions;
  • gain first-hand experience within an international space mission environment and contribute to activities supporting future European lunar exploration. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Priority will be given to candidates pursuing a degree in planetary science, geology, geophysics, remote sensing, geography, physics, computer science, aerospace engineering, or a related field. Experience with data analysis, programming, machine learning, numerical modelling, or Geographic Information System software would be an advantage.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.
