Title: Intern in the Utilisation and Enabled Science Team - ACES Data Analysis Support
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

​​Within the European Space Agency (ESA)’s Directorate for Human and Robotic Exploration, the Exploration Science activities are a cornerstone of the Explore2040 strategy, driving innovation at the intersection of human exploration and scientific discovery. HRE-SU (Utilisation and Enabled Science) team at ESA coordinates the Agency’s research activities in physical sciences and biology under microgravity conditions and for space exploration. Using platforms like the International Space Station, as well as Moon and Mars missions, the team supports a wide range of cutting-edge research—from Earth atmospheric studies and quantum sensors to heat transfer phenomena, soft matter, and advanced materials processing. 

​​ 

Launched in April 2025, Atomic Clock Ensemble in Space (ACES) is a flagship mission of the HRE Directorate dedicated to fundamental physics using high stability and accuracy atomic clocks in the microgravity environment of the International Space Station.  

 

At ESA-ESTEC, the ACES team supports mission operations, monitors the performance of the on-board clocks and links and contributes to data analysis. The ESA-ESTEC data analysis pipeline processes ACES microwave link (MWL) measurements and is used alongside the Paris Observatory pipeline to validate space-to-ground desynchronisation measurements.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​You will join the ACES team at ESA-ESTEC and support the analysis of MicroWave Link MWL measurements, which are central to the mission’s high-precision comparisons between space-based and ground-based clocks. 

​ 

​MWL is a two-way, three-frequency system, with uplink and downlink signals in the Ku-band and a downlink signal in the S-band. It provides pseudorange measurements at all three frequencies using both code and carrier phase. Before the desynchronisation between the space and ground clocks can be evaluated, these measurements must be corrected for signal-propagation delays, including link asymmetries, tropospheric and ionospheric delays and antenna phase patterns, as well as instrumental effects such as amplitude-to-phase conversion, temperature variations, Doppler rate and tracking-loop errors. 

​ 

​On Earth, a network of MWL ground terminals connects some of the world’s best clocks to the space clock, including clocks operated at NIST and JPL in the United States, LTE in France, PTB and Wettzell in Germany, NPL in the United Kingdom and NICT in Japan. 

​ 

​Desynchronisation measurements are the main data product of the ACES mission. They support tests of general relativity, searches for dark matter and differential geopotential measurements between ground clocks. 

​ 

​During the internship, you will contribute to the following activities: 

  • ​cross-check and validate corrections for signal propagation delays;
  • ​improve the modelling and the calibration of instrumental effects, including amplitude-to-phase conversion, temperature variations, Doppler rate and tracking-loop errors;
  • ​improve carrier cycle ambiguity resolution using code phase measurements;
  • ​help improve the existing data analysis pipeline by optimising selected processes;
  • ​use space-to-ground desynchronisation measurements to support ACES science in one or more of the following areas:​
    • tests of general relativity, including gravitational redshift, time variation of fundamental constants and dark-matter searches;
    • ​comparison of ground clocks;
    • ​clock synchronisation and time-transfer experiments;
    • ​differential geopotential measurements between ground clocks. 

​ 

​These activities will strengthen your background in: 

  • ​data analysis and processing of highly stable time and frequency signals;
  • ​stability and accuracy characterisation of high-performance space clocks and links;
  • ​clock comparison and time transfer experiments;
  • ​general relativity and alternative theories of gravitation;
  • ​chronometric geodesy.

 

​You will work in a stimulating, multicultural environment that brings together space agencies, mission operations centres, industry, scientific institutes and academia. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in orbital mechanics, time and frequency metrology, data analysis and general relativity is an asset.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Software and Artificial Intelligence Team - Data Management and AI Readiness
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

​HRE-FI mission is to advance digital and AI-driven capabilities for human and robotic exploration across all destinations, from low Earth orbit to Mars. Its activities focus on four pillars: Artificial Intelligence, Extended Reality, IoT & Robotics, and Quantum Technologies, supported by robust data governance. Key initiatives include AI-enabled mission planning, immersive XR training, predictive maintenance, and digital continuity. The environment is highly collaborative, combining ESA experts, industry partners, and research institutions, fostering innovation through labs and pilot projects. HRE-FI operates within a dynamic, multidisciplinary setting, integrating cutting-edge technologies to enhance operational efficiency, astronaut support, and future mission readiness.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Under the supervision of the HRE Data Lab Lead, you will: 

  • ​perform exploratory data analysis and metadata tagging on heterogeneous datasets from past and current missions (e.g. spacecraft telemetry, experiment results, technical reports, 3D models);
  • ​support the cataloguing and profiling of data assets, identifying how they are structured, where they are stored, and how they can be accessed;
  • ​help design a data categorisation and governance model, aligned with international standards such as FAIR principles;
  • ​contribute to the development of automated workflows for metadata enrichment and data organisation;
  • ​assess the potential of datasets for future AI/ML exploitation and digital twin applications;
  • ​support the implementation of recommendations from ESA’s ongoing AI study, particularly those related to data infrastructure and readiness;
  • ​collaborate with colleagues across engineering, science, and IT to ensure consistency and avoid duplication;
  • ​(optional stretch task) develop small prototypes (e.g. scripts for automatic tagging, clustering, or text search) to demonstrate how data could be prepared for AI. 

​ 

​Learning Outcomes 

​During this internship you will: 

  • ​gain insight into space mission data and documentation and the challenges of managing them;
  • ​acquire hands-on experience in data wrangling, metadata design, and governance;
  • ​learn how to prepare real datasets for AI/ML training, analytics, and simulation workflows;
  • ​understand the role of data engineering in enabling digital twins, AI agents, and decision support;
  • ​work in an international and interdisciplinary team, engaging with experts in engineering, science, and IT. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in data science, data management standards, computer science, information engineering, or a related field is an asset.

Experience with Python (pandas, numpy, Jupyter), SQL, or similar data handling tools is an asset. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. Title: Intern in the Vulcan Team
description_html:
Location
ECSAT, Harwell, United Kingdom  

Due to the location of ECSAT and current UK legislation, only UK citizens, students enrolled in a UK university, or those with pre-settled status (right to study) in the UK are eligible to apply for this internship.

Our team and mission

The Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration (D/HRE) is the main ESA entity in charge of supporting and coordinating efforts towards the current and future endeavours of human spaceflight and robotic exploration. The exploration activities are part of the strategic plans in securing a central role for Europe with respect to the global initiatives. The strategy includes three destinations where humans will work with robots to gather new knowledge: Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the Moon, and Mars. 

​ 

​The Vulcan Analogue Sample Facility is uniquely positioned within D/HRE’s Exploration Preparation, Research and Technology (ExPeRT) team to support long-term Lunar and Martian Surface Exploration by developing operational concepts and low TRL technologies. The Vulcan team provides expert support (on analogue sample topics) to research and technology development projects (focused on space exploration and planetary science applications) within ESA, its Member States, and the rest of Europe. 

​ 

​The Vulcan Facility is a geological repository and analytical laboratory operated by a multidisciplinary, onsite team of staff and contractors. It is located on the Harwell Campus in the UK (part of ESA’s ECSAT site) and serves as a European focal point for the research, curation, and characterisation of analogue samples. The facility acts to: 

  • ​support validation and de-risking of low TRL technologies & key operational concepts; 
  • ​improve confidence in European simulants; 
  • ​inspire the next generation of planetary geoscientists. 

 

For more information on the VULCAN Analogue Sample Facility, please look at its website.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Planetary & Material science 

 

​​Research activities focus on analogue samples and related technologies through collaboration with other ESA teams (primarily Spaceship ECSAT). They include:

  • ​new, customised analogue sample recipes for present and future missions:  
    • ​low-medium fidelity simulants for a range of target planetary bodies and sites; 
    • ​high fidelity, mechanical simulants for a range of engineering and geotechnical applications e.g. plume surface interaction, dust interaction, mitigation, and contamination testing; 
    • ​high fidelity, ISRU simulants focused on resource extraction and additive manufacturing test purposes; 
    • ​investigation of artificial (i.e. non-geological) simulant components e.g. simulated agglutinates.
  • ​adapted techniques for advanced characterisation of the physical, mechanical, mineralogical, and chemical properties of analogue samples. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in Planetary Science or Geoscience is required. Knowledge in coding languages, geotechnical engineering, and materials processing is an asset.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Aerothermodynamics and Flight Vehicles Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Aerothermodynamics and Flight Vehicles Engineering Section is part of ESA’s Propulsion, Aerothermodynamics and Flight Vehicles Engineering Division in the Directorate of Technology, Engineering and Quality.

 

The Aerothermodynamics and Flight Vehicles Engineering Section provides expertise and functional support to ESA projects and carries out technology research and development on fluid mechanics, aero(thermos)dynamics, fluidic engineering and flight physics. The Section is also the focal point for the architecture design, analysis and technical assessment of flight vehicles, including suborbital, (re-)entry, space transportation and exploration vehicles

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Understanding and predicting the behaviour of highly rarefied plumes, such as those created by electric propulsion thrusters, is important for assessing their interaction with spacecraft surfaces and instruments, as well as for distinguishing vacuum facility effects on thrusters’ performance. The modelling of such plumes presents a challenging fluid mechanics problem, combining rarefied gas dynamics, plasma physics, surface interactions and the influence of the surrounding environment.

 

This internship will provide an opportunity to apply and improve numerical modelling tools of the Section to simulate and analyse plasma plumes and their interaction with ESA's Electric Propulsion Laboratory (EPL) vacuum facilities. Experimental measurements from tests in EPL will be used as a reference dataset to investigate these phenomena and to improve the understanding of plume behaviour in both flight-like and ground-test conditions.

 

During this internship, you will:

  • analyse experimental measurements of a rarefied thruster plume obtained in a vacuum test facility;
  • develop and/or improve numerical models to reconstruct and simulate plume expansion and flow-field characteristics;
  • investigate the influence of vacuum-facility boundaries (background pressure, chamber size, pumping speed and walls interactions) and test conditions on the measured plume behaviour;
  • compare numerical predictions with experimental data and assess the validity and limitations of different modelling approaches;
  • explore simplified system-level models to understand how operating conditions influence plume characteristics and flow behaviour.

 

This internship will provide hands-on experience in rarefied flow modelling, computational fluid mechanics, experimental data analysis and model validation, while developing your understanding of how advanced numerical methods can be applied to complex spacecraft engineering problems.

 

Close collaboration with ESA’s Electric Propulsion Section is foreseen during the execution of the internship, in support of the analysis and comparison with experimental test results.

Behavioural competencies

Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

Education

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Experience with scientific programming in Fortran or C++ is an asset.
Knowledge and background in numerical modelling using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) or Particle-in-Cell (PIC) is an asset.

Title: Intern in the Space Safety Programme - Planetary Defence Office - Assessing Flyeye Telescope Survey
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

The ESA Space Safety Department takes care of all potential hazards and threats from space or in space, which can impact human activities, infrastructure, or related applications. The spectrum of tasks ranges from gathering the basic understanding of space hazards originating from our Sun, from human space debris, or from asteroids potentially colliding with the Earth. It also addresses basic approaches to mitigate these hazards and to implement space systems end-to-end in a sustainable and eco-compatible way. Moreover, several corner stone missions are underway to demonstrate basic methods of space weather forecasting, asteroid deflection and active space debris removal from orbit.

 

In execution of these tasks, the Space Safety Department has the following entities:

  • Mission Implementation Division (OPS-SM);
  • COSMIC Project Management Office (OPS-SC);
  • Space Weather Office (OPS-SW);
  • Planetary Defence Office (OPS-SP);
  • Space Debris Office (OPS-SD);
  • Clean Space & Circular Economy Office (OPS-SY);
  • Frequency Management Office (OPS-SF);
  • Programme Coordination Office (OPS-SX).

 

The Planetary Defence Office (PDO) is addressing the “…prediction and detection [of] the potential impact of a near-Earth object”. Concerning the information needs for NEO monitoring, the following are defined:

  • knowledge of the current and future positions of all NEO objects above a given size threshold or risk level, in particular their minimum fly-by distance to the Earth and time of this event;
  • maintain awareness of collision risks with the Earth;
  • access to verifiable, dependable, timely data with integrity and known accuracy. 

 

The top-level Office tasks are: 
1. Issue NEO impact warnings and news releases. 
2. Provide direct access to data in the NEO database. 
3. Provide access to data in the NEO database available only via registration. 
4. Perform additional observations. 
5. Provide high priority information. 
6. Provide educational and outreach material. 
7. Provide user tools. 

 

The PDO is structured along three vertical pillars differentiating following activity area:

  • observation;
  • information provision;
  • mitigation.


You can see following domains of the department's expertise:

  • ground Station Engineering;
  • flight Dynamics and Mission Analysis;
  • mission Operations Data Systems Engineering;
  • navigation Support;
  • multi-Mission Infrastructure – Ground Segment Integration and Testing.

 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will join the observers team at the Near-Earth Object Coordination Centre, contributing to work that helps shape how one of Europe's planetary defence assets is used. The Flyeye network will be the first European telescope survey network dedicated to searching for imminently impacting near-Earth objects, combining multiple telescope units to scan the sky for asteroids that could pose a threat to Earth. The first unit, Flyeye-1, is currently being commissioned, and a second unit, Flyeye-2, has passed its Critical Design Review and will shortly join the network.

 

You will engage with Sorcha, an open-source, modular survey simulator originally developed for the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), and adapt it to model the Flyeye network. Using this tool, you will explore how current discovery-rate predictions compare against real performance data, whether the network should prioritise depth or width in its observing strategy, how well Flyeye complements LSST's own coverage, and how best to operate Flyeye-1 and Flyeye-2 together, a configuration that has not previously been simulated.

 

Your activities will include:

  • reviewing the architecture of the survey simulator and its existing use for LSST;
  • building a Flyeye-specific configuration covering telescope parameters, cadence, field footprint and network geometry;
  • characterising the network's discovery performance;
  • running comparative simulations to test different observing strategies, such as prioritising survey depth versus sky coverage;
  • assessing how Flyeye's coverage could best complement that of LSST;
  • modelling how the network's telescope units can best be operated together.

 

Depending on your interests, there may also be scope to extend the project, for example by investigating how best to scale exposure time to adapt to sky background conditions, or by evaluating Heliolink, a tracklet-linking approach, and its applicability to Flyeye data.

 

Through this internship, you will gain hands-on experience with a simulation tool used across the wider planetary defence and astronomy community, direct exposure to how survey strategy decisions are made operationally, and the opportunity to contribute to the planning of Europe's next-generation planetary defence network. You will also have the opportunity to collaborate with members of the LSST team.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Additional requirements:

  • A degree track in astronomy, astrophysics, physics, planetary science, or a related field;
  • solid Python programming skills, including working with scientific libraries (numpy, pandas, astropy);
  • basic familiarity with orbital mechanics / solar system dynamics;
  • comfortable working with large datasets; running and interpreting simulations;
  • familiarity with near-Earth object science or planetary defence concepts is an asset;
  • experience with data visualisation and statistical analysis is an asset;
  • ability to work independently on an open-ended research question;
  • you shall have a good knowledge of a scripting/programming language (preferably Python);
  • background in celestial mechanics, is a valuable asset for this role.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Structures Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Structures Section TEC-MSS is in charge of all structural engineering aspects:

  • Structural Design and Verification Methods / Tools;
  • Static / Dynamics / Vibro-Acoustics;
  • Crash / Impacts / Meteoroids Absorption Analysis;
  • Damage Tolerance / Fracture Control / Health Monitoring;
  • Fluid Structure Interaction (e.g. Sloshing);
  • Launcher Coupled Dynamic Analysis;
  • Demisability / Re-Usability;
  • Thermo-Elastic distortion;
  • High Stability / High Precision Structures;
  • Active / Adaptive Structures;
  • Inflatable and Deployable Structures;
  • Launchers / Re-Entry (Hot Structures) / Planetary Landing Vehicles;
  • Crew Habitation / EVA Suits.

 

The ESA Structures Section brings together a diverse team of approximately 43 engineers and specialists covering the complete structural lifecycle of space systems—from early concept development and structural sizing to analysis, verification, testing and in-flight performance.

 

Our expertise includes structural design and analysis, loads and coupled-loads analysis, structural dynamics, vibro-acoustics, shock, micro-vibration, thermo-elastic performance, fracture control and fatigue, advanced materials and manufacturing, deployable structures, structural digitalisation and emerging technologies. The team supports ESA missions across Earth observation, science, exploration, telecommunications, navigation and space transportation, working closely with project teams, European industry, research organisations and partner agencies.

 

Our mission is to ensure that European spacecraft, payloads and launch systems are structurally robust, reliable and fit for purpose throughout their operational life. We provide independent technical expertise, solve complex engineering challenges and help projects manage structural risks through sound engineering judgement and proportionate verification.

 

Beyond direct project support, the Section develops new technologies and methodologies, preserves and shares structural-engineering knowledge, contributes to European standards and technical guidelines, and strengthens industrial capabilities. By connecting operational experience with research and innovation, we aim to anticipate future needs and maintain Europe’s technical excellence and autonomy in spacecraft structures.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will contribute to the development and analysis of advanced structural solutions for space systems. The internship will focus on applying modern design, simulation, and testing methods to improve the performance, reliability, and efficiency of spacecraft structures.

 

Depending on your background and interests, you may work in one of several key domains, such as:

  • structural optimisation: exploring lightweight and high-performance structural concepts through numerical and computational design methods;
  • fracture control and damage tolerance: supporting studies and simulations related to material strength, crack propagation, and structural integrity in extreme environments;
  • vibro-acoustics: analysing vibration and acoustic environments during launch and their influence on structural behaviour;
  • ultra-stable structures: investigating thermo-elastic stability and precision design techniques for optical or scientific payloads;
  • hypervelocity impacts: studying the effects of micrometeoroid and debris impacts on spacecraft structures and assessing protection or resilience strategies through modelling and test data.

 

You will learn how advanced structural engineering is applied to real space missions, gaining hands-on experience with modelling tools, simulation techniques, and engineering processes. Throughout the internship, you will be supported by experienced mentors who will help you connect theoretical knowledge with practical challenges in spacecraft design and verification.

 

Learning outcomes include developing a system-level understanding of spacecraft structures, applying modern analytical and computational methods, and strengthening problem-solving and communication skills in a multidisciplinary engineering environment.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation

The ESA Structures Section brings together a diverse team of approximately 43 engineers and specialists covering the complete structural lifecycle of space systems—from early concept development and structural sizing to analysis, verification, testing and in-flight performance. Our expertise includes structural design and analysis, loads and coupled-loads analysis, structural dynamics, vibro-acoustics, shock, micro-vibration, thermo-elastic performance, fracture control and fatigue, advanced materials and manufacturing, deployable structures, structural digitalisation and emerging technologies. The team supports ESA missions across Earth observation, science, exploration, telecommunications, navigation and space transportation, working closely with project teams, European industry, research organisations and partner agencies. Our mission is to ensure that European spacecraft, payloads and launch systems are structurally robust, reliable and fit for purpose throughout their operational life. We provide independent technical expertise, solve complex engineering challenges and help projects manage structural risks through sound engineering judgement and proportionate verification. Beyond direct project support, the Section develops new technologies and methodologies, preserves and shares structural-engineering knowledge, contributes to European standards and technical guidelines, and strengthens industrial capabilities. By connecting operational experience with research and innovation, we aim to anticipate future needs and maintain Europe’s technical excellence and autonomy in spacecraft structures. Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Optics Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Optics, Robotics and Life Sciences Division is responsible for the technical and strategic management in the following space segment domains at subsystem and instrument level:
 

  • optical systems: design, engineering and verification in all optical related areas, including optical component technology, micro-optics, fibre and passive integrated optics; spectro-radiometric imaging instruments in the x-ray, ultra-violet, visible and infrared region; optical metrology, and space micro-nano technology systems, stray-light analysis and verification. Calibration and verification of optical payloads, covering the definition, procurement and commissioning of Optical Ground Support Equipment (OGSE). In orbit commissioning of optical payloads. Measurement of optical properties of key optical components by devising ad-hoc measurements in the Optical and Optoelectronics Laboratory (OOEL);
  • optoelectronics: laser systems and sensors, LIDAR and laser ranging systems, including optical metrology and time and frequency distribution, photo-detectors and focal plane technologies for the x-ray, ultra-violet, visible and infrared range; photonics technologies and application, including integrated and fibre optics, RF photonics, micro-nano-photonics, opto-pyrotechnics, fibre sensors, non-linear optics, superconductor technology and optical atomic clocks; optical communication technologies and systems, optical communication links and optical payloads; optoelectronics/photonics for spacecraft applications; quantum technologies including quantum devices, metrology, sensing, quantum key distribution and cold atom interferometry;
  • optical chain architecture: design, analysis, and technical assessment of optical instruments, subsystems, detection chain systems and focal plane instrumentation, optical communication systems for classical and quantum communications, time and frequency transfer, intersatellite ranging and similar end-to-end systems;
  • automation and robotics: space automation and robotic systems, including planetary (surface, sub-surface and aerial) robotics probes, space robot payloads and their control systems, space laboratory automation, human-robot interaction, tele-robotics in manned and unmanned missions, as well as automation and robotics technology for ground MAIT;
    life & physical sciences instrumentation: technologies needed for planetary exploration missions and for life and physical sciences experiments in space, as well as technologies needed for life support, crew health and habitability of manned missions, and In-Situ Resources Utilisation;

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Use of machine learning in optical design
 
Define a database of potential architectural solutions based on high level requirements (spectral range, F#, field of view, etc.) and develop/use AI tools to define potential starting points. Explore then the possibility of reinforcement learning techniques to optimise the solution.

 

2) Topic 2: Increase capabilities of open source optical design software (e.g. Optiland)

 

Explore the possibility to expand the software e.g. a) starting the implementation of a non sequential raytracing, b) implementing the possibility to introduce mechanical elements, or c) improving straylight analysis capabilities (e.g. ghost analysis, semi-analytical calculations similar to an existing ESA tool called ‘Straylux’).

 

3) Topic 3: Define a simulator for the Vigil HI instrument

 

The simulator should contain the specific scene definition (F+K corona, planets, stars, coronal mass ejections), introduce instrumental effects (noise, straylight, etc.). Based on the simulator, detection methods for the coronal mass ejections should be investigated.

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

Knowledge and background in optics and optical instrumentation is an asset.

Title: Intern in the Space Safety Programme - Planetary Defence Office - Bringing Lost Asteroids Back
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

​​The ESA Space Safety Department takes care of all potential hazards and threats from space or in space, which can impact ​human activities, infrastructure, or related applications. The spectrum of tasks ranges from gathering the basic understanding of space hazards originating from our Sun, from human space debris, or from asteroids potentially colliding with the Earth. It also addresses basic approaches to mitigate these hazards and to implement space systems end-to-end in a sustainable and eco-compatible way. Moreover, several corner stone missions are underway to demonstrate basic methods of space weather forecasting, asteroid deflection and active space debris removal from orbit. 

​ 

 

​In execution of these tasks, the Space Safety Department has the following entities: 

  • ​Mission Implementation Division (OPS-SM); 
  • ​COSMIC Project Manageent Office (OPS-SC);
  • ​Space Weather Office (OPS-SW);
  • ​Planetary Defence Office (OPS-SP); 
  • ​Space Debris Office (OPS-SD); 
  • ​Clean Space & Circular Economy Office (OPS-SY); 
  • ​Frequency Management Office (OPS-SF); 
  • ​Programme Coordination Office (OPS-SX). 

​ 

 

​The Planetary Defence Office (PDO) is addressing the “…prediction and detection [of] the potential impact of a near-Earth object”. Concerning the information needs for NEO monitoring, the following are defined:  

  • ​knowledge of the current and future positions of all NEO objects above a given size threshold or risk level, in particular their minimum fly-by distance to the Earth and time of this event;  
  • ​maintain awareness of collision risks with the Earth;  
  • ​access to verifiable, dependable, timely data with integrity and known accuracy.  

​ 

 

​The top-level Office tasks are:  

​1. Issue NEO impact warnings and news releases.  

​2. Provide direct access to data in the NEO database.  

​3. Provide access to data in the NEO database available only via registration.  

​4. Perform additional observations.  

​5. Provide high priority information.  

​6. Provide educational and outreach material.  

​7. Provide user tools.  

​ 

 

​The PDO is structured along three vertical pillars differentiating following activity area: 

  • ​Observation; 
  • ​information provision; 
  • ​mitigation. 

 

​You can see following domains of the department's expertise: 

  • ​Ground Station Engineering; 
  • ​flight Dynamics and Mission Analysis; 
  • ​mission Operations Data Systems Engineering; 
  • ​navigation Support; 
  • ​multi-Mission Infrastructure – Ground Segment Integration and Testing. 

 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​Each year, thousands of asteroids are discovered, but many are observed only for a short period before becoming difficult to locate again. At the same time, large archives of astronomical observations contain many unlinked detections that may correspond to previously observed objects. Connecting these observations can improve orbital knowledge and support the recovery of poorly observed asteroids. 

 

​In this internship, you will contribute to the development of a software tool to automatically search for asteroid identifications within existing observational databases. The project will focus on building a robust and efficient pipeline that compares known asteroid predictions against large collections of observations and highlights promising candidate matches for further analysis. 

 

​You will contribute to the design, implementation and validation of the pipeline, using real astronomical data and modern orbit analysis techniques. The final outcome will be a prototype tool capable of running automatically and supporting daily asteroid identification activities. 

​ 

​You will have the opportunity to: 

  • ​Develop software components for the automated processing of asteroid observation data; 
  • ​implement methods to search large observational databases for candidate identifications; 
  • ​evaluate and rank potential matches using orbital uncertainty information; 
  • ​validate the performance of the pipeline using historical asteroid observations; 
  • ​contribute to the development of an operational prototype suitable for integration into existing asteroid-monitoring activities. 

​ 

​Through this internship, you will learn: 

  • ​How asteroid observations are used to determine and improve orbital solutions; 
  • ​how uncertainty in orbital predictions affects object identification; 
  • ​how to design and implement scalable scientific software; 
  • ​how to process and analyse large astronomical datasets; 
  • ​how to transform a scientific concept into an operational tool. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

 

Additional requirements:

  • A degree track in astronomy, astrophysics, physics, planetary science, or a related field; 
  • solid Python programming skills, including working with scientific libraries (numpy, pandas, astropy); 
  • basic familiarity with orbital mechanics / solar system dynamics; 
  • comfortable working with large datasets; running and interpreting simulations; 
  • familiarity with near-Earth object science or planetary defence concepts is an asset; 
  • experience with data visualisation and statistical analysis is an asset; 
  • ability to work independently on an open-ended research question; 
  • you shall have a good knowledge of a scripting/programming language (preferably Python);
  • background in celestial mechanics, is a valuable asset for this role.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - Automated Tools for ESEC SmallSat Operations
description_html:
Location
ESEC, Redu, Belgium   

 

In consideration of the geographical location of ESEC-Redu, successful applicants are recommended to have or obtain a driving license prior to the take up of duties.

Our team and mission

ESEC, the European Space Security and Education Centre, at Redu in Belgium is a centre of excellence for space cyber security services, home to ESA's SmallSat Control Centre, the Space Weather Data Centre, the ESA Education Training Centre as well as part of ESA’s ground station network. 

 

ESEC provides S-band links for ESA’s network of ground stations, as well as in-orbit testing (IOT) for telecommunication and navigation satellites for which it hosts all the facilities used to test the Galileo signal. 

 

The prime function of the operations team (OPS-OEU) at ESEC/Redu is to interface satellites and ground facilities required for their control and utilisation. The main tasks are: 

  • Satellite mission operations (planning, monitoring and control) for PROBA and other SmallSat projects;
  • operational preparation for new missions;
  • in-orbit testing of communications, data relay and navigation satellites; 
  • ground facility operations and maintenance. 

 

ESA activities at ESEC/Redu cover a wide range of disciplines and there is significant hands-on work. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​As an intern you will support the ESEC SmallSat Operations team by developing an automated tool to support the SmallSat operations. The tool to be developed will be chosen based on the mission’s needs at start of the internship as well as your capabilities and preferences. This activity shall be carried out at the ESA/ESEC and will be supported by different ESA experts; since the product will be used operationally close interaction with the SmallSat operations team is expected. 

​ 

​Possible topics include but are not limited to: 

  • ​Development of a new antenna controller for the S-band antennae used by the SmallSat missions; 
  • ​improvement of the planning tool used to coordinate/deconflict activities between missions, negotiate passes with external providers, and generate a pass plan for use by the automation systems; 
  • ​development of basic flight dynamics scripts for pass prediction and antenna tracking; 
  • ​development of a real-time interface between the mission control system and a visualisation tool to display current spacecraft position and attitude. 

​ 

​In all cases, the data required by the implemented tool must be retrieved, generated and processed automatically at regular intervals to allow seamless integration into the ESEC ground segment and support operations without adding additional workload. 

​ 

​You should be able to operate independently but you will be supported by the ESEC SmallSat operations team.​ 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

As an intern, you should have good interpersonal and communication skills and should be able to work in a multi-cultural environment, both independently and as part of a team.  

Experience in Python programming, software development and testing/validation is required.  

Knowledge of Git version control, Linux command line use, and basic flight dynamics knowledge are considered assets.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Space Safety Programme - Clean Space Office
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands or ESAC, Villanueva de la Cañada, Spain 

Our team and mission

​The ESA Space Safety Department takes care of all potential hazards and threats from space or in space, which can impact ​human activities, infrastructure, or related applications. The spectrum of tasks ranges from gathering the basic understanding of space hazards originating from our Sun, from human space debris, or from asteroids potentially colliding with the Earth. It also addresses basic approaches to mitigate these hazards and to implement space systems end-to-end in a sustainable and eco-compatible way. Moreover, several corner stone missions are underway to demonstrate basic methods of space weather forecasting, asteroid deflection and active space debris removal from orbit. 

​ 

​In execution of these tasks, the Space Safety Department has the following entities: 

  • ​Mission Implementation Division (OPS-SM) 
  • ​COSMIC Project Management Office (OPS-SC) 
  • ​Space Weather Office (OPS-SW) 
  • ​Planetary Defence Office (OPS-SP) 
  • ​Space Debris Office (OPS-SD) 
  • ​Clean Space & Circular Economy Office (OPS-SY) 
  • ​Frequency Management Office (OPS-SF) 
  • ​Programme Coordination Office (OPS-SX) 

​ 

​The ESA Clean Space Office (OPS-SC) leads the Agency’s activities aimed at improving the long-term sustainability of space activities. Its mission is to develop, coordinate and promote innovative solutions that reduce the environmental impact of space systems, prevent the generation of space debris, and enable a future circular economy in space. The office addresses the full lifecycle of space assets, from design and manufacturing to operations, servicing, disposal, reuse and recycling. 

 

​The Clean Space Office coordinates ESA initiatives in three complementary domains: 

  • ​Ecodesign, aimed at reducing the environmental footprint of space missions throughout their lifecycle. 
  • ​Zero Debris, aimed at developing technologies, standards and operational approaches that minimise the generation of debris and support the sustainability of Earth and Lunar orbits. 
  • ​In-Orbit Servicing and Circular Economy in Space, aimed at enabling future capabilities such as inspection, rendezvous and proximity operations, servicing, refurbishment, repair, assembly, reuse and recycling of space assets. 

 

​Beyond technology development, the office supports the definition and preparation of future missions, including the study of novel Active Debris Removal (ADR), In-Orbit Servicing (IOS) and Circular Economy mission concepts from the earliest project phases (Phase 0/A/B1) through to implementation and in-orbit demonstration activities. The office also contributes to the development of standards, policies and best practices that support the adoption of sustainable space solutions across ESA and the wider space sector. 

 

​To achieve these objectives, the Clean Space Office coordinates activities implemented under ESA's Space Safety Programme (S2P), ESA's programme dedicated to protecting Earth, society, space infrastructure and future space activities from hazards originating in space or from space activities, including space debris, space weather and near-Earth objects. The office also coordinates and supports Clean Space activities across other ESA R&D programmes, working with ESA technical experts, projects, programmes, but also with Member States, industry and international partners to mature and promote innovative solutions for future space missions. 

 

​For interns, the Clean Space Office offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge engineering, sustainability and innovation activities that are helping to shape the future of sustainable and circular space operations. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

​​1) Topic 1 - Ecodesign for space (ESAC)  

​The environmental impact of space missions is a topic of growing importance. Understanding the impacts is the only way to be able to tackle the problem. ESA has been pioneering this field and has become a world-wide leader in ecodesign for space. The Agency has published the first dedicated Life-Cycle Assessment Handbook and a specific database. ESA is the first entity to require all Space missions to perform ecodesign through its mission development.  

​You will have the opportunity to support the team to review and wrap-up past studies, support the development of datasets for improvement of the ESA LCA Database and support on-going studies to define the way forward.  

​ 

​2) Topic 2 - Zero Debris approach and End-of-Life Management (ESTEC)  

​The traffic in valuable Earth orbits is expected to continue increasing significantly in the coming decades. Despite internationally recognised space debris mitigation guidelines, technical standards and national regulations, the successful disposal of space systems and the prevention of in-orbit break-ups remain major challenges. ESA is addressing these challenges through the implementation of the Zero Debris approach, helping to preserve the space environment for future generations. 

​  

​You will support the team responsible for further developing the Zero Debris approach and improving the End-of-Life management of current and future missions. Activities may include contributing to engineering studies, requirements, methodologies, technology roadmaps and analyses related to space debris mitigation, disposal strategies and the implementation of Zero Debris objectives across ESA projects. 

​ 

​3) Topic 3 - Active Debris Removal and In-Orbit Servicing (ESTEC)  

​Globally significant progress has been made in both the technical and commercial validation of in-orbit servicing activities such as debris removal, AOCS takeover for life extension, asset relocation, refuelling and in-orbit inspection. Looking forward, ESA aims to contribute to the creation of the demand for In-Orbit Servicing (IOS) in Europe by fostering both the service-offering side and to stimulate and enable the demand side of the developing IOS market. You will be supporting the team working on enabling the In-Orbit Servicing activities at ESA.​ 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Having a keen interest in Clean Space activities is beneficial and having a collaborative team spirit is highly valued. 

 

For Topic 1: 

knowledge and background in environmental and/or space system engineering and previous knowledge on LCA and Ecodesign methodology and tools are considered an asset.   

For Topic 2: 

knowledge and background in space debris mitigation and/or system engineering is an asset. 

For Topic 3:  

knowledge and background in space debris remediation and/or other in-orbit servicing and/or system engineering is an asset. 

 

Due to the nature of the post, a commitment of six months is preferred, depending on the candidate’s availability. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - Python Tools for Earth Explorer Flight Operations
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

​​In this internship, you will become part of the Flight Control Teams responsible for flight operations of the FLEX, Biomass, EarthCARE, Swarm, and CryoSat missions at the European Space Operations Centre in Darmstadt, Germany. These missions are part of the Earth Explorer family, focused on advancing Earth science through observation of Earth’s key systems. 

 

​The Flight Control Team is responsible for conducting day-to-day operations of these missions, working closely across ground segment and science interfaces to ensure that the missions deliver high-quality data to the scientific community. During the routine operations phase of the missions, the team develops and relies on a set of tools and processes that make operations safer, faster and more efficient, balancing reliability and innovation, while maintaining robust space and ground segment operations. 

 

​As the intern in our team, you will join an international, collaborative and supportive environment. You will gain direct exposure to real spacecraft operations and experience how software, automation, and operational processes are used in a unique control centre environment. ​ 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​You will design and implement Python scripts, tools and frameworks that support routine spacecraft operations and automate recurring tasks. Your tools will be used by the Flight Control Team in a live mission environment and will contribute directly to safer and more efficient operations. 

 

​The exact scope of the activities will be decided together with you, depending on your profile, interests, and the mission needs. Possible tasks include both development of new tools, as well as adaptation of existing tools to make them generic and improve harmonisation across the different missions. Example use cases include automating daily checks of spacecraft state, the generation of reports, and creating dashboards, as well as tools for modelling expected spacecraft states. 

 

These activities will include extracting relevant data from ESOC internal interfaces, processing and validating it, and presenting the results clearly to operators. The resulting tools should be packaged in a reusable Python library with helpful documentation and examples. You will also share your results with the team through short demonstrations or training sessions. 

 

​During your internship, you will learn about the mission control systems, tools, and interfaces used at ESOC. You will gain hands-on experience in how satellite operations are planned and conducted during routine activities, with direct exposure to the Flight Control Team and the control room environment.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - ESTRACK Stations and Infrastructure Section
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

ESA’s tracking station network (ESTRACK) is a global system of ground stations providing the vital link between spacecraft and the European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, Germany, is a critical part of Europe’s space infrastructure, supporting some of the Agency’s most ambitious missions in science, exploration and space safety. From spacecraft orbiting Earth and travelling to the Lagrange points, to missions exploring the Solar System, studying the Sun or contributing to planetary defence, ESTRACK provides the essential ground infrastructure that enables these missions to operate. 

 

The ESTRACK network brings together antennas located around the globe, communication systems, control and monitoring equipment, IT infrastructure and a wide range of supporting facilities, all working together to provide reliable and continuous services to spacecraft and mission operations. 

 

Our teams are responsible for ensuring that this complex infrastructure remains safe, reliable and available 24/7. This includes operating and maintaining ground station systems, managing assets and configurations, supporting upgrades and obsolescence activities, and continuously improving processes, technologies and ways of working across the network. 

 

Beyond supporting individual missions, ESTRACK contributes to Europe’s autonomy, resilience and ability to operate as a leading space power. Through cross-support agreements with international partners, the network also strengthens international cooperation, while enabling more efficient and sustainable space operations.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​You will report to the Head of the ESTRACK Stations and Infrastructure Section in the Ground Facilities Operations Division. This Section is responsible for the maintenance and operational management of the ESA Tracking Network (ESTRACK). 

​ 

​The ESA Link Budget Tool is the reference tool of the European Space Operations Centre for the characterisation of the radio-frequency communication link between spacecraft and ground antenna. 

 

​You will contribute to the continuous development, support, and optimisation of the ESA Link Budget Tool in a collaborative, user-focused environment. 

​ 

​This role will also focus on assessing the environmental impact of ground station operations in line with the ESA Green Agenda initiatives.

You will focus particularly on analysing data in terms of carbon footprint and providing concrete metrics and insights to guide future actions.  

 

​Key Responsibilities: 

 

​Link Budget Tool: Expand the Link Budget Tool catalogue for Near-Earth missions and ground stations 

​With the growing number and diversity of missions supported by ESA, you will contribute to expanding the Link Budget Tool’s mission and ground-station catalogues. You will have the opportunity to analyse new requirements, perform testing, and further enhance the tool’s capabilities to support the Agency’s evolving operational needs. 

​ 

​Link Budget Tool: Analyse capacity and optimise ESTRACK scheduling 

​You will contribute to analysing ground-station capacity and workload, helping to identify opportunities to improve the allocation and utilisation of ESTRACK resources across missions. You will support studies and development activities aimed at integrating the Link Budget Tool with the ground-station scheduling system, which allocates ESTRACK ground-station coverage to supported space missions. This activity will involve close interaction with ground-station and mission operations teams, providing a unique opportunity to understand and contribute to the end-to-end process of planning spacecraft communications. 

​ 

​Green ESTRACK: Review and Assess Sustainability Measures at ESTRACK Ground Stations 
You will evaluate existing and future sustainability initiatives and operational activities at selected ESTRACK ground stations, assessing their documented environmental impact, energy consumption, and effects on local energy grids. You will analyse available data from past and ongoing measures to determine operational efficiency and alignment with ISO 50001 energy management standards.  

​ 

​Green ESTRACK: Develop and Maintain Sustainability Metrics and Dashboards 
You will design and maintain metrics in alignment with recognised sustainability standards. These metrics will help track the effectiveness of initiatives and demonstrate the tangible benefits of adopting sustainable practices. You will present the results clearly for both internal use and external reporting, highlighting the positive environmental and operational impact. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

​You should have a keen interest in sustainability, strong analytical skills and the ability to collaborate across different technical and administrative teams. 

 

  • Basic knowledge of Python programming code;  
  • basic knowledge of atmospheric propagation; 
  • familiarity with sustainability principles, carbon accounting, or environmental standards like energy management/ISO 50001; 
  • proactive, able to multitask and have strong self-motivation; 
  • good communication skills for handling a broad range of interfaces and the ability to work as part of an interdisciplinary team. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Contracts Department - Earth Observation Contracts Service
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

​​The intern will join the Earth Observation Contracts Service team, in the Contracts Department. The Service is composed of a Head of Service (the Manager) and 15 team members. The Service is in charge of small to medium R&D procurements as well as large satellite procurements. Such procurements encompass ESA classical fully funded Mission, as well as Missions in partnership with the European Union (e.g. Copernicus) and EUMETSAT (e.g. Meteorological Missions).

​As an intern you will have the opportunity to familiarise yourself with the full procurement cycle under the Agency’s procurement rules and how the Agency’s rules are adapted for EU co-funded procurements.

​This will give you the opportunity to familiarise yourself with the different public procurement rules (ESA, EU) and get a solid knowledge of the underlying public procurement principles.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​As an intern, you will be involved in the following activities:

 

  • ​analysis of the ESA Contracting Regulations and ESA’s unique rules and context;
  • ​analysis of the ESA procurement rules as adapted for activities funded by the EU;
  • ​analysis of the ESA General Clauses and Conditions for ESA Contracts;
  • ​participation in the full procurement cycle starting from the preparation of tender packages, issue of the tender, evaluation of the proposals and placement of the Contracts.

 

​Through the participation in the above activities you will have a clear view of the main principles of public procurement applying to ESA procurements and at the same time you will have learnt the principles and international standards applicable to public procurement around the world which are mirrored in the ESA procurement rules.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements
