Title: Intern in the Industrial Policy and Auditing Department - SME Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Industrial Policy and Auditing Department is responsible for elaborating and implementing the Agency's industrial policy, for defining and implementing the geographical return and industrial audit policies, for fostering the relations between industry and the Agency and for supporting the successful accession of new Member and Cooperating States.

SMEs¹ (Small and Medium Enterprises) and start-ups play an ever-increasing role in the activities of ESA and the industrial landscape of its Member States. Today they represent more than 30% of the companies contracted by the Agency and are important contributors of innovation for ESA Programmes. The SME Section of the Department implements the ESA SME Industrial Policy with the objective to facilitate both the introduction and the sustainable involvement of SMEs in the activities of the Agency and to support their introduction into the industrial space supply chain. To this end the SME Office performs a variety of activities also including analyses concerning the involvement of SMEs in the Agency's activities and their economic and financial characteristics as well as the evolution of the SME landscape.  

 

1) SMEs are defined as companies having a staff headcount <250, annual turnover ≤ 50M€ or a balance sheet total ≤ 43M€, see Recommendation of the European Commission 2003/361/EC of 6 May 2003.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​In the context of elaborating and implementing the Agency's industrial policy it is important for ESA to maintain an in-depth understanding of the space industry and its characteristics. The focus of the here concerned activity is to contribute to the characterisation of the European space SME community. This concerns in particular statistical analyses of the economic and financial characteristics of European space SMEs and their involvement in the activities of ESA.  

​ 

​To this end you will access a variety of available data sources of the Agency comprising programmatic, financial, and economic data (current and historic) concerning the European space industry working with ESA (note that access to the data and publication will be subject to a non-disclosure agreement). Your analyses will contribute to the extension and consolidation of the existing collection of data and models of relevant economic and financial characteristics of the space SME and Start-Up community. Your analyses will consist of performing in depth studies and statistical analysis that will consist of coding of related algorithms, machine learning and AI-based data exploitation as required. For the analyses you will be using a range of data sources of industrial policy relevance.  

​ 

​The precise scope and content of the specific analyses to be performed during the period of the internship can be agreed with you in line with your research interests.  

​ 

​You will be supported in your activities by the members of the SME Section and other services of the Department.​ 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge of economics, statistics, econometrics.

The activity requires the handling of large datasets. Proficiency with MS Excel is required and experience with data analysis software such as Python, Power BI, machine learning tools would be an asset. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Space Safety Programme - Space Debris Office
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany or ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands   

Our team and mission

The ESA Space Safety Department takes care of all potential hazards and threats from space or in space, which can impact human activities, infrastructure, or related applications. The spectrum of tasks ranges from gathering the basic understanding of space hazards originating from our Sun, from human space debris, or from asteroids potentially colliding with the Earth. It also addresses basic approaches to mitigate these hazards and to implement space systems end-to-end in a sustainable and eco-compatible way. Moreover, several corner stone missions are underway to demonstrate basic methods of space weather forecasting, asteroid deflection and active space debris removal from orbit. 

 

In execution of these tasks, the Space Safety Department has the following entities: 

  • Mission Implementation Division (OPS-SM); 
  • COSMIC Project Management Office (OPS-SC); 
  • Space Weather Office (OPS-SW); 
  • Planetary Defence Office (OPS-SP); 
  • Space Debris Office (OPS-SD); 
  • Clean Space & Circular Economy Office (OPS-SY); 
  • Frequency Management Office (OPS-SF); 
  • Programme Coordination Office (OPS-SX). 

 

The Space Debris Office constitutes the focal point for ESA space debris activities and is responsible for coordinating the Agency’s space debris research activities, for all space debris related operational and analysis services in support of ESA missions, and for ESA’s cooperation on space debris issues at inter-agency level. Its work is centred around a wide range of operational and scientific analysis software, developed, maintained and operated under its control. Through the provision of domain expertise, the office is deeply involved in implementing the Agency’s zero debris approach, and technology development through ESA’s Space Safety Programme, as well as the technology development programmes. 

 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will support the implementation and further development of ESA’s Zero Debris Approach, aligned with the Zero Debris Charter.  

​ 

You can choose between the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Your activities will include analysing the current and future evolution of the space debris environment and supporting ongoing and future satellite missions.  

 

2) Topic 2: You will contribute to topics such as debris mitigation and remediation techniques, the evaluation of new concepts, the development and application of methods to verify and qualify these concepts.  

​ 

​Both topics will link with the use of new technologies to address operational needs. 

​ 

​With a special focus on optical performance models for space debris detections or operational re-entry risk assessments, your activities will support mission development and linked analyses within the Space Safety Programme.  

 

​You will help define relevant studies, contribute to their technical follow-up, attend regular team meetings, and support coordination within a group of experts. You will also contribute to the further development of the Office’s analysis tools. 

​ 

​You will be part of a small team, actively contributing to ongoing projects, research activities, and tool development, while presenting results to internal and international audiences.​ 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Good knowledge and background in engineering modelling, data science, simulation and mathematics is an asset. 

Previous demonstrated experience with scientific computing in Python is an asset.  

Knowledge of orbital mechanics is an asset.  

Experience in space systems engineering is an asset. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Science Contracts Service
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Science Contracts Service supports the European Space Agency’s Science Programme by delivering effective, transparent and timely procurement for scientific missions, studies, technology activities and mission operations. 

Our focus is to help Science teams move efficiently from contract planning to contract signature and implementation, while maintaining sound governance, fair competition and value for money, including (but not limited to) for the upcoming exciting missions of LISA, EnVision, NewAthena. 

 

Within the Contracts Department, the CFO-CX Contracts Division is in charge of the implementation of all activities in support of the Science and the Human and Robotic Exploration Programmes Directorates. The relevant contracts cover a wide range of complexity, from a few 100 K€ R&D to large Satellites Projects of several 100 M€.  

The Division implements all related contracting tasks, ranging from tendering, planning and issue of invitations to tender, to evaluation of proposals, negotiation of contracts as well as their signature and monitoring. 

Also, in parallel the Division contributes to the improvement of the overall Regulatory frame in the Contracts Department, and supports the general work initiated in the Department to improve time to contract. 

 

You will join an international team at the European Space Research and Technology Centre in Noordwijk in the Netherlands, collaborating with contracts officers and engaging with Science stakeholders. 

The environment combines procurement, legal and programmatic analysis, collaboration and continuous improvement.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will support contracting activities for the Science Programme.

You will help review procurement documentation and contractual provisions;  

​analyse contractual, programmatic and procedural questions;  

​compare approaches across different contract types;  

​and contribute to active procurement cases under the supervision of a contracts officer, with due regard to operational and time-efficiency as well as continuous evolutions. 

​ 

​By the end of the internship, you will understand the main stages of public procurement in the space sector, apply contractual and regulatory principles and collaborate effectively with technical, legal and programmatic stakeholders.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Priority will be given to candidates studying Law.

Knowledge and background in space domain/technology is considered an asset. 

A good knowledge in contract, procurement or international business law, intellectual property law is considered an asset.

Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written.

Ability to interact with multiple international actors and to work collaboratively in a team to achieve organisational goals.

Discretion and integrity.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - Web-Based Operations Tools
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

​​The Operations Definition and Engineering Team is an expert team responsible for providing Ground Segment and Operations support throughout the early phases of missions, including participation in CDF and phase A/B1. The Team also provides expertise to other projects and studies, including research and development of tools and methods for operations, and providing operations to non-traditional missions. The Team currently supports missions like Cluster (disposal phase), SpaceRider, Plasma Observatory and Henon.​ 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​During your internship, you will be assigned to the Solar System & Exploration Missions Division which is responsible for ​operating the spacecraft of the Agency’s interplanetary fleet. Your assignment will focus primarily on the creation and ​extension of web-based operations tools which will support the flight control teams and spacecraft controllers in the execution of their daily work. In particular, you will design and develop backend functionalities for the retrieval, ​processing and generation of operational planning information and spacecraft configuration data as well as frontend ​features for appropriate visualisation and modification of said data. 

​ 

​This will involve tasks such as: 

  • ​Assessment of relevant existing tools and functionalities within the division; 
  • ​collection of user requirements; 
  • ​devising a concept and software architecture to support the identified requirements; 
  • ​implementation and testing of the identified solution(s)​. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and experience in the following areas would be an asset: 

  • Python, Javascript or other programming languages;
  • back-end development, e.g. Django; 
  • front-end development, e.g. Angular; 
  • Web Server Architecture; 
  • REST APIs. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics.

Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - JUICE Flight Control Team
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

​​Our team is responsible for mission preparation and flight operations for the ESA fleet of solar and interplanetary spacecraft. The Division currently operates multiple missions (Mars Express, Exomars-TGO, BepiColombo, Solar Orbiter, HERA and JUICE) and is preparing for the launch of several others (Rosalind Franklin Mission, RAMSES, Comet Interceptor, Argonaut and EnVision). 

​ 

​JUICE - JUpiter ICy moons Explorer - is the first large mission in the ESA Cosmic Vision programme. The mission was launched in April 2023 and is currently en route to Jupiter, encountering several gravity assist manoeuvres at Earth and Venus on its way. After the arrival at Jupiter in 2031, JUICE will spend at least 5 years making a thorough investigation of the Jupiter system in all its complexity with emphasis on the three ocean‐bearing Galilean moons Ganymede, Europa and Callisto, and their potential habitability. 

​

​

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​You can choose between the following topics: 

 

​Topic 1: Enhancement of the ground-based mission planning system used for spacecraft command generation, with a focus on improving link budget calculations and tuning of the spacecraft power model. 

​ 

​Topic 2: Development of telemetry monitoring tools for the JUICE Flight Control Team. Title: Intern in the Human Exploration Science Office - Blood Flow Restriction Training
description_html:
Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

​​Within the Exploration Science Office of the Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration, the Human Exploration Science Team (HRE-SH) conducts research that enables future human space exploration while leveraging spaceflight and analogue platforms to advance knowledge and improve human health on Earth. HRE-SH uses a wide range of terrestrial and (sub-) orbital research platforms, as well as the International Space Station (ISS), to investigate the effects of selected or combined spaceflight stressors on human health and performance. These platforms include parabolic flight, dry immersion, bed rest, isolated and confined environments, and spaceflight. This work focuses on the identification and mitigation of challenges to astronaut health and performance to enable the safe exploration of European Astronauts to low-Earth orbit, the Moon, and beyond. Furthermore, by leveraging the platforms developed for exploration, scientific experiments can be conducted under unique conditions, generating benefits on Earth in fields such as healthcare, ageing research, and health management. HRE-SH works closely with international partners, astronauts, medical support, and the scientific community to define and address operational needs and scientific priorities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

 

Background 

​Prolonged exposure to microgravity induces cardiovascular and musculoskeletal deconditioning, making effective exercise countermeasures essential for maintaining astronaut health during long-duration space missions. Blood Flow Restriction (BFR) training is a promising strategy to enhance the efficiency of these countermeasures. By partially restricting blood flow to the limbs using pressurised cuffs during exercise, BFR can induce physiological adaptations typically associated with high-intensity training while using substantially lower exercise loads. 

​As a result, BFR has the potential to improve training effectiveness and/or reduce the time required for exercise before, after, and potentially during spaceflight. Although BFR is increasingly applied in sports performance, rehabilitation, and clinical practice on Earth, its efficacy and safety under spaceflight-relevant conditions remain insufficiently understood. 

​In particular, spaceflight-associated physiological stressors may alter the cardiovascular and haemodynamic responses to BFR. Furthermore, the effects of BFR on blood coagulation and its potential role in the development of venous thromboembolism require further investigation before the technique can be considered for operational use in human spaceflight. 

​ 

​This internship will contribute to ongoing research investigating BFR as a potential countermeasure for spaceflight-induced physiological deconditioning. The work will help improve our understanding of the safety, physiological responses, and optimal application of BFR, supporting the development of future exercise countermeasure strategies. 

​ 

​Objectives

​The intern will contribute to research investigating the physiological responses and potential applications of BFR in spaceflight analogue environments. The focus will be on cardiovascular and coagulation responses, with the aim to define benefits and limitations of BFR as a countermeasure for human exploration missions. 

​ 

​Main Activities related to the overall research initiative include: 

  • ​support experimental studies and physiological data collection;
  • ​analyse and interpret human physiology data from ongoing research;
  • ​contribute to scientific reports, presentations, and publications related to human spaceflight and countermeasures. 

​ 

​Through this internship, you will: 

  • ​receive close mentorship and guidance from experienced researchers in space physiology and medicine;
  • ​gain hands-on experience with blood flow restriction and human physiology research;
  • ​develop skills in data analysis, scientific writing, and critical thinking;
  • ​learn how analogue studies support human space exploration;
  • ​gain insight into space medicine and astronaut health;
  • ​work in an international and interdisciplinary research team. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Desired assets:  

 

  • background in medicine, sports science, physiology, and/or health sciences;
  • experience in Blood Flow Restriction, human spaceflight physiology, and/or biomedical engineering;
  • experience with data analysis, statistics, or scientific writing;
  • familiarity with research related to spaceflight, extreme environments, or analogue studies is desirable.

 

The ability to work independently and communicate effectively in an international team is required. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.

Title: Intern in AI-enabled Scientific Knowledge Management and Discovery
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands

Our team and mission

​The Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration is responsible for Europe’s human and robotic exploration activities in low Earth orbit, including the International Space Station and future post-Station activities, as well as exploration of the Moon and Mars. Its work combines science, technology development, mission preparation and operations. 

​ 

​For this internship, you will work across two complementary teams: 

​ 

​The Exploration Science Office (HRE-S) develops and implements the scientific element of the Human and Robotic Exploration programme, including the biological and life sciences research. The team works closely with the European scientific community to define research priorities, prepare experiments and bring biological payloads and investigations to the International Space Station and other research platforms. It also captures and maintains the scientific knowledge, experimental results and lessons learned generated through these activities. This team will provide the scientific context for your internship and represents the main user community for the solution you will develop. 

​ 

​Your technical home base will be the Software and Artificial Intelligence Team (HRE-FI), which develops and applies software and emerging digital technologies across human and robotic exploration. The team works in areas including software engineering, artificial intelligence, robotics, extended reality, data technologies and quantum technologies. You will work in a multidisciplinary technical environment and receive support in areas such as software development, data systems, artificial intelligence and digital solution design. 

​ 

​By working across both teams, you will have the opportunity to translate a real scientific knowledge-management challenge into a practical technical solution, while working directly with the scientists and stakeholders who are expected to use it.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​The European Space Agency’s Exploration Science Office has established a Life Sciences Handbook to capture scientific knowledge, lessons learned, experimental results, technologies, standards and research recommendations generated through decades of space life sciences activities. 

​ 

​The handbook is intended to help researchers make better use of previous experience when designing new experiments, payloads and protocols. This can include very practical questions, such as which materials, methods, environmental conditions or preservation approaches have already been demonstrated successfully. By making this knowledge accessible, the handbook can help researchers avoid repeating known mistakes, build on previous findings and design more robust science.

 

​As the handbook grows, its value will increasingly depend on how easily the scientific community can discover, understand and reuse its content, and on how effectively new knowledge can be captured and added over time.

​During this internship, you will design and develop a digital solution that helps the scientific community make best use of this growing knowledge base.

Tasks

During the internship, you will:

 

1. ​Understand users, data and existing solutions

  • ​work with scientists to understand how they would use the handbook, what information they need and where current barriers to adoption and discovery lie;
  • ​consider different levels of digital affinity and trust within the user community and translate these into functional and technical requirements;
  • ​analyse the structure, content and metadata of the existing handbook and associated data;
  • ​review relevant existing tools, platforms and approaches within and outside the European Space Agency, for example ESA Data Labs, scientific data archives and comparable knowledge-access solutions used by other research communities, and assess their relevance to the use case in order to inform build, reuse, integration and hosting decisions.
     

2. ​Design, prototype and evaluate the solution  

  • ​assess suitable ways of making the solution accessible to its intended users, for example through integration with an existing website or other digital environment, taking into account hosting, authentication, access rights, permissions and deployment constraints;
  • ​coordinate access, integration and deployment considerations with relevant scientific, technical and service stakeholders and reflect the resulting requirements in the proposed solution;
  • ​assess and prototype suitable user interfaces for accessing the knowledge base, for example structured browsing, category-based navigation, filters, search, visual exploration or conversational artificial-intelligence interfaces;
  • ​evaluate suitable retrieval approaches, including semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation and conversational artificial intelligence, considering accuracy, transparency, user trust and maintainability;
  • ​design and implement a working prototype connecting the underlying knowledge base with the selected user interface and search and retrieval components;
  • ​test and refine the prototype with representative users from the scientific community.

​ 

3. Enable sustainable growth and future operation 

  • ​design a sustainable data pipeline that allows new experimental results, lessons learned and recommendations to be captured, reviewed and incorporated into the knowledge base with minimal manual effort;
  • ​document the solution and provide recommendations for further development and operational use. 

​ 

​Through this internship, you will gain hands-on experience in scientific data and knowledge management, user-centred design, software prototyping, web-based information access, artificial intelligence, information retrieval and data pipelines, while contributing directly to the reuse of scientific knowledge in future space life sciences research.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You bring the following skillset to the team:  

 

  • academic background in data science, scientific computing, bioinformatics, information science, knowledge management, human-computer interaction, biology or a related scientific or technical field;
  • experience working with scientific data, structured datasets or knowledge bases;
  • ability to translate user needs into functional requirements for a digital solution;
  • practical programming or scripting skills sufficient to build and adapt a working prototype;
  • experience designing or prototyping web-based interfaces, including search, filtering, navigation or data-driven components;
  • understanding of databases, data structures and how digital applications connect to underlying data sources;
  • familiarity with artificial intelligence, semantic search, large language models or retrieval-augmented generation is an asset;
  • experience in academic, research or space-related environments is an asset.  

 

We are particularly interested in candidates who combine an understanding of scientific or research data with the ability to design and prototype digital tools for accessing and reusing that information.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

The Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration (D/HRE) is the main ESA entity in charge of supporting and coordinating efforts towards the current and the future endeavours of human spaceflight. The exploration activities are part of the strategic plans in securing a central role for Europe with respect to the global initiatives. The strategy includes three destinations where humans will work with robots to gather new knowledge: Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the Moon, and Mars.

 

The “Spaceship EAC” initiative is investigating low Technology Readiness Level (TRL) technologies for supporting the future cislunar space mission as well as surface activities on the Moon as part of the Exploration Preparation, Research and Technology (ExPeRT) team. This multidisciplinary, innovation-driven team composed of researchers, graduate and undergraduate students is based at the ESA European Astronaut Centre (EAC). The mission statement of “Spaceship EAC” is centred on three main pillars: enhance, enable and inspire.  

 

The Spaceship team is involved in supporting the development of our new LUNA Analog Facility at EAC. This facility will serve as a central hub for lunar exploration preparations at ESA and DLR. It features a 700 sqm lunar surface testbed, facilitating the development and validation of operational concepts, astronaut training, and technology demonstrations for Moon exploration. Additionally, the facility will showcase elements of an analogue Moon base, such as a habitat/laboratory module, and a closed-loop plant growth facility.  

 

We are continually looking for innovative applicants with skills or interests in these areas to join the Spaceship EAC team. An outline of some of the projects that we have recently been progressing can be found at the ESA blog.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will support ESA’s effort to evolve and to utilise the LUNA Analog Facility together with DLR as project partner. 

​ 

1. ​Background and Motivation

 

​The LUNA Analog Facility is the central hub for the preparation, validation and training for lunar surface activities and technologies. While focusing on operational concepts and mission simulations, it also allows for substantial technology testing, scientific investigations, optimisation of operational protocols and procedures, and much more.

 

​The LUNA facility has been inaugurated in September 2024 and is being used for various research and simulation activities of ESA, DLR and external partners. Those include suited activities with suit simulators and dedicated EVA tools, as well as robotic activities concerning mobility, imaging, localisation and communications. At the same time that utilisation is ramping up, the facility is still being evolved with additional capabilities to further enhance and increase the immersion and simulation quality. 

​ 

2. ​Objectives

 

​This internship project aims to support ESA’s evolution and utilisation of the LUNA Analog Facility by:

  • ​supporting the development and integration of new capabilities through the element engineering process from requirements engineering to system design, manufacturing, testing and verification, commissioning and operations;
  • ​supporting the operations and utilisation of LUNA in campaign activities with internal and external partners.  

​ 

3. ​Methodology and Tasks

 

​The internship will integrate into the existing Spaceship EAC/LUNA team at ESA and – based on interest and needs – support one or multiple of the development and utilisation activities below. Additional topics may also be identified throughout the internship period.

 

  • ​refinement of the concept of operations of LUNA and its application for campaign utilisation;
  • ​habitation systems development and their integration into mission simulations;
  • ​analogue space suit evolution and operations, incl. tools development;
  • ​robotic or autonomous systems developments to support LUNA utilisation;
  • ​dust monitoring and mitigation strategies for LUNA operations and future Moon missions;
  • ​integration of research and technologies related to in-situ resource utilisation with LUNA.

​ 

​4. Expected Outcomes

 

​Based on the actual task assignments, the outcomes of the internship will include contributions to the LUNA operations and utilisation documentation as well as procedures and training manuals. You will be directly involved in the LUNA operations, work with actual hardware and interface with scientific investigations in LUNA which could lead to production or contributions to publications and conference presentations. 

​ 

​5. Relevance

 

​As ESA, NASA, and international partners plan sustainable human presence on the Moon, LUNA will be instrumental to prepare and bring together European expertise for lunar science, technology development, astronaut and operator training, and lunar mission operations.

Relevance ​As ESA, NASA, and international partners plan sustainable human presence on the Moon, LUNA will be instrumental to prepare and bring together European expertise for lunar science, technology development, astronaut and operator training, and lunar mission operations. Title: Intern in the Contracts Department
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

Your internship will be split into two equal periods in two separate contracts divisions of ESA's Contracts Department:

•    half the duration of your internship within the Space Transportation Contracts Division (CFO-CL);

•    half the duration of your internship within the Operations & Ground Segment Contracts Division (CFO-CO).

 

This experience in two different contracts divisions of ESA's Contracts Department will allow you to maximise your experience of ESA's procurement process and contract management in a large variety of space (launchers, Earth Observation) and non-space (IT, facility management, communication) domains.

 

The Space Transportation Contracts Division is composed of 11 professionals of various backgrounds and nationalities, located both in Paris (France) and in Rome (Italy).

Our mission is to provide support to the Space Transportation Directorate with regard to the procurement process related to launchers in the European Space Agency. In particular, we are involved in procurement strategy definition, preparation of internal decision documents related to procurement, preparation and release of Invitation to Tender/Request for Quotation/Call for Proposals, evaluation of proposals, preparation and negotiation of contracts and contractual amendments

Our work is organised in four (4) teams reporting to the Head of Division according to the main areas of responsibility, as follows:

  • in ESA HQ Daumesnil, Paris, France:  Ariane 6 Team; Space Transportation Ground Infrastructure Team; Future Space Transportation Developments Team;
  • in ESRIN, Frascati, Italy: VEGA/Space Rider Team.

For half the duration of your internship, you will be part of the Space Transportation Contracts Division (CFO-CL) with an organisational reporting line to the Team Leader in ESRIN.

 

The Operations & Ground Segment Contracts Division is composed of 21 professionals, located at ESRIN (the Agency’s Earth Observation Centre) in Frascati, near Rome (Italy), and at ESOC (European Space Operations Centre) in Darmstadt, near Frankfurt (Germany).

The Division is specialised in the placing and monitoring of large service contracts with the European space industry for ground segment activities and operations of a variety of ESA and third-party space missions, as well as for general activities, especially in the IT domain for the whole Agency.

The Division is split into two contract services:

The ESRIN Contracts Service (CFO-COE) focuses on space activities at the Agency’s Earth Observation Centre in Frascati (Italy), which include in particular: developing and maintaining Earth observation ground segments and distributing Earth observation data from satellites.

The ESOC Contracts Service (CIC-COM) supports activities at the Agency’s European Space Operations Centre. Its work covers the Space Safety Programme (S2P), contractual actions for the Mission Operations Department and the Ground Systems Engineering and Innovation Department, and general procurement at ESOC. In particular, it places and manages contracts for flight operations and for the development and maintenance of the Agency’s worldwide network of space antennas, which connect satellites in orbit with ESOC.

During half the duration of your internship, you will be part of the Operations & Ground Segment Contracts Division (CFO-CO) with an organisational reporting line to the head of the CFO-COE Contracts Service in ESRIN.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will be requested to provide analysis of several procurement or contractual texts, including on ESA General Contractual Clauses and Conditions; i.e. legal analysis of ESA specific regimes (Intellectual Property Rights, disclosure, Personal Data Protection, liability, export control ...) and their implementation in ESA General Clauses and Conditions; with specific focus on differences between General Procurement contracts, Express Procurement contract and Manpower and Service contracts, in the frame of the Contracting Regulations.

 

You will obtain hands-on procurement experience in the space sector, while getting used to ESA procurement process through involvement in practical procurement cases, under the supervision of Contracts Officers from the two Divisions.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Additional requirements:

  • excellent communication skills, both verbal and written; 
  • ability to interact with multiple international actors and to work collaboratively in a team to achieve organisational goals; 
  • discretion and integrity. 

 

The following would be considered assets: 

  • knowledge and background in space domain/technology; 
  • a good knowledge of contract, procurement or international business law, intellectual property law; 
  • a background in law, economics. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the CAVES & PANGAEA Team - Development of the PANGAEA Analytical Toolset
description_html:
Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

The CAVES and PANGAEA team specialises in training programmes that equip astronauts and mission developers with scientific, expeditionary and behavioural skills. The group’s primary output is focused around two training programmes, CAVES, a course that uses natural cave systems for expeditionary and human behavioural and performance training, and PANGAEA, a course for geological and astrobiological field training. Complementary to their training goals, these programmes are used as research and development platforms to advance several of ESA’s technological, scientific and operational areas.  

 

One such tool developed for PANGAEA and future missions is the PANGAEA Analytical Toolset. This comprises the Mineralogical Database (MinDB), a curated collection of information on all the minerals found on the Moon, Mars and in meteorites, and the Machine Learning (ML) software that combines deep learning multi-class and multi-label classification algorithms analysing fused multi-modal spectroscopic measurements, enabling a significant accuracy increase of mineral and rock recognition. 

 

Further information on PANGAEA and CAVES programmes can be found on the following websites: 

 

https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/CAVES_and_Pangaea/What_is_PANGAEA 

 

https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/CAVES_and_Pangaea/What_is_CAVES 

 

We are looking for internships to start throughout 2027. Candidates are invited to state their preferred starting date in the cover letter.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​Interns are sought to contribute to the ongoing expansion, enhancement, and integration of the Mineralogical & Spectroscopic data analysis and curation part of the PANGAEA analytical toolset. Working alongside Machine Learning developers, interns will collect, organise, and evaluate analytical data to ensure training datasets meet scientific standards, while offering subject matter expertise to guide mineral identification algorithms development.

 

Key responsibilities include:

 

  • ​expanding, curating and quality-assessing multi-spectral archives within the Mineralogical Database, focusing on its analytical reference library, validation mineral samples, and petrographic information catalogue of planetary analogue minerals and rocks; 
  • ​assisting in validation of spectral identification methods through expert review of ML outputs;  
  • ​supporting PANGAEA training course development, where additional opportunities might arise. 

​

Title: Intern in the Ground Systems Engineering & Innovation Department - Navigation Support Office
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

​​You will join a team responsible for providing the spatial and temporal reference that enables European space missions to determine their position, navigate accurately, and maintain precise timing. The team supports missions from low Earth orbit to the Moon, delivering operational services, scientific expertise, and advanced analysis capabilities that are essential for mission success. 

 

​The team operates a global infrastructure for the collection, processing and analysis of satellite navigation and geodetic observations. By combining data from satellite navigation systems, laser ranging stations and other space geodetic techniques, the team generates high-precision products used by space missions, scientific communities and international partners. The team also contributes to the global geodetic infrastructure that underpins positioning, navigation, and timing services worldwide.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an intern, you will be part of an international and multidisciplinary environment involving precise satellite navigation, space geodesy, orbit determination, data analysis, and software development.

 

Depending on the specific project, you may contribute to: 

  • ​Analysing satellite and space geodetic observation data; 
  • ​developing or validating algorithms, models and software tools; 
  • ​supporting the generation and assessment of high-precision navigation and geodetic products; 
  • ​investigating satellite performance and orbit determination results; 
  • ​collaborating with experts from universities, research institutes, and international organisations.  

​ 

​You will be part of a team that combines operational responsibility with research and innovation. The working environment offers exposure to real mission applications, international collaborations and state-of-the-art technologies supporting current and future European space missions. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in precise navigation topics such as orbit determination and geodesy are an asset. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - Infrastructure Analytics and Anomaly Detection
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

Mission Operations IT (MOI-IT) and the Operational Control Centre (OCC) provide and operate the critical infrastructure, platforms, workplace services, and facilities that support ESA's space mission operations at ESOC. Our mission is to lead the evolution of MOI-IT & OCC services, delivering modern, resilient, and scalable solutions that enable current and future mission operations. We strive to be perceived as enablers for our customers and colleagues, supporting the deployment of innovative systems, applications, and operational capabilities across the organisation. 

 

The environment comprises a large-scale and highly available infrastructure supporting multiple operational missions, including servers, network devices, virtualised platforms, security services, monitoring systems, and operational applications. MOI-IT & OCC continuously evolves its infrastructure and platform services to provide greater flexibility, scalability, and operational efficiency while maintaining the highest standards of reliability and service delivery. 

 

Above all, MOI-IT & OCC aim to remain the home of safe, secure, and efficient space and ground operations.  

 

Interns joining the team will gain exposure to real operational environments, modern infrastructure technologies, cybersecurity, observability platforms, automation, and the unique challenges of supporting ESA's mission operations infrastructure. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​As an intern you will investigate and analyse the data available within the Mission Operations Infrastructure – Information Technology (MOI-IT) Elasticsearch, Logstash, and Kibana (ELK) infrastructure, which centrally collects the infrastructure logs across the different operational environments. The platform currently ingests around 200 GB of log data per day, with data volumes continuously growing as additional systems and services are onboarded. The objective is to understand the available data sources, identify operational relevant information, and create meaningful dashboards that support the operations teams in monitoring the infrastructure health, troubleshooting issues, and identifying long term trends. 

​ 

​Building on this analysis, you will explore and evaluate anomaly detection techniques to identify unusual behaviour, recurring issues, and early indicators of infrastructure degradation. The project will investigate how operational events can be correlated, visualised, and transformed into actionable notifications to help teams react more effectively to potential problems. The selected dashboards and anomaly detection capabilities will be implemented and demonstrated using the existing MOI-IT ELK platform, with a focus on improving operational visibility and providing proactive insights. 

​ 

​This project offers a great opportunity for hands-on experience with large scale log analytics, observability platforms, data visualisation, and operational intelligence techniques, while delivering tangible value to MOI-IT operations.

Title: Intern in the Industrial Policy and Auditing Department - BUC and PMSO Office Corporate Directorates
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The BUC&PMSO Office Corporate Directorates supports the Capability & Country Support Division, Industrial Policy and Auditing Department, based at ESTEC, which is responsible for implementing integration measures for the New Member States (NMS), Associate Members (AM), and Cooperating States (PECS) in cooperation with Programme Directorates and the ESA Technical Directorate. 

 

The Division manages in particular the Incentive Schemes and RPA Schemes which aim at developing and reinforcing sustainable industrial and academic capabilities in the space domain in these countries, through technology development contracts, selected through specific Calls for Activities, on topics related to ESA’s overall future programmes' activities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an intern, you will be integrated in the Capability & Country Support Division and will participate in the following tasks:

 

  • process automation in SharePoint using Power Automate, Power Apps, Python and HTML/CSS/JavaScript;
  • web-based apps development using React;
  • Linux for the virtual machines;
  • financial data handling and Power BI dashboards development;
  • creation of supporting tools and procedures for the team to function more efficiently.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Systems Department - End-to-End Systems Communications Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The End-To-End Systems Engineering Division (TEC-SE) is responsible for supporting projects for the Engineering of E2E systems, the associated security aspects, E2E systems integration/verification activities (SIV), and service preparation. To serve these functions, the Head of the End-To-End Systems Engineering Division defines and executes the associated technology developments and studies, as well as the verification and validation laboratory facilities, and supports the preparation of the relevant engineering standards.

 

TEC-SE supports and develops the following engineering competences:

  • E2E generic engineering tools, processes and competences;
  • All aspects of Security engineering at System level, including cyber security, crypto, hardware and software security, link and data protection, frameworks, processes, vulnerability assessment, countermeasures at system, element and application levels including AI and Quantum;
  • Telecommunication and connectivity systems and techniques;
  • Radio Navigation and PNT Systems and techniques, Formation Flying and RF metrology;
  • E2E System Comms for Telemetry, Telecommand and Payload Data Dissemination, Tracking, Ranging, Radio Science and Time Transfer functions.

 

The responsibilities include the definition of concepts and algorithms, System/Segment/Payload-System architecture and trade-offs, performance and budgets analysis, interfaces and data flows, design and processing of signal in space, networks and protocols for the Ground to Space, Space to Space links, for RF and Optical systems.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Assessment and End-to-End Analysis of Space Communications links, including Tracking Telemetry and Command (TT&C) links for Science and Exploration missions up to Deep Space, and/or Payload Data Transmission (PDT) Links for Earth Observation missions, as well as other lunar and planetary space communication links.

 

Your tasks will include:

  • assessing techniques;
  • performing simulations;
  • upgrading existing simulators in Python or other programming languages;
  • supporting the development and testing of Software Defined Radio prototyping platform for TT&C/PDT and other space communication applications (possibly using GNU radio).

 

The analysis and simulation tasks are covering assessment of modulation, coding, acquisition and tracking techniques for satellite communication links.

 

Participation as Communications expert team member in early design studies of future space missions from Earth Orbiting to Deep Space.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • good knowledge of MATLAB, Python or other related programming languages;
  • some familiarity with satellite communications.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Electrical Department - Equipment and Technology Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Radio Frequency Payloads & Technology Division (TEC-EF) is responsible from early definition to full qualification of RF payloads, TT&C subsystems, RF instruments and technologies for space and ground applications, including all equipment having a Radio Frequency space/ground interface and its associated Laboratories.

 

The division consists of four sections covering the following domains:

  • payloads with RF interface exploiting different technologies (e.g., analogue, digital, optical) including design and performance analysis tools and testing;
  • RF active and passive instruments, including design and performance analysis, engineering and testing up to sub-millimetre waves;
  • telemetry, tracking and control (TT&C) subsystems, payload data transmission (PDT) subsystems including deep space and near Earth transponders, proximity and intersatellite (ISL) link antennas and equipment, high speed downlink modulators, digital communication equipment;
  • wave-propagation and interaction, including signal impairments and regulatory aspects;
  • performance assessment of RF and Optical remote sensing data products (including spurious effects mitigation and calibration techniques);
  • antenna systems, architecture, technologies, and techniques for all space applications, including space vehicle TT&C and user segment terminals, sub-millimetre wave instruments and associated technologies, as well as antenna engineering, and RF testing of antenna and materials;
  • RF equipment and technologies, including RF passive technologies, RF active technologies, vacuum electronics and high power RF phenomena (multipactor, corona, power handling and passive intermodulation);
  • RF Payload digital equipment, and on-board Payload Signal and Data Processing algorithms and techniques for RF payloads and instruments in close collaboration with TEC-ED;
  • time and frequency generation and distribution equipment (e.g. microwave and optical with RF interfaces), techniques, performance tools, measurements and characterisation.

 

Within the TEC-EFE section, the team works on Time and Frequency (T&F) technologies: oscillators, atomic clocks, clock monitoring units or UTC laboratory tools for time realisation and time transfer require extensive characterisation and performance analysis under a wide range of operational and environmental conditions. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: AI-Assisted Analysis of Compact Clocks

 

You will contribute to the analysis and characterisation of space atomic clocks, with a particular focus on the investigation of compact clocks anomalies, including frequency jumps and their correlation with housekeeping telemetry parameters. Working with real measurement data obtained from long-term laboratory and environmental test campaigns, you will analyse clock performance and compare the observed behaviour against existing in-house clock models.

 

The activities will include post-processing and visualisation of time and frequency data from both conventional space-qualified atomic clocks and emerging low Size, Weight and Power (low-SWaP) timing technologies. You will identify trends, recurring patterns, frequency excursions and deviations from the expected clock behaviour, while assessing potential correlations with operational and environmental factors.

 

The internship will also provide exposure to state-of-the-art techniques for atomic clock monitoring and performance assessment. You will investigate and evaluate the applicability of data-driven approaches, including machine learning methods, for anomaly detection, classification and prediction. Particular emphasis will be placed on the development of tools and methodologies capable of supporting the automated analysis of large telemetry and frequency datasets.

 

Through this work, you will gain hands-on experience in space timing technologies, signal processing, statistical analysis, data analytics and machine learning, while contributing to activities relevant to current and future navigation, telecommunications and scientific missions relying on highly stable frequency references.

 

2) Topic 2: AI aided design for THz applications

 

The design of millimetre and sub-millimetre wave receivers featuring Schottky diode devices as non-linear elements for mixers and multipliers is traditionally done via a combination of 3D Electro-Magnetic (EM) simulations and linear/non-linear circuit simulations with harmonic-balanced capabilities. Software EM/circuit suites usually integrate both types of solvers with direct interaction between modules, but the optimisation and circuit topology including waveguide cavities, active device modelling and packaging rely heavily on the designer's experience. In that respect, the final circuit design often looks like the previous ones with only minor modifications.

 

Your objective for this internship is to train an Artificial Intelligence (AI) using existing designs successfully demonstrated in the past and recently published designs from peer-reviewed literature, in order to improve the performance of combined building blocks (mixer, multiplier) in a co-design approach at the higher integration level for best system performance. You will investigate the use of AI to explore novel circuit topologies with improved waveguide coupling, better non-linear device models, and possibly coupling to a thermal software package.

 

This work will greatly benefit potential future integration and performance optimisation of radiometer instruments on-board future meteorological missions (i.e. next generation of MetOp-SG, AWS (sub)-millimetre-wave payload instruments, EE12 Keystone THz spectrometer candidate missions, …).

 

Additionally, the new design methodology based on AI could be extended in the future to any transmit/receiver development at higher frequencies (D-band and above) where the packaging of active devices (transistors, diodes, …) plays a key role in the optimisation of the performance.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • good knowledge of signal processing, data analysis, probability and statistics;
  • prior experience in high-level programming languages such as Python and MATLAB.

 

The following will be considered assets:

  • knowledge of time-series analysis and measurement data processing;
  • experience with scientific computing and data visualisation tools;
  • familiarity with measurement systems, instrumentation or test automation;
  • knowledge of Machine Learning techniques.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.
