Title: Intern in the Systems Department - Navigation Systems Implementation and Validation Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The End-To-End Systems Engineering Division (TEC-SE) is responsible for supporting projects for the Engineering of E2E systems, the associated security aspects, E2E systems integration/verification activities (SIV), and service preparation. To serve these functions, the Head of the End-To-End Systems Engineering Division defines and executes the associated technology developments and studies, as well as the verification and validation laboratory facilities, and supports the preparation of the relevant engineering standards.

 

The E2E Systems Division consists of five sections and associated laboratory facilities:

  • Navigation Systems Definition Section;
  • Navigation Systems Implementation and Validation Section;
  • Systems Security Engineering Section;
  • Telecommunication Systems and Techniques Section;
  • E2E System Comms Section.

 

The role will be within the Navigation Systems Implementation and Validation Section, which provides expert advice and engineering support to ESA projects, programmes, and studies in the fields of Navigation and Earth Observation.

 

Future space missions are increasingly moving from traditional ground-centric data processing towards Distributed In-Space Processing (DISP) architectures, where computational resources are deployed directly on satellites, constellations, orbital platforms, or distributed space infrastructures. Such architectures can significantly reduce latency, optimise communication links, improve autonomy, and enable advanced services for Navigation, Positioning, Timing (PNT), Earth Observation (EO), and future space data centre concepts.
Within TEC-SEI and NAVLAB, there is a growing need to assess the benefits, limitations, and implementation challenges of distributed computing architectures in space and to establish laboratory capabilities capable of demonstrating representative operational scenarios through Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) experimentation.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will perform an end-to-end system study aimed at:

 

  1. Identifying and analysing candidate distributed in-space processing architectures applicable to:
    • satellite Navigation and PNT services;
    • space-based augmentation and integrity monitoring;
    • earth observation data processing and analytics;
    • future space data centre and orbital cloud computing concepts.
  2. Assessing key architectural trades, including:
    • centralised versus distributed processing;
    • edge computing in space;
    • data routing and communication requirements;
    • on-board AI/ML processing opportunities;
    • inter-satellite networking and resource sharing;
    • resilience, scalability, and cybersecurity considerations.
  3. Defining representative use cases relevant to ESA activities, including:
    • GNSS signal processing and integrity monitoring;
    • collaborative navigation services;
    • earth observation image pre-processing and data reduction;
    • autonomous onboard decision-making;
    • multi-satellite cooperative processing.
  4. Designing and preparing a Hardware-in-the-Loop compute node to be installed in the NAVLAB, enabling experimentation with representative distributed processing scenarios.

 

You will gain practical experience in:

  • space systems engineering;
  • distributed computing architectures;
  • navigation and PNT systems;
  • earth observation processing chains;
  • hardware-in-the-Loop testing methodologies;
  • high-performance embedded computing;
  • AI/ML applications for space systems;
  • laboratory integration and experimentation.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • good knowledge of Python and data analysis tools;
  • some familiarity with satellite systems and space communications;
  • some familiarity with cloud computing, data centre architectures or distributed computing;
  • basic understanding of artificial intelligence and high-performance computing concepts.

 

Familiarity with systems engineering and modelling/simulation tools would be an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - Space Weather & OPS-SAT Lab Mission Operations
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

OPS-SAT Space Lab is an international award winning project which for the first time allows European and Canadian external experimenters to develop, load and execute their own software and firmware in space free of charge. The first mission, OPS-SAT-1 (2019 – 2024), has now finished and two follow-on missions will be launched in 2027 and another is presently in flight (https://opssat.esa.int/). The Lab has evolved from a single mission to a multi-mission infrastructure. Many experimenters have used the Lab, ranging from other space agencies such as NASA, JAXA, CNES and DLR, to big primes such as Airbus down to university departments and start-ups. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​ESA must support the OPS-SAT experimenter community, helping them get familiar with the different OPS-SAT mission on-board environments and how to control the many sensors, actuators and payloads. You will provide this support directly interacting with the experimenters and arranging tests of their experiments through the various parts of the lifecycle and finally supervising the tests on the real spacecraft. You will also support the development cycle of spacecraft in preparation, launch, and commissioning.    

​ 

​Through these activities, you will be exposed to many of the important domains making up mission control and many of the institutions and companies that make up the experiment community. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Proven experience in software development (e.g. Linux, Python) is an asset. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the ESA Education Office - STEM Education, Didactics and E-Learning for Teachers
description_html:
Location
ESEC-Galaxia, Libin, Belgium   

 

In consideration of the geographical location of ESEC-Redu, successful applicants are recommended to have or obtain a driving license prior to the take up of duties.

Our team and mission

The intern positions concern the ESA Education programme, in particular the initiatives to support educators from formal and non-formal education venues, starting from early-ages up to upper secondary age groups, including: professional teacher and educator training, didactics resources, interdisciplinary school projects, thematic workshops and hackathons, and an international community of practice. Such activities are implemented at national level through the ESA ESERO project (www.esa.int/esero), a network of dedicated national offices and consortia of partners established by ESA in its Member and Associate States. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​Within the Education Office, the intern will contribute to the design and development of innovative educational resources and online learning activities aimed at supporting teachers and educators in integrating STEM topics and space-related content into their teaching. Particular emphasis will be placed on learner-centered methodologies, digital tools, accessibility and the effective use of ESA’s space-related resources in educational contexts.

 

Tasks will include: 

  • ​contributing to the creation of the new didactics activities and resources making use of space mission examples; 
  • ​contributing to the definition of learning objectives and e-learning products architecture; 
  • ​writing video message scripts, story boards, and developing physical video demonstrations; 
  • integrating e-learning content in the ESA Education LMS (Learning Management System); 
  • other STEM didactics-related tasks. 

​ 

​Learning areas: school-level STEM education, technology applied to school-level education, inquiry-based/project-based didactics, Instructional Design, Learning Management Systems, e-learning content Authoring Tools.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge of and/or experience in any of the following areas is a major asset:  

  • STEM subject knowledge and/or STEM education/didactics and/or Instructional Design; 
  • basic knowledge and/or experience in e-learning systems (LMS) and or Content Management Systems (CMS); 
  • basic knowledge and/or experience in video/image processing;
  • knowledge and background in both English and French is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics.

Title: Intern in the Electrical Department - Flight Software Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Avionics and EEE Division plays a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability and advancement of spacecraft avionics and component technologies. Its mission spans design assurance, qualification, and testing of EEE components, as well as radiation hardness assurance for space systems in its domain of responsibility. The division operates specialised laboratories and provides expertise to ESA projects, industry, and research partners. It actively disseminates knowledge through internal and external training, conference participation, and tutoring of PhD students, ESA Graduate Trainees (EGTs), and National Trainees, fostering innovation and professional growth.

 

Components
The Section is responsible for ensuring that all EEEE Components (passive & active) flown on ESA missions are suitable for their application and the environment for which they are intended, lead the development of EEEE Components and their qualification. European Space Component Coordination (ESCC) executives and actively supporting European Cooperation for Space Standardisation (ECSS) standardisation activities. The section conducts Research and Development (R&D) activities in their domain of responsibility. 


Radiation & Component Reliability
The Section is responsible for assessing all aspects of EEEE Component Radiation Effects to ensure EEEE Components flown on ESA Missions are suitable for the Radiation Environment and their assigned application for the duration of the mission. It is also responsible for all EEEE Component laboratory Test and Analysis activities. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the EEEE Component Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ESCC/ECSS standardisation activities.

 

Microelectronics 
The section is responsible for development and verification of all Microelectronic devices flown on ESA missions such as AI Accelerators, FPGAs, ASICs, Microprocessors, microelectronic processes, Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), radiation-aware design, prototyping and test for space‑grade microelectronics. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the Microelectronics Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ECSS standardisation activities.

 

Avionic Architecture 
Responsible for supporting all ESA missions in the area of Avionics Sub-System development, their verification and validation, and their qualification within the framework of the agency's strategic objectives. 

 

Data Handling
Responsible for on-board data handling sub-systems (Platform and Payload). Responsible for developing and qualifying equipment for data acquisition, processing, and distribution (buses, interfaces, mass‑memory, data‑processing chains, remote interface units, etc.). on-Board data processing is an important focus of the section including development of turn-key AI HW solutions for ESA Missions. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the Data Handling Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ECSS/CCSDS standardisation activities.

 

Flight Software
This section designs and maintains flight software for spacecraft control and payload management. It addresses real-time operating systems, fault detection and recovery, and software validation frameworks. The team also explores advanced concepts such as AI-assisted on-board processing, ensuring adaptability and resilience in increasingly complex missions. The section conducts R&D activities in their domain of responsibility and manages the Flight Software Laboratory Facility. Actively supporting ECSS/CCSDS standardisation activities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Enabling the Next Generation of Spacecraft with Linux

 

You will create and validate a mixed criticality multicore processor configuration accommodating both Linux and a real-time operating system (such as RTEMS). The solution will be deployed on a range of on-board computer platforms. The work will be published as a reference framework enabling a wide range of missions to benefit from novel hardware solutions developed within the Avionics and EEE Division.

 

This internship offers the opportunity to gain hands-on experience with (real-time) Linux in the context of space missions, work with cutting-edge open-source technologies, and contribute to the development of reliable software platforms for future spacecraft.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in the following areas is an asset:

  • Linux kernel configuration;
  • Yocto Project;
  • U-boot boot loader;
  • Real-time embedded software development;

Title: Intern in the ESA Security Office - Cyber Internal Audit Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

In the ESA Security Office, the Cybersecurity Industrial Audits play a major role in the security assurance process, contributing to the cybersecurity risk management associated to the organisation and infrastructure that the directorates deliver to their customers. The Cybersecurity Industrial Audits are part of the ESA Security Policy.   

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an intern, you will have the following tasks:  

 

  • contributing to the security assurance process and cybersecurity risk management for ESA's programmes under the European Space Security Policy;  
  • researching and analysing emerging Artificial Intelligence (AI) cybersecurity frameworks (such as FAICP, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, and NIST AI RMF);  
  • contributing to the analysis and design of integration solutions with the current Cyber Internal Audit Framework used across the supply chain of the ESA programs.  

 

Learning areas:  

 

  • ESA Cyber Internal Audit Framework;   
  • Cybersecurity Frameworks such as NIST, FACIP, SSDF, BSA or Secure Control Framework; 
  • Cybersecurity International Standards such as ISO27K series, ISO22301or ISO31K; 
  • Cybersecurity Guides and Guidelines such as OWASP, the CMMC or the Cloud Control Matrix; 
  • auditing standards and guidelines from ISACA or the IIA.  

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Basic knowledge or training in information security and auditing aspects will be considered as an asset. 

Knowledge of software development is considered as an asset. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Resilience, Navigation and Communication Product Assurance Section provides Product Assurance and Safety support to all missions of the Resilience, Navigation and Communication Directorate where AI technologies are starting to be used and developed.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Your work will consist of the analysis of the state of the art of product assurance and/or quality, as well as verification and validation techniques and activities applied to the development of AI systems for space and other critical system areas such as aircraft, automotive, train and nuclear industry. 

 

The aim of your project is to derive and propose Product Assurance or quality assurance techniques and verification and validation techniques to be used in the space domain. Identification of possible techniques to improve the security assurance of such systems is considered a plus.

 

Additionally, you will work with the PA team to assess the feasibility of using an AI tool (Xcert) for developing the requirement baseline and recording the verification artefacts.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Title: Intern in the Earth Observation Projects Department - CHIME Enhanced Spatial Detection Capabilities
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Within the Earth Observation Projects Department, the Copernicus Sentinel Expansion missions are currently under development. One of those missions is the CHIME (Copernicus Hyperspectral Imaging Mission for the Environment). CHIME plans to carry a unique visible to shortwave infrared spectrometer to provide routine hyperspectral observations to support new and enhanced services for sustainable agricultural and biodiversity management, as well as soil property characterisation.

 

You will join the CHIME project and work with the system engineering and mission-performance teams on end-to-end simulation, uncertainty propagation and the reliability of hyperspectral satellite data products.

 

Further details on the CHIME mission can be found at:

  • ESA - Copernicus Sentinel Expansion missions;
  • ESA - Going hyperspectral for CHIME;
  • CHIME: an overview of its mission, system and planning status; SPIE Proceedings Volume 12729; 1272909 (2023) The copernicus hyperspectral imaging mission for the environment (CHIME): an overview of its mission, system and planning status;
  • CHIME's end to end simulator (CHEES): simulating, testing and generating hyperspectral products;
  • Geolocation error impact on retrieval uncertainty: a new algorithm for high-resolution Earth observation missions;
  • Examples for typical CHIME Level 2 products: Prototyping Vegetation Traits Models in the Context of the Hyperspectral Chime Mission Preparation | IEEE Conference Publication | IEEE Xplore, Retrieval of carbon content and biomass from hyperspectral imagery over cultivated areas - ScienceDirect.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Enhanced spatial detection capabilities for Imaging spectrometer CHIME

 

Can imaging spectroscopy reveal materials smaller than a ground pixel, and can spatial enhancement improve their detection and quantification? You will investigate these questions for selected scientific applications using simulated or suitable reference observations. 

 

What you will do:

  • review the baseline pixel-binning approach and the telescope, spectrometer and pixel contributions to spatial performance;
  • develop a simulation and prototype processing algorithm;
  • evaluate sensitivity to noise, channel misregistration and differences in scene content between wavelengths;
  • quantify spatial improvement alongside any loss of radiometric accuracy or spectral fidelity;
  • document expected improvements and limitations of the proposed approach;
  • test the methods using representative mission scenarios and discuss the results with mission scientists and industrial simulator teams.

 

Learning objectives

By the end of the internship, you will be able to:

  • assess how instrument modulation transfer function (MTF) affects CHIME’s spatial resolution;
  • develop reproducible simulation and reconstruction methods to compare the baseline product with potential enhanced products;
  • evaluate achievable spatial improvement and its sensitivity to noise, channel misregistration and spectral differences;
  • communicate quantitative evidence to scientific, engineering and industrial specialists.

 

The principal outcome will be a tested software prototype that enables a feasibility assessment quantifying the achievable spatial improvement relative to the baseline CHIME product.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • background in physics, applied mathematics, Earth observation, signal processing or aerospace engineering;
  • experience with Python, numerical modelling and statistical analysis;
  • familiarity with uncertainty propagation, sensitivity analysis or imaging spectroscopy is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Future Missions and Architecture Department - Microwave Instruments Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Microwave Instruments Section is part of the Future Missions and Instruments Division, Future Missions and Architecture Department, Directorate of Earth Observation Programmes.

 

Within the Division, the Section is responsible for the definition, engineering, technology breadboarding and pre-development of active and passive microwave instruments for future Earth Observation research missions, e.g. Earth Explorers and Missions of Opportunity, and operational missions, e.g. Earth Watch, Copernicus and meteorology missions.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Performance Analysis Support for Sentinel-6 Next Generation

 

Sea level rise is a powerful climate indicator, since it is the result of changes occurring in Earth's climate system. Further, sea level rise poses a great threat to coastal communities and is therefore an important global concern for governments and policymakers. Copernicus Sentinel-6 first generation is the radar altimetry reference mission to provide sea-surface height measurements until at least 2030. To continue this legacy, the Sentinel-6 Next Generation mission is currently being developed. 

 

You will support the Sentinel-6 Next Generation international development by extending and improving the performance software tool for engineering and geophysical parameters. Furthermore, you will support the study team with the analysis and comparison of different performance parameters.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in the following areas is an asset:

  • Python;

Our team and mission

​​The Ground Systems Engineering and Innovation Department is responsible for all the ground systems engineering and support activities required to support mission operations and implement innovation.   

 

​The Department maintains and manages a full level of competences, technologies and services in all engineering disciplines related to ground systems, infrastructure, technology evolution and Engineering R&T and innovation.   

 

​The Department provides expert support in these areas to the Directorate of Operations for all current and potential missions and leads, in the role of architect, ground systems evolution and innovation implementation in the infrastructure and to other ESA programmes.   

 

​The Department is furthermore responsible for the overall technical innovation and technical standardisation coordination for the ground segment.   

​ 

​The Department is relying on the following domains of expertise:   

  • ​Ground Station Engineering;    
  • ​Flight Dynamics and Mission Analysis;   
  • ​Mission Operations Data Systems Engineering;  
  • ​Navigation Support;    
  • ​Multi-Mission Infrastructure – Ground Segment Integration and Testing.   

​   

​For further details, interested candidates are encouraged to visit:    

​http://www.esa.int/Our_Activities/Operations/gse/Building_infrastructure_on_Earth_to_support_satellites_in_space   ​ 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Data Foundation Platform Adoption for Missions Operations 


Spacecraft and their associated ground data systems generate vast amounts of data during the monitoring and control process. This data is stored, processed, and analysed within the mission operations ground segment to ensure spacecraft health, correlate events, and support the development of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms.  The Data Foundation Platform is a key initiative supporting the digital transformation of mission operations through trusted, governed, and accessible data. As the platform continues to evolve, increasing awareness, user engagement, and adoption across mission teams is critical to ensuring that its capabilities deliver value to the organisation.


 
In this topic, you will explore the Agency's data foundations and structures, focusing on how governed and accessible data can enable advanced mission operations, analytics, and AI. You will contribute to data governance activities related to data ownership, quality, lineage, accessibility, and compliance, while supporting the adoption of the Data Foundation Platform. Collaborating closely with operational teams and stakeholders, you will identify new use cases, help onboard data products and datasets, and assess how data-driven solutions can address operational challenges. Through this experience, you will gain hands-on experience with modern data platform concepts, stakeholder engagement, data engineering practices, and the promotion of data-driven innovation within mission operations.


 
You are invited to express your interest in specific areas of the topic. 

2) Topic 2: Artificial Intelligence for Space Operations 

 

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming a key technology in modern spacecraft operations applications. It is highly relevant to support automation, correlate data and execute pattern recognition and even enable digital assistants for operators, helping them operate the spacecraft and ground systems, including ground stations.  
 
As part of this topic, you will contribute to the AI programme of the Directorate.  
 
Spacecraft and ground segment operations still depend heavily on manual expert effort: interpreting telemetry, judging when something needs attention, working out what to do about it, and writing up the outcome. AI offers a way to support each of these steps and, more importantly, to connect them.

 

A system able to recognise unusual or degrading behaviour in telemetry can pass that insight downstream to planning and scheduling tools, which propose and sequence candidate actions; those actions, in turn, can be tested and refined against simulation engines (whose fidelity and representativeness can themselves have been enhanced with AI and digital twin solutions), closing the loop back to a sharper read on system state and better-informed decisions. None of this is useful, though, if it stays locked inside modelling pipelines that only specialists can query: generative AI, spanning text, code, and other modalities, can turn telemetry, engineering documentation, and analysis outputs alike into structured knowledge that operators interact with directly: asking questions in natural language, generating reports and summaries, or even drafting supporting code or configuration, rather than assembling insights by hand across disconnected tools.

 

The internship will explore how these strands (monitoring and diagnostics, decision support, enhanced simulation, and generative, multi-modal interaction with data) reinforce one another as parts of a single operational picture. The project will build on and extend existing operational tools, based on frequent inputs and feedback from end-users.

 

You will prototype and assess one such integrated approach, or a representative slice of it, on operational telemetry and documentation, leveraging agentic coding approaches and including automatic benchmarking against existing and synthetically generated benchmarks.

 

You are invited to express your interest in specific areas of the topic.  

3) Topic 3: Agentic software engineering for Space Mission Operations Systems

​

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming a key technology in modern spacecraft operations applications. It is highly relevant to support automation, correlate data, and execute pattern recognition and even enable digital assistants for operators, helping them operate the spacecraft and ground systems, including ground stations.   

​  

​As part of this topic, you will contribute to the AI programme of the Directorate.   

​ 

​The topic is related to investigating and implementing agentic AI approaches for software engineering in the space operations domain, covering two complementary scenarios: 

​ 

​1. Agentic development for existing software systems. This direction will investigate how AI agents can understand an existing codebase and support software evolution through tasks such as feature implementation, bug fixing, refactoring, testing, documentation and maintenance. PULSE, as the next generation Mission Control System, will be used as a representative existing operational software system. 

​2. Agentic development of new software components. This direction will investigate how agentic workflows can generate new software components for space applications from requirements and frequent interactions with end-users, including design, implementation, testing, documentation and iterative verification. 

​ 

You are invited to express your interest in specific areas of the topic.   

​ 

​4) Topic 4: Digital Twins, AI-Enhanced Simulation Models and Machine Learning for spacecraft operations and health monitoring 

​  

​Spacecraft health monitoring and control still rely largely on limit checking and expert interpretation of telemetry. Digital twins, physics-based or hybrid models kept synchronised with the live asset, offer a way to reason about system state beyond what raw telemetry shows: estimating unobservable parameters, simulating what-if scenarios, and predicting degradation before it becomes an anomaly. Combining these models with machine learning and, increasingly, with LLM-based reasoning over engineering documentation opens the way to end-to-end prognostics and health management. In this light, advancements in simulation technologies include the integration of Digital Twins concepts and the use of Machine Learning algorithms to process signals (time-series) and enhance the modelling of the complex spacecraft systems, predicting their behaviour under various operational conditions and helping support and address resolution of operational issue.    

​ 

You will investigate how digital twins, AI models and advanced simulation can be combined to support detection, diagnosis, prognosis and control of spacecraft subsystems, and will prototype and assess one such approach on representative telemetry.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge or academic specialisation in data-centric architectures and engineering, data science and artificial intelligence solutions, digital twins, time-series forecasting, machine learning or simulation technology to complex systems is an asset.   

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Climate Action, Sustainability and Science Department - AI for Earth Observation
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

You will be part of the ESA Φ-lab. Our mission is to accelerate the future of Earth Observation (EO) by embracing disruptive innovation and being the catalyst for disruptive/transformative innovation in the sector.

 

Our vision is to become an “EO innovation hub” connecting EO with a growing ecosystem of disruptive and transformative innovation like AI, ML, Quantum Computing, Edge Computing, Metamaterials, Photonics, etc. Many of the challenges posed by new technologies still need to be tackled at scientific, application and capability levels to deliver the maximum value from satellite-derived EO assets for our climate, society, and economy. The Φ-lab will bring together early career and senior researchers from a variety of disciplines across EO and disruptive/transformative innovation to contribute to developing innovative EO solutions.

 

We offer:

  • a stimulating multinational, interdisciplinary and open work environment;
  • access to high-performance computing infrastructure and unparalleled EO and technology expertise;
  • a unique opportunity to work on innovative solutions to address global challenges;
  • freedom and focus to conduct creative research while making an impact in relation to ESA’s strategy;
  • a wide network of relationships and collaboration with top academia, industry and research centres;
  • the opportunity to contribute to the Φ-lab strategy and activities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming Earth Observation (EO) by enabling the extraction of actionable insights from vast and complex datasets. ESA’s Φ-lab is at the forefront of this transformation through its active exploration of cutting-edge AI4EO technologies, spanning application-specific AI models, generative models, foundation models, and autonomous AI agents, with applications ranging from ground-based analytics to onboard satellite payload data processing (i.e., edge computing). 


You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: AI for Earth Observation

As part of this internship, you will actively engage with Φ-lab researchers, staff, and Visiting Researchers and support a set of Φ-lab AI4EO research activities, including Geospatial Foundation Models (GFMs) for EO.  
You’ll gain hands-on experience across a number of steps of the AI development cycle: from EO data preparation and model training to benchmarking and testing of developed models. 

 

Tasks may include: 

  • preparing EO datasets for AI pipelines;
  • training and benchmarking AI models for EO applications;
  • supporting AI design and optimisation;
  • supporting the ideation, preparation, and hosting of Φ-lab Challenges related to AI4EO.


2) Topic 2: Agentic AI for Earth Observation

As part of this internship, you will develop and evaluate agentic AI for Earth Observation, contributing to research on how agents discover and access EO resources, plan and execute multi-step workflows, interact with external tools, and produce results that are scientifically grounded. 
 

Tasks may include: 

  • designing agentic workflows that decompose high-level EO objectives into sequences of analysis and processing steps;
  • integrating EO tools and data services into agentic systems — data discovery, retrieval, processing, and interaction with specialised models;
  • investigating reasoning, planning, and tool-use strategies that let agents adapt workflows to intermediate results and resource availability;
  • building and testing prototype EO assistants, combining language models, geospatial foundation models, scientific models, and external tools as needed;
  • benchmarking agentic systems on task completion, tool selection, reliability, efficiency, robustness, and scientific correctness;
  • contributing to analysis, technical documentation, and scientific dissemination of results.

 

You will gain hands-on experience in agent design, tool integration, scientific workflow automation, and evaluation for geospatial applications — and develop a working understanding of what it takes to make autonomous AI systems reliable, transparent, and scientifically trustworthy in Earth Observation.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

The following elements are considered an asset:

  • background in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Remote Sensing or related fields;
  • knowledge and previous experience in AI4EO and EO data processing.

 
Familiarity with the following would be appreciated:

  • knowledge of agentic AI concepts with an interest in their application to Earth Observation;
  • foundation Models for EO (Geospatial Foundation Models - GFM);
  • Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR);
  • previous participation in scientific challenges related to AI or AI4EO;
  • knowledge of Edge computing or other disruptive computing paradigms for EO.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

description_text: Location ESRIN, Frascati, Italy Our team and mission You will be part of the ESA Φ-lab. Our mission is to accelerate the future of Earth Observation (EO) by embracing disruptive innovation and being the catalyst for disruptive/transformative innovation in the sector. Our vision is to become an “EO innovation hub” connecting EO with a growing ecosystem of disruptive and transformative innovation like AI, ML, Quantum Computing, Edge Computing, Metamaterials, Photonics, etc. Many of the challenges posed by new technologies still need to be tackled at scientific, application and capability levels to deliver the maximum value from satellite-derived EO assets for our climate, society, and economy. The Φ-lab will bring together early career and senior researchers from a variety of disciplines across EO and disruptive/transformative innovation to contribute to developing innovative EO solutions. We offer: a stimulating multinational, interdisciplinary and open work environment; access to high-performance computing infrastructure and unparalleled EO and technology expertise; a unique opportunity to work on innovative solutions to address global challenges; freedom and focus to conduct creative research while making an impact in relation to ESA’s strategy; a wide network of relationships and collaboration with top academia, industry and research centres; the opportunity to contribute to the Φ-lab strategy and activities. Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int Field(s) of activity for the internship Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming Earth Observation (EO) by enabling the extraction of actionable insights from vast and complex datasets. ESA’s Φ-lab is at the forefront of this transformation through its active exploration of cutting-edge AI4EO technologies, spanning application-specific AI models, generative models, foundation models, and autonomous AI agents, with applications ranging from ground-based analytics to onboard satellite payload data processing (i.e., edge computing). You can choose among the following topics: 1) Topic 1: AI for Earth Observation As part of this internship, you will actively engage with Φ-lab researchers, staff, and Visiting Researchers and support a set of Φ-lab AI4EO research activities, including Geospatial Foundation Models (GFMs) for EO. You’ll gain hands-on experience across a number of steps of the AI development cycle: from EO data preparation and model training to benchmarking and testing of developed models. Tasks may include: preparing EO datasets for AI pipelines; training and benchmarking AI models for EO applications; supporting AI design and optimisation; supporting the ideation, preparation, and hosting of Φ-lab Challenges related to AI4EO. 2) Topic 2: Agentic AI for Earth Observation As part of this internship, you will develop and evaluate agentic AI for Earth Observation, contributing to research on how agents discover and access EO resources, plan and execute multi-step workflows, interact with external tools, and produce results that are scientifically grounded. Tasks may include: designing agentic workflows that decompose high-level EO objectives into sequences of analysis and processing steps; integrating EO tools and data services into agentic systems — data discovery, retrieval, processing, and interaction with specialised models; investigating reasoning, planning, and tool-use strategies that let agents adapt workflows to intermediate results and resource availability; building and testing prototype EO assistants, combining language models, geospatial foundation models, scientific models, and external tools as needed; benchmarking agentic systems on task completion, tool selection, reliability, efficiency, robustness, and scientific correctness; contributing to analysis, technical documentation, and scientific dissemination of results. You will gain hands-on experience in agent design, tool integration, scientific workflow automation, and evaluation for geospatial applications — and develop a working understanding of what it takes to make autonomous AI systems reliable, transparent, and scientifically trustworthy in Earth Observation. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship. Additional requirements The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset. During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored. The following elements are considered an asset: background in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Remote Sensing or related fields; knowledge and previous experience in AI4EO and EO data processing. Title: Intern in the Ground Systems Engineering & Innovation Department - Optical Technologies Section
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

​​​The Ground Systems Engineering and Innovation Department is responsible for all the ground systems engineering and support activities required to support mission operations and implement innovation. 

 

​The Department maintains and manages a full level of competences, technologies and services in all engineering disciplines related to ground systems, infrastructure, technology evolution and Engineering R&T and innovation. 

 

​The Department provides expert support in these areas to the Directorate of Operations for all current and potential missions and leads, in the role of architect, ground systems evolution and innovation implementation in the infrastructure. The Department is furthermore responsible for the overall technical standardisation coordination for the ground segment, in particular in the Management Council of the Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS).

 

The Department is relying on the following domains of expertise: 

  • ​Ground Station Engineering; 
  • ​Flight Dynamics and Mission Analysis; 
  • ​Mission Operations Data Systems Engineering; 
  • ​Navigation Support; 
  • ​Multi-Mission Infrastructure – Ground Segment Integration and Testing. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Measuring Space with Light: Satellite Retroreflector Arrays In-Orbit Validation Using Laser Ranging 

 

​​Satellite Laser Ranging (SLR) is one of the most accurate space measurement techniques available today, enabling millimetre-level orbit determination and supporting a wide range of scientific and operational applications as precise orbit determination (POD), geodesy, Earth observation missions, navigation systems and space debris tracking. Within this context ESA offers an exciting internship opportunity for students interested in optics, space systems, data analysis and laser technologies to contribute to the in-orbit validation of spacecraft Retroreflector Arrays (RRAs). Using real mission data acquired from operational SLR stations, you will help analyse laser returns, assess optical performance in orbit, and develop innovative methods to characterise the behaviour of retroreflector arrays under real operational conditions. 

​ 

You will contribute to the development and application of advanced techniques for the in-orbit validation of spacecraft Retroreflector Arrays (RRAs) through Satellite Laser Ranging observations. Activities may include: 

 

  • ​designing and supporting laser ranging observation campaigns for satellites equipped with RRAs; 
  • ​modelling retroreflector array performance, including signal return characteristics, pulse spreading and observation geometry effects; 
  • ​analysing high-precision laser ranging measurements to assess RRA performance and ranging accuracy in orbit; 
  • ​comparing in-orbit observations with numerical predictions to validate optical models and mission assumptions; 
  • investigating performance trends and anomalies caused by spacecraft attitude, thermal conditions or operational constraints; 
  • ​developing data-analysis pipeline and visualisation tools to support the interpretation of SLR measurements; 
  • ​contributing to technical reports and engineering assessments supporting current and future ESA missions. 

​ 

What you will gain experience with:

  • ​Satellite Laser Ranging systems and optical ground stations; 
  • ​precision optical measurements and timing systems;
  • ​numerical modelling and simulation of optical payloads; 
  • ​spacecraft orbit and attitude geometry;
  • ​scientific data analysis and visualisation tools; 
  • ​real mission data from satellites operating in orbit. 

​

This internship offers a unique opportunity to gain experience at the intersection of spacecraft engineering, optics, laser systems and data analytics, contributing to the validation of technologies that enable millimetre-level satellite positioning and support scientific and operational space missions.

2) Topic ​2: Optical Systems Performance Characterisation Using Astronomical Observations 

 

​​Laboratory measurements and design analyses provide the reference expectations of the performance of an optical system. However, the operational verification of an optical system requires the ability to assess its image quality and its system-level performance using observational data acquired under real operating conditions. Stellar observations provide a unique and powerful means to evaluate the end-to-end performance behaviour of a telescope, enabling the characterisation of optical, geometric, photometric, tracking and dynamic performance directly from observational data. 

​ 

​The main objective of the internship is to develop a methodology and establish a comprehensive framework for the characterisation of optical systems from on-sky observations under real operational conditions and to identify measurable indicators that describe the overall performance of the instrument. 

 

​The activities will address topics such as: 

 

  • ​field-dependent image quality characterisation; 
  • ​optical distortion and geometric calibration;
  • ​throughput, vignetting, and photometric uniformity; 
  • ​tracking accuracy and dynamic effects;
  • ​wavefront behaviour and wavefront error estimation; 
  • ​field-dependent aberration characterisation;
  • ​focus and optical alignment assessment; 
  • ​stability and repeatability of performance over time;
  • ​comparison between measured performance and optical design predictions;
  • ​definition of performance indicators suitable for operational performance assessment. 

​ 


You will contribute to: 

 

  • ​analysis of observational datasets acquired under representative operational conditions;
  • ​development of methods and automated processing workflows for optical performance assessment;
  • extraction and visualisation of image quality, geometric, photometric, and stability metrics;
  • investigation of methodologies to characterise optical performance across the field of view;
  • ​generation of performance maps, statistical summaries, and trend analyses;
  • ​assessment of the impact of operational and environmental conditions on system behaviour;
  • ​comparison of observational results with optical models and expected performance;
  • ​consolidation of characterisation results into a coherent set of performance indicators and assessment products;
  • ​preparation of technical documentation and presentation of results;
  • ​verification and refinement of the optical model and optical prescription through comparison between measured performance and theoretical predictions. 

​ 

​This internship offers practical experience at the intersection of optical engineering, astronomical instrumentation, scientific computing, and performance verification, contributing to the assessment and validation of advanced telescope systems in an operational environment.​​

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

1) Topic 1: Measuring Space with Light: Satellite Retroreflector Arrays In-Orbit Validation Using Laser Ranging 

 

  • a strong interest in space and ground-based systems, optics, laser technologies, and satellite applications;
  • basic knowledge of optics, photonics, astrodynamics, spacecraft engineering, or scientific instrumentation; 
  • experience with scientific programming and data analysis (e.g. Python, MATLAB, or similar tools);
  • familiarity with numerical modelling, signal processing, or statistical analysis would be considered an asset;
  • good analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills;
  • the ability to work both independently and as part of an international multidisciplinary team; 
  • prior experience with astronomical instrumentation, satellite tracking, optical measurements, or space mission analysis is beneficial but not required;  
  • curiosity, enthusiasm for learning, and a passion for applying engineering and scientific methods to real mission challenges are highly valued. 

 

2) Topic 2: Optical Systems Performance Characterization Using Astronomical Observations 

 

Applicants should be pursuing a degree in: 

 

  • optical engineering; 
  • physics; 
  • astronomy or astrophysics; 
  • aerospace engineering; 
  • applied mathematics; 
  • computer science; 
  • or a related scientific or engineering discipline.

 

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be advantageous: 

 

  • optics and imaging systems; 
  • scientific programming (Python); 
  • image processing and data analysis; 
  • astronomical instrumentation; 
  • statistical analysis and data visualisation. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.

Title: Intern in the Ground Systems Engineering & Innovation Department - Visualisation and Communication
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

​​The Ground Systems Engineering and Innovation Department is responsible for all the ground systems engineering and support activities required to support mission operations and implement innovation.   

 

​The Department maintains and manages a full level of competences, technologies and services in all engineering disciplines related to ground systems, infrastructure, technology evolution and Engineering R&T and innovation.   

 

​The Department provides expert support in these areas to the Directorate of Operations for all current and potential missions and leads, in the role of architect, ground systems evolution and innovation implementation in the infrastructure and to other ESA programmes.   

 

​The Department is furthermore responsible for the overall technical innovation and technical standardisation coordination for the ground segment.   

​ 

​The Department is relying on the following domains of expertise:   

  • ​Ground Station Engineering;    
  • ​Flight Dynamics and Mission Analysis;   
  • ​Mission Operations Data Systems Engineering;   
  • ​Navigation Support;    
  • ​Multi-Mission Infrastructure – Ground Segment Integration and Testing.   

​   

​For further details, interested candidates are encouraged to visit:    

​http://www.esa.int/Our_Activities/Operations/gse/Building_infrastructure_on_Earth_to_support_satellites_in_space   ​ 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) ​Topic 1: Mission-Agnostic Space Operations Visualisation Platform 
 

​Modern mission operations require intuitive ways to explore and understand complex information. In this internship, you will help extend an existing visualisation tool with additional features and data integrations, to support mission planning, spacecraft monitoring, and training activities.  

 

​You will contribute to the development of an advanced 3D visualisation platform for space missions operations. This includes displaying spacecraft trajectories, communication networks, events, and operational annotations in a clear and engaging way. 

 

​Throughout this internship, you will gain experience in: 

  • ​developing interactive 3D and virtual reality applications; 
  • integrating and visualising operational data from different sources; 
  • ​designing features that improve situational awareness and decision making; 
  • ​working with modern game engines, such as Godot.

2) ​Topic 2: ​Communication and Community Building for Space Innovation 

 

The OPS-GA Division develops a variety of innovative projects that support ESA's mission operations activities in areas such as data, artificial intelligence, software engineering, and digital transformation. Many of these projects are released under an ESA Community Licence to encourage collaboration and enable external communities to contribute, learn, and innovate alongside ESA. 

​ 

​In this internship, you will help increase the visibility and impact of these projects by developing communication strategies, creating engaging content, and identifying effective channels for outreach. Collaborating closely with technical teams and communication specialists, you will transform complex engineering concepts into clear and compelling messages tailored to different audiences. 

​ 

​As part of these activities, you will contribute to the maintenance and improvement of project websites, document communication activities, support the creation of presentations and promotional material, and help define communication guidelines that can be applied across multiple projects. 

​ 

​Throughout this internship, you will gain experience in: 

  • ​developing communication strategies for innovative space and technology projects; 
  • ​translating complex technical concepts into engaging and accessible narratives; 
  • ​working with technical experts and communication professionals to promote project outcomes; 
  • ​understanding how AI, data, and innovation projects contribute to ESA mission operations; 
  • ​measuring and documenting the impact of communication and outreach activities. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

For Topic 1, experience with 3D graphics or visualization software (i.e., game engines, such as Godot, Unreal Engine, or Unity) is an asset. 

 

For Topic 2, the ability to communicate complex topics to diverse audiences through presentations, web content, and other communication materials is an asset.  

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Ground Systems Eng. & Innovation Dep. - Global Interplanetary Trajectory Optimisation
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

You will be part of the Mission Analysis Section, Flight Dynamics Division, Ground Systems Engineering Department.   

 

The Mission Analysis Section is entrusted with mission studies for future terrestrial, lunar and interplanetary missions as well as scientific missions located in planetary or lunar libration points. The emphasis is typically on trajectory and attitude related aspects, and on supporting ground segment design and operations. This includes trade-offs for selection of the nominal mission trajectory, definition of manoeuvering strategies, optimisation of orbital manoeuvres (low- and high-thrust propulsion, including rocket ascent trajectories), calculation of propellant budget, analysis of launch window, analysis of orbit perturbations and navigation. The task also includes the development of the necessary analytical and numerical methods and software tools. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​Trajectory optimisation plays a central role in mission design and analysis at ESA’s European Space Operations Centre (ESOC). Interplanetary trajectories, lunar tours, and other complex missions all rely on sophisticated global search and optimisation methods. Typically, coarse initial solutions are refined through local, gradient-based techniques to achieve the required mission accuracy and feasibility. 

 

​The Mission Analysis Section at ESOC employs different tools for trajectory design and optimisation, and has defined a unified software framework called SALTO. This framework implements an innovative approach for interplanetary trajectory design, separating the energy-based unphased solutions from the phasing problem, although still requiring a certain degree of expert input in order to efficiently obtain mission solutions. 

​ 

​You will contribute to the development of SALTO, with a particular focus on global optimisation techniques, to find wide ranges of mission possibilities once an interplanetary mission profile is established. Your tasks include, but are not limited to: 

  • ​Investigating the integration of global optimisation methods (e.g. genetic algorithms, differential evolution, or other metaheuristics) within the SALTO framework;
  • ​improving the usability, robustness, and automation of the tool based on user experience and mission requirements; 
  • ​enhancing the performance of SALTO through parallelisation and algorithmic optimisation;
  • ​investigating the use of General Purpose Graphical Processing Units (GP-GPUs) to accelerate the global search methods. 

​

The use of GPUs is particularly of interest for this internship. ESOC has developed a set of GPU-based tools, which can be used to accelerate the global optimisation methods. The position offers the opportunity to contribute to the future of ESA’s mission design capabilities, combining theoretical research with hands-on software development and validation on real-world problems.​

description_text: Location ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany Our team and mission You will be part of the Mission Analysis Section, Flight Dynamics Division, Ground Systems Engineering Department. The Mission Analysis Section is entrusted with mission studies for future terrestrial, lunar and interplanetary missions as well as scientific missions located in planetary or lunar libration points. The emphasis is typically on trajectory and attitude related aspects, and on supporting ground segment design and operations. This includes trade-offs for selection of the nominal mission trajectory, definition of manoeuvering strategies, optimisation of orbital manoeuvres (low- and high-thrust propulsion, including rocket ascent trajectories), calculation of propellant budget, analysis of launch window, analysis of orbit perturbations and navigation. The task also includes the development of the necessary analytical and numerical methods and software tools. Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int Field(s) of activity for the internship ​​Trajectory optimisation plays a central role in mission design and analysis at ESA’s European Space Operations Centre (ESOC). Interplanetary trajectories, lunar tours, and other complex missions all rely on sophisticated global search and optimisation methods. Typically, coarse initial solutions are refined through local, gradient-based techniques to achieve the required mission accuracy and feasibility. ​The Mission Analysis Section at ESOC employs different tools for trajectory design and optimisation, and has defined a unified software framework called SALTO. This framework implements an innovative approach for interplanetary trajectory design, separating the energy-based unphased solutions from the phasing problem, although still requiring a certain degree of expert input in order to efficiently obtain mission solutions. ​ ​You will contribute to the development of SALTO, with a particular focus on global optimisation techniques, to find wide ranges of mission possibilities once an interplanetary mission profile is established.
