Title: Intern in the Spaceship ECSAT team
description_html:
Location
ECSAT, Harwell, United Kingdom  

Due to the location of ECSAT and current UK legislation, only UK citizens, students enrolled in a UK university, or those with pre-settled status (right to study) in the UK are eligible to apply for this internship.

Our team and mission

​​The Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration (D/HRE) is the main ESA entity in charge of supporting and coordinating efforts towards the current and the future endeavours of human spaceflight. The exploration activities are part of the strategic plans in securing a central role for Europe with respect to the global initiatives. The strategy includes three destinations where humans will work with robots to gather new knowledge: Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the Moon, and Mars.  

​ 

​The “Spaceship ECSAT” initiative is investigating low Technology Readiness Level (TRL) technologies for supporting the future cislunar space mission as well as surface activities on the Moon as part of the Exploration Preparation, Research and Technology (ExPeRT) team. This multidisciplinary, innovation-driven team composed of researchers, graduate and undergraduate students is based at the ESA European Centre for Space Applications and Telecommunications (ECSAT). The founding idea behind this initiative is to prepare the future of space exploration. To do so, a pragmatic and research-focused approach is adopted, and knowledge acquired is disseminated within ESA, partners and the relevant scientific community.  

​ 

​Within Spaceship ECSAT, we have a number of fields where we carry out different projects. These fields are:  

​ 

  • ​demonstrating disruptive technologies such as Virtual/Augmented Reality, collaborative robotics and their potential use cases for exploration;
  • ​investigating novel concepts in the domain of Space Resources/In-Situ Resource Utilisation, to enable sustainable human exploration;
  • ​topics related to ‘off world living’, e.g. human factors, design and concept illustration.

​ 

​We are continually looking for innovative applicants with skills or interests in these areas to join the Spaceship ECSAT team. 

​ 

​For more information on the Spaceship ECSAT, please look at the ESA blog (Spaceship ECSAT).

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Robotics
Our Spaceship team is always on the lookout for talented and motivated persons to join our projects and contribute to ESA’s exploration activities. The main areas in which the initiative is currently active are remote manipulation, embedded systems and machine learning.


2) Topic 2: VR/XR
Our Spaceship team is always on the lookout for talented and motivated persons to join our projects and contribute to ESA’s exploration activities. The main areas in which the initiative is currently active are virtual and augmented reality applied to training, graphic design, human-machine interfaces & robotics.


3) Topic 3: Human Factors
Our Spaceship team is always on the lookout for talented and motivated persons to join our projects and contribute to ESA’s exploration activities. The main areas in which the initiative is currently active are decision making and outreach with a focus on embedded systems, graphic design and human-machine interfaces.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

A background in robotics, computer science, electrical/electronic engineering, mechatronics, aerospace engineering or a related field (Topic 1), together with an interest in virtual and augmented reality, simulation, visualisation (Topic 2) and human–machine interfaces (Topic 3), would be an asset. Familiarity with tools such as ROS/ROS 2, Unreal Engine or Simulink, and an interest in their application to space exploration and planetary surface operations, would also be advantageous.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Title: Intern in the Communication Department - Outreach Activities for Italian Audiences
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

The ESA Member States Outreach Office interfaces and coordinates the ESA Member States Advisory Communication Committee to the Director General (ACC), while ensuring the harmonisation, development and implementation of public and media relations activities as well as social media coverage across the various ESA establishments and Member States.
The team, based at ESA ESRIN in Frascati, Italy, focuses on communication activities for the ESRIN establishment as well as for Italy, Greece, Hungary, Romania and Slovenia.
They work with governments, the press and the general public to inform and educate about all of our space activities, from astronauts to asteroids, Earth observation to satellites flying to Jupiter. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Outreach Activities for International Audiences

 

How do we engage diverse audiences across Europe? How can we make the best use of digital platforms to share compelling stories about space? What types of outreach activities help bring these stories to life and connect with people?


By joining the Communications team at ESA's Establishment in Italy (ESRIN), you will gain hands-on experience in digital communications and public outreach. Working alongside experienced professionals, you will develop your understanding of how international organisations create and deliver effective, integrated communication campaigns in a multilingual environment.

 

Your main tasks will include:

 

  • supporting, in close collaboration with the Public Relations team, the organisation of the School Days taking place in March and April and the organisation of the ESA Open Day, taking place at the end of September.

 

Additional tasks will include:

 

  • assisting with organisational and logistical activities;
  • drafting communications articles in English and Italian about PR events taking place at ESRIN;
  • identifying and contacting event stakeholders;
  • liaising with colleagues and other stakeholders within the Communication Department.

Title: Intern in the Operations Strategy and Coordination Office - Innovation and Knowledge Management
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of the Director of Operations, the Operations Strategy and Coordination Office is responsible for preparing and formulating strategies in collaboration with the Director and the Management Team, and providing the Directorate’s overarching coordination function. 

 

The main responsibilities of the Operations Strategy and Coordination Office, which works directly with the Director of Operations, are: 

 
Preparing and formulating strategies in collaboration with the Director and the Operations Directorate (D/OPS) Management Team. This includes: 

 

  • formulating, communicating and evolving the Directorate’s overall strategy. Leading the Directorate’s strategy evolution; 
  • establishing and leading the Directorate Innovation Governance e.g. through D/OPS-wide innovation cups; 
  • coordinating the strategic planning and implementation of the Directorate Research and Technology (R&T) activities, in close cooperation with the relevant other ESA actors; 
  • fostering the development and supporting the establishment of the Directorate’s strategic partnerships. Coordinating and fostering cooperation and exchange with academia, other space agencies, and industry; 
  • developing the Directorate’s Business Intelligence, by monitoring and analysing the external and internal environment and overlooking the socio-economic impact of the Directorate’s business; 
  • economic impact of the Directorate’s business. 

 
Managing the Directorate’s governance process with respect to the Mission Operations Infrastructure (the overall system infrastructure that is required to operate space missions):

 

  • Investment and Core Technical Expertise strategic planning and budget management. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will be based at the European Space Operations Centre (ESOC): the main mission control centre for the European Space Agency (ESA).  

 

ESOC’s primary function is to operate unmanned spacecraft on behalf of ESA as well as launch and early orbit phases. ESOC plays a role of sole service provider and its resources are dedicated to mission operations.  

 

Two of the challenges the Office faces are supporting the innovation culture in a high reliability environment, and the capturing and dissemination of the vast amounts of knowledge collected as part of this work.  

 

You will enjoy supporting Innovation and Knowledge Management at ESOC, whose aims will be defined depending on the skill of the candidate. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Additional requirements: 

A STEM background is an asset. 

Knowledge Management experience is an asset. 

Due to the nature of the post, a commitment of six months is preferred, depending on the candidate’s availability.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Ground Systems Engineering & Innovation Department - Mission Analysis Section
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

You will be part of the Mission Analysis Section, Flight Dynamics Division, Ground Systems Engineering Department.   

 

The Mission Analysis Section is entrusted with mission studies for future terrestrial, lunar and interplanetary missions as well as scientific missions located in planetary or lunar libration points. The emphasis is typically on trajectory and attitude related aspects, and on supporting ground segment design and operations. This includes trade-offs for selection of the nominal mission trajectory, definition of manoeuvering strategies, optimisation of orbital manoeuvres (low- and high-thrust propulsion, including rocket ascent trajectories), calculation of propellant budget, analysis of launch window, analysis of orbit perturbations and navigation. The task also includes the development of the necessary analytical and numerical methods and software tools. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​Comet Interceptor, the first ESA F-class mission under the Cosmic Vision Programme, targets a yet-to-be-discovered dynamically new or long-period comet. To retain the ability to select a target even after launch, the spacecraft will wait in a parking orbit around the Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point. Once a suitable comet is identified, the transfer trajectory may follow one of two baseline strategies: a direct escape from L2 or an escape assisted by a lunar gravity assist. A small number of particularly challenging targets may require more complex trajectories exploiting an Earth powered swing-by, the weak stability boundary, or a Delta-V Earth Gravity Assist (ΔVEGA). 

​ 

​In this internship, you will develop a trajectory optimisation framework based on ESA's mission analysis software infrastructure to investigate the most suitable transfer strategies under the full-ephemeris dynamics of the Sun-Earth-Moon system. Even when formulated within the simplified Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP), the transfer trajectory optimisation problem exhibits a rich landscape of local optima and a wide variety of feasible trajectory geometries. 

The study will investigate:

  • The range of comet encounter geometries in the ecliptic plane that can be achieved within the spacecraft propulsion capabilities;
  • the influence of the parking orbit characteristics, including variations resulting from launch-window and injection conditions;
  • ​the exploitation of the unstable manifolds associated with the parking orbit to reduce the required ΔV;
  • the influence of the encounter date optimisation;
  • the impact of mission and operational constraints, as well as available flexibility on the optimisation of encounter conditions for scientific return;
  • the sensitivity of transfer solutions to uncertainties in the target orbit knowledge and the evolution of these solutions as orbit determination improves;
  • ​the trade-off between transfer time and ΔV through Pareto-front analysis, comparing at least the direct escape and lunar gravity-assist strategies.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Title: Intern in Exploration Science Strategy
description_html:
Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany or ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands

Our team and mission

Within the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Directorate for Human and Robotic Exploration, the Exploration Science activities are a cornerstone of the Explore2040 strategy, driving innovation at the intersection of human exploration and scientific discovery. It integrates exploration-focused science, essential for future missions, with exploration-enabled science, leveraging space for groundbreaking research. With access to ground-based analogues, the ISS, future commercial LEO platforms, the Moon, and Mars, the programme offers unique opportunities for transformative research in diverse environments. Guided by European values of collaboration, excellence, and responsibility, the programme emphasizes open science, international cooperation, and inspiring future generations. From developing countermeasures for spaceflight to searching for life on Mars, ESA Exploration Science advances knowledge for space and Earth alike.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

We are offering an internship opportunity to support the consolidation of the Human and Robotic Exploration science strategy. You will help bring together a broad set of inputs, including ESA white papers, existing science strategy and roadmap documents, strategy documents from other space agencies, and peer-reviewed scientific articles. The objective is to organise these sources into a coherent knowledge base, extract the main scientific priorities and recurring themes, and support the preparation of concise synthesis material that can inform future science planning.

 

Tasks include:  

 

  • collect, catalogue and structure relevant strategy documents, white papers, roadmaps and scientific articles related to HRE science;
  • compare the priorities, science questions, capabilities and implementation approaches identified across ESA material and documents from other agencies;
  • map the scientific literature against the main HRE science themes to highlight evidence, trends, gaps and emerging topics;
  • prepare clear summaries, tables, and visual synthesis material to support discussions within the team and contribute to the consolidation of future science strategy documents;
  • apply existing AI/Machine Learning tools to identify knowledge gaps;
  • through this work, you will learn how science strategy is developed in an international space agency context and how scientific evidence, community inputs and programme constraints are translated into strategic priorities.   

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background required:

 

  • Master’s level background in data science, space science, life sciences, physical sciences, engineering, or another discipline relevant to human and robotic exploration;
  • good ability to review, analyse and synthesise scientific literature, white papers, roadmaps and strategy documents;
  • interest in human spaceflight, microgravity research, exploration science, or the development of science strategies for space programmes;
  • good command of Microsoft Office tools, in particular Word, Excel and PowerPoint, for document preparation, source tracking, tables and synthesis material;
  • basic knowledge of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and statistical  methods.  

 

Assets:

 

  • experience with reference management and literature review tools, such as Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote, Web of Science, Scopus, or similar platforms, would be an asset;
  • familiarity with artificial intelligence-assisted tools for literature screening, document analysis, summarisation, text mining or knowledge organisation would be an asset, together with the ability to use such tools critically and responsibly;
  • proficiency in Python or other relevant programming languages.   

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Space Safety Programme - Mission Implementation Division (Clear Space 1)
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The ESA Space Safety Department takes care of all potential hazards and threats from space or in space, which can impact human activities, infrastructure, or related applications. The spectrum of tasks ranges from gathering the basic understanding of space hazards originating from our Sun, from human space debris, or from asteroids potentially colliding with the Earth. It also addresses basic approaches to mitigate these hazards and to implement space systems end-to-end in a sustainable and eco-compatible way. Moreover, several corner stone missions are underway to demonstrate basic methods of space weather forecasting, asteroid deflection and active space debris removal from orbit. 

 

In execution of these tasks, the Space Safety Department has the following entities: 

  • Mission Implementation Division (OPS-SM); 
  • COSMIC Project Management Office (OPS-SC); 
  • Space Weather Office (OPS-SW); 
  • Planetary Defence Office (OPS-SP); 
  • Space Debris Office (OPS-SD); 
  • Clean Space & Circular Economy Office (OPS-SY); 
  • Frequency Management Office (OPS-SF); 
  • Programme Coordination Office (OPS-SX). 

 

Within the Space Safety Missions Implementation Division, you will operate in a dynamic, international environment where new mission concepts become real spacecraft and you will contribute to missions in their detailed design, development, integration and operational preparation phases (Phase B2/C/D). The focus is on active debris removal and in-orbit servicing—two fast-growing fields that are redefining how spacecraft are maintained and how crowded orbits are managed. 

 

These missions develop and demonstrate technologies for rendezvous, inspection, capture, life extension, relocation, de-orbiting and repair. You will collaborate with experienced ESA specialists and innovative European companies, gaining a close-up view of both cutting-edge engineering and the emerging commercial market for sustainable space services. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​ClearSpace-1: Contribute to the first mission designed to capture and remove an unprepared, non-cooperative ESA space object from low Earth orbit. The mission must operate in challenging dynamic and lighting conditions and will demonstrate Europe’s commitment to taking responsibility for the space environment. 

​ 

​As a member of one of the two above project teams, you will support system engineering activities for the spacecraft detailed design and preparation of its verification. Depending on the project’s needs and your interests, you may help analyse requirements implementation and interfaces, review technical documentation, follow detailed design trade-offs, help organise project reviews, and coordinate inputs across engineering disciplines. 

​​ 

​Throughout the internship, you will learn how a complex space mission is developed end to end, how systems engineers turn mission goals into coherent technical solutions, and how multidisciplinary teams make decisions under real programme constraints. You will strengthen your ability to communicate technical information clearly, work collaboratively and apply system thinking to an operational space project. 

​ 

​This is an opportunity to make a visible contribution to a real mission while learning from experts at the forefront of sustainable spaceflight. ​

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You will thrive in this internship if you are curious about debris removal and in-orbit servicing, enjoy working with others and are ready to take initiative.  

We welcome students who are eager to learn, ask thoughtful questions and contribute ideas. 

A background in space systems engineering would be an asset, but enthusiasm for complex space missions and a strong willingness to learn are equally important. 

Due to the nature of the post, a commitment of six months is preferred, depending on the candidate’s availability. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

Title: Intern in the Space Safety Programme - Frequency Management Office
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

​​The ESA Space Safety Department takes care of all potential hazards and threats from space or in space, which can impact ​human activities, infrastructure, or related applications. The spectrum of tasks ranges from gathering the basic understanding of space hazards originating from our Sun, from human space debris, or from asteroids potentially colliding with the Earth. It also addresses basic approaches to mitigate these hazards and to implement space systems end-to-end in a sustainable and eco-compatible way. Moreover, several corner stone missions are underway to demonstrate basic methods of space weather forecasting, asteroid deflection and active space debris removal from orbit. 

​ 

​In execution of these tasks, the Space Safety Department has the following entities: 

  • ​Mission Implementation Division (OPS-SM); 
  • ​COSMIC Project Management Office (OPS-SC); 
  • ​Space Weather Office (OPS-SW); 
  • ​Planetary Defence Office (OPS-SP); 
  • ​Space Debris Office (OPS-SD); 
  • ​Clean Space & Circular Economy Office (OPS-SY); 
  • ​Frequency Management Office (OPS-SF); 
  • ​Programme Coordination Office (OPS-SX). 

​ 

​Within OPS-S, the ESA Frequency Management Office (OPS-SF) manages Agency frequency activities, develops and maintains policy, and ensures implementation per International Telecommunication Union (ITU) provisions. The Office interfaces with ESA satellite projects across Directorates for frequency assignment and coordination to minimise interference, leads ESA participation in radiocommunication meetings and international regulatory bodies, and chairs the Inter-Directorate Frequency Management Working Group. The Office interfaces with host country and Member States regulators on frequency regulation matters and supports radio frequency standardisation. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​Protection from Radio frequency interference of the Earth stations supporting ESA missions is critical. The ESA Frequency Management Office has developed an internal software tool in order to determine the protection area around Earth stations so that interference from other terrestrial radio transmitters can be avoided.  

​ 

​As part of the internship, your task will include the following aspects: 

  • ​Getting familiar with the above mentioned software tool, and the underlying methodology derived from ITU regulations;
  • ​running the tool in order to create a catalogue of protection contours for a range of scenarios addressing ESA receiving and transmitting Earth stations;
  • proposing optimisation and update of the tool. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in radio frequency communications and radio propagation is an asset.  

Knowledge of the Matlab programming language is required.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Systems Department - Space Systems Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

This internship is hosted by the Space Segment Systems Engineering section (TEC-SYS), which is providing systems engineering support across all ESA directorates in both early and later mission phases. During your internship, you are going to collaborate with experts from both the AI & Advanced Eng. Methods section (TEC-SFA) and the Concurrent Design Facility section (TEC-SFD). TEC-SFA is developing and providing cutting-edge methods and tools to systems engineers across the Agency. TEC-SFD is performing early-phase studies for both internal and external customers to define mission scenarios and high-level system design trades.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Under the supervision of the tutor, you are going to:

  • assess the modelling use cases for systems engineering during early phase studies;
  • develop a systematic approach to how AI can support modelling mission concepts and spacecraft design options;
  • identify the relevant tools and toolchains with which the AI would have to interact;
  • develop and evaluate interfaces allowing AI agents to use selected modelling and engineering tools;
  • demonstrate the approach through a prototype on representative early phase engineering tasks.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Experience in systems engineering, early phase studies and concurrent design, as well as experience with Large Language Models, AI agents, software development or engineering modelling tools, is also considered an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics.

Title: Intern in the Systems Department - AI and Data Science Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Systems Department is responsible for Systems Engineering, its implementation within Projects and In Orbit Demonstration and the innovative solutions - in terms of technology and methodology - enhancing its effectiveness: Artificial Intelligence, Advanced Simulation, Augmented Reality, Concurrent and Collaborative Engineering, Cost Engineering, Digital Engineering, MBSE, Sustainability. Standardisation is also within the responsibility of the Systems Department, ensuring that processes are formalised and shared cross the broad community of space stakeholders. 

 

The Future Engineering Division (in support of the programme directorates) is responsible for developing and providing the right Engineering Tools, Methods and Standards:

  • leading the Agency's centre of excellence for Artificial Intelligence and processing technologies for space applications;
  • leading the centre of excellence for Advanced Simulation Methods, including scientific data processing and databases, software applications including human-computer interfaces, support for science operation centres and downstream applications;
  • supporting projects with the centre of competence in Sustainability Engineering for all areas related to Clean Space, Life Cycle Analysis, EcoDesign, Zero Debris, REACH and RoHS;
  • performing pre-Phase A mission and system design studies in support of programmes' preparation of future missions, providing cost assessments and developing next-generation methodologies including Concurrent Design Facility (CDF), MBSE, and associated ontologies;
  • supporting the evolution of ECSS standards supported by all TEC departments and in full coordination with programmes.

 

The purpose of the AI and Data Science Section is to implement the ESA AI Competence Centre and lead the Agency's centre of excellence for advanced technologies supporting the development and exploitation of future space missions, contributing to the main mission of the Technology, Engineering and Quality Directorate in supporting European projects and their success through excellent engineering and the provision of innovative and enabling technologies, processes, methods, tools and applications. The AI and Data Science Section carries out technology research in the field of Artificial Intelligence, Data Science and related areas.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Knowledge Graph-powered Agentic workflows for Space Applications


This internship first explores methods for combining knowledge graphs with agentic workflows (e.g., graph-as-memory, Agentic Graph RAG, or graph-as-coordination-hub for multi-agent systems) and maps these methods against candidate use cases in the space domain. Building on this exploration, you will then design, develop and evaluate a prototype implementing one selected use case, demonstrating how the chosen method addresses a concrete space-related challenge.

 

2) Topic 2: Synthesis of Pareto-Optimal Interpretations for Neural Network-Based Anomaly Detection Systems


This internship explores the synthesis of Pareto-optimal interpretations for neural network-based anomaly detection systems intended for autonomous onboard satellite operations. The objective is to investigate methods for generating simple, human-understandable representations (such as decision diagrams) of complex black-box models (such as neural networks), while balancing competing objectives including predictive fidelity, interpretability, and representation complexity. Constructing transparent and trustworthy interpretations is a key requirement for machine learning components in mission-critical domains, where accountability and explainability are essential. You will tailor state-of-the-art symbolic reasoning techniques to machine learning models relevant to ESA programmes, with a particular focus on neural network-based onboard anomaly detection.

 

3) Topic 3: LLM-Assisted Verified Code Generation


The increasing complexity of safety-critical software for space systems calls for new development methodologies that combine automation with rigorous correctness guarantees. This internship investigates the role of Large Language Models (LLMs) as assistants in the development of formally verified software components for critical systems. You will explore LLM-assisted formal specification, where natural-language system requirements are translated into precise formal properties. Building on these specifications, the internship will study approaches for automated code generation and refinement, using formal verification techniques to validate correctness, safety, and reliability. The objective is to move beyond treating LLMs as autonomous code generators and instead establish a workflow in which LLMs serve as efficient engineering assistants whose outputs are systematically checked and validated through formal methods.

 

4) Topic 4: Symbolic AI to Simulate Quantum Convolutional Neural Network for Satellite Data Classification


Quantum machine learning (QML) is emerging as a promising technology in image classification and remote sensing tasks that naturally arise in Earth observation. However, due to current hardware limitations, the quantum circuit embedded into the AI pipeline is limited in size and the gate basis that it can use. We can still assess the potential advantage of QML approaches using simulators for the quantum circuit. In this internship, you will integrate novel quantum-circuit simulators based on automated reasoning techniques into the QML pipeline to classify satellite images. The automated reasoning approach is agnostic to the gate basis used by the circuit, allowing quantum circuits of different sizes and with different gates to be implemented and evaluated in this context. The outcome of the project will help us prepare for the time when quantum computers are commonly available and provide you with a unique opportunity to apply cutting-edge machine learning and quantum computing technologies to real satellite data.

5) Topic 5: Agentic-LLM ROS2 Controller for Rover Autonomy

 

Increased autonomy of rovers would allow for further scientific exploration. This internship explores the potential role agentic Large Language Models could play in enabling this autonomy, as well as its potential limitations. In this internship, you will implement an agentic LLM model framework that can take as input a task list and subsequently issue commands to the rover (using the ROS/ROS2 library) to accomplish these tasks and test the resulting quality of this framework. The internship objectives include integrating pathfinding and collision avoidance tools and models into this agent; deploying this agent both in a lunar simulation environment and on board an analogue rover for performance evaluation; and exploring which stopgaps to implement to minimise machine error.

 

6) Topic 6: Evaluation Methods for Agentic AI in Systems Engineering


Agentic AI systems are increasingly capable of performing complex engineering tasks involving information retrieval, reasoning and the use of external tools. However, systematically evaluating their correctness, consistency and robustness remains challenging, particularly for tasks where results must be supported by different engineering sources.
In this internship, you will investigate evaluation methods for agentic AI applied to systems engineering tasks. You will define representative tasks and evaluation criteria, and develop a reproducible framework for comparing different agent configurations, models and reasoning strategies.
The evaluation will consider representative activities such as requirements analysis, traceability assessment and verification support.
The outcome of the project will be a reusable methodology for assessing the capabilities and limitations of agentic AI in engineering applications, with the aim of supporting engineering activities and project reviews.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

 

Topic 1: Knowledge Graph-powered Agentic Workflows for Space Applications

  • knowledge of Large Language Models and agentic systems is required;
  • familiarity with Knowledge Graphs is considered an asset. 

 

Topic 2: Synthesis of Pareto-Optimal Interpretations for Neural Network-Based Anomaly Detection Systems

  • basic knowledge of machine learning models is required, particularly neural networks and decision trees;
  • an interest in explainable AI and familiarity with automated reasoning techniques (e.g., SAT and MaxSAT solving) are considered assets.

 

Topic 3: LLM-Assisted Verified Code Generation

  • familiarity with Large Language Models and agentic systems is required, along with a strong background in software design and programming;
  • experience with formal methods and automated theorem provers, especially the LEAN proof assistant, is considered an asset.

 

Topic 4: Symbolic AI to Simulate Quantum Convolutional Neural Network for Satellite Data Classification

  • knowledge of gate-based quantum computing and experience in developing AI pipelines in Python are required;
  • a basic understanding of propositional logic and symbolic AI is an asset.

 

Topic 5: Agentic-LLM ROS2 Controller for Rover Autonomy  

  • familiarity with Large Language Models and their agentic systems is required;
  • experience working with robotics libraries (ROS/ROS2) is considered an asset.

 

Topic 6: Evaluation Methods for Agentic AI in Systems Engineering

  • familiarity with Large Language Models and agentic systems is required, along with good programming skills, particularly in Python;
  • an interest in systems engineering and experience with evaluating AI systems, information retrieval or automated reasoning are considered assets.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Chemical Propulsion Engineering Section (TEC-MPC), part of the Propulsion, Aerothermodynamics and Flight Vehicles Engineering Division, has the following tasks:

  • provide technical support and consultancy in space transportation propulsion (liquid, including storable and cryogenic technologies, and solid propulsion) and spacecraft propulsion (various chemical propulsion technologies) to the Agency project teams responsible for the development of launchers and spacecraft, throughout all project phases;
  • contribute to the preparation of work plans in the areas of space transportation and spacecraft propulsion in the Agency’s technological programmes, with a particular contribution expected on systems and new propulsion aspects;
  • prepare and manage, from a technical perspective, ESA contracts for studies, experimental investigations, and engineering development activities in space propulsion.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will be integrated into the ESA Chemical Propulsion Section, reporting directly to the Head of Section and the Head of Division. In this role, you will develop skills and expertise while supporting the team in implementing the Innovative Propulsion Cross-Cutting Initiative (ESA IP-CCI) through technical and personal development in the following areas:

  • contributing to the development of key ESA technologies, including monitoring progress and updating the IP-CCI technology roadmaps;
  • conducting comprehensive assessments of European R&D activities related to IP-CCI topics;
  • supporting the Division in implementing activities approved at the ESA Ministerial Conference 2025 (CM25), preparing internal performance indicators and supporting the preparation of ESA Ministerial Conference 2028;
  • assisting with OSIP campaigns related to IP-CCI, including producing synthesis reports;
  • contributing to corporate initiatives, such as workshops and conferences, to enhance the visibility of the propulsion strategy and its implementation to ESA stakeholders.

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

Education

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • successfully completed a university course in aerospace engineering, with a particular focus on space propulsion;
  • knowledge of space propulsion engineering, including propulsion subsystems and their interactions with, and impact on, other associated spacecraft/space vehicle subsystems;
  • a strong interest in spacecraft and space vehicles, particularly those related to missions undertaken by ESA;
  • a solid theoretical and historical understanding of space propulsion, combined with the ability to envision how future propulsion systems could operate and be integrated into spacecraft and space vehicles under development;
  • knowledge of systems engineering would be considered an additional asset.

Title: Intern in the Systems Department - Zero Debris Approach and End-of-Life Management
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Sustainability Engineering & Standards Section (TEC-SFS), part of ESA's Future Engineering Division (TEC-SF), supports the development and implementation of sustainable engineering approaches across ESA programmes and projects. The section works at the intersection of system engineering, sustainability and innovation, helping to ensure that future space systems are designed, developed and operated in a more sustainable, efficient and responsible manner.

 

A significant part of the section's activities is dedicated to supporting ESA's Clean Space initiatives. Working in close collaboration with the Clean Space Office, TEC-SFS engineers contribute to the development and application of methodologies, technologies and engineering practices that advance the long-term sustainability of space activities. This includes activities related to Ecodesign, Zero Debris and the future Circular Economy in Space.

 

The team supports ESA projects from the earliest mission definition phases through technology development and implementation, helping projects integrate sustainability objectives into system design, engineering trades, verification approaches and operational concepts. Activities span topics such as life cycle assessment, environmental impact reduction, space debris mitigation, sustainable mission design, in-orbit servicing and future circular space architectures.

 

For interns, TEC-SFS offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge sustainability engineering activities and to support the development of future technologies, missions and engineering approaches that will help ensure the long-term sustainability of space activities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Zero Debris approach and End-of-Life Management

 

The traffic in valuable Earth orbits is expected to continue increasing significantly in the coming decades. Despite internationally recognised space debris mitigation guidelines, technical standards and national regulations, the successful disposal of space systems and the prevention of in-orbit break-ups remain major challenges. ESA is addressing these challenges through the implementation of the Zero Debris approach, helping to preserve the space environment for future generations.

 

You will support the team responsible for further developing the Zero Debris approach and improving the End-of-Life management of current and future missions. Activities may include contributing to engineering studies, requirements, methodologies, technology roadmaps and analyses related to space debris mitigation, disposal strategies and the implementation of Zero Debris objectives across ESA projects.

 

While the primary focus of the internship will be on Zero Debris and End-of-Life management, opportunities may also arise to contribute to activities in the areas of Ecodesign and In-Orbit Servicing and Circular Economy in Space, depending on the intern's interests and the needs of other ongoing activities.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Having a keen interest in Clean Space activities is beneficial and having a collaborative team spirit is highly valued. 

Knowledge and background in Zero Debris, space debris mitigation and/or space system engineering is an asset.

Due to the nature of the post, a commitment of six months is preferred, depending on the candidate’s availability.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Materials, Environments and Contamination Control Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Materials, Environments and Contamination Control Section (TEC-MSE) provides expert engineering support to ESA projects, conducts technology research, develops and implements laboratory testing activities focusing on:

  • multi-faceted characterisation of materials (thermal, optical, chemical and physical properties evaluation) and associated processes;
  • space environment effects and compatibility of materials (including atomic oxygen, particle irradiation, charging, UV exposure, and synergistic degradation mechanisms);
  • cleanliness and contamination control (including particulate and molecular contamination, outgassing, UV- and laser-induced contamination, planetary dust, gas lines purity);
  • flight safety related assessments (including habitable and pressurised environments, materials off-gassing, toxicity).

 

TEC-MSE maintains a strong focus on space hardware qualification and the development of advanced laboratory capabilities, innovative environmental testing facilities, and non-standard test methods. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Spacecraft materials must perform reliably in all mission environments, and they are often exposed to harsh environments with temperatures from cryogenic conditions up to several hundred degrees Celsius. During this internship, you will have the opportunity to contribute to the development of new test methodologies related to the thermal properties of adhesives and potting materials, using common thermal analysis techniques like Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA), Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), Thermomechanical Analysis (TMA), Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) and rheometry.

 

Specific topics to investigate include: 

  • characterisation of novel materials for potting applications;
  • creation and population of a materials database for key engineering properties of adhesives for space applications;
  • understanding the relation between mechanical characterisation using DMA and standard tensile testing.

 

Your work will involve:

  • literature research on common relevant materials and familiarisation with existing techniques and standards;
  • familiarisation with the TEC-MSE laboratory and instruments;
  • implementation of experimental test campaigns;
  • data analysis, uncertainty evaluation and documentation of results.

 

You will gain experience working in an international team of experts with varied backgrounds and you will use the world leading experimental facilities of the ESA/ESTEC Materials and Electrical Components Laboratory.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in materials, physics and chemistry or vacuum technologies will be an asset. The internship will have a significant experimental content, and so strong motivation to work in a laboratory environment is required.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. Title: Intern in the Future Missions and Architecture Department - EO Constellation Analysis Tool
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

You will join the Future Missions & Architecture Department – Mission and System Studies Section, which supports the preparation of future Earth Observation missions through mission analysis, system studies and architecture assessments.

 

The Section contributes to the evaluation of new mission concepts, the definition of mission requirements and architectures, the preparation of early mission studies, and the assessment of future Earth Observation capabilities. The Section also develops analytical methods, mission performance simulators and engineering tools to support the design and evaluation of future space systems.

 

You will work in a multidisciplinary environment combining mission analysis, systems engineering, architecture trade-offs and technology assessment to support the preparation of future Earth Observation missions and services.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Development of a Mission Analysis Tool for Earth Observation Constellation Deployment and Replenishment

 

Earth Observation is increasingly relying on satellite constellations to provide services such as environmental monitoring, disaster response, maritime surveillance and security applications. As these constellations grow in size and complexity, understanding how to efficiently deploy, operate and sustain them throughout their lifetime becomes an important mission-analysis challenge.

 

In this internship, you will develop a mission-analysis tool to assess and optimise deployment and replenishment strategies for Earth Observation constellations. The tool will model how a constellation evolves over time, including performance degradation, and determine the launch effort and cadence needed to maintain the required performance.

 

Your activities will include:

  • developing lifecycle simulation models for constellation deployment, operations and replenishment;
  • developing algorithms to model how constellation performance evolves as satellites are launched, commissioned, reach end of life, fail or are replaced;
  • developing optimisation methods to identify efficient deployment and replenishment strategies;
  • developing models for launch preparation, commissioning times, spare satellite management and replacement policies;
  • developing capabilities to estimate the launch cadence required to achieve and maintain specified performance objectives;
  • implementing the developed methodologies within a mission-analysis software tool;
  • verifying and validating the tool using representative Earth Observation mission scenarios;
  • documenting the design, methodology and results of the tool.

 

Through this internship, you will gain experience in mission analysis, space systems engineering, satellite constellation operations, lifecycle modelling, optimisation, simulation, engineering trade-off analysis and software development.

 

The outcome of the internship will be a reusable mission-analysis tool supporting the assessment of deployment and replenishment strategies for future Earth Observation constellations.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • a good understanding of orbital mechanics and space mission analysis;
  • experience with Python programming;
  • ability to analyse engineering problems using mathematical models and simulations;
  • familiarity with software development practices is an asset;
  • familiarity with optimisation techniques applied to engineering problems is an asset;
  • familiarity with engineering trade-off analysis and design space exploration is an asset;
  • familiarity with numerical methods and scientific computing applied to engineering problems is an asset;
  • familiarity with deployment, operations or lifecycle analysis of satellite systems is an asset;
  • familiarity with statistical analysis and Monte Carlo simulation techniques is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Copernicus Space Office
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

The Copernicus Space Office is responsible for programmatic activities, which are relevant to the Copernicus Space Component.

 

The tasks of the Office include, in particular:

  • monitoring ESA's Copernicus Space Component activities and ensuring their coordination;
  • ensuring coordination with the ESA-EU matters Committee and with COM in the implementation of the Copernicus Space Component by interfacing with COM Copernicus related Units services;
  • coordinating the implementation of the EU-ESA Agreement on Copernicus and supporting negotiations for any amendments;
  • preparing and planning programmatic aspects of the Copernicus Space Component evolution;
  • preparing Copernicus Space Component programmatic documents and supporting Copernicus related negotiations with COM and other parties.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Sustainability, climate neutrality, competitiveness and the future of the Copernicus Space Component


The released proposal for a Regulation on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act) introduces several articles on environmental sustainability of space activities affecting Copernicus related activities. The intern will review the latest EU legislation and assess the potential implications on the Copernicus Space Component and its implementation of the ESA Green Agenda and propose the possible next steps needed to achieve climate neutrality including short, medium and long term milestones such as: introduction of sustainability requirements for all CSC related activities, optimisation of related organisational schemes, etc.

 

2) Topic 2: Security and resilience in Europe and the future of the Copernicus Space Component 


Security and Resilience are among the priorities of the European Union. In particular, Article 1 of the proposed Regulation for the future European Competitiveness Fund clearly identifies a "Resilience and Security, Defence, Industry and Space" window. As an EU led programme, Copernicus is called to address these concerns. In order to properly assess the possible implications of these concerns, the intern will survey emerging security and resilience requirements and related EU communications and legislation and explore the potential implications on the Copernicus Space Component proposing possible solutions to best respond to these growing needs.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in EU policies, familiarity with the aerospace sector and engineering is an asset.
