Title: Intern in the Human Exploration Science Office - In-flight Venous Thrombosis Countermeasures
description_html:
Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

​Within the Exploration Science Office of the Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration, the Human Exploration Science Team (HRE-SH) conducts research that enables future human space exploration while leveraging spaceflight and analogue platforms to advance knowledge and improve human health on Earth. HRE-SH uses a wide range of terrestrial and (sub-) orbital research platforms, as well as the International Space Station (ISS), to investigate the effects of selected or combined spaceflight stressors on human health and performance. These platforms include parabolic flight, dry immersion, bed rest, isolated and confined environments, and spaceflight. This work focuses on the identification and mitigation of challenges to astronaut health and performance to enable the safe exploration of European Astronauts to low-Earth orbit, the Moon, and beyond. Furthermore, by leveraging the platforms developed for exploration, scientific experiments can be conducted under unique conditions, generating benefits on Earth in fields such as healthcare, ageing research, and health management. HRE-SH works closely with international partners, astronauts, medical support, and the scientific community to define and address operational needs and scientific priorities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

 

Background 

Although upper extremity venous thrombosis also occurs on Earth, spaceflight conditions may increase its likelihood and make it a serious medical risk. Microgravity redistributes body fluids and can reduce or reverse venous blood flow, particularly in the head and neck, promoting venous stasis - one of the main mechanisms of thrombus formation. Managing this risk will become increasingly important during exploration missions, where constraints on mass, volume, crew time, medical expertise, and communication with Earth will limit available countermeasures. Several preventive approaches may modify venous flow or other contributors to thrombosis, but their evidence, safety, operational suitability, and readiness for in-flight use have not been assessed within a common framework. This internship will address this gap by reviewing evidence from ESA research platforms and relevant terrestrial clinical contexts to identify and prioritise countermeasures that could be safely and realistically implemented during spaceflight. 


Aim 

Based on a structured review of the available literature, you will assess candidate countermeasures according to their physiological mechanism, evidence of efficacy and safety, operational feasibility, and technology maturity. The findings will inform adjustments to scientific and operational priorities and roadmaps, support the translation of evidence into operational and technology requirements, and identify priorities for further validation. 


Main activities 

  • conduct a structured review of relevant spaceflight, analogue, terrestrial clinical, and technology-development evidence;
  • evaluate candidate approaches, including lower body negative pressure, venous thigh cuffs, modifications to existing exercise protocols, simple neck-flow interventions, respiratory or positional manoeuvres, and compact compression technologies;
  • develop structured comparison tables to assess the evidence, safety, technology maturity, and operational feasibility of each countermeasure for future exploration missions;
  • create a safety and decision framework separating routine prevention, use with abnormal flow or suspected thrombosis, and use after confirmed thrombosis;
  • identify promising emerging technologies, rank the most suitable approaches using pre-defined criteria, and propose a validation study for the highest-priority option.


Expected outputs

The primary outputs will be an internal report documenting the literature-review methods, findings, and recommendations; evidence and technology-readiness matrices; a safety and decision framework; a prioritised shortlist; a validation-study concept; and concrete recommendations for updating ESA priorities and the venous thrombosis roadmap and for defining operational and technology requirements. Subject to the maturity and scientific novelty of the work, you will also prepare a manuscript for submission to a peer-reviewed journal. 


Learning objectives 

Through this internship, you will gain experience in systematic evidence synthesis, health-technology assessment, technology-readiness evaluation, risk–benefit analysis, human spaceflight operations, scientific writing, and translation of research evidence into practical recommendations for astronaut health. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Desired assets: 

  • background in medicine, human physiology, biomedical engineering, health technology assessment, sports science, or a related field;
  • good knowledge of cardiovascular physiology, haemodynamics, coagulation, venous thrombosis, or Virchow’s triad;
  • experience with structured literature reviews, evidence grading, data extraction, and/or scientific writing;
  • interest in medical devices, point-of-care diagnostics, ultrasound, technology-readiness assessment, or human spaceflight operations;
  • ability to compare heterogeneous evidence critically, document assumptions transparently, and communicate conclusions clearly to scientific and operational audiences.

 

You should be able to work independently, manage a six-month analytical project, and collaborate effectively within an international and interdisciplinary team. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - Solar Orbiter Mission Planning System Automation
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

You will be part of the Inner Solar System Mission Operations Unit, which is responsible for the flight operations of the ESA Bepi Colombo, Solar Orbiter and Cluster missions. Preparation activities for the ENVISION mission to Venus are also performed in the Unit. 

​ 

​The Solar Orbiter Flight Control Team is composed of 6 Spacecraft Operations Engineers who are in charge of the flight operations of the Solar Orbiter spacecraft. Operations planning is performed with the Mission Planning System on a weekly basis, which consists of validating and uplinking a consolidated set of payload and platform operations requests.​ 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​This internship aims to further develop the automation of the Mission Planning System and support its integration into operations. 

​ 

​During the internship, you will: 

  • ​Be part of the Solar Orbiter Flight Control Team; 
  • ​extend the capabilities of the existing automation system; 
  • ​integrate existing tools into the automation framework; 
  • ​collaborate with the Mission Planning Development Team to implement and validate new features; 
  • ​perform validation and testing activities; 
  • ​support the deployment of automation solutions into operational use. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Required skills: 

  • Proficiency in Python and Linux/Bash scripting. 

Desirable skills: 

  • Experience with query-based languages.

ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. Title: Intern in the Spaceship EAC Team
description_html:
Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

The Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration (D/HRE) is the main ESA entity in charge of supporting and coordinating efforts towards the current and the future endeavours of human spaceflight. The exploration activities are part of the strategic plans in securing a central role for Europe with respect to the global initiatives. The European Exploration Envelope Programme (E3P) is integrating the ESA activities in this field to ensure a single exploration process. The strategy includes three destinations where humans will work with robots to gather new knowledge: Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the Moon, and Mars.  

 

The “Spaceship EAC” initiative is investigating low Technology Readiness Level (TRL) technologies for supporting the future cislunar space mission as well as surface activities on the Moon as part of the Exploration Preparation, Research and Technology (ExPeRT) team. This multidisciplinary, innovation-driven team composed of researchers, graduate and undergraduate students is based at the ESA European Astronaut Centre (EAC). The mission statement of “Spaceship EAC” is centred on three main pillars: enhance, enable and inspire. The founding idea behind this initiative is indeed to enhance the capabilities of EAC via exploiting the spaceflight experience of the centre to develop and validate new operational concepts and valuable technologies in support of future human exploration scenarios. A pragmatic and research-focused approach is adopted, and knowledge acquired is disseminated within ESA, partners and the relevant scientific community. Spaceship EAC is one node of the larger Spaceship Initiative team, with locations at ECSAT, France and Poland. 

 

Within Spaceship EAC, we have a number of fields where we carry out different projects. These fields are:  

 

  • demonstrating disruptive technologies such as Virtual/Augmented Reality, collaborative robotics and their potential use cases for exploration;
  • investigating novel concepts in the domain of Space Resources/In-Situ Resource Utilisation, to enable sustainable human exploration;
  • using advanced manufacturing methodologies, such as additive manufacturing, for projects within the centre and for space exploration;
  • developing new ideas around medical technologies, for example, using machine learning techniques to support long-term exploration;
  • topics related to ‘off-world living’, e.g. human factors, design and concept illustration;
  • Crew Health and Performance Technologies and Knowledge build-up.

 

Additionally, the Spaceship team is involved in supporting the development of our new LUNA facility at EAC. This facility will serve as a central hub for lunar exploration preparations at ESA and DLR. It features a 700 sqm lunar surface testbed, facilitating the development and validation of operational concepts, astronaut training, and technology demonstrations for Moon exploration. Additionally, the facility will showcase elements of an analogue Moon base, such as a habitat/laboratory module, and a regenerative energy system among others.  

 

We are continually looking for innovative applicants with skills or interests in these areas to join the Spaceship EAC team. An outline of some of the projects that we have recently been progressing can be found at the ESA blog.

For more information on Spaceship EAC internships, please look at the Spaceship EAC blog (Spaceship EAC – ESA – Exploration).

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will support the innovation team that is Spaceship EAC, working to further develop and advance the projects of the team.

 

1. Background and Motivation

 

The Spaceship EAC team is always on the lookout for talented and motivated persons to join our projects and contribute to ESA’s exploration activities. The main areas in which the initiative is currently active are:  

 

  • energy production and storage;
  • radiation shielding;
  • In Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU);
  • VR/AR technologies for exploration;
  • embedded systems and IoT;
  • exercise hardware and countermeasure concepts;
  • machine learning for exploration;
  • robotics and human factors;
  • conceptual illustration/design.

 

2. Objectives

 

As a member of the team, you will be asked to work on a project relevant to the topical areas aforementioned, advancing the project with the team and contributing to the overall Spaceship EAC environment. 

 

3. Methodology and Tasks

 

The internship will integrate into the existing Spaceship EAC/LUNA team at ESA and work on a specific project in the domains listed. The Spaceship approach relies heavily on practical engineering and proof-of-concept demonstration, adopting an agile, skunkworks-type mindset to our work. The project will demand a high degree of flexibility and creativity, in line with the innovation focus of Spaceship work. 

 

4. Expected Outcomes

 

You will help advance a specific Spaceship EAC project as well as become involved in the larger team. You will provide the technical outputs, prototypes and relevant documentation as a final deliverable to the team. 

 

5. Relevance

 

Spaceships exist as part of the ExPeRT team and are integral in early-stage practical demonstration of low-TRL technologies and concepts. These projects are then commonly advanced to higher TRL activities via other mechanisms within ESA or externally (e.g. in cooperation with research teams). Additionally, Spaceship projects can directly support activities at their home centre, e.g. EAC at Cologne, enabling new capabilities at the centre. Spaceship activities align with the broad objectives of the E3P and are enabling elements for low-TRL activities within the programme. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in mechanical engineering, materials, computer science, life science, VR/AR development, industrial design or other relevant backgrounds are welcome.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Human Exploration Science Office - Human Research Project Management
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands or EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany 

Our team and mission

​​Within the Exploration Science Office of the Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration, the Human Exploration Science Team (HRE-SH) conducts research that enables future human space exploration while leveraging spaceflight and analogue platforms to advance knowledge and improve human health on Earth. HRE-SH uses a wide range of terrestrial and (sub-) orbital research platforms, as well as the International Space Station (ISS), to investigate the effects of selected or combined spaceflight stressors on human health and performance. These platforms include parabolic flight, dry immersion, bed rest, isolated and confined environments, and spaceflight. This work focuses on the identification and mitigation of challenges to astronaut health and performance to enable the safe exploration of European Astronauts to low-Earth orbit, the Moon, and beyond. Furthermore, by leveraging the platforms developed for exploration, scientific experiments can be conducted under unique conditions, generating benefits on Earth in fields such as healthcare, aging research, and health management. HRE-SH works closely with international partners, astronauts, medical support, and the scientific community to define and address operational needs and scientific priorities.  

​ 

​For this internship, there will be a close coordination also with the Exploration Software and Artificial Intelligence Office. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​Human Research activities involve information and workflows distributed across different processes and systems.  Human Exploration Project Scientists have a need for simple and reliable ways to access information relevant to their work, update it when necessary, and interact with complementary systems while avoiding duplicate processes. This includes interaction and coordination with the Agency’s Medical Boards for human research projects.  

​ 

​During this internship, you will contribute to the design and development of user-facing software built on the common Exploration Science data infrastructure, particularly supporting the interaction with the Agency’s Medical Boards. You will work with scientists and other users to understand operational needs, translate broad requirements into technical solutions, and implement maintainable application components. The work will focus on improving processes across life sciences projects while ensuring that the resulting software can be maintained and extended after the internship. 

​ 

​Through this internship, you will: 

​ 

  • ​analyse user needs and existing workflows and translate them into software requirements for interaction with the Agency’s Medical Boards;
  • ​design and develop intuitive web-based interfaces for viewing, editing and validating human research science activity information;
  • ​build application services that connect the user interface with the common Human Exploration Science data infrastructure;
  • ​integrate the application with relevant human research and Agency information systems;
  • ​develop digital workflows for areas such as medical board interactions, project monitoring, proposal review, approval processes, publication validation and reporting;
  • ​implement authentication, authorisation, user roles and appropriate data-protection measures;
  • ​explore artificial-intelligence-supported functions for search, matching, extraction and validation where they provide clear user benefits across human exploration science activities;
  • ​test and document the application to support reliable maintenance and future development and expansion across human research applications;
  • ​receive mentorship and guidance by experts in the field;
  • ​work on solutions with a clear operational relevance in human exploration science. 

​ 

​You will collaborate with colleagues developing the underlying data infrastructure and with users from life sciences and operational backgrounds. Through the internship, you will gain practical experience in software architecture, web application development, systems integration, user-centred design, secure application development and the delivery of maintainable software in a multidisciplinary environment with a specific focus on human research data and interaction with the Agency’s Medical Boards.​

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

A background in computer science, software engineering, information systems or a related technical discipline would be an asset. 

 

You should have: 

 

  • strong programming skills and practical experience developing software applications;
  • experience with web applications, including frontend or user-interface development;
  • familiarity with application programming interfaces, relational databases and version control;
  • interest and/or experience working with human research data, including sensitive data protection;
  • an ability to translate user needs into intuitive and practical technical solutions;
  • an interest in user-centred design, data protection, secure development and maintainable software;
  • motivation to contribute within the field of human spaceflight and science management. 

 

Experience with software deployment, authentication, artificial intelligence, or machine learning applications would be additional assets.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Title: Intern in the Utilisation & Enabled Science Team-Modelling Subsurface CO₂ & Methane Hydrates on Mars
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

​​Within the European Space Agency (ESA)’s Directorate for Human and Robotic Exploration, the Exploration Science activities are a cornerstone of the Explore2040 strategy, driving innovation at the intersection of human exploration and scientific discovery. HRE-SU (Utilisation and Enabled Science) team at ESA coordinates the Agency’s research activities in physical sciences and biology under microgravity conditions and for space exploration. Using platforms like the International Space Station, as well as Moon and Mars missions, the team supports a wide range of cutting-edge research—from Earth atmospheric studies and quantum sensors to heat transfer phenomena, soft matter, and advanced materials processing.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​The Martian subsurface is believed to contain significant reservoirs of water ice and volatile-rich phases such as carbon dioxide and methane hydrates. Understanding the formation, stability and dissociation of these reservoirs is important for planetary science and for future in-situ resource utilisation concepts.

 

​During the internship, you will contribute to the development of numerical models of coupled thermal and fluid processes governing hydrate formation and dissociation in the Martian subsurface, using the Delft Advanced Research Terra Simulator (DARTS) and supporting numerical tools.

 

Your activities will be: 

  • ​review the current scientific literature on carbon dioxide and methane hydrates under Martian conditions;
  • ​implement and adapt numerical models describing hydrate formation, dissociation and volatile transport in porous media;
  • ​perform simulation campaigns to investigate the influence of temperature, pressure, soil properties and climate conditions on hydrate stability;
  • ​analyse and interpret modelling results and compare them with existing studies and observational constraints;
  • ​contribute to the preparation of technical reports and scientific presentations.

 

​Learning objectives

​Through this internship, you will gain practical experience in:

  • ​numerical modelling of coupled thermo-hydraulic processes in planetary environments;
  • ​thermodynamics, fluid transport and phase-change processes in porous media;
  • ​scientific data analysis, interpretation and communication of results;
  • ​conducting research within an international space science environment.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in the following topics is an asset:

 

  • strong knowledge and experience of modelling tool (Matlab, Python);
  • knowledge of fluid dynamics and thermodynamics (energy, exergy, enthalpy).

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the ExPeRT Mars Exploration Studies Team
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

​​The Mars Exploration Studies Team in ESA’s Human and Robotic Exploration Directorate is tasked with formulating future Mars missions. This is done in coordination with relevant stakeholders and specialists within ESA, selected definition teams and with external stakeholders in the Member States and Associates, including industry and the science and instrument development communities. The Mars Exploration Studies Team is currently engaged in parallel mission studies and technology developments for ESA’s future missions to Mars (beyond the Rosalind Franklin rover mission planned for launch in 2028). These encompass elements of infrastructure around Mars for communications and navigation support, measurements needed to address knowledge gaps for future exploration, remote sensing from Mars orbit and in situ measurements from the martian surface. The team is a small, dynamic and multidisciplinary grouping within the ExPeRT (Exploration Preparation, Research and Technology) division. Part of the team’s work is to track the potential and proposed payload equipment, which needs to meet the desired technology readiness, resources, and technical and operational interfaces with the spacecraft.​

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will work in close coordination with the Mars exploration payload systems engineer, the Directorate’s scientific support for Mars exploration, and Definition Teams for Mars lander Science and Instrumentation. You will support tracking and elaboration of the information provided by the definition teams as it is used iteratively with mission studies, to help define a set of properly-margined payload resource (mass, power, volume, data, etc.) allocations, interfaces and operational concepts. You will support MarsX in generation of a first issue of a Payload Definition Document, which helps formalise the instructions to industry for studying the mission at Phase A level. You have an opportunity to broaden your knowledge of payload instruments and the technical aspects of their interfaces and operations.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in multiple engineering disciplines (mechanical, electrical, thermal, digital, etc.) is an asset. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Title: Intern in the Climate Action, Sustainability and Science Department - FLEX Mission
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Earth Science Division, of the Climate Action, Sustainability and Science Department, Earth Observation Programmes Directorate, is based at the European Space Research and Technology Centre. The Earth and Mission Science Division provides the creative vision for innovation and new discoveries in Earth system science, using Earth Observation (EO) in close cooperation with the scientific community.

 

The Earth Science Division team:

  • bridges science and technology by translating ideas and concepts into technical reality and scientific success. It does this by defining, consolidating and managing scientific mission requirements throughout all phases of a mission, and by measuring the maturity of the resulting mission concept;
  • manages scientific research-based studies, providing the scientific foundation for mission concepts and approval, supports the successful development of space and ground segment, in-orbit satellite commissioning and in-orbit scientific achievements;
  • undertakes airborne, marine and terrestrial campaigns contributing to the development of new technologies, mission feasibility assessments, calibration/validation and application development.

 

You will work within the Earth Surfaces and Interior Section of the Earth Science Division, whose role is to provide scientific support throughout the full lifecycle of Earth Observation missions, from mission concept and assessment studies through development, commissioning and routine operations. The Section contributes to mission requirements definition, scientific performance assessment, calibration and validation activities, product development, mission data exploitation, and the advancement of Earth science through the exploration of emerging scientific questions, novel methodologies and future research directions. The Section has expertise spanning Earth surfaces and interior processes, including terrestrial, oceanic and cryospheric systems, as well as geodesy, gravity and magnetic field observations and solid Earth dynamics. Your activities will contribute to and benefit from a diverse and international team of scientists working across a variety of Earth science disciplines.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an ESA Intern, you will contribute to the early validation of data products generated by FLEX, a new Earth Explorer satellite mission focused on monitoring photosynthesis and vegetation health. Your activities will span across the early operational phase of the mission, allowing you to contribute to the mission's scientific success from the very onset.

 

Your responsibilities will include analysing selected satellite products acquired during the FLEX commissioning and early operational phases, investigating potential anomalies, and supporting the benchmarking of retrieval and validation methods. Depending on the progress of the mission and the specific activities ongoing during the internship, you may also contribute to the comparison of satellite products with reference and in-situ measurements. You will document your analyses and communicate the results to scientific and technical audiences, contributing to the assessment and progressive improvement of the mission’s products.

 

Throughout your internship, you will gain practical experience in satellite data processing and validation, working with diverse datasets and collaborating in an international research environment. You will develop skills in data analysis, scientific communication, and project coordination, preparing you for a future career in Earth observation.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Sound scientific knowledge of remote sensing principles and applications is required.
Demonstrated experience in using Python and C++ is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the External Relations Department
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

​​The External Relations Department shapes and delivers ESA’s international engagement strategy with non-Member States, their institutions, and international organisations. It develops and coordinates cooperation frameworks, supports high-level exchanges and representation – including through ESA offices in Washington and Tokyo – and provides strategic, political and diplomatic advice on international relations to senior management. 

​ 
​By monitoring geopolitical developments, preparing key engagements and ensuring alignment with Agency priorities, the Department plays a central role in advancing ESA’s international partnerships and positioning the Agency as a trusted and influential global partner.​ 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: External Relations 

 

As an intern in the External Relations Department, you will have the unique opportunity to contribute directly to the management of the Agency’s relations with its international partners.

This includes research on geopolitical and geostrategic developments of relevance to ESA and the space sector more broadly; foreign policy analysis; contribution to the formulation of internal positions and support to the implementation of ESA’s missions and programmes jointly carried out with international partners, in coordination with relevant programme directorates; and support to the handling of high-level meetings with international delegations.

In doing so, you will be fully integrated into the team, contribute to the practice of international relations in a dynamic period of global change, and gain insights into the functioning of an intergovernmental organisation at the heart of the space sector. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge of the global space sector, relevant foreign policies or international relations is an asset.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality

Title: Intern in the Future Space Transportation Preparation Department - Reusability Section
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

​As part of the ESA Directorate of Space Transportation (STS), the Future Space Transportation team (STS-F, including the Future Launchers Preparatory Programme - FLPP) is leading the maturation of the required technologies, demonstrators and enabling capabilities for future space transportation systems. It is therefore responsible for:  

 

  • ​conducting system studies and establishing Technology Roadmaps based on strategy-driven guidelines; 
  • supporting the assessment of the overall coherence of all technologies related to space transportation systems and products, including technology policy and harmonisation; 
  • preparing new elements and follow-on activities of the Future Launchers Preparatory Programme (FLPP); 
  • leading the implementation of the FLPP Technology Roadmaps, including the maturation of key technologies for future space transportation (Avionics & GNC, Structures, Materials and Processes, Propulsion and Modelling & Simulation) and the development of flagship demonstrators (such as Prometheus and Themis).

​

The STS-FR section is in charge of the technologies maturations and flagship demonstrations related to reusability of space transportation systems and their associated support equipment. ​

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will be expected to provide technical project support to the reusability section of the Future Launchers Preparatory Programme, which leads the maturation of the required technologies, demonstrators and enabling capabilities for future space transportation systems.  

 

The main priority will be determined jointly at the start of the internship, depending on the department’s actual needs: 

 

  • conducting “business and technical intelligence” on reusabe launch systems development approaches, establishing and maintaining a synthesis of the different realised or intended systems in the US, China, India, Europe, etc.;
  • conducting global space transportation analysis using various internal and external sources, organising a synthesis by segment and associated needed transportation systems, and comparing market studies received from contractors, assessing the proposed business cases;
  • depending on your technical capabilities and profile, providing support for specific tasks related to ongoing ESA demonstration projects.

 

In addition, and as running support activities: 

 

  • supporting the BEST! Initiative on first stages reusability;
  • supporting the Access to Space Club - organisation of online and in-person events as needed;
  • identifying best practices and improvements in Future Launchers Preparatory Programme (FLPP) open competition procurement actions, with a focus on improving the connection between technology providers and primes; 
  • supporting FLPP knowledge management processes; standardisation and simplification of project management processes including the development and use of efficient tools for management.

Result Orientation

Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

Title: Intern in the Communication Department - Internal Communication Products and Channels Office
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

As an Intern within the Internal Communication Products and Channels Office of the Products and Channels Division within the Communication Department, Director General’s Services, you will be working as part of a small team distributed over several European Countries, with duty station being ESTEC in the Netherlands. Under the supervision of the Head of Internal Communication Products and Channels, you, as an Intern, will assist with internal communication activities within the European Space Agency. 

Current internal communication objectives are to inform employees about the 2040 strategic objectives, unify ESA's workforce with a clear brand narrative, enhance engagement and support cultural transformation, in particular through a new communication and intranet platform (called One ESA), inspire staff by emphasising the impact of their contributions, increase visibility of leadership communication, and improve internal corporate and institutional communication. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Audio-Visual Production, Workforce Engagement and Communities, and Event Organisation.

 

As an intern, you will support the work of the Internal Communication Products and Channels Office by carrying out the following tasks:

 

  • creating Shorts for the OneESA Experience Platform addressing the ESA workforce. Shorts are an engaging way to display video content, based on posts from a Media news channel. They are ideal for the Employee App, bringing a familiar social media-style experience to the platform;
  • creating and maintaining a dedicated Media channel or News page for Shorts on the OneESA Intranet platform;
  • supporting the production of podcasts, images and videos;
  • contributing to organising events and town halls for the workforce.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge of corporate communication, in particular internal communication and video production is a plus. 
 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Communication Department - Digital Content and Outreach for International Audiences
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

The ESA Member States Outreach Office is responsible for all media and public relations between the European Space Agency and its member states.
The team, based at ESA ESOC in Darmstadt, Germany, focuses on Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Poland and the Czech Republic.
They work with governments, the press and the general public to inform and educate about all of our space activities, from astronauts to asteroids, Earth observation to satellites flying to Jupiter. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Digital Content and Outreach for International Audiences

 

How do we engage diverse audiences across Europe? How can we make the best use of digital platforms to share compelling stories about space? What types of outreach activities help bring these stories to life and connect with people?


By joining the Communications team at ESA's European Space Operations Centre (ESOC), you will gain hands-on experience in digital communications and public outreach. Working alongside experienced professionals, you will develop your understanding of how international organisations create and deliver effective, integrated communication campaigns in a multilingual environment. 

 

Your tasks will include:

 

  • exploring ways to make articles, information sheets, and other content more accessible and engaging for the public through ESA's new content management system;
  • supporting fact-checking and research activities;
  • reviewing translated content;
  • contributing to the creation and distribution of digital and audiovisual materials. 

 

Depending on your interests and skills, additional tasks may include:

 

  • supporting new outreach initiatives;
  • contributing to the development of audiovisual communication products for international audiences.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Due to the nature of this position, native-level proficiency in German is mandatory.
Knowledge of Polish and/or Czech language is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics.

If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Title: Intern in the Climate Action, Sustainability and Science Department - Applications Section
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

The Applications Section is primarily engaged in research and development (R&D) for Earth observation-based solutions that address both European and global environmental and development agendas. Our projects typically involve key stakeholders throughout the design, development, and validation phases to ensure that the innovative EO-based solutions are effectively integrated into end-users’ operational systems and practices. The Applications Section, based at the ESRIN site of ESA, comprises several EO experts, each overseeing specific domains where EO data is utilized, including marine, carbon, and agriculture, among others. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Cocoa from Space: Operationalising Cocoa Monitoring

 

This internship will build upon a recently developed global cocoa map, currently under review, with open-source code available through ESA. This work provides a 10-metre resolution baseline of this important cash crop worldwide, revealing that nearly two-thirds of global cocoa is grown under agroforestry and that 28–53% of cocoa areas are misclassified as natural forest in existing baselines—a critical challenge for deforestation-free supply chain regulations.

 

While the scientific algorithm is established, it has not yet been translated into a tool accessible to cocoa technicians, certification bodies, and national agencies. You will bridge this gap by transforming the research workflow into a user-friendly pipeline and developing interactive demonstrations for ESA's Application Propagation Environments (APEx) platform.

 

Your tasks will include:

  • package the existing deep learning workflow into a streamlined pipeline that generates cocoa maps for selected regions with minimal user intervention;
  • test the pipeline with case studies from two cocoa-producing countries, documenting performance and limitations;
  • create simple visualisation and reporting tools—such as area statistics, confidence maps, and basic change indicators;
  • develop interactive demonstrations on the APEx platform to showcase the tool's capabilities to the broader community;
  • prepare clear documentation and a step-by-step user guide for cocoa monitoring agencies.

 

Learning objectives: You will gain hands-on experience in large-scale satellite image processing and time-series analysis, cloud-based Earth observation workflows, translating scientific research code into user-facing tools, software packaging, preparing Earth observation applications for community showcase on APEx, and understanding cocoa supply chain policy. You will deliver a working pipeline, user manual, demonstration maps for selected countries, and APEx-ready interactive demonstrations.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge of and background in Earth observation, image analysis, and data processing are assets. Strong programming skills in Python and experience using geospatial libraries (e.g., rasterio, xarray, GDAL) are highly desirable. Familiarity with cloud computing platforms for Earth observation applications and experience with time-series analysis of satellite data are assets. 

 

The preferred duration for this internship is six months.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Earth Observation Projects Department - CO2M mission
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The CO2M mission aims at monitoring the anthropogenic CO2 emissions from Space. It is a key element providing the European Commission with the means to monitor worldwide at a high spatial resolution the evolution of the main greenhouse gases. The spacecraft is made of three optical instruments: A CO2&NO2 Imaging Spectrometer (CO2I), a Cloud Imager (CLIM) and a Multi Angle Polarimeter (MAP). CO2I is the main instrument measuring the spectral signature of CO2 in the NIR and SWIR domains. MAP aims at measuring the aerosols concentrations to improve the retrieval of the CO2 while CLIM aims at flagging the acquisitions performed in the presence of clouds. 
Flight models of the three instruments are now available and their on-ground characterisation and calibration have started. Such an on-ground campaign is a key step in the build-up of the database used for the data processing of the in-flight measurements to come.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: CO2I instrument

 

In the first instance you will have to familiarise yourself with the concept of the CO2I instrument, in particular its optical design and its detection chain architecture. You will then have to get familiar with optical ground support equipment used to perform the characterisation of the instrument and the processing chain developed to extract the key performance parameters from them (so called Calibration Key Data). 
A large quantity of data has already been recorded during the CO2I, first characterisation and calibration campaigns and their processing has started. You will be involved in the processing of such a large set of data, and in further developing existing simulators of the instrument acquisitions and processing to refine the understanding of the mission performances.
You will work with the engineers responsible for the instruments, together with the optical engineer, the detection chain engineer and the performance engineers. 

 

2) Topic 2: MAP & CLIM instruments


In the first instance you will have to familiarise yourself with the concept of the MAP & CLIM instruments, in particular their optical design and their detection chain architecture. You will then have to get familiar with optical ground support equipment used to perform the characterisation of the instrument and the processing chain developed to extract the key performance parameters from them (so called Calibration Key Data). 
A large quantity of data has already been recorded during the MAP & CLIM first characterisation and calibration campaigns and their processing has started. You will be involved in the processing of such a large set of data, and in further developing existing simulators of the instrument acquisitions and processing to refine the understanding of the mission performances.
You will work with the engineers responsible for the instruments, together with the optical engineer, the detection chain engineer and the performance engineers. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation

Continuous Improvement

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

A good knowledge of MATLAB (or Python) software is required.

Title: Intern in the Mission Management and Ground Segment Department - Common Services Section
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of the Director of Earth Observation Programmes, the Head of the Mission Management and Ground Segments Department is responsible for the management of the EO missions handled by ESA in their Phase E2, and for the design, development and operation of the related Payload Data Ground Segments (PDGS) as well as the related data management.

 

In executing these functions, the Head of Department is supported by the:

  • Mission Management and Product Quality Division (EOP-GM);
  • Copernicus Ground Segment and Data Management Division (EOP-GC);
  • ESA Ground Segment and Data Management Division (EOP-GE);  
  • Project Control and Management Support Office (EOP-GP).

 

Under the ESA Ground Segment and Data Management Division, the section of Common Services (EOP-GES) is responsible for:

  • Earth Observation data management through the design, implementation and operations of data acquisition, generation, access and archiving services to users including the day-to-day interface to the users;
  • Evolution of the Earth Observation data management concept and architecture in response to emerging operational needs and including specific R&D projects.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Background
The Earth Observation domain is exceptionally relevant at this time, becoming determinant in the definition of earth models for the prediction of environmental changes and at the same time identification of factors that could reduce their impact. The science community is confronted with a challenge objective for which it is critical to provide all the necessary elements for effective research. The increased amount of information and data available is creating the need to follow closely and timely the scientific community and react promptly to incoming needs.
A close monitoring of the services deployed in the Earth Observation Framework for the handling of the data management, namely generation, archival and dissemination, is the only means of following closely the user behaviour and come back with proper solutions. 
Applying modern technology, a service for the monitoring of all functions deployed, together with a set of timely populated dashboards and regular generation of reports allows for faster reaction to issue or demand changes.

 

In this particular case, we are looking for a young expert that could support the validation, identify improvements and further evolution of the approach in the collection, management and visualisation of metrics derived from all the operational services.

 

Objective

Title: Intern in the Legal Services Department - Institutional Law Division
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

The European Space Agency is an international organisation and the European gateway to space. Together with its Member States, the Agency expands the boundaries of discovery and exploration and provides space applications for the benefit of citizens on Earth.

The Legal Services Department provides the full range of legal services across ESA’s programmes and legal disciplines, such as public international law, European law and the national law of ESA’s Member States.

 

The Legal Services Department provides authoritative legal advice to the Director General, the Directorates, but also to Council and other organs of the Agency, to achieve the objectives set out in the ESA Convention. As such the Legal Services Department participates in the decision making among Member States, formulating legal opinions and bringing new ideas to formalise space policies and programmes in Europe.
You will be part of a team of highly motivated, skilled lawyers working in an inspirational, interdisciplinary and multicultural environment.

https://www.esa.int/About_Us/Law_at_ESA/ESA_Legal_Services_Department

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will support the Institutional Law Division on legal matters relating to the governance and functioning of an international organisation. Topics may include:

 

  • the institutional framework and decision-making procedures of the European Space Agency, including the work of its Council and subordinate bodies;
  • the interpretation and application of the Agency’s internal rules, policies and legal instruments;
  • legal questions concerning the status, privileges and immunities of an international organisation;
  • the interaction between public international law, European Union law and the national laws of Member States;
  • legal research, analysis and drafting in support of the Division’s advisory work.

 

Through these activities, you will gain practical knowledge of institutional law and strengthen your legal research, analytical and drafting skills.

 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks:

 

  • carry out legal research and analysis on public international law, including European Union law, and the relevant national laws of the jurisdictions in which the Agency operates;
  • prepare and contribute to the drafting, review and processing of a variety of legal instruments (agreements, memoranda, etc.) and other documents;
  • monitor and review developments in international law, including the evolution of legal doctrine and its practical application in international organisations;
  • contribute to the Department’s daily operations by supporting the work of legal officers.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in public international law, including European Union law, and the relevant national laws of the jurisdictions in which the Agency operates, demonstrated through both study and experience, are an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Intellectual Assets Strategic Management Office
description_html:
Location

European Space Deep-Tech Innovation Centre (ESDI), Villigen, Switzerland  

Our team and mission

The Intellectual Assets Strategic Management Office supports the protection, management, and exploitation of European Space Agency inventions and related intellectual assets. The office provides advice and operational support on the protection and utilisation of these assets, with a particular focus on patents, licensing, portfolio management, and commercialisation pathways. The work helps ensure that inventions generated within the Agency environment can be protected where appropriate, made visible to industry, and used in missions, industrial products, services, or technology transfer activities.
During this internship, you will join a team working at the interface between inventors, technical experts, legal and commercialisation colleagues, and external innovation stakeholders. The role will focus on ESA patent assets and, where relevant, selected software assets linked to technology transfer or commercialisation. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will support the Intellectual Assets Strategic Management Office in the monitoring, administration, and utilisation of ESA patent assets and, where relevant, selected software assets.

Your internship will focus on practical portfolio administration, licensing support, and the preparation of patent assets for commercialisation and technology transfer. 

 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks: 

 

  • supporting patent utilisation tracking by collecting, checking, and organising information on how selected patent assets are used in missions, research and development activities, licensing discussions, industrial products, services, or technology transfer cases;
  • assisting with portfolio administration, including the preparation of short portfolio notes, status updates, and supporting material for internal review and decision-making;
  • helping to prepare clear, non-confidential descriptions of selected patent assets for promotion to industry, including summaries of the technical problem addressed, the proposed solution, possible applications, and development status;
  • supporting licensing and commercialisation activities by helping to organise information on potential users, interested companies, relevant technology domains, and follow-up actions under the supervision of the office;
  • contributing to the review of selected software assets where they are connected to patent promotion, technology transfer, or commercialisation opportunities;
  • interacting with ESA inventors and technical experts to clarify technical content and understand the maturity, possible uses, and exploitation potential of selected inventions;
  • supporting coordination with ESA commercialisation stakeholders, including Business Incubation Centres, Technology Brokers, Phi-Labs, industry, and academia, where relevant to the promotion or use of patent and software assets;
  • helping to maintain structured records, trackers, and short analytical summaries that support portfolio management, licensing follow-up, and reporting;
  • supporting other related activities within the office, as required.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in intellectual property or technology management is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment.
