Title: Intern in the Future Missions and Architecture Department - System Architect Office
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

This position, located in the Earth Observation System Architecture Office within the Department of Future Earth Observation Missions and Architecture, will be responsible for establishing and maintaining a reference Architecture for European Earth Observation systems, encompassing all ESA Earth Observation missions (Earth Explorers, Sentinels, Meteorological, Third Party, Scouts) and taking account of European, national, and commercial systems as well as of systems of international partner Agencies.  

 

The office maintains a detailed view of the European Earth Observation Ecosystem (real world current and planned missions) and a Reference Architecture Blueprint (future world strategic view). Annual observation gap analyses are conducted against user/stakeholder needs that are utilised in formulating EOP strategy. 

 

Using foresight and scenario building approaches and together with the Earth Observation Science Department and with an active external network, the office explores ahead for new domains of Earth Observation with an observatory function. It permanently searches for innovation and opportunities to evolve the Reference Architecture Blueprint. Promising approaches are studied in detail to facilitate the scientific and technical readiness of new Earth Observation concepts.

 

In close dialogue with users and stakeholders, the office conducts system of systems analyses, to assess the scientific, technological, industrial and operational synergies of different Earth Observation missions and systems to identify potential opportunities out to the 2050+ timeframe.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will develop innovative technical Earth Observation scenarios and apply or develop relevant simulation tools to analyse the effectiveness of the use of Earth Observation satellite systems in synergy. The analysis will identify gaps in capability and explore opportunities for new systems of systems architectures and Earth system observatory concepts considering evolving European user needs in a holistic manner. Analyses will cover the 2024 – 2040 and 2040 – 2060 time horizons. 

 

Initial scenarios are to be built around mandatory core missions with reference quality performances (e.g. large Copernicus missions) complemented by other elements in a mixed system architecture approach.

 

Potential tools / guidelines include initial EO system scenarios, an internal data base as well as complementary approaches to benchmark system design and compare different scenarios.

 

These activities offer ample scope for the successful candidate to develop a detailed understanding of future EO space system architecture development using a system analysis-scenario based approach.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • knowledge of Earth Observation remote sensing technologies and the respective downstream science and applications;
  • knowledge of relevant strategic and technological trends and developments inside/outside the space EO domain;
  • IT knowledge in the areas of data bases and programming (e.g. Python).

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Climate Action, Sustainability and Science Department - Harmony Mission
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Earth Science Division, of the Climate Action, Sustainability and Science Department, Earth Observation Programmes Directorate, is based at the European Space Research and Technology Centre. The Earth and Mission Science Division provides the creative vision for innovation and new discoveries in Earth system science, using Earth Observation (EO) in close cooperation with the scientific community.

 

The Earth Science Division team:

  • bridges science and technology by translating ideas and concepts into technical reality and scientific success. It does this by defining, consolidating and managing scientific mission requirements throughout all phases of a mission, and by measuring the maturity of the resulting mission concept;
  • manages scientific research-based studies, providing the scientific foundation for mission concepts and approval, supports the successful development of space and ground segment, in-orbit satellite commissioning and in-orbit scientific achievements;
  • undertakes airborne, marine and terrestrial campaigns contributing to the development of new technologies, mission feasibility assessments, calibration/validation and application development.

 

You will work within the Earth Surfaces and Interior Section of the Earth Science Division, whose role is to provide scientific support throughout the full lifecycle of Earth Observation missions, from mission concept and assessment studies through development, commissioning and routine operations. The Section contributes to mission requirements definition, scientific performance assessment, calibration and validation activities, product development, mission data exploitation, and the advancement of Earth science through the exploration of emerging scientific questions, novel methodologies and future research directions. The Section has expertise spanning Earth surfaces and interior processes, including terrestrial, oceanic and cryospheric systems, as well as geodesy, gravity and magnetic field observations and solid Earth dynamics. Your activities will contribute to and benefit from a diverse and international team of scientists working across a variety of Earth science disciplines. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Harmony is ESA’s 10th Earth Explorer mission dedicated to the observation and quantification of small-scale motion and deformation (velocity gradient) fields to allow data-driven representations of processes in Earth System models, primarily, at the air-sea interface, of the solid Earth, and in the cryosphere. Due to the multi-faceted mission, a number of different simulation and performance estimation models have been constructed. 
The European Space Agency (ESA) is seeking a talented and enthusiastic intern to join our team to use and potentially further enhance the currently available mission performance evaluation tools. 

 

Key Responsibilities:

  • use high-fidelity simulation environments to demonstrate the mission’s capability to deliver science data within the stated mission requirements;
  • identify and suggest areas of improvement within the existing tools, both on fundamental aspects and on user-friendliness;
  • use derived performance evaluations to construct, assess and quantify science data (Level-2) error budgets with a view to product validation metrics.

 

Information on the Harmony mission can be retrieved here: EE10_Harmony_Report-for-Selection_21June2022.pdf. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • a solid understanding of and background in at least one of the Harmony science disciplines and applications;
  • demonstrable programming skills with Python;
  • knowledge of either active microwave (e.g. SAR) or optical remote sensing is considered an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. Title: Intern in the Vega-E Programme Division
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of D/STS, the Head of the Space Transportation Flight Programmes is responsible in particular for:

 

  • preparing and implementing the Space Transportation Flight Programmes;
  • leading the development activities related to Ariane, Vega and Space Rider and managing the exploitation accompaniment of the related flight programmes, except those entrusted to other departments;
  • complementing the Ariane 6 development and implementing the Ariane 6 Competitiveness improvement programme, implementing Prometheus as from the Ariane 6 Maiden Flight onwards and implementing the ESA responsibilities with regard to Ariane 6 exploitation;
  • complementing the Vega C development, implementing the Vega C Competitiveness improvement programme and the Vega Evolution preparatory activities, implementing the ESA responsibilities with regard to Vega C exploitation;
  • completing the development of the P120C and preparing and implementing activities related to solid propulsion of the products and systems described above;
  • establishing the Launch System Master Files resulting from the Ariane 6 and Vega C developments.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Within the framework of the VEGA-E programme, the development of engineering tools is necessary to ensure continuous monitoring of the design loops of liquid rocket engines. The proposed internship is related to the development and validation of engineering models at both engine level (for the MR10 and MR60 engines) and stage level for the VEGA-E LPM (Liquid Propulsion Module). You will use state-of-the-art modelling tools to develop or extend the mathematical models of the aforementioned systems. These models will then be validated using available test results. 

 

The internship will include an initial training phase, during which you will be expected to become familiar with Liquid Rocket Engines (in particular MR10 and MR60) and propulsion systems (LPM), the modelling of their main elements using the EcosimPro software platform and the models already developed. 

 

The second part of the internship will be dedicated to the extension and validation of the dedicated engine and system models, using available experimental data. 

 

During the final phase, you will carry out data analysis and draft reports.  

 

During this activity, you will have the opportunity to collaborate closely with the IPT propulsion specialists and gain a broader understanding of the VEGA Space Transportation System. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in Rocket Propulsion, Fluid Dynamics, Thermodynamics, and Heat Transfer are an asset. 

Due to the nature of the post, a commitment of six months is preferred, depending on the candidate’s availability.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Director General's Cabinet - Protocol Office
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

The Protocol Office is part of the Director General's Cabinet and supports the Director General's engagement with ESA Member States, institutional partners, industry representatives, diplomatic missions and other high-level stakeholders. The office is responsible for coordinating protocol activities across ESA, ensuring consistency in the application of protocol rules and standards, and promoting best practices throughout the Agency.

Under the leadership of the Head of Protocol, the team manages the protocol aspects of official visits, high-level meetings and events at ESA Headquarters and ESA establishments. It also coordinates guest operations for major launch campaigns and mission milestone events, ensuring a professional experience for VIP guests and stakeholders while safeguarding ESA's institutional image and reputation.

The Protocol Office works closely with ESA Directorates and Establishments, Member States' delegations, diplomatic missions, launch service providers, communication teams and external partners to facilitate high-level interactions and represent ESA on protocol-related matters.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will support the Head of Protocol in a broad range of activities related to protocol coordination, VIP relations, event management and guest operations. Depending on operational priorities, tasks may include:

 

  • Protocol and VIP Relations
    • supporting the preparation of official visits by ministers, ambassadors, heads of agencies and other high-level stakeholders;
    • assisting in the preparation of briefing material, guest profiles and protocol documentation.
    • contributing to the maintenance of VIP and diplomatic contact databases.
    • supporting research on protocol practices, diplomatic etiquette and international protocol standards.

 

  • Events and Guest Operations
    • assisting in the planning and execution of high-level ESA events, receptions, inaugurations and official ceremonies;
    • supporting guest registration and accreditation processes;
    • assisting with seating plans, order of precedence, flag arrangements and ceremonial aspects of events;
    • contributing to the coordination of VIP participation in ESA launch campaigns and mission milestone events;
    • supporting the coordination and management of protocol gifts for high-level guests, official visits and institutional events.

 

  • Coordination and Communication
    • liaising with ESA establishments, directorates and external partners on protocol-related matters;
    • supporting the coordination of invitations, guest correspondence and event logistics;
    • assisting in the preparation of protocol guidelines, presentations and internal communication material.

 

  • Policy and Knowledge Management
    • contributing to the continuous development of the ESA Protocol and Guest Operations Handbook and related guidance material;
    • supporting the ESA-wide protocol network by gathering and sharing best practices;
    • assisting in the preparation of reports, statistics and lessons learned from events and launch campaigns.

 

Learning Opportunities: through this internship, you will gain practical experience in:

 

  • international and institutional protocol;
  • stakeholder and VIP relationship management;
  • event and project coordination;
  • guest operations for major international space events and launch campaigns;
  • working within a multicultural and international environment at the European Space Agency.

 

This internship offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the preparation and delivery of high-visibility ESA activities involving senior government representatives, diplomats, industry leaders and international partners.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.
 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality

Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Life Support and Physical Sciences Instrumentation Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Life Support and Physical Sciences Instrumentation Section is part of the Optics, Robotics and Life Sciences Division. Our team works in the area of life support technologies for Human spaceflight, In Situ Resource Utilisation, planetary protection and small payload development for planetary missions, like the Moon and Mars. We do technology development for future missions and support flight projects under implementation as well. In this context we work on In Situ Resource Utilisation processes, with a focus on molten salt electrolysis.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Currently, experiments on oxygen production using molten salt electrolysis are being performed in the ESTEC laboratories. 
These experiments will reduce the samples to extract the oxygen and turn the samples into metallic powders, potentially suitable for additive manufacturing. Although these electrochemical experiments can use powder material, a sintered block is preferred. The whole process poses many challenges in terms of material and electrolyte stability, process efficiency and yield, sintering process parameters and optimisation.

 

In this internship, you are expected to:

  • learn about the lunar materials and environment;
  • learn about the lunar soil simulants and variations to actual lunar soil;
  • learn about existing processes in the field of In-Situ Resource Utilisation (ISRU);
  • develop a comprehensive procedure to sinter lunar soil and lunar soil simulant;
  • characterise lunar soil simulant before and after sintering by SEM/EDX, XRD, XRF, X-Ray Tomography;
  • support the electrochemical experiments extracting the oxygen from the sintered lunar soil simulants.
     

You will also be immersed in the ESA environment which includes space mission preparation and experimentation.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge of Materials Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering or Aerospace Engineering.
Experience with molten salt electrolysis and high-temperature materials is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - Deep Space and External Services Section
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

You will be directly contributing to the objectives of the Facility for Operations Experimentation (FOX) (https://www.esa.int/Enabling_Support/Operations/Facility_for_Operations_Experimentation_FOX).

​ 

​FOX, based at ESA’s European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, Germany, is an initiative designed to support operational experimentation, technology validation, in-orbit demonstration/validation (IOD/IOV), qualification activities, end-to-end operational assessment and experimentation support for both traditional and New Space missions.  

 

​FOX facilitates experimentation, qualification, interoperability and operational validation activities that may be difficult to perform within purely operational service environments. Experimental applications, services and concepts can be tested and progressively adopted by mainstream missions. Furthermore, FOX contributes to increased interoperability and operational readiness across the evolving New Space ecosystem. 

​ 

​FOX supports ESA internal users as well as universities, research institutes and companies prototyping, testing and validating innovative operations concepts and technologies by fostering innovation, experimentation, and cross-functional collaboration in the domain of ground operations. Typical users benefitting from FOX services span from traditional space missions to CubeSats and SmallSats manufacturers and operators, as well as Ground segment developers and ground station service providers. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will be part of the FOX team, gaining insight into operational challenges and contributing to the development of novel solutions for future mission support. You will be actively involved in ongoing experimental activities, including system prototyping, testing, integration, and performance evaluation, and will participate in regular technical discussions and collaborative reviews across disciplines. The internship provides an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a highly dynamic and interdisciplinary environment at the intersection of operations, engineering, and research. 

​ 

​You can choose between the following topics: 

​ 

​Topic 1: Integration and validation of Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability (DIFI) solutions 

 

​Activities include the use of Software Defined Radio (SDR) & Digitizers/Samplers to be integrated, configured and validated within the FOX operational environment. In particular, you will focus on the implementation of DIFI to enable SDR interoperability using a generic DIFI enabled sampler. You will learn how to configure and operate SDRs, especially for what concerns user-friendliness, sustainability and reliability aspects. 

​ 

​Topic 2: Harmonisation of ground station interfaces and protocols for enhanced interoperability 

​

You contribute to the integration of external systems using different protocols into the centralized FOX ground segment environment. You will tailor and validate interfaces with the aim of improving interoperability aspects for both real-time telecommanding and telemetry reception, as well as tracking and scientific data downlink. The final goal is to centralise services and allow users to transparently adapt well-established standardardised protocols without the need to embark in developing custom interfaces. You will learn how mission users connect to ground stations with a special focus on interoperability aspects and their trade-offs for real operational environments.​ 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

  • Knowledge of Python or another relevant programming language; 
  • general understanding of Radio Frequency communication systems and signal processing; 
  • basic understanding of ground station operations; 
  • familiarity with software defined radios and/or ground station protocols is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Technology and Commercialisation Contracts Division
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The team you would be joining is a dynamic and international group of legal professionals who share a strong passion for space and for the transformative potential of space technology. Our work sits at the intersection of law, technology and innovation, supporting projects that turn space capabilities into practical applications and services on Earth. 

 

In particular, the team is involved in the contractual and legal aspects of space technology application projects, including projects making use of satellite-based assets and services. We work closely with technical teams and other experts to understand the objectives of each project and identify the most appropriate contractual and legal solutions to support their successful implementation.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As a Contracts intern, you would have the opportunity to gain first-hand exposure to the legal and contractual challenges arising from innovative space projects, while developing an understanding of how legal expertise can contribute to the development, deployment and commercialisation of space technologies and applications.

You would learn alongside contract officers and specialists from different nationalities and professional backgrounds, in a collaborative and international environment. This is an opportunity to combine your legal skills with an interest in cutting-edge space technology and to see how contracts and legal frameworks can help transform innovative ideas and space assets into real-world satellite applications.

You will learn how procurements are performed at an international level, you will understand what the requirements to launch a public procurement are, what is the best procurement procedure for your objective, how to make sure that the procurement is performed according to the principle of fairness, ensuring equal treatment of the involved bidders and how to select the best offer with respect to the budget available.

The experience you will gain may help you further to go on working in the legal practice as a lawyer or as legal counsel in a company dedicated to the booming space sector. During your internship, you will prepare contracts, adapting them to the objectives of the procurements.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in mergers and acquisitions is an asset and so is the knowledge of AI. 

Knowledge of technology and law would also be an asset. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Electrical Department - Antenna and Sub-millimetre Waves Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Antennas and Sub-millimetre Waves Section provides functional support to ESA projects across all the various domains (Navigation, Earth Observation, Telecommunication/Secure Connectivity, Human Robotic Exploration and Launchers) and carries out technological research (R&D) in the field(s) of space antenna systems, submillimetre wave instruments and associated technologies. 

 

The Antennas and Sub-millimetre Waves Section covers:

  • analysis, engineering, RF modelling and design tool developments of stand-alone antennas (ground and space) as well as interference effects among antennas and with the spacecraft structure or other platform (like aircraft/train/vehicle);
  • design and analysis of all antenna (active and passive) sub-systems including e.g., stand-alone radiators, arrays, reflector, lens optics, dichroics and their associated focal plane;
  • analysis, engineering, RF modelling and design tool developments of instrument architecture, antenna, front-end technology and components for sub-millimetre wave applications;
  • antenna measurements and RF material characterisation.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Assessment of Error Sources and Calibration Techniques in Active Phased Arrays

 

Calibration is a key element in the operation of active phased array antennas. Small amplitude and phase errors caused by component tolerances, thermal effects, and ageing can significantly degrade beamforming performance, antenna gain, pointing accuracy, and sidelobe levels. Effective calibration enables these imperfections to be identified and compensated, ensuring that the array achieves its expected performance throughout its operational lifetime.

 

The goal of this internship is to investigate the calibration of active phased array antennas, assess the impact of hardware imperfections on beamforming performance, and evaluate modern calibration techniques applicable to large-scale and next-generation antenna system. Activities for this internship include:

  • conduct a comprehensive literature review of modern calibration techniques for active phased arrays, including conducted, radiative, adaptive and automated calibration approaches;
  • identify the main error sources and performance drivers affecting active phased arrays, including manufacturing tolerances, gain and phase variations, thermal drifts, mutual coupling and frequency-dependent effects;
  • gather and analyse performance and stability data of key array components to quantify their contribution to overall array performance degradation;
  • develop a representative numerical model of an active phased array using MATLAB and, where appropriate, HFSS, CST, TICRA or ADS, including realistic hardware impairments and environmental effects;
  • implement and evaluate one or more selected calibration techniques and assess their effectiveness, robustness and scalability in mitigating identified error sources;
  • summarise the findings in a detailed technical report, including recommendations, identified technology gaps and potential future developments in active phased-array calibration.

 

What you will learn:
The intern will develop knowledge of active phased-array antennas, modern calibration techniques, RF system modelling and performance analysis, while gaining practical experience in assessing the impact of hardware imperfections and evaluating calibration approaches through numerical simulations.

 

2) Topic 2: Real-Time Reconfigurable Active Arrays with Nulling Capabilities for LEO Constellation Ground Stations

Context & Problem

To monitor and track the growing number of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, next-generation ground stations require advanced active antenna systems. Currently, market solutions are virtually non-existent or come at prohibitive costs (>€10M per system) due to the strict demands of multi-beam operation, True Time Delay (TTD) performance, and wide fields of view (FoV). Existing commercial alternatives offer limited bandwidth and a restricted number of concurrent beams. Meanwhile, conformal solutions—like the truncated pyramid architecture using 5–6 inclined panels—add significant mechanical and structural complexity.

 

Proposed Solution & Key Technical Novelties
Building upon a recent ESA patent [RD1] filed in June 2026, this project focuses on optimising a completely flat active phased array capable of dynamically generating 10–12 real-time reconfigurable beams over a wide scanning range (up to 70° from boresight across all azimuthal planes).

 

Key technical features and advantages include:

  • Flat Architecture: Completely replaces complex conformal/pyramidal structures, drastically simplifying fabrication and maintenance.
  • Dynamic Sub-Arraying: The number and spatial layout of active radiating elements adjust dynamically per beam. Beams pointing toward the horizon automatically allocate more elements to compensate for scan loss compared to zenith-pointing beams.
  • Seamless Hand-Over: Solves panel-to-panel hand-over issues inherent in multi-panel conformal systems by synthesizing all beams across a single aperture.
  • Maximised DC-to-RF Efficiency: Employs equi-power (uniform) amplitude excitation across active elements to optimise amplifier efficiency, using element positioning, phase tapering, and selective element activation as the primary degrees of freedom.
  • Interference Mitigation (Nulling): Integrates adaptive pattern nulling to enhance system resilience and support dual-use communications in contested or high-interference environments.

 

Design Trade-offs & Market Impact
While the flat footprint is physically larger than a truncated pyramid structure, it significantly reduces mechanical complexity. For professional ground station applications, operational constraints on size, weight, and power (SWaP) can be relaxed in favour of maximizing RF performance—specifically EIRP, operational bandwidth, and angular coverage.

 

Once realised, this array architecture will offer high-value commercial opportunities across Satellite Telecommunications, Earth Observation (EO), and Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS).

 

[RD 1] P. Angeletti, M. Pellet, G. Toso, “Method for Antenna Array Synthesis and Dynamic Operation with Steerable Main Beam and Targeted Nulls”, filed June 1st 2026, patent application PCT/FR2026/010143

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Mechanisms Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Structures, Mechanisms and Materials Division (TEC-MS) is the centre of competence of the Agency in all areas related to Spacecraft and Launcher Structures, Mechanisms, as well as Materials and Processes.

 

Within this frame, the Mechanism Section (TEC-MSM) is the focal point for matters relating to the design, engineering and verification of space mechanisms.

 

This entails in particular responsibility for:

  • overall mechanisms definition, design and engineering;
  • mechanisms performance evaluation, simulation and analysis (including hardware tests where appropriate);
  • mechanisms technology research and development (addressing areas such as tribology/lubrication engineering, tribology free and compliant mechanisms, mechanical components including ball bearings and gears, position sensors, electric motors, new/alternative actuation principles e.g. by using active/smart materials, …);
  • mechanism and actuator drive and control concepts targeting higher positioning accuracy and/or lower micro-disturbances;
  • pyrotechnics.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will be given some specific tasks, which may include:

 

  • critical review of design / analysis / simulation / optimisation / test activities / characterisation / validation (up to the correlation of analysis with test results) in the domain of space mechanisms;
  • feasibility assessment of new mechanism design concepts;
  • participation in the definition and implementation of R&D activities;
  • participation in the project review process;
  • participation in CDF (Concurrent Design Facility) studies;
  • support of in-house research and technology investigations using hands-on laboratory facilities.

 

In the frame of above-mentioned activities, you may have to use the following software packages: MATLAB/Simulink®, CAD design tools (such as FreeCAD or SolidWorks) or other more specialised software tools (such as Abaqus, ANSYS Maxwell, COMSOL, ADAMS, LabVIEW, CABARET, RBS-DYN, OptiStruct, etc.), with particular emphasis on:

 

  • time and frequency domain performance representation and analysis;
  • multi-body system modelling and simulation;
  • design (including topology optimisation) and FEM analysis of compliant mechanisms;
  • electromagnetic system modelling and simulation;
  • multiphysics modelling and simulation;
  • ball bearing loading/strength and stiffness analysis;
  • test data acquisition and post-processing

 

Furthermore, you may be involved in development, design, manufacturing and test activities using and extending the test benches of the Space Mechanisms Hands-on Laboratory Facility at ESTEC. You may also be involved in the prototyping of various mechanisms by utilising additive manufacturing capabilities available at ESTEC.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Specific competence in one of the following disciplines will be considered an asset:
Mechanical and mechatronics engineering, with a good understanding of tribology, ball bearings, gears, electrical motors, sensors, smart materials and compliant mechanisms, as well as of instrumentation and testing of electro-mechanical equipment.
Proficiency in the use of engineering software tools would be very helpful.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Systems Department - Development of PVT Algorithms for Lunar Users
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The End-To-End Systems Engineering Division (TEC-SE) is responsible for supporting projects for the Engineering of E2E systems, the associated security aspects, E2E systems integration/verification activities (SIV), and service preparation. To serve these functions, the Head of the End-To-End Systems Engineering Division defines and executes the associated technology developments and studies, as well as the verification and validation laboratory facilities, and supports the preparation of the relevant engineering standards.

 

The E2E Systems Division consists of five sections and associated laboratory facilities:

  • Navigation Systems Definition Section;
  • Navigation Systems Implementation and Validation Section;
  • Systems Security Engineering Section;
  • Telecommunication Systems and Techniques Section;
  • E2E System Comms Section.

 

The role will be within the Navigation Systems Implementation and Validation Section, which provides expert advice and engineering support to ESA projects, programmes, and studies in the fields of radio navigation and Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS).

 

Moonlight is one of ESA's ongoing programmes, under which a Lunar Communications and Navigation System (LCNS) constellation is being developed to provide communication and navigation services for lunar environment.

 

The role includes advanced lunar navigation algorithms development capable of estimating a user's Position, Velocity, and Time (PVT) using measurements from a single navigation satellite orbiting the Moon. The resulting capability will support the provision of navigation services during the initial deployment phase of the Moonlight system, when only a single navigation satellite may be available before the full constellation is established.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Advanced lunar navigation algorithms development capable of estimating PVT using measurements from a single navigation satellite orbiting the Moon.

 

Your tasks will include:

  • conducting research and developing innovative algorithm(s) for Position, Velocity and Time (PVT) estimation in the lunar environment using measurements (i.e. doppler and code) from a single Moonlight navigation satellite;
  • developing, implementing and validating the PVT algorithm(s) through simulation and performance assessment activities;
  • performing sensitivity analyses to assess the impact of key error sources, including satellite orbit determination and timing synchronisation (ODTS) and receiver clock errors;
  • investigating and analysing the use of additional information sources available in the lunar environment, such as Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) and communication signals from the ESA Pathfinder satellite, to enhance navigation performance;
  • evaluating the algorithm performance under different lunar operational scenarios, including the initial Moonlight deployment phase when only a single navigation satellite may be available.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • good knowledge of MATLAB, Python or other related programming languages;
  • familiarity with Satellite based navigation concepts such as Earth GNSS.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Title: Intern in the Space Safety Programme - Space Weather Office
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

The ESA Space Safety Department takes care of all potential hazards and threats from space or in space, which can impact human activities, infrastructure, or related applications. The spectrum of tasks ranges from gathering the basic understanding of space hazards originating from our Sun, from human space debris, or from asteroids potentially colliding with the Earth. It also addresses basic approaches to mitigate these hazards and to implement space systems end-to-end in a sustainable and eco-compatible way. Moreover, several corner stone missions are underway to demonstrate basic methods of space weather forecasting, asteroid deflection and active space debris removal from orbit. 

 

In execution of these tasks, the Space Safety Department has the following entities: 

  • Mission Implementation Division (OPS-SM); 
  • COSMIC Project Manageent Office (OPS-SC); 
  • Space Weather Office (OPS-SW); 
  • Planetary Defence Office (OPS-SP); 
  • Space Debris Office (OPS-SD); 
  • Clean Space & Circular Economy Office (OPS-SY); 
  • Frequency Management Office (OPS-SF); 
  • Programme Coordination Office (OPS-SX). 

 

Space Weather Office is responsible for developing the ESA Space Weather System that allow nowcasting and forecasting space weather, i.e., the enormous eruptions in the Sun that impact the environment everywhere in our solar system. When these eruptions hit the Earth, they can cause major damage in the infrastructure on the surface, damage satellites and endanger the health of the astronauts in space. Geomagnetic storms triggered by the solar events can cause blackouts in power grids, disturb satellite navigation and communication, disturb aviation, transport, and many other functions that we are used to in our daily life. Energetic particles from the solar events can also damage space probes that we have sent to other planets in the solar system. This is why Space Weather Office is developing space weather forecasting capability for other planets like Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter. Space Weather Office is also responsible for development and implementation of the satellite missions for space weather monitoring to make the space weather services to the users possible.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) ​​Topic 1: Space weather missions and instruments design 

​ 

​ESA is developing an enhanced Space Weather Sensor System to provide data for forecasting and to monitor Space Weather effects. Due to the to the asymmetry and complexity of Earth's magnetosphere, the involved particle environment and its dynamics, it is necessary to capture the state of the magnetic field and the particle distribution in a sufficiently large number of sampling points around the Earth, such that it allows state-monitoring and modelling of the involved processes with sufficient accuracy and timeliness. An important aspect for the realisation of observation systems for Space Safety is the need of high reliability, sufficiently long lifetime and low data latencies as the data will be used in operational purposes. 

 

​For this, ESA is currently implementing and studying multiple dedicated Space Weather missions, from hosted payloads to nanosatellites and small satellites, that will be flying in a wide range of orbits. This will allow you to look into the different steps of an ESA space mission, from early study to mission implementation and management of flying missions. 

​ 

​Your role would be to contribute to the mission development of upcoming missions, through analysis of the mission performance utilising different Space Weather models, instrument simulations and data, and mission analysis tools. These analyses will provide insight into the optimisation of the mission design and operations concept and will support the Space Weather team in guiding ongoing industry developments. 

2) Topic 2: Space Weather Product Front-End and UI/UX design 

​ESA coordinates a large-scale project called the ESA Space Weather Service Network. One of the main roles of the Network is to provide a user interface through the ESA Space Weather Service portal (swe.ssa.esa.int) where dozens of European experts display hundreds of different space weather products, from solar observations, to numerical space weather forecasts, all the way down to the tracing of space weather effects on electric grid infrastructure. Academia and industry provide very rich, complete, and high-quality data which is made available through APIs and machine-machine interfaces. The goal of this internship is to investigate upgrading of the front-end layer of this complex system providing a modern, ergonomic, and visually attractive interface with enhanced user experience. 

​ 

​Your role would be to design a prototype of a modern front-end interface for some of the most recent space weather products available for display in the ESA Space Weather portal. Your knowledge of UX/UI and human-machine interfaces will be put to the test, as well as your ability to propose high-quality professional graphic designs. Your tasks will include a detailed report on existing UX and graphic design guidelines from the Agency, and a guideline on key concepts for excellent web design (as expressed for example in the book “Don’t make me think” by Steve Krug). You will be asked to propose a visual identity document, a usability analysis document, and mock-ups of front-end designs for the new space weather products. You will finalise your internship by developing a first software prototype of the new front-end and its interface with the back-end. 

​ 

​The focus of this project will be to define a professional user interface and visual identity. The Agency encourages candidates with high interest and expertise in user experience (UX), user interface (UI) and human-machine interface (HMI) design to demonstrate their ability to transform high-quality data into high-value information for our end-users. A tailored CV and motivation letter highlighting how your profile fits this topic is the best way to apply for this internship.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Topic 1: 

Knowledge and background in space/particle physics, simulations, and data science are assets. 

Previous demonstrated experience with programming is desirable. 

 

Topic 2: 

Background and demonstrated experience in UX, UI, HMI design and programming for software is essential 

Knowledge in designing ergonomic user interfaces and graphics is desirable 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Thermal Control Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Thermal Control Section (TEC-MTT): The section is responsible for all ESA activities related to thermal engineering, related R&D activities and hardware for the thermal control of space systems. It is the centre of competence within the Agency for design and verification of passive and active thermal control systems, cryogenics and refrigeration, heat transport, heat storage and rejection, thermal insulations and thermal protection.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Space Thermal Control Engineering, covering one or several of the activities below:

 

  1. Thermal Design & Analysis: Perform thermal design and associated analysis, including steady state/transient analyses of instrument and satellites following familiarisation with project requirements and Agency’s tools (ESATAN-TMS). This may also include in-flight correlation of thermal analysis models for ESA projects;
  2. Cryogenics: Investigate cryogenic technologies (active and passive coolers) for applications in future ESA spacecraft and launchers;
  3. Heat Transfer & Heat Rejection: Investigate heat transport technologies such as capillary and mechanically pumped two-phase loops, single-phase loops, heat pipes for thermal control;
  4. Thermal Protection: Investigate thermal protection technologies (both re-usable and ablative) for on-going and future missions (e.g. planetary exploration and sample return missions) and re-usable launchers;
  5. Generic thermal control technologies: Investigate innovative and advanced technologies for the Thermal Control Subsystem e.g. tunable infrared emittance coatings with electrochromic-based solutions, phase-change materials, heat pumps, etc. Investigate specific thermal technologies for small satellites and CubeSats.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Title: Intern in the Space Safety Programme Coordination Office
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

The ESA Space Safety Department takes care of all potential hazards and threats from space or in space, which can impact human activities, infrastructure, or related applications. The spectrum of tasks ranges from gathering the basic understanding of space hazards originating from our Sun, from human space debris, or from asteroids potentially colliding with the Earth. It also addresses basic approaches to mitigate these hazards and to implement space systems end-to-end in a sustainable and eco-compatible way. Moreover, several corner stone missions are underway to demonstrate basic methods of space weather forecasting, asteroid deflection and active space debris removal from orbit. 

 

In execution of these tasks, the Space Safety Department has the following entities: 

  • Mission Implementation Division (OPS-SM); 
  • COSMIC Project Management Office (OPS-SC); 
  • Space Weather Office (OPS-SW); 
  • Planetary Defence Office (OPS-SP); 
  • Space Debris Office (OPS-SD); 
  • Clean Space & Circular Economy Office (OPS-SY); 
  • Frequency Management Office (OPS-SF); 
  • Programme Coordination Office (OPS-SX). 

 

The Space Safety Programme Coordination Office is responsible for leading strategic and coordination activities relating to the ESA Space Safety Programme, in close cooperation with the Programme division and offices, including but not restricted to programme strategy, identification of future activities, managing the programme board, overseeing international and European relations, managing industry relations, managing the programme’s communication activities, etc.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​You will be based at the European Space Agency (ESA) Headquarters in Paris. During this internship, you will support the Head of the Space Safety Programme Coordination Office in a number of their duties through the preparation of reports, briefs, background material and presentations for the coordinators’ interactions with the rest of the Agency, ESA Member States and other partners (e.g. foreign agencies, industry, EU).  

 

​You will also be involved in the operations of the Strategic Space Safety Initiatives, especially on activities related to the Zero Debris Charter and space weather services. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Academic and/or practical experience in both engineering/science and social science would be a strong asset. 

Due to the nature of the post, a commitment of six months is preferred, depending on the candidate’s availability.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).
