Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - Astrophysics Missions Division - Spacecraft Operations
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

You will join the Flight Control Team of the PLAnetary Transits and Oscillations of stars mission as it completes its preparations for launch. The mission will use the planetary transit method to discover and characterise planets orbiting other stars, with particular emphasis on Earth-like planets. 

 

Based at the European Space Operations Centre in Darmstadt, the Flight Control Team is responsible for preparing and conducting spacecraft operations. The team has been testing the spacecraft and validating the operational ground segment, including the mission control system, spacecraft simulator, operational procedures and interfaces needed to monitor and control the spacecraft. 

 

The team works closely with the spacecraft manufacturer, the German Aerospace Center, flight dynamics and mission analysis specialists, and the science operations team in Spain. It brings together the contributions of these partners to plan spacecraft activities, send commands, monitor spacecraft health and respond to unexpected situations. 

 

At the beginning of your internship, the team will be conducting an intensive simulation campaign covering both nominal operations and contingency scenarios for the launch and early orbit phase. This will be followed by spacecraft commissioning and the transition towards routine operations. You will therefore support the team during one of the most important phases of the mission and gain first-hand experience of how a spacecraft is prepared for launch and operated in space. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​​Your main task will be to help the Flight Control Team establish a maintainable and extensible data-processing framework for routine spacecraft monitoring and operational reporting. 

​ 

​All telemetry received from the spacecraft and all commands sent to it are stored in a database cluster. This information can be retrieved, analysed and displayed through a web interface or through software interfaces. The European Space Operations Centre provides a common set of tools for automated monitoring, trend analysis and reporting. Before these tools can be used for spacecraft operations, however, they must be configured, tailored to the mission and validated. 

​ 

​You will contribute to the development of a monitoring framework that can be maintained collaboratively by the team and extended with additional spacecraft health-monitoring functions. The framework will include automated execution of monitoring tasks, configuration and change tracking, documentation, and collaborative software-development workflows. Where appropriate, you will also help define methods for testing and validating the monitoring functions before their operational use. 

​ 

​A secondary activity will be to configure tools for monitoring the operational ground segment. This may include monitoring the health of software processes and applications, file exchanges and telemetry database updates, as well as forwarding relevant alarms to the operations team. 

​ 

​You may also support other spacecraft operations preparation activities, including the development and testing of operational procedures and software scripts. 

​ 

By the end of the internship, you will have gained practical experience in spacecraft telemetry monitoring, operational data analysis, software configuration management, collaborative development and the validation of tools used to operate a spacecraft. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

A background in computer science, software engineering, data science or a related technical discipline would be an asset. 

Practical knowledge or experience in one or more of the following areas would also be useful: 

  • programming in Python, including the use of data-analysis and interactive computing libraries; 
  • retrieving and processing data through software interfaces; 
  • development of web-based applications or services; 
  • containerised software environments; 
  • collaborative software development and version control; 
  • automated testing, continuous integration or deployment workflows; 
  • time-series data analysis, monitoring or data visualisation. 

 

You are not expected to have experience in all these areas. An interest in learning new technologies and applying software-development practices in an operational environment is important. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality

Title: Intern in the Systems Department - FDIR System Engineering
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Our team is responsible for Failure Detection, Isolation and Recovery. We support the development of space missions throughout their lifecycle, from early concept studies to operations, with a particular focus on fault management, system autonomy, mission robustness and operational safety.

The team contributes to the continuous improvement of engineering practices across ESA missions by capturing lessons learned from past and ongoing programmes and by supporting the evolution of engineering handbooks, methods and tools. In particular, we contribute to the development of Failure Detection, Isolation and Recovery methodologies and associated engineering toolchains used to improve mission availability, fault tolerance and operational efficiency.

You will work in a multidisciplinary environment involving systems engineering, reliability, software, operations and mission analysis. You will have the opportunity to analyse real mission operational data and spacecraft anomaly reports, identify recurring patterns and engineering lessons, and contribute to the development of future Failure Detection, Isolation and Recovery concepts and monitoring approaches for ESA missions.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

During your internship, you will contribute to the analysis of spacecraft operational history from multiple ESA missions with the objective of extracting actionable lessons learned for future mission designs.

 

Your activities may include:

  • analysing spacecraft anomaly reports, operational events and mission databases from multiple missions;
  • identifying failures, false positives, nuisance alarms and operational workarounds associated with Failure Detection, Isolation and Recovery functions;
  • assessing the effectiveness of monitoring strategies, recovery actions and autonomous fault management concepts;
  • identifying recurring weaknesses, missing observability, excessive complexity or design shortcomings in monitoring and recovery architectures;
  • collecting evidence-based lessons learned and mapping them to engineering recommendations for future missions;
  • supporting the development and maintenance of a structured database of spacecraft monitors, recovery actions and operational experience;
  • contributing to the evolution of engineering tools supporting Failure Detection, Isolation and Recovery design and analysis;
  • supporting the consolidation of traceability between anomaly reports, failure modes, monitoring mechanisms and recovery concepts;
  • contributing to updates of the ESA SAVOIR FDIR Handbook and associated lessons learned repositories;
  • supporting comparative analyses across missions to identify common fault management patterns and best practices;
  • participating in technical discussions with system, reliability and operations engineers.

 

Through this work you will gain practical experience in spacecraft systems engineering, mission operations, fault management, engineering data analysis and knowledge management for complex space systems. 

 

The internship offers a unique opportunity to work with real operational experience from spacecraft missions and contribute directly to improving the robustness and autonomy of future ESA missions.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in one or more of the following areas is an asset:

  • spacecraft systems engineering;
  • Failure Detection, Isolation and Recovery concepts;
  • mission operations or spacecraft operations;
  • data analysis and large dataset processing;
  • aerospace engineering, electrical engineering, computer engineering or a related discipline;
  • experience with Python, databases or data analytics tools;
  • ability to analyse technical documentation and derive engineering conclusions;
  • interest in lessons learned, knowledge management and continuous improvement processes;
  • strong analytical and structured thinking skills;
  • ability to communicate technical findings clearly in written reports and presentations.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Systems Department - Cost Engineering Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Cost Engineering Section provides cost engineering support, tools and estimates to ESA projects and studies, including studies conducted in the Concurrent Design Facility. The focus of the section is the preparation of cost estimates and the review of cost estimates and financial proposals prepared by industry for projects in the early stages of definition (Phase 0, A and B1). The cost estimating process is approached from a system engineering point of view, and is hence more of a technical discipline than a financial/economic one.

 

The section is relatively small, with a total of nine permanent staff, a great team spirit, and good support and interesting work for interns, providing valuable experience for a career in cost engineering, system engineering and project management.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an intern in the Cost Engineering section, you will be involved in the following activities:

  • maintenance of the technical-economic database that constitutes the backbone of the cost modelling capabilities;
  • maintenance and development of cost engineering tools and models;
  • support to Cost Engineers in various studies, mostly those performed in the Concurrent Design Facility.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation

Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

The following are assets for this internship:

  • knowledge of cost estimating and cost modelling;
  • knowledge and background in engineering, and specifically space system engineering;

Title: Intern in the Systems Department - Navigation Systems Definition Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Navigation Systems Definition Section (TEC-SEN) is leading, or providing support to, the Agency’s activities that require expertise in the field of Positioning, Navigation, Timing (PNT) and Geolocation Systems definition, design and development. The PNT and Geolocation domain covers the End-to-End (E2E) Engineering of Positioning, Navigation, Timing and Geolocation Systems, at System, Space, Ground and User segments level, covering links, elements and equipment, system concepts, and all related techniques and technologies, for Earth, Space and Solar System applications, System/Segment/Payload System architectures and performance, signal-in-space and signal processing, GNSS receivers, algorithms, OD&TS, formation-flying and RF/Optical metrology.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Under the supervision of a tutor in the navigation system definition section, you will shape the future Solar System Internet (SSI) Navigation system. You will develop simulators and analysis tools to characterise the performance of SSI at both system and user level. In addition, you will support the definition of an SSI In-Orbit Demonstrator (IOD) mission in cislunar space, aimed at de-risking key SSI technologies, and enabling future lunar science and exploration activities.

 

In particular, you will:   

  • develop end-to-end simulation tools for System Internet Navigation Performance assessment;
  • perform mission analysis for a Solar System In-Orbit Demonstrator in cislunar space;
  • analyse and address navigation use cases for future Solar System missions;
  • investigate autonomous positioning, navigation and time synchronisation concepts for deep-space users and infrastructure nodes;
  • contribute to the definition and evaluation of SSI architectures and deployment scenarios.

  • software development in MATLAB or Python;
  • orbital mechanics, astrodynamics and space mission analysis;

Title: Intern in the Systems Department - Concurrent Engineering and Future Missions Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Systems Department is responsible for Systems Engineering, its implementation within Projects and In Orbit Demonstration and the innovative solutions - in terms of technology and methodology - enhancing its effectiveness: Artificial Intelligence, Advanced Simulation, Augmented Reality, Concurrent and Collaborative Engineering, Cost Engineering, Digital Engineering, MBSE, Sustainability. Standardisation is also within the responsibility of the Systems Department, ensuring that processes are formalised and shared cross the broad community of space stakeholders.


The post you are applying for will be very much connected with the concurrent design environment (e.g. Concurrent Design Facility – ESA - Concurrent Design Facility) and the digital tools enhancing collaboration (e.g. MBSE); moreover, you will get involved in diverse multidisciplinary tasks touching upon all the areas of competence of the Systems Department, making the experience unique and enriching.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will learn about competencies required to cover the role of a Systems Engineer by:

 

1) Actively participating in and supporting:

  • systems and concurrent engineering activities (including CDF Studies);
  • technology developments (e.g. Digital Engineering, MBSE, Augmented Reality, AI and the innovative trends as identified by the ESA Technology Vision 2040);
  • design models and methodologies developments (including MBSE, design to cost, sustainability and Zero Debris roadmaps implementation, etc.).

 

2) Investigating how technology developments in digitalisation (e.g. MBSE, AI) and improved visualisation solutions (e.g. VR/AR) will shape integrated digital environments connecting data, processes and people.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in Engineering is an asset, as well as the following:

  • knowledge and background in Systems Engineering, Mission Analysis and other system-related disciplines;
  • knowledge and background in (model based) Systems Engineering and familiarity with COMET or similar tools;
  • programming experience in either C-sharp and/or Python;
  • proficiency with office automation software and customisation (e.g. Microsoft SharePoint and Excel);
  • experience with SysML and modelling tools such as Cameo Systems Modeler, Enterprise Architect or Capella;
  • experience with engineering tools such as MATLAB Simulink, CATIA, ASTOS, ECOSIM pro;
  • experience with web application development (front and back-end);
  • practical experience with AR/VR/XR technologies, such as Hololens, Blender, Unity, Physx or similar.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Mechanical Department - Materials, Manufacturing and Assembly Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Materials, Manufacturing and Assembly Section (TEC-MSP) ensures that materials and processes used for assembly of spacecraft’s and launchers are fit for purpose over the mission life-time. Its areas of responsibility include:

 

  • the qualification for space flight of all advanced metallic and non-metallic materials, structural ceramics and glasses as well as all related manufacturing and surface treatment processes for all ESA spacecraft and launchers Programme;
  • the development of revolutionary materials and innovative manufacturing technologies both internally and in cooperation with other space agencies and organisations;
  • the failure investigation of materials and processes under performing and impacting ESA space missions;
  • the development, certification and support of new European industrial capabilities, manufacturing processes and manpower skills training related to space applications of materials and components;
  • the establishment and implementation of requirements and standards for the development and the procurement of space grade materials and manufacturing processes;

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

The European Space Agency is implementing the ESA Advanced Manufacturing Cross-Cutting Initiative, which captures the opportunity of adopting revolutionary manufacturing capabilities, advanced materials and associated processes and creates sustainable competitive advantage for the European Space Industry in the global market.

 

The current space missions are often limited in their performances and scientific achievements by the traditional manufacturing processes/concepts. Though Advanced Manufacturing technologies are readily available in the current European industrial landscape, these can be adopted for next generation space hardware manufacturing. This will enable new and highly innovative spacecraft and launchers designs, with significantly reduced manufacturing constraints (including costs and lead-time) and tremendous performances improvement.

 

Through this initiative, the Agency has identified a number of highly innovative materials and associated manufacturing processes which can be span-in and which will be matured to a space qualification level. In particular the following materials and processes are currently targeted:

  1. Additive Manufacturing: Process/structure/property performance evaluation and model verification through mechanical and µ-mechanical characterisation;
  2. Friction Stir Welding, Solid State Joining Technologies for hybrid (metallic/Non-metallic) joining;
  3. Advanced composite materials (polymer, metal and ceramic matrix composites) and their performance characterisation and prediction in extreme environment;
  4. Advanced surface engineering for thermal and corrosion management;
  5. Solder joint reliability (mechanical and thermal fatigue) for high/low temperature electronics;
  6. Performance evaluation and Whisker growth behaviour of Pb-free solder alternatives;
  7. Integrated Computational Materials Engineering - model development and validation.

 

You will use the world leading facilities of the ESA/ESTEC Materials and Electrical Components Laboratory, in order to characterise the above advanced materials and manufacturing processes and perform detailed materials investigations aiming for process/structure/property evaluation and modelling, related to advanced manufacturing processes. This includes the use of a variety of different laboratory methods such as mechanical and µ-mechanical testing, optical microscopy, SEM-EDX/EBSD, X-ray tomography, and XRD. Your work will be integrated into a team which will give guidance for project applications for future missions.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in materials science and engineering covering metallic, ceramic, or polymeric materials. 
An understanding of computational materials engineering, fracture mechanics and diagnostic techniques such as optical microscopy, electron microscopy and mechanical testing is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Title: Intern in the Exploration Science Office - Data Infrastructure
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Within the European Space Agency (ESA)’s Directorate for Human and Robotic Exploration, the Exploration Science activities are a cornerstone of the Explore2040 strategy, driving innovation at the intersection of human exploration and scientific discovery. It integrates exploration-focused science, essential for future missions, with exploration-enabled science, leveraging space for groundbreaking research. With access to ground-based analogues, the International Space Station (ISS), future commercial low Earth orbit (LEO) platforms, the Lunar Gateway, the Moon, and Mars, the programme offers unique opportunities for transformative research in diverse environments. Guided by European values of collaboration, excellence, and responsibility, the programme emphasizes open science, international cooperation, and inspiring future generations. From developing countermeasures for spaceflight to searching for life on Mars, ESA Exploration Science advances knowledge for space and Earth alike.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​Exploration Science activities rely on information about science projects, research teams, organisations, facilities, milestones and scientific outputs. Part of this information is currently distributed across different files and systems, making it difficult to maintain a consistent and authoritative view of ongoing activities and their results. 

​ 

​During this internship, you will contribute to the development of a common data infrastructure for Exploration Science. Working with existing data sources (scientific publications, archiving tools) and user requirements, you will help design and implement reliable ways to structure, integrate, validate and maintain this information. Your work will provide the data foundation for user-facing applications, reporting and future analysis. 

​ 

​Through this internship, you will: 

​ 

  • ​analyse existing data sources and translate information requirements into a structured data model;
  • ​design and implement a relational database with appropriate data-integrity rules;
  • ​build repeatable processes to migrate, clean and transform existing data;
  • ​develop data pipelines and interfaces for retrieving information from external sources, including scientific publication metadata;
  • ​implement data-quality methods for validation, provenance, deduplication and entity matching;
  • ​create reusable data services for applications and reporting tools;
  • ​test and document the data infrastructure to support long-term maintenance and future development. 

​ 

​You will work closely with colleagues developing user-facing applications that use this common data infrastructure. Through the internship, you will gain practical experience in data architecture, relational database development, application programming interfaces, data quality, scientific information management and the development of maintainable data systems in a multidisciplinary environment.​   

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

A background in computer science, data engineering, software engineering, data science or a related technical discipline would be an asset. 

 

You should have: 

 

  • good programming skills, preferably in Python;
  • practical knowledge of Structured Query Language, relational databases and data modelling;
  • familiarity with application programming interfaces and version control;
  • an interest in data quality, data protection and maintainable software. 

 

Experience with data pipelines, machine learning, automated testing, containerisation or scientific data sources would be an additional asset.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Director General's Cabinet
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

The Director General, Council Support and Member State Relations Division within the Director General's Cabinet is responsible for providing all necessary support to the day-to-day work of the ESA Director General, in particular:

 

  • supporting the Director General’s operational activities in coordination with the Director General’s Office;
  • maintaining relations with ESA Member States, including pre-Council consultations, as well as meetings and visits of the Director General. This responsibility includes maintaining briefing notes and up-to-date dossiers on each Member State and ensuring ESA-wide coordinated preparation;
  • preparing the Director General’s internal meetings, providing in particular the secretariat of the Executive Board and organising bilateral meetings with Directorates;
  • the Director General’s correspondence, speeches, presentations, reporting and contributions to publications;
  • the protocol service, in particular maintaining a diplomatic network and managing the VIP participation to launch events with the support of the communication services;
  • monitoring subsidies granted to third parties and memberships.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will put into practice the knowledge acquired during your studies, while supporting the activities of the DG Support and Members States Relations Section within the Director General’s Cabinet. The main tasks will be, in coordination with the other interns in the team, to support the daily tasks of the team and in particular:

 

  • continuous monitoring of space activities and trends, political developments, and policy-related topics of selected ESA Member States;
  • contributing to the weekly updating and distribution of the Member States observatory and associated products;
  • supporting the preparation of background input for meetings of the Director General with ESA Member States;
  • supporting the preparation of presentation material for engagements of the Director General;
  • ad-hoc tasks in support of the team’s activities.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in the areas of political or social science, international relations, space law, policy, politics, and/or related fields would be an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Communication Department - Brand Engagement Office
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

The Brand Engagement Office (DG-COB) is part of the Outreach Division within the ESA Communication Department. Its role is to oversee the application and deployment of the ESA Brand and its components, through communication vehicles aimed at enhancing the brand recognition and reputation such as merchandising, brand partnerships and licensing and ESA establishments’ signage and application.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an intern reporting directly to the Head of the Brand Engagement Office at the ESA Communication Department, you will play an active role in the office’s graphic design projects. As an intern, you will support the work of the Office by carrying out the following tasks:

 

  • supporting the graphic and UX development of digital brand engagement products;
  • supporting the launch of a new range of ESA merchandise through the ESA Shop, both in physical locations and online;
  • creating graphics for merchandise and supporting their implementation and promotion;
  • creating digital products combining graphic design, UX design and creative storytelling; 
  • collaborating with various teams to ensure all products adhere to ESA’s branding standards and are communicated clearly online.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in graphic design, UX/UI design and tools such as Figma, and communication are an asset. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Title: Intern in the EU Relations Office in Brussels
description_html:
Location
EBO, Brussels, Belgium  

Our team and mission

The ESA Brussels office act as the main channel of communication between the Agency and the EU Institutions. Under the authority of the Head of the ESA Brussels office, you will support the activities of the office, related to the actions towards EU Institutions (Council, Parliament, Commission, EDA, EEAS etc.), attending events and conferences, producing reports, contributing to the Office newsletter of the office and carrying out other tasks according to the needs of the Office. 


You will be asked to support the SLE-UB activities both internally, with the programme directorates, and externally, with EU Institutions.


You will have the opportunity to gain experience in a dynamic environment with a large number of contacts within the Brussels “space bubble”, learning how the EU legislative process really works.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

During this internship, you will support the EBO Team with the following tasks:

 

  • ​assist in monitoring of discussions, policy initiatives and legislative developments within European institutions; 
  • ​support the preparation of briefings, reports, presentations and background material related to institutional relations and cooperation with European institutions; 
  • ​contribute to the follow-up of legal and regulatory files, assessing their potential impact on space activities and programmes; 
  • ​participate in meetings, conferences and events, preparing summaries and identifying relevant outcomes and follow-up actions; 
  • ​collaborate with experts from different disciplines and gain insight into how policy, legal, institutional and programme-related activities support the development of the European space sector.

 

​Through this internship, you will develop a practical understanding of European institutional processes, space policy and governance frameworks, regulatory developments affecting the space sector and the implementation of major European space programmes. You will also strengthen your analytical, research, communication and stakeholder engagement skills in an international environment. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

​​Knowledge and background in EU institutions and/or space policy is an asset. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Science Operations Department-AI Automation of Product Assurance & Quality Engineering
description_html:
Location
ESAC, Villanueva de la Cañada, Spain  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of D/SCI, the Head of the Science Operations Department is responsible for the development of the science operations infrastructure under the Directorate's responsibility, the operation of the Directorate’s missions once successfully commissioned, and the curation of all scientific data in the missions’ legacy phase. These responsibilities are discharged in full coordination with the Directorate’s Departments and Offices and as appropriate, with the Directorate of Operations (D/OPS).

 

In implementing their duties, SCI-S is supported by the:

  • Mission Management and Science Operations Division (SCI-SO);
  • Science Operations Development Division (SCI-SD);
  • Data Science and Archives Division (SCI-SA).

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: AI-based Automation of Product Assurance and Quality Engineering

 

Product Assurance activities increasingly rely on information distributed across multiple repositories and tools, including Jira, Confluence, Git-based repositories, SonarQube, software release documentation, and configuration management systems. As projects grow in complexity, a significant amount of effort is devoted to repetitive activities such as collecting metrics, reviewing documentation, preparing reports, verifying data consistency, assessing quality, and consolidating information from different sources.

 

This internship will investigate how recent advances in Artificial Intelligence and Automation can be applied to support and automate process assurance and software quality. You will analyse existing workflows and identify areas where AI can provide benefits in terms of efficiency, quality, consistency, and traceability. Particular attention will be given to activities such as the automatic creation of Jira tickets from user inputs, engineering artefacts or meeting outputs, the generation of Scrum sprint summaries, the production of software release notes, the assessment of Jira ticket completeness and quality, the extraction and interpretation of software quality metrics from SonarQube, and the verification of the completeness and consistency of software release documentation. Additional investigations may include auditing Configuration Item Data Lists (CIDLs) and Verification Control Documents (VCDs), analysing compliance with established processes, identifying inconsistencies between documentation and project repositories, and developing AI-driven assistants capable of supporting Product Assurance engineers in their daily activities.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • knowledge of Software Engineering process;
  • knowledge of Artificial Intelligence and Automation technologies;
  • programming languages: Python;
  • knowledge of testing processes and tools;
  • knowledge of CI/CD and relevant tools such as Jira, Confluence, SonarQube;
  • knowledge of SW quality assurance practices and techniques.

The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Title: Intern in the Earth Observation Projects Department - Event-Aware On-Board Processing for CHIME
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Within the Earth Observations Projects Department, the Copernicus Sentinel Expansion missions are currently under development. One of those missions is the CHIME (Copernicus Hyperspectral Imaging Mission for the Environment). CHIME plans to carry a unique visible to shortwave infrared spectrometer to provide routine hyperspectral observations to support new and enhanced services for sustainable agricultural and biodiversity management, as well as soil property characterisation.

 

You will join the Copernicus Hyperspectral Imaging Mission for the Environment project and work with the system and satellite engineering teams on on-board artificial-intelligence processing and the evaluation of end-to-end mission performance.

 

Further details on the CHIME mission can be found at:

  • ESA - Copernicus Sentinel Expansion missions;
  • ESA - Going hyperspectral for CHIME;
  • CHIME: an overview of its mission, system and planning status; SPIE Proceedings Volume 12729; 1272909 (2023) The copernicus hyperspectral imaging mission for the environment (CHIME): an overview of its mission, system and planning status;
  • CHIME's end to end simulator (CHEES): simulating, testing and generating hyperspectral products;
  • Adrien IGARSS paper;
  • Examples for typical CHIME Level 2 products: Prototyping Vegetation Traits Models in the Context of the Hyperspectral Chime Mission Preparation | IEEE Conference Publication | IEEE Xplore, Retrieval of carbon content and biomass from hyperspectral imagery over cultivated areas - ScienceDirect.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Event-Aware On-Board Processing for CHIME: From Detection to Operations

 

Join the Copernicus Hyperspectral Imaging Mission for the Environment and help turn two public research prototypes into an integrated mission-level on-board processing concept. Previous work produced public results on marine-anomaly screening and night-time fire detection. You will integrate these methods into a configurable decision layer that identifies scientifically valuable pixels and controls how data are preserved, compressed and prioritised for downlink.

 

Core activities:

  • define configurable processing modes for land, ocean and night-time observations;
  • integrate the existing compact detection methods into the mission end-to-end simulator;
  • connect detection masks with selective compression and data-prioritisation policies;
  • quantify detection performance, false alarms, scientific-data preservation and potential downlink savings;
  • assess robustness across different geographic regions, seasons, illumination conditions and representative instrument effects;
  • define operating limits, verification criteria, traceability information and fallback behaviour;
  • deliver reproducible software, trained models, documented datasets and a technical report suitable for public presentation or publication.

 

Depending on the progress:

  • develop a staged validation concept using reference and candidate processing configurations, including possible use of the two-satellite constellation.

 

Learning objectives

By the end of the internship, you will be able to:

  • translate machine-learning prototypes into a mission-level processing and operations concept;
  • evaluate detection performance together with data-volume, product-quality and operational constraints;
  • design reproducible end-to-end simulation and validation campaigns;
  • understand how on-board processing interacts with satellite operations, data compression and ground processing;
  • define operational limits, verification evidence and safe fallback behaviour for configurable processing methods;
  • communicate results through clear technical documentation, well-structured software and quantitative evidence.

 

You will work with mission engineers, data-processing specialists and Earth-observation scientists. You will have access to mission simulation tools, curated datasets and the results of previous internships.

 

The principal outcome will be a reproducible prototype and validation package demonstrating how event-aware processing could increase mission value while maintaining scientific traceability and controlled operational complexity.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • background in machine learning, computer vision, signal processing or remote sensing;
  • practical experience with Python and a deep-learning framework;
  • familiarity with hyperspectral data, transfer learning, model compression or uncertainty estimation is an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Communication Department - Audio-Visual Archiving
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

The ESA Communication Department’s overarching goal is to raise awareness and understanding of ESA’s programmes and activities, and to highlight the concrete benefits these activities provide to every citizen. 
Our content is inspiring through science, technology and innovation, to attract or retain the best talent for European space programmes. We aim to demonstrate the value of space activities to our Member States and their taxpayers.
Within ESA’s Communication Department, the Digital Products and Channels Office is responsible for carrying out and coordinating the planning, technical management, implementation, and publishing of ESA’s digital media and online channels.

As intern, you will join the ESA Video team, which falls within the Digital Products and Channels Office. 
The video production team is producing a wide range of corporate audiovisual productions, from video shoots to live streams and a wide range of video products (editorial videos, explainer videos, long-form interviews, short promotional videos, support for short-form content, and B-roll footage for external media and productions) for various platforms (ESA website, ESA social media and outreach events).

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an intern, you will be part of the video team and support the implementation of its new video storage system by carrying out the following tasks:

 

  • testing the server: sustained read and write speed, upload/download speed, network utilisation, simultaneous utilisation, latency;
  • ensuring that the metadata system is linked to the relevant media;
  • developing a storage architecture, including structuring folder hierarchies and transcoding files where necessary;
  • following the pre-established metadata system and keyword thesaurus, maintaining continuous collaboration with the video editors to ensure that indexing is aligned with media searches on the server, and updating the keyword thesaurus when necessary;
  • transferring video files from archived hard drives to an ESA server (XMAM/NAS);
  • ingesting video files from day-to-day shoots to an ESA server (XMAM/NAS).

 

You will also have the opportunity to collaborate with the ESA archiving project to develop a similar architecture/AI-assisted data management system.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in video editing and data management are an asset.
 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Science Engagement and Oversight Office - Evolution of Borealis Planitia, Mercury
description_html:
Location
ESAC, Villanueva de la Cañada, Spain  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of D/SCI, the Head of the Science Engagement and Oversight Office is responsible for overseeing the scientific content of the Programme, interfacing with the scientific community and providing scientific expertise to studies, projects and missions, also in other Directorates as needed.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Effusive to Explosive to Hollows: Evolution of Borealis Planitia, Mercury

 

Mercury’s northern hemisphere is home to the planet’s largest contiguous expanse of smooth volcanic plains named ‘Borealis Planitia’. Different areas of this continuous unit, however, look very different with concentrated fields of rough ground, and material intertwining amongst raised topography forming smooth-floored valley-like systems. Whilst an effusive origin is accepted for Borealis Planitia, morphologically and spectrally some areas suggest younger explosive volcanic activity. Further still, hollows — small ‘fresh’ looking landforms — are observed in and around what appears to be rough ground formed by explosive volcanism as well as within the effusively emplaced smooth plains.

 

This internship will investigate the relationship between hollows, pitted ground and their parent smooth plains unit. You will use GIS to analyse image and spectral data to decipher how pitted ground and hollows may have evolved through time in respect of their spatial distribution.

 

This work will add to our understanding of the evolution of Mercury’s volcanic material providing valuable context for BepiColombo with MPO and MIO operating in orbit at the time of this internship. Borealis Planitia, particularly the “Vallis” and surrounding areas are of strategic interest to numerous instrument teams and the work undertaken for this internship can help refine targets for the extended phase of the mission.

 

You will be working directly with members of the BepiColombo science team, affording you the unique opportunity to observe a planetary mission as the science campaign commences.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • a background in geosciences;
  • competency using GIS;
  • familiarity with remote sensing data is useful but not essential;
  • knowledge of Mercury geology is desired, but not essential;
  • interest in Planetary Sciences;
  • interest in Scientific Research.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Climate Action, Sustainability and Science Department - Forest Applications
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

The Applications Section is primarily engaged in research and development (R&D) for Earth observation-based solutions that address both European and global environmental and development agendas.

The typical projects of the EOP-SGA Section involve key stakeholders throughout the co-design, development, and validation phases to ensure that the innovative EO-based solutions are effectively integrated into end-users’ operational systems and practices.

The Applications Section, based at the ESRIN site of ESA, comprises several EO experts, each overseeing specific domains where EO data is utilised, including marine, carbon, and agriculture, among others. 

Some of the activities are presented here: eo4society - eo science for society.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Forest Applications

 

1) Your first core task will involve a research-based exercise: 

About 21% of the world’s forest area is currently designated under legal protection. These forests are highly valuable for carbon storage and sustaining biodiversity. However, high annual rates of tree cover loss continue to this day, with impacts both on forest carbon stocks and their biodiversity. It therefore remains difficult to assess how effective protected area designation is as a forest conservation tool. The legal status of a protected area does not automatically mean that active protection is being implemented, particularly in regions with limited financial resources for conservation.

 

ESA’s Sentinel missions are widely used to monitor forests by providing frequent, consistent, and freely available satellite data on forests. In April 2025, ESA also launched the BIOMASS mission with a novel P-band synthetic aperture radar designed to deliver crucial information about forest conditions, changes, and their role in the carbon cycle. 

 

You will utilise BIOMASS mission data in synergy with several other EO missions (particularly the Sentinels) to achieve the following: 

  • develop forest (a) carbon and (b) structural/functional biodiversity indicators for protected areas;
  • map land cover and land cover change within protected boundaries using long-term EO time series, comparing trends inside protected areas with surrounding unprotected lands;
  • evaluate ecosystem condition, for example by tracking vegetation health, fragmentation, or recovery after disturbance;
  • summarise key findings that will concisely and accurately inform international/national policies aimed at forest conservation. 

 

2) Your second task will involve support activities to the Applications Section of EOP, Green Solutions Division. These tasks are aimed at developing management skills and soft skills, supporting the overall career development of the candidate. Some activities include: 

  • design and preparation of materials for conferences/meetings held at ESRIN;
  • participation in project meetings, assisting in review of ESA project reports;
  • participation in inter-section meetings (e.g. with ESA PhiLab), co-development of research ideas and agendas.

 

You will utilise ESA-supported cloud computing platforms for conducting your research. By the end of the internship, you will demonstrate practical experience in scalable Earth Observation processing, applied analytical methods for land monitoring, product validation and uncertainty assessment, and stakeholder-driven development in an international setting. You will also develop a broader understanding of how EO-derived forest information supports international policy and reporting frameworks.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

In addition to the standard requirements in the form, the following would be considered an asset:

  • experience with Earth Observation for land cover mapping and multi temporal satellite data processing; familiarity with forest ecosystems is an asset;
  • strong programming skills (e.g. R, Python), including geospatial data processing;
  • knowledge of machine learning and deep learning for image and time series analysis;
  • experience with cloud or high performance computing environments;
  • ability to communicate results clearly in writing and presentations and to collaborate effectively with international partners.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.
