Title: Intern in the Climate Action, Sustainability and Science Department - ROSE-L Mission
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Earth Science Division, of the Climate Action, Sustainability and Science Department, Earth Observation Programmes Directorate, is based at the European Space Research and Technology Centre. The Earth and Mission Science Division provides the creative vision for innovation and new discoveries in Earth system science, using Earth Observation (EO) in close cooperation with the scientific community.

 

The Earth and Mission Science Division team:

  • bridges science and technology by translating ideas and concepts into technical reality and scientific success. It does this by defining, consolidating and managing scientific mission requirements throughout all phases of a mission, and by measuring the maturity of the resulting mission concept;
  • manages scientific research-based studies, providing the scientific foundation for mission concepts and approval, supports the successful development of space and ground segment, in-orbit satellite commissioning and in-orbit scientific achievements;
  • undertakes airborne, marine and terrestrial campaigns contributing to the development of new technologies, mission feasibility assessments, calibration/validation and application development.

 

You will work within the Campaigns Section of the Earth and Mission Science Division, whose role is to provide support throughout the preparation and development of new future Earth Observation missions, and to validate the data being delivered by those satellites already in orbit. Your activities will contribute to and benefit from a diverse and international team of scientists working across a variety of Earth Science disciplines in support of Earth Explorer, Copernicus Sentinels, Earth Watch and other EO missions.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

ROSE-L (Radar Observing System over Europe in L-band) is a Copernicus Expansion SAR mission that will provide L-band radar imaging of Europe, the global landmass, ice, and oceans. The uniqueness of ROSE-L is linked to the L-band wavelength, that penetrates deeper into natural materials like vegetation, dry snow, and ice compared to C-band, and enhances robustness for interferometric applications in scenarios with abrupt and large surface and ice motion. By coordinating data collection with Sentinel-1 operating at C-band, ROSE-L will maximise the benefits for users providing complementary information, more frequent radar images, and improved coverage across Europe and globally. 
The expanding availability of L-band satellite observations from missions such as the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar mission (NISAR), the JAXA ALOS-2 mission and the CONAE SAOCOM mission, together with dedicated airborne campaigns such as AGRIROSE-L and AfriSAR-2, provides a unique opportunity to support and shape future ROSE-L science activities through the analysis of real datasets.

 

The European Space Agency is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic intern to support the assessment of the sensitivity and added value of L-band radar observations for selected applications.

 

During your internship you will:

  • identify, collect and process datasets from existing L-band SAR satellite missions and/or airborne campaigns such as AgriROSEL using established tools;
  • transform the SAR image data into information such as soil moisture, land cover, forest biomass and other geophysical products for selected application areas, and assess the quality of the information through comparison with independent measurements e.g. field measurements;
  • investigate the unique capabilities of L-band observations and their complementarity with other radar missions, with particular emphasis on the Sentinel-1 mission;
  • document the datasets, methods, assumptions and analysis results in a clear, traceable and reproducible manner.

 

Learning objectives

By the end of the internship, you will have developed practical experience in:

  • understanding how future Earth Observation missions are scientifically prepared, assessed and validated within ESA;
  • processing and analysing spaceborne and airborne radar imagery;
  • understanding how radar measurements contribute to higher-level geophysical products;
  • communicating technical results through documented and reproducible analyses.

 

More information on the ROSE-L mission can be found here: Copernicus L-band SAR Mission Requirements Document. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • solid understanding of at least one Earth observation application relevant to ROSE-L;
  • demonstrable programming skills in Python;
  • experience in processing and analysing satellite imagery.

 

Knowledge of Synthetic Aperture Radar principles, microwave remote sensing, or geospatial data analysis would be considered an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Space Training Team - Video and Multimedia Production
description_html:
Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

The Space Training Team is responsible for the training of European, International Partner (NASA, ROSCOSMOS, JAXA, Canadian Space Agency) and other astronauts about the systems and payloads (experiments) of the Columbus European Laboratory. In addition, the Space Training Team conducts specialist training in Robotics and Space Analogues. In  addition to astronauts, we also train the Ground Support Personnel, or communicators, who support the operation of systems and payloads on board the International Space Station (ISS).

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​We are looking for talented, enthusiastic interns with great multimedia skills (video, graphics, design) to be involved in exciting projects in the Space Training Team. You might be involved in making videos that will be watched by astronauts on board the International Space Station (or even on Artemis Moon missions!) or preparing media for training material for astronauts and the ground-based communicators who support them. There is always a new challenge, and new opportunities. Are you ready for them?

 

​Your tasks might include filming astronauts and editing material for production of public outreach and space training videos, as well as developing assorted multimedia (eg. infographics, illustrations, animations) for use in videos, PowerPoint slides, E-Learning, posters and other purposes.

 

For further information on this internship, please click here: ESA - Space training team – media production​ 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Excellent spoken and written English (C1). 

An interest in human spaceflight would be an advantage but is not essential as you will develop this! A scientific background or interest in science is advantageous but not a requirement as we will help you. Above all you must be enthusiastic, flexible and self-motivated.


Essential skills:

 

  • proficient in using Adobe CC (especially Premiere) or equivalent;
  • good camera skills (Photo and video);
  • good general multimedia/design skills.


Helpful:

 

  • experience in creating infographics and/or working with technical/scientific information;
  • experience of using Learning Management Systems (eg Moodle, Blackboard, Canvas);
  • audio processing skills. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

Title: Intern in the Industrial Audit Services Office - Audit Baseline Services Unit
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Industrial Audit team performs cost audits of the Industries working with ESA and is responsible for a wide range of audit activities. These include:

  • the agreement of cost rates that Industry will use in the preparation of price estimates and proposals for ESA Programmes;  
  • auditing the cost incurred in ESA contracts;  
  • assessing the financial viability and nationality of companies;  
  • assisting in price negotiations and review of financial proposals for ESA contracts.  

 

The team’s vision is to provide high-quality audit services that achieve cost effectiveness and value creation.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​During the period of internship you will be faced mainly with the following tasks:

  1. ​identify areas where AI can enhance the audit process;
  2. ​gathering requirements from various stakeholders to ensure AI solutions meet their needs;
  3. ​researching and evaluating AI tools suited for audit processes;
  4. ​select and propose the appropriate AI technology;
  5. ​propose and possibly execute a plan for AI implementation for auditing activities, considering the following: 
  6. ​ensure data quality, consistency and accessibility for AI applications including review and sustainable maintenance;
  7. ​ensure AI applications comply with relevant ESA regulations and standards;
  8. ​implement and conduct a pilot project to test AI applications in real audit scenarios;
  9. ​monitoring and validating AI model performance and making necessary adjustments;
  10. ​propose policies and procedures, as well as training material for the team members;
  11. ​generate reports and present findings to management and stakeholders.

​ 

​Learning Objectives:

  1. ​introduction and implementation of AI in highly regulated teams and processes;
  2. ​AI implementation at the European Space Agency;
  3. ​Industrial Cost Auditing processes;
  4. ​the European Space Agency environment;
  5. ​international Teams and teamwork.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in business economics or audit is an asset.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the CAVES & PANGAEA Team - Machine Learning Development
description_html:
Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

The CAVES and PANGAEA team specialises in training programmes that equip astronauts and mission developers with scientific, expeditionary and behavioural skills. The group’s primary output is focused around two training programmes, CAVES, a course that uses natural cave systems for expeditionary and human behavioural and performance training, and PANGAEA, a course for geological and astrobiological field training. Complementary to their training goals, these programmes are used as research and development platforms to advance several of ESA’s technological, scientific and operational areas.  

 

One such tool developed for PANGAEA and future missions is the PANGAEA Analytical Toolset. This comprises the Mineralogical Database (MinDB), a curated collection of information on all the minerals found on the Moon, Mars and in meteorites, and the Machine Learning (ML) software that combines deep learning multi-class and multi-label classification algorithms analysing fused multi-modal spectroscopic measurements, enabling a significant accuracy increase of mineral and rock recognition. 

 

Further information on PANGAEA and CAVES programmes can be found on the following websites: 

 

https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/CAVES_and_Pangaea/What_is_PANGAEA 

 

https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/CAVES_and_Pangaea/What_is_CAVES 

 

We are looking for internships to start throughout 2027. Candidates are invited to state their preferred starting date in the cover letter.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the Internship: Machine Learning, Software Development, Spectroscopic Analysis, Planetary Mineralogical Characterisation​

 

​​Interns are sought to contribute to the ongoing enhancement, integration and deployment of the PANGAEA analytical toolset. Depending on the primary specialization, the intern will join one of three complementary streams: Machine Learning (ML) Development and Operations, Applied Software Development or Mineralogical & Spectroscopic Data Curation.


​The activities will include:

 

  • ​developing and testing ML classifiers for multi-method spectroscopic data, including signal unmixing, multi-modal data fusion, hierarchical classification, incremental few-shot learning, conformal prediction and uncertainty estimation; 
  • ​building, maintaining and optimising the PANGAEA Analytical Toolset software applications; 
  • ​evaluating ML outputs against ground-truth multi-spectral MinDB reference archives and petrographic databases, and expanding and curating the datasets.


​For detailed information on this internship position, please click here:  https://www.esa.int/About_Us/EAC/Space_training_team_Planetary_Mineral_Database_Development_and_Validation_of_Spectra_Classification_Methods 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Candidates should possess practical experience in classification techniques, particularly those based on Machine Learning supervised hierarchical classification and regression. Relevant experience includes, but is not limited to, Data mining, Data fusion, Statistics, Clustering, Signal decomposition/unmixing, Incremental few-shot learning, Conformal prediction, CNN or KAN ML architectures. Practical experience in processing and analysing data derived from analytical instrumentation, or working with databases, is also valuable.  

 

Academic or professional proficiency with the Python programming and core scientific computing/ML libraries: NumPy, JAX, TensorFlow, Keras, CatBoost, Scikit-learn.  

 

Additional skills and experience in one or more of the following key areas will be considered a valuable asset:

 

  • accelerating Python code using Cython, JAX or similar performance optimisation tools;
  • practical experience with analysis and visualisation of scientific data (Matplotlib);
  • familiarity with MLOps workflows and dataset integration;
  • for applied ML, experience with modern web application development, user interface design for applications and web frontend integration, and backend services using FastAPI.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Mission Operations Department - XMM-Newton and INTEGRAL Mission Operations
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

The Astrophysics Missions Division is responsible for the design, implementation, and operation of the mission operations ground segment and the spacecraft operations for Science and selected Space Safety programme missions in the area of operations, typically from start of phase B through in-flight commissioning to routine mission operations until the end of mission. The division comprises a variety of missions that are either in preparation, like Plato and Ariel, or in operations, like Euclid, XMM-Newton and INTEGRAL.  

 

The internship takes place in the XMM-Newton and INTEGRAL Flight Control Team, the team of engineers responsible for the day-to-day operation of the spacecraft and its ground systems. The work of the team includes monitoring of spacecraft health and performance, planning and execution of operational activities, investigating and responding to anomalies, and ensuring that the mission continues to meet its scientific objectives safely and efficiently.  

 

XMM-Newton is an X-ray observatory that combines the largest mirror assembly ever flown with advanced detector technology such as CCD cameras and high-resolution grating spectrometers and an optical monitor, observing cosmic objects like black holes, active galaxies or super nova remnants.  

 

INTEGRAL is a gamma-ray observatory equipped with instruments for gamma-ray, X-ray and optical observations, studying highly energetic cosmic phenomena such as neutron stars, black holes, supernova remnants and gamma-ray bursts. It investigates the most extreme physical processes in the universe by observing high-energy radiation. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will support the XMM-Newton and INTEGRAL Flight Control Team to execute the mission operations and to assess the performance of the missions and their ground segment. 

 

You will build up experience in the following areas: 

  • General insight in the know how, organization and culture of satellite operations;   
  • Systems that measure the performance of the various ground segment and spacecraft elements.  

 

Specifically, you will have the opportunity to contribute to the development of a Ground and Space Segment Awareness System. This activity will also involve interaction with a European Graduate Trainee at ESOC. The exact tasks will be tailored to your skills, interests, and project needs. Through this assignment, you will gain valuable knowledge and hands-on experience in the design, functionality, and operations of a satellite control centre, with a particular focus on monitoring and visualising ground segment status.  

 

The Ground and Space Segment Awareness System provides a real-time overview of the spacecraft, ground segment and mission status, helping engineers understand what is happening across the mission. It enables them to maintain situational awareness, assess mission status and support investigating operational anomalies. 

 

The system should be updated and enhanced with new capabilities. Planned developments include the integration of spacecraft orbit visualisation with information on the Earth's radiation environment and improvements to the user interface and experience. Additional activities may include the implementation of further operational and user-driven requirements, such as enhanced visualisation of attitude and orbit control information.  

 

Depending on your interests and the project priorities at the time, there will also be opportunities to contribute to other system enhancements and operational support tools. 

 

This assignment provides exposure to both operational and engineering aspects of mission support systems and offers experience in a multidisciplinary environment closely linked to spacecraft operations at ESOC. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

What you bring: 

  • Good programming skills in Python and familiarity with web technologies (JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, CSS);  
  • interest in developing practical software for data processing, visualisation and operational awareness;  
  • curiosity about satellite operations, space systems and ground-segment engineering;  
  • motivation to write clear, maintainable and well-documented code;  
  • a collaborative mindset and readiness to develop solutions iteratively based on operational needs and user feedback;  
  • experience with dashboards, data visualisation, Grafana or CesiumJS would be an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Exploration Science Office - Assessment of Societal Benefits of Exploration Science
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands or EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

Within the European Space Agency (ESA)’s Directorate for Human and Robotic Exploration, the Exploration Science activities are a cornerstone of the Explore2040 strategy, driving innovation at the intersection of human exploration and scientific discovery. It integrates exploration-focused science, essential for future missions, with exploration-enabled science, leveraging space for groundbreaking research. With access to ground-based analogues, the ISS, future commercial LEO platforms, the Moon, and Mars, Exploration Science offers unique opportunities for transformative research in diverse environments. Guided by European values of collaboration, excellence, and responsibility, the programme emphasises open science, international cooperation, and inspiring future generations. From developing countermeasures for spaceflight to searching for life on Mars, ESA Exploration Science advances knowledge for space and Earth alike. 

 

This internship will be done in close collaboration with the Exploration Strategy Office.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Assessment of Societal Benefits of Exploration Science:

​You will support the Exploration Science Office, in close coordination with the HRE Strategy Office, in developing and applying a structured approach to identify and evaluate the societal benefits generated by ESA’s exploration science activities, from ground-based analogue studies to research performed on ground and suborbital platforms, the International Space Station and future Moon and Mars missions. 

​ 

​Societal Impact Framework Development:

​You will review methodologies and frameworks used by space agencies, research funders, and international organisations to assess the societal, economic, technological, health, and educational returns of publicly funded research. Building on this benchmarking, you will help identify indicators and propose a structured methodology tailored to exploration science, covering benefits such as advances in human physiology and countermeasure development, contributions to terrestrial healthcare (e.g. ageing, rehabilitation, cardiovascular and musculoskeletal health), technology and knowledge transfer (e.g., innovative materials, robotics, sensor and monitoring technologies, data science and AI), industrial and economic spin-offs, and educational and inspirational outcomes. 

​ 

​Impact Mapping and Case Study Compilation:

​Using this framework, you will identify and document concrete examples of societal benefit arising from past and ongoing exploration science studies, such as bed rest and dry immersion analogue research, research on suborbital platforms, and ISS-based investigations, just to name a few. Working with scientists across the Exploration Science Office and the HRE Strategy Office, you will trace research outcomes to real-world applications and compile these into case studies and a reference repository to support impact reporting, stakeholder communication, and the design of future research calls. 
This internship offers insight into science policy and impact evaluation within human space exploration, with practical experience in framework design, benefit-mapping methodologies, and stakeholder communication.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Background: 
A background in life sciences, physical sciences, health or biomedical sciences, economics, public policy, or science communication is essential, along with a strong interest in space research and its wider societal relevance. You should possess strong analytical and synthesis skills, excellent written and verbal communication abilities, and a motivation to contribute to the assessment and communication of research impact. The ability to work independently while maintaining coordination with a team is important. 
The internship is designed for students in their final or second-to-last year of university studies, ensuring they have a solid academic foundation relevant to the tasks involved. 

 

Experience: 
Prior experience in space research is not required. However, familiarity with impact assessment methodologies, research evaluation, socioeconomic analysis, or science communication is considered beneficial. Any relevant experience in structured research, literature reviews, policy analysis, or data synthesis will be advantageous. Given that the internship targets students, the focus is on providing hands-on experience and skills development, rather than requiring extensive professional background.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the ESA Education Office - Inspiration and Education Outreach
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands     

Our team and mission

The intern position concerns the ESA Education programme, in particular inspiration initiatives for 3- to 18-years-old children and school students, including: inspirational events, role modelling, career awareness initiatives, access to space experts for youth and their families to be attracted to space and STEM, and to understand their importance for society and economy. In doing so, address diversity and promote sustainability for a better future. 

 

The intern position also involves communication and promotion activities of the ESA Education programme at large for all target groups (from early childhood to PhD levels) such as web and social media communication, video and goodie production, and event organisation.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​Within the Education Office, you will build experience in inspiration activities for school-level children and families, and in outreach activities for the education programme, such as: 

 

  • ​support the creation and organisation of inspirational events and informal education resources;
  • ​User Experience/Interface (UX/UI) and Publications: web front-end towards user experience optimisation, writing and publishing of articles, social media posts, video scripts;
  • ​other school level STEM education related tasks. 

​ 

​Learning areas: Web User experience (UX/UI), Informal STEM Education, Social media, Communication, event organisation. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge of and/or experience in any of the following areas is a major asset:  

 

  • STEM subject knowledge;  
  • communication, science communication; 
  • content management systems and social media;
  • basic video editing; 
  • event organisation; 
  • knowledge and background in both English and French is an asset. 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Title: Intern in the Exploration Strategy Office - Strategic Communication Support
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Using a partnership between humans and robots, the Directorate of Human and Robotic Exploration Programmes (D/HRE) is dedicated to exploring destinations in space where humans are already living and working – or will live and work in the future – for the purpose of scientific research, economic development, international cooperation and public inspiration.  

 

The Exploration Strategy Office shapes the Directorate’s strategy and policy in line with guidance from ESA leadership, Member States and advisory bodies. It defines future directions for exploration in low Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond, maintains the long-term implementation roadmap, and translates strategic priorities into programme proposals for ESA Council meetings at ministerial level. The Office also develops the Directorate’s benefits plan and leads engagement in international exploration coordination fora. In parallel, it coordinates internal and external communication, manages exhibition assets and visual identities, and acts as the interface with central ESA services on strategy, policy and communication matters.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​Working with the Strategy team, you will help strengthen awareness of space exploration, ESA’s Human and Robotic Exploration programme and its benefits among decision-makers, space and non-space professional communities, and the public. You will contribute to:

 

  • ​translating the directorate’s strategy and objectives into a coherent visual identity and brand;
  • ​using the running and planned exploration missions (e.g. Astronaut missions, International Space Station, European Service Modules for Orion, Argonaut, Rosalind Franklin Mission) as a teaser to develop communication content to promote the exploration benefits and strategy narrative;
  • ​initiatives to enlarge the evidence base of and communicate about exploration and socioeconomic, cooperation, political and science benefits;
  • ​designing and implementing innovative ways to make the directorate’s activities more visible and accessible to the public and decision-makers;
  • ​developing communication strategies, campaign concepts, plans, content and briefing materials;
  • ​supporting the preparatory work to set up a communication strategy and plan for ESA's next Council meeting at Ministerial level, including defining objectives, key messages, target audiences and suitable channels.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Specific competence in one of the following disciplines is essential: Communication sciences, Science communication, Journalism and multimedia or similar.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Audit and Evaluation Department - Evaluation Office
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Evaluation Office is responsible for conducting objective and independent evaluation projects and providing appraisal services to the Director General (DG) and ESA management aimed at improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the Agency’s activities, by:

 

  • conducting a thorough examination of the status of a defined set of activities and assessing their achievements against requirements and objectives, resource constraints, benchmarks and previous lessons learned; 
  • providing recommendations and optimisation advice on how to achieve intended outcomes; 
  • providing specialised advisory services for the timely implementation of transformation actions.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You will support the Evaluation Office in conducting evaluations, organisational reviews and analytical studies aimed at improving organisational performance, efficiency and effectiveness. The team leverages a broad spectrum of analytical approaches, ranging from social science research methods to advanced data analytics and artificial intelligence to produce evidence-based recommendations. As a result, you will contribute to a diverse set of evaluation and analytics activities.

 

Research and evaluation activities may include:

 

  • conducting research, literature reviews and environmental scans;
  • collecting, analysing and synthesising qualitative and quantitative information;
  • supporting interviews and surveys;
  • contributing to benchmarking studies;
  • assisting in the preparation of analytical reports, presentations and management briefings.

 

Data analytics and business intelligence activities may include:

 

  • analysing administrative datasets;
  • supporting data modelling and business intelligence;
  • developing visualisations using Power BI;
  • helping transform structured and unstructured data into actionable insights.

 

This internship offers practical experience at the intersection of research, evaluation, data analytics and organisational transformation within an international public-sector environment.

Title: Intern in the Ground Systems Engineering & Innovation Department - ESTRACK Antenna Performance
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

​The Ground-Based Communication and Tracking Assets Section at the European Space Operation Centre is in charge of the ground station antennas used to transmit telecommands to the satellites operated by the centre and receive their telemetry and payload data, while maintaining stable tracking. 

 

​In our team we take care of the design, procurement, maintenance and evolution of those antennas and their infrastructure. Our expertise spans from radio-frequency to mechanical and servo engineering, and from power generation and distribution to air conditioning systems.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​Electromagnetic simulations, and antenna design analyses provide the reference expectations for the performance of a deep-space ground station antenna system. However, the operational verification of antenna performance requires the ability to assess system noise temperature and antenna temperature under real environmental and operational conditions. Observations of astronomical radio sources, together with environmental and site-specific measurements, provide a unique and powerful means to evaluate the end-to-end performance of deep-space antenna systems, enabling the characterisation of radio-frequency, environmental, geometric, and operational effects directly from observational data. 

​ 

​The main objective of the internship is to develop a methodology and software framework for determining the performance of ESTRACK deep-space antennas for any pointing direction, frequency band, and environmental condition, and to identify measurable indicators that describe the overall receiving performance of the antenna system. 

​ 

​The activities will address topics such as: 

  • ​Antenna temperature and system noise temperature modelling;
  • characterisation of environmental noise contributions from the antenna surroundings;
  • analysis of radio-frequency interference and site-dependent noise sources;
  • development and refinement of antenna radiation pattern models at deep-space communication frequencies.
  • investigation of spillover, blockage, scattering, and ground noise effects;
  • assessment of the impact of antenna pointing direction on receiving performance;
  • integration of antenna structural characteristics and site geometry into performance models;
  • evaluation of atmospheric and environmental effects on system noise temperature;
  • comparison between predicted and measured antenna performance;
  • definition of performance indicators suitable for operational assessment of deep-space antenna systems;
  • investigation of future frequency-band implementations and their impact on existing antenna infrastructures. 

​ 

As an intern, your tasks will include: 

  • ​Become familiar with ground-station antenna systems and simulation tools; 
  • ​define the software requirements for the specific antenna temperature tool; 
  • ​update and improve the available radio-frequency antenna models at the relevant frequencies;  
  • ​analyse and characterise the radio-frequency environments at existing and future deep-space antenna sites and their effects on antenna system performance;  
  • ​combine the antenna models with environmental and pointing conditions to determine system performance; 
  • ​propose upgraded layouts to accommodate new frequency bands in existing antennas; 
  • ​compare model predictions with measurement data and operational performance observations; 
  • ​prepare technical documentation and present the results. 

​ 

​This internship offers practical experience at the intersection of deep-space communications, antenna engineering, radio-frequency system analysis, scientific computing, and ground-station performance verification, contributing to the characterisation and enhancement of ESA's ESTRACK deep-space antenna infrastructure under real operational conditions. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in RF and electromagnetics is an asset. 

Knowledge of programming tools such as Python is an asset. 

Knowledge of antenna simulation tools such as GRASP is an asset. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Title: Intern in the Director General's Cabinet - Senior Security Coordinator's Office
description_html:
Location
ESA Headquarters, Paris, France  

Our team and mission

Compact, proactive and dedicated team embedded in the ESA Director General’s Cabinet. The Head of the Office is the main advisor to ESA Director General (DG) on matters linked to the use of space assets in support of resilience, crisis management but also defence matters (resolution 11 of outcome of Council at Ministerial level in 2025). 

The Office interacts with all relevant ESA Directorates on those topics in particular in reaching out to the European Resilience in Space programme outreach to MoDs of ESA Member States as well as Associated States.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose between the following topics:

 

1)    Topic 1: ESA Member States National security policy and capabilities’ review in support of DG-OS daily work as well as the EU security, defence and space evolution.

Security from Space aims at defining space contributions to mitigate security challenges on Earth (the impact of Climate Change on land, sea and air and how this affects local populations including but not limited to human migration, human trafficking, illegal activities, border control, conflict areas, etc.). Space supports security crisis response. 

 

You will support the Office to:

 

  • identify national policies of European states and their allies, the EU, as well as competitors  regarding civil security/safety/protection; 
  • monitor existing national space capabilities and their link to security applications and if and how they can network together in support of the European Resilience from Space (ERS) programme. This entails the identification of capability gaps. And potential cooperation (Pooling and Sharing). 

 

2)    Topic 2: Space systems and Dual-Use: the case for ESA and commercial companies.
The commercial sector both in the US and in Europe is successfully developing solutions that were previously only pursued by government. This has led the US Space Force to work on fully integrating commercial solutions into the national security space architecture to maintain the US’s competitive advantage in the sector.

 

You will support the Office in investigating key questions, such as:

 

  • How could ESA contribute to creating European commercial space champions in support of European space security and defense for Europe to leverage the use of commercial space solutions in a new “hybrid” architecture?
  • How could the US Space Force Commercial Space Strategy be translated into the European context?

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in Space Systems and European Defence current Architecture is an asset.

Title: Intern in the Ground Systems Engineering & Innovation Department - Lunar Image Super-Resolution
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

​​The Mission Analysis Section is the solution architect for future terrestrial, lunar, minor-body and ​interplanetary missions, as well as scientific missions to other planets or missions to the libration points. The emphasis is on trajectory optimisation and attitude-related aspects, and on providing ​solutions for the spacecraft itself, the ground segment design, and operations preparations. 

 

​In recent years, the section has expanded its activities towards lunar surface analysis, supporting landing site selection, hazard assessment, and mission design for future Moon missions.​ 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​Future lunar missions require detailed knowledge of the surface environment for landing site selection and mission planning. However, the spatial resolution of existing lunar orbital imagery limits the detection and characterisation of sub-pixel scale terrain features, posing a risk to landing safety. 

 

​The objective of this internship is to investigate and develop methodologies for generating enhanced-resolution lunar surface imagery, by exploiting the slight differences in spacecraft position and camera pointing between repeated observations of the same area under similar lighting conditions. The working hypothesis is that reconstruction of surface details at a higher effective resolution than that of the original sensor should be achievable. 

​ 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks: 

  • Review state-of-the-art techniques for multi-image super-resolution and image reconstruction; 
  • ​investigate the characteristics and limitations of existing lunar image datasets; 
  • ​utilise algorithms for precise image registration and sub-pixel alignment of lunar orbital imagery; 
  • ​implement reconstruction techniques combining multiple observations into enhanced-resolution products; 
  • ​assess the influence of illumination conditions, viewing geometry and image quality on reconstruction performance; 
  • ​validate the generated products using higher-resolution reference datasets where available; 
  • ​evaluate the potential benefits for lunar landing site characterisation, terrain mapping and hazard assessment.​ 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in the following is an asset: 

  • Python / C++ coding; 
  • image processing.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Projects Department - EnVision Project: Thermo-Elastic Modelling
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

EnVision is a Venus orbiter mission selected by ESA’s Science Programme Committee as the fifth Medium-class mission in the Agency’s Cosmic Vision plan. It will be the first mission to investigate Venus from its inner core to its upper atmosphere, characterising the interaction between its atmosphere, surface/subsurface and interior. It aims at providing a holistic view of Venus, studying the planet’s history, activity, and climate.


The project team in which this internship is proposed is in charge of the implementation of the mission: the procurement of the spacecraft and the launch vehicle and the liaising with the developers of the instruments that will be embarked on EnVision. As with most Science missions, the instruments are provided by Member States, with ESA providing several specific payload elements.


At the time of writing (September 2026), the EnVision spacecraft is undergoing the Preliminary Design Review. This proposed activity is of significant interest to the EnVision project, as thermo-elastic distortion analyses play a key role in the verification of several mission performance requirements, particularly those related to the pointing stability of scientific instruments or the link budget of communication antennae.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Improving Thermo-Elastic Modelling of Spacecraft and Payload Coupling

 

You will be part of the EnVision project team at ESA's European Space Research and Technology Centre and will work closely with spacecraft engineering specialists and experts from the ESA Technical Directorate. Your task will be to investigate how interactions between a spacecraft platform and its payload equipment influence thermo-elastic distortions, and how these effects can be represented more accurately and efficiently in engineering analyses.

 

Starting from the existing EnVision thermo-elastic analysis model, you will enhance the spacecraft structural model by integrating representations of payload instruments, electronics units, and other heat-dissipating equipment. You will then perform thermo-elastic analyses to evaluate how the thermal and structural behaviour of these units affects the deformation of the spacecraft structure.

 

A particular focus of the work will be to assess coupling effects between payload equipment and the spacecraft platform. You will investigate how temperature gradients and structural stiffness within payload units and electronics boxes influence the deformation of the spacecraft panels on which they are mounted, and how these distortions may propagate to neighbouring areas supporting other sensitive instruments.

 

Based on your findings, you will develop simplified modelling approaches that can reproduce the key coupling effects without requiring the use of highly detailed models. These simplified representations could significantly improve analysis efficiency while maintaining the accuracy needed for engineering assessments.

 

Finally, you will evaluate the extent to which separate analyses of the spacecraft platform and payload units can reproduce the results of a fully integrated thermo-elastic analysis. Where appropriate, you will propose methods to better capture platform-to-payload interactions when payload units are analysed independently.

 

The results of this work could contribute to improving future thermo-elastic modelling practices and increasing the representativeness of performance predictions for space missions. Using the EnVision mission as a case study, you will explore modelling aspects that are often neglected in conventional analyses and help identify practical methods to account for spacecraft-payload coupling effects.

 

During this internship, you will gain experience in:

  • thermo-elastic analysis of spacecraft structures;
  • structural and thermal modelling using finite element methods;
  • interpretation of spacecraft performance impacts arising from thermo-mechanical distortions;
  • development and validation of simplified engineering models;
  • collaboration with multidisciplinary spacecraft engineering teams;
  • application of advanced analysis techniques to a real ESA space mission.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in Finite Element Analysis, use of NASTRAN or other similar Finite Element Analysis software, Thermo-elastic distortion analysis and Mechanical Engineering are an asset.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.

Title: Intern in the Science Engagement and Oversight Office - Innovative BepiColombo Science Communication
description_html:
Location
ESAC, Villanueva de la Cañada, Spain  

Our team and mission

Under the direct authority of D/SCI, the Head of the Science Engagement and Oversight Office is responsible for overseeing the scientific content of the Programme, interfacing with the scientific community and providing scientific expertise to studies, projects and missions, also in other Directorates as needed.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Pioneering New Ways to Communicate BepiColombo Science

 

BepiColombo is set to arrive at Mercury in November 2026, with the start of its nominal science phase in April 2027 for several years to come. The mission will deliver an unprecedented wealth of scientific results, offering a unique opportunity to reshape how planetary science is shared with both the scientific community and the wider public. While ESA’s Science Communication Office will highlight major milestones and achievements, many of the mission’s rich and diverse results will require additional, creative approaches to fully reach their audiences.

In a context where media landscapes and communication practices are rapidly evolving, there is a growing need to explore new formats, platforms, and strategies to effectively reach and engage the right audiences.

We are looking for a motivated and imaginative intern to help develop and implement innovative ways of communicating BepiColombo’s science results and key milestones, complementing ESA’s core communication activities.

The role will encourage fresh ideas and new formats to enhance the visibility and impact of the mission’s discoveries. This may include crafting engaging scientific stories, contributing to the preparation and visibility of data releases, designing visual materials such as posters and infographics, developing scientific visualisations, and exploring novel formats such as data sonification, alongside proposing new concepts for outreach and dissemination. This internship offers a unique opportunity to experiment with new, creative, and transformative approaches to science communication at a pivotal moment for the BepiColombo mission.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

You should also have:

  • broad knowledge of science, with the ability to quickly understand and engage with new scientific concepts (knowledge of planetary science is an asset);
  • strong interest in science communication, with the ability to translate complex scientific results into clear, engaging, and accessible content for different audiences;
  • experience in at least one of the following areas is required: science writing, visualisation, or multimedia content creation. Depending on the profile, the internship will focus on developing innovative applications of these skills rather than basic training;
  • creativity and curiosity to explore new communication formats and approaches, including emerging media, interactive content, or unconventional storytelling techniques (e.g. data visualisation, sonification, digital storytelling);
  • awareness of evolving media landscapes and interest in identifying effective ways to reach and engage different target audiences across platforms.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).
