Title: Intern in the Future Missions and Architecture Department - Knowledge-Centric Mission Engineering
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Missions and System Studies Section, within the Future Missions and Instruments Division of the Future Missions and Architecture Department in the Directorate of Earth Observation Programmes, contributes to the conception, definition and preparation of future Earth observation missions.

 

The Section supports the early phases of mission development through mission analysis, system engineering and architecture studies, contributing to the definition and assessment of new mission concepts, requirements and system architectures. Its activities include the evaluation of emerging technologies and innovative mission concepts, architecture trade-offs, mission performance assessment and the development of engineering methods and tools supporting future Earth observation systems.

 

The Section operates in a multidisciplinary environment at the intersection of Earth observation science, space systems engineering and technology innovation. Its work addresses the evolution of Earth observation towards increasingly capable and interconnected space systems, including distributed and federated architectures, advanced onboard processing, artificial intelligence and new operational concepts.

 

Working closely with other engineering and scientific teams, industry and external partners, the Section contributes to transforming new ideas and technologies into credible mission concepts and future Earth observation capabilities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Topic of the internship: Knowledge-centric engineering environment for future EO missions

 

Space projects continue to rely heavily on document-based engineering practices. Requirements, architectural descriptions, risks, interfaces, verification activities and technical decisions are frequently distributed across multiple documents, making navigation, traceability and maintenance increasingly complex throughout the project lifecycle.

 

The objective of this internship is to investigate how engineering knowledge can be managed as structured and interconnected information rather than exclusively through traditional document deliverables. The work will explore the concept of a knowledge-centric engineering environment capable of promoting a single source of truth while preserving engineering governance, review processes and traceability.

 

Using the EOCognitiveLab mission concept as a reference case, you will:

  • analyse the information flows and engineering artefacts typically produced during mission preparation and system engineering activities;
  • identify and classify key engineering knowledge objects such as requirements, decisions, risks, interfaces, verification activities, stakeholders and deliverables;
  • develop a lightweight engineering knowledge model describing relationships and dependencies between engineering artefacts;
  • investigate how modern collaborative technologies such as SharePoint, Microsoft Lists, Power Automate, Power BI and artificial intelligence assistants can support engineering knowledge management;
  • design and implement a prototype engineering knowledge portal demonstrating selected system engineering capabilities such as requirements traceability, review baselines, decision tracking and verification management;
  • develop visualisation concepts allowing engineers to understand dependencies, impacts and relationships across a complex mission architecture;
  • assess benefits, limitations and adoption challenges associated with knowledge-centric engineering approaches for future Earth observation programmes.

 

By the end of the internship, you will have gained practical experience in system engineering, digital engineering methods, collaborative platforms, knowledge management, data visualisation and Earth observation mission preparation. The results of the work are expected to support future initiatives aimed at improving the efficiency, accessibility and consistency of engineering information across complex space projects.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge and background in one or more of the following areas is considered an asset:

  • systems engineering and complex engineered systems;
  • aerospace engineering or space systems engineering;
  • information systems and knowledge management;
  • computer science, software engineering or data engineering;
  • business process modelling and workflow automation;
  • database design and information modelling;
  • web applications and collaborative platforms;
  • data analytics and visualisation;
  • artificial intelligence applications for engineering environments;
  • Microsoft 365 technologies, including SharePoint, Microsoft Lists, Power Platform or similar environments.

 

Additional desirable skills include:

  • ability to analyse complex processes and convert them into structured information models;
  • interest in digital transformation and engineering collaboration;
  • familiarity with graph-based data models and traceability concepts;
  • strong analytical and problem-solving skills;
  • ability to work independently while interacting with multidisciplinary teams;
  • good communication and technical writing skills in English.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.

Title: Intern in the Ground Systems Engineering & Innovation Department - Disruption Tolerant Networking
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

Our team develops ground-segment software for space communication systems and for the European Space Agency’s worldwide network of ground stations. We investigate, develop and validate new communication technologies that support reliable data exchange with spacecraft and between distributed space and ground systems. 

 

Our activities combine software engineering, communication protocol development, system integration, simulation and operational experimentation. We also contribute to international standardisation and collaborate with other space agencies, European industry, universities and research organisations. 

 

As part of the team, you will gain experience in an international engineering environment and contribute to technologies supporting future missions to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond. Your activities will form part of wider efforts to establish interoperable communication services for a future Solar System Internet.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​Space communication is often characterised by long round-trip delays and less reliable communication links. Communication links are typically planned in advance and are only available for limited time. Data rates on the individual links may vary between a few kilobits per second and several gigabits per second and a continuous end-to-end path may not be available. To overcome these challenges, Delay or Disruption Tolerant Networking (DTN) communication architectures have been proposed and related communication protocols have been standardised for the space domain (Bundle Protocol, Licklider Transmission Protocol). These protocols are being implemented by ESA, simulated, and validated for various scenarios, including Earth Observation and lunar or Mars exploration scenarios. 

​ 

As an intern, you will contribute to the following tasks: 

  • ​test and validation of protocol implementations and prototypes;
  • ​deployment and validation of prototype operational systems on ground to prepare DTN communication experiments and demonstrations;
  • ​support the execution of DTN experiments and demonstrations with external partners (space agencies, commercial entities, academia);
  • ​depending on your interests, you could also be involved in areas currently under active development and standardisation, such as Bundle Protocol (BP) naming schemes, hybrid BP-IP networks or mission operations for DTN-enabled spacecraft. 

​ 

​Through this internship, you will gain substantial experience in ground segment software development at ESA, obtain a comprehensive understanding of space communication systems, and engage with advanced technologies for future networked space communications aimed at establishing the Solar System Internet.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Experience with software development in Java, Rust or C++ on Linux is required. Knowledge and background in terrestrial networking (IP, TCP, UDP) or space communication protocols is an asset. 

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

 

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Applicants from Canada as a Cooperating State can apply as well as those from Bulgaria, Croatia and Malta as European Cooperating States (ECS).

Title: Intern in the Flight Dynamics Division - Science Mission Support Section
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

The Science Mission Support Section is responsible for: 

  • Mission preparation, LEOP (Launch and Early Orbit Phase), critical and routine operations in the field of flight dynamics for future interplanetary and Lagrange missions, including Plato, Rosalind Franklin, Ramses, Comet Interceptor, Ariel, Envision, Argonaut and LISA; 
  • critical and routine flight dynamics operations for inner solar system missions Bepi-Colombo and Solar-Orbiter; 
  • critical and routine flight dynamics operations for Juice, the Jupiter moons mission; 
  • critical and routine flight dynamics operations for the Hera asteroid mission; 
  • routine operations for Mars missions ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter and Mars Express; 
  • routine operations for the Euclid observatory mission; 
  • development, validation and utilisation of operational solutions for the above science missions. 

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​Tracking of interplanetary spacecraft suffer from plasma effects along the signal’s line of sight. The effect is larger the closer the signal gets to the Sun. There has been a significant evolution in the recent decade by ESA and other external entities to model the interplanetary plasma distribution in quasi real-time based on data from space weather observatories.  

 

You will exploit this data and verify whether these can be suitably used to improve deep-space orbit determination of ESA spacecraft. The following will be your tasks for this activity:   

 

  • ​Retrieve and extract relevant interplanetary plasma data from ESA Space Weather products;  
  • ​implement functionality to compute total plasma content along the line-of-sight from ground station to an ESA interplanetary spacecraft, making use of in-house astrodynamics software;  
  • ​derive plasma delays for Doppler and range data based on the physical interaction along the signal path; 
  • ​apply the mechanism on historic data trying to reproduce and verify the methodology; 
  • ​produce predictions of plasma effects on radiometric data based on current Space Weather data; 
  • ​configure a near-realtime nowcasting functionality to flag current tracking data of deep-space missions for impact of interplanetary plasma effects in the routine orbit determination; 
  • ​if the method is proven to be successful, extend it to an operational tool for orbit determination to compute interplanetary plasma corrections. ​ 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have.

Title: Intern in the Future Missions Department - Market Intelligence and Data Infrastructure
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

Space technology, and satellite communications in particular, have a significant impact on our daily lives. The satellite communications sector is one of the most dynamic segments of the space industry, with evolving business strategies, the emergence of new actors, and shifting user demands driving profound change. 

The Connectivity Market and Business Intelligence Section is responsible for the analysis and business intelligence of markets and businesses relevant to resilience and communication, as well as for defining and providing market guidance for the Directorate’s programme and business development. As part of our dynamic, collaborative, and passionate team, you will help shape the future of the space industry through cutting-edge market intelligence activities.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Recently, the space sector has been evolving at a rapid pace. This change has mainly been triggered by the emergence of New Space actors from various parts of the world and an enormous rise of start-ups in the space economy. This new era has also seen the re-emergence of system concepts, such as constellations, and the adoption of advanced technologies, including new frequency bands, artificial intelligence, and autonomous collision avoidance. For commercial satellite applications, it is becoming increasingly challenging to keep track of and understand the underlying movements, initiatives, actors, and technology developments worldwide.

In that context, ESA has been enhancing its Market and Business Intelligence (BI) activities, and intends to reinforce its toolset, infrastructure and data systems to respond to such dynamism and capitalise on state-of-the-art BI capabilities.  

 

The main priorities are:

 

  • improving the dissemination and accessibility of information;
  • enabling data integration from multiple sources;
  • developing tools for interactive visual data analysis. 

 

As an intern, you will have the following tasks:  

 

  • contributing to the further development of Market and Business Intelligence capabilities;
  • supporting the design and implementation of data integration solutions;
  • applying these developments to the satellite communications domain;
  • helping transform raw data into actionable insights for the industry.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

Title: Intern in the Space Resilience Office - Space Security and Geopolitical Analysis
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Directorate of Resilience, Navigation and Connectivity supports Europe's ability to anticipate, withstand and respond to threats affecting satellite navigation and secure connectivity services that underpin everyday life, including transport, energy, health, defence and civil protection. This requires close engagement with European institutions, Member States, industry, academia and international partners to build a coordinated and resilient European space posture.
As Europe's reliance on space systems grows, so does its exposure to cyber attacks, jamming and spoofing of satellite signals, physical interference with ground and space infrastructure, supply-chain dependencies and wider geopolitical tensions. Understanding both the technical characteristics of these threats and their policy and geopolitical context is essential to keep European navigation and connectivity services safe, dependable and resilient.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

Under the direct guidance of the Head of the Space Resilience Office, you will support activities at the interface between engineering, security analysis and policy, helping the team assess threats to space systems, understand their strategic implications and position resilience activities within Europe's wider security and defence framework.

This opportunity is therefore suited to candidates from either a technical or policy background who are motivated to develop a multidisciplinary perspective.

 

You will contribute to security and threat analysis within the Space Resilience Office of the Directorate of Resilience, Navigation and Connectivity, supporting activities that may combine technical assessment with policy and geopolitical analysis. As an intern, you will have the following tasks:  

 

  • monitoring and analysing technical, security, policy and geopolitical developments relevant to European satellite navigation and secure connectivity programmes;
  • supporting the analysis of threats affecting space systems, including cyber threats, radio-frequency interference, jamming, spoofing and vulnerabilities across space, ground and user segments;
  • contributing to security, risk and resilience assessments of space systems, services and architectures, including the identification of vulnerabilities and potential mitigation measures;
  • tracking policy, regulatory and strategic developments affecting European space security and resilience activities;
  • supporting the assessment of security and geopolitical risks associated with international partnerships, critical technologies and supply chains;
  • preparing concise briefings, structured assessments and strategic positioning material for management, governing bodies and stakeholder meetings;
  • maintaining a structured repository of open-source information on threats, incidents, technologies and geopolitical developments relevant to the Office's activities;
  • supporting coordination with other Agency teams and with European institutions, Member States, industry, academia and international partners on security-related matters.

 

Through this internship, you will learn how technical evidence, threat analysis and geopolitical context are combined to support decisions on European space security and resilience.

You will also develop skills in multidisciplinary analysis, concise strategic communication and cooperation with technical and institutional stakeholders.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

The following are considered assets:

 

  • knowledge and background in space telecommunications and navigation domains;
  • familiarity with threat and risk analysis;
  • knowledge of international relations and space treaties.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Electrical Department - GNC Systems Architecture Section
description_html:
Location
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands  

Our team and mission

The Guidance, Navigation and Control (GNC) Systems Architecture Section provides functional support to ESA projects in the technical field of GNC systems for planetary exploration orbiters and landers, launch and transportation systems, re-entry vehicles, and new generation space vehicles for in-orbit servicing, in-orbit assembly, debris removal and specialised applications such as rendezvous and formation flying.
 
The GNC Systems Architecture Section carries out technological research in the domain of GNC systems for space vehicles including interplanetary cruise, aero assistance, precision landing, ascent, rendezvous and docking, re-entry, formation flying and drag-free systems. 
Special emphasis is placed on the following areas: autonomous and fault-tolerant systems (including health monitoring systems), advanced guidance, control, estimation and optimisation techniques and tools, and the technology development of GNC sensors with a focus on vision-based navigation and hybrid navigation concepts.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

As an intern in the GNC Systems Architecture Section, you will adapt the internal simulation infrastructure to support the definition of the GNC System for future planetary exploration missions.
In particular, the activity focuses on adapting existing Descent and Landing simulators to support the Enceladus L4 mission (Science future mission).

 

The objective is to develop a tool to be used to assess preliminary landing performance and identify the key GNC challenges associated with the mission, in order to inform the mission designers of the critical developments needed in future project phases.

 

The work will involve defining the GNC System architecture (sensors, actuators, modes, functional GNC architecture), designing a suitable landing trajectory taking into account the relevant mission and environmental constraints, and tailoring the existing guidance, navigation, and control algorithms to meet mission requirements.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

Knowledge and background in GNC simulator architectures and a basic knowledge of the Julia programming language is an asset.

Title: Intern in the Robotics and IoT Lab
description_html:
Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

​​The Robotics & IoT Lab at the European Astronaut Centre focuses on advancing robotic systems and human–robot interaction in support of space exploration. Our work spans robotic autonomy, AI-supported decision-making, and XR-enabled control concepts. 

​ 

​This internship addresses humanoid robotics in environments relevant to exploration: locomotion on uneven terrain in our lunar analogue facility, operation under extreme conditions like the lunar south pole, and collaboration with humans in shared workspaces. A particular focus is exploring XR-based teleoperation and supervision of humanoid robots, including predictive simulation approaches that compensate for pronounced communication delays in off-Earth scenarios. Additionally, a key objective is to integrate modern AI methods into control and decision-making, enabling humanoid robots to adapt to unpredictable environments and support astronauts more effectively. 

​ 

​The project contributes to ESA’s efforts to bridge human presence, robotic autonomy, and immersive control systems, strengthening Europe’s expertise in humanoid robotics and human–robot teaming for future exploration missions.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​You will work directly with a humanoid robot platform and support the development of control and interaction concepts in exploration-relevant scenarios. 

​ 

​Your activities will include:

  • ​programming locomotion and balance behaviours for humanoid robots on uneven terrain;
  • ​developing strategies for robot operation under constrained conditions (e.g. extreme lighting at the lunar south pole);
  • ​exploring XR-based teleoperation and supervisory control, enabling intuitive interfaces for astronauts and operators;
  • ​exploring how AI techniques such as reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and predictive models can be applied to locomotion, teleoperation, and human–robot interaction;
  • ​investigating predictive simulation and state estimation approaches to mitigate the effects of communication latency in off-Earth teleoperation;
  • ​contributing to methods for human–robot interaction in shared tasks, including safety and usability considerations, using AI and traditional approaches;
  • ​supporting simulation, benchmarking, and hardware validation of behaviours and interaction methods. 

​ 

​Your learning objectives are:

  • ​gain experience in humanoid robotics hardware, locomotion, and control stacks;
  • ​understand the challenges of XR-based teleoperation with communication latency in off-Earth contexts;
  • ​learn how to combine AI methods and predictive simulation for robust autonomy and remote operation;
  • ​develop insight into human–robot teaming and interaction design for exploration scenarios. 

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Essential background and skills 

  • studies in robotics, computer science, mechatronics, AI, or a related engineering field; 
  • programming experience in current programming frameworks such as Python and C++;
  • understanding of control principles, algorithms, and 3D mathematics;
  • interest in humanoid robotics, teleoperation, and human–robot interaction;
  • experience with Git and collaborative coding;
  • experience with agentic and AI-enhanced workflows. 

 

Desirable 

  • familiarity with XR environments (VR/AR/MR) and their application to teleoperation;
  • experience with simulation environments (Isaac Sim, Omniverse, Gazebo, MuJoCo, or similar);
  • exposure to reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or predictive simulation approaches;
  • curiosity about space robotics, comms latency challenges, and immersive control concepts. 

 

We are looking for a motivated intern who can apply both robotics fundamentals and creative approaches to XR-based teleoperation, human–robot interaction, and AI-supported control, helping us explore how humanoid robots can best support future off-Earth missions.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Intern in the Ground Systems Engineering & Innovation Department - Security Engineering
description_html:
Location
ESOC, Darmstadt, Germany  

Our team and mission

​​The Ground Systems Engineering and Innovation Department is responsible for all the ground systems engineering and support activities required to support mission operations and implement innovation.   

 

​The Department maintains and manages a full level of competences, technologies and services in all engineering disciplines related to ground systems, infrastructure, technology evolution and Engineering R&T and innovation.   

 

​The Department provides expert support in these areas to the Directorate of Operations for all current and potential missions and leads, in the role of architect, ground systems evolution and innovation implementation in the infrastructure and to other ESA programmes.   

 

​The Department is furthermore responsible for the overall technical innovation and technical standardisation coordination for the ground segment.   

​ 

​The Department is relying on the following domains of expertise:   

  • ​Ground Station Engineering;    
  • ​Flight Dynamics and Mission Analysis;   
  • ​Mission Operations Data Systems Engineering;   
  • ​Navigation Support;    
  • ​Multi-Mission Infrastructure – Ground Segment Integration and Testing.   

​   

​For further details, interested candidates are encouraged to visit:    

​http://www.esa.int/Our_Activities/Operations/gse/Building_infrastructure_on_Earth_to_support_satellites_in_space

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

You can choose among the following topics:

 

1) Topic 1: Post-Quantum Cryptography Research for Space

 

ESA is working towards a future Solar System Internet, an interoperable network that will enable secure and reliable communication across satellites, ground stations, lunar, and deep-space infrastructures. Space communications face unique challenges, including high latency, intermittent connectivity, and limited computing, storage, and bandwidth resources. At the same time, advances in quantum computing pose a long-term threat to many of today's cryptographic mechanisms, motivating an urgent, worldwide transition towards post-quantum cryptography. Ensuring that post-quantum security technologies can operate efficiently under the constraints of space environments remains an important research challenge.

 

In this topic, you will explore how next-generation cryptographic technologies can be applied to secure future space communications. This may include the design and implementation of post-quantum cryptographic algorithms, the analysis of security and performance trade-offs in resource-constrained environments, or the investigation of implementation security aspects such as side-channel and fault-injection attacks. Depending on your interests, you may focus on security analyses, software development, or contributions to ongoing international standardization. Overall, you will contribute to the development of resilient and future-proof security solutions for the next generation of space communication infrastructures.

 

2) Topic 2: Next-Generation Mission Data Interfaces for ESA Mission Control Systems  

 

The Pulse project is ESA’s activity developing and operationalizing its next-generation system for mission control and mission operations preparation. It is built on top of the European Ground System Common Core (EGS-CC) framework, targeting a standardised, secure and automation-ready system that enables interoperability and European sovereignty.

 

This topic is about designing and prototyping a Mission Control System agnostic interface for data archiving and dissemination services, enabling seamless integration between operational systems and mission data repositories. The activity will define common information models, APIs, and interaction patterns that can be adopted across current and future mission control environments, reducing system coupling and improving interoperability.

 

The solution will be implemented and validated within the Pulse ecosystem, leveraging modern AI-assisted software engineering approaches, rapid prototyping techniques, and stringent security-by-design principles. The technical activity will explore how intelligent development workflows can accelerate innovation while maintaining the reliability, traceability, and cybersecurity standards required for mission-critical space operations.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Knowledge or academic specialisation in one or more of the following areas: system and software security engineering, security risk analysis, network security, and secure communication protocols.  

 

Knowledge of basic cryptography is considered a strong asset.

Title: Intern in the XR Lab
description_html:
Location
EAC, Porz-Wahn, Germany

Our team and mission

​​The XR Lab at the European Astronaut Centre explores how Extended Reality technologies can enhance human spaceflight and future space exploration. Our work spans astronaut training, mission simulation, operational support, hardware development, and exploration mission design. By integrating virtual, augmented, and mixed reality technologies into spaceflight activities, we help develop innovative solutions for crews, engineers, and operators, while supporting the preparation of future missions beyond Earth orbit. The use of XR for training at EAC includes spacewalks, robotics, human anatomy and training technology demonstrators onboard the ISS.  

​ 

​Within the XR Lab, this opportunity is to further develop Extended Reality tools based on Unreal Engine for astronauts. This would specifically focus on preliminary work for projects using some Meta Quest 3 headsets onboard the International Space Station. In this context, the work combines extended reality development with machine learning techniques to improve interaction, perception, environment understanding, data interpretation, or context-aware assistance in constrained operational environments. The work may involve prototyping, testing, and refining methods that can increase robustness and usability for astronaut applications. 

​ 

​You will collaborate closely with engineers in the XR-Lab and experts in the European Astronaut Centre to contribute to ongoing developments that connect software engineering, human-centred design, and ISS Operations. The internship offers exposure to both practical implementation and experimentation, with opportunities to support the maturation of tools that are relevant to prepare future operational and research use cases.

 

Candidates interested are encouraged to visit the ESA website: http://www.esa.int

Field(s) of activity for the internship

​​You will work directly with a Meta Quest 3 and support the development of new concepts in using such headsets onboard the International Space Station. 

​ 

​Your activities will include:

  • ​combining immersive application development with machine learning methods to explore new capabilities for onboard assistance, interaction, data interpretation, and experimental operational concepts;
  • ​helping to design, prototype, implement, and evaluate software components in close collaboration with the team;
  • ​developing on-device real-time interaction features, sensor or data processing pipelines, computer vision-based functions, or software tooling depending on project needs;
  • ​contributing to technical trade-offs, implementation work, and iterative testing of candidate solutions in a demanding applied environment. 

​ 

​Your learning objectives are:

  • ​obtain a high-level understanding of Human Spaceflight in Europe;
  • ​gain experience in extended reality development;
  • ​understand how applied machine learning methods can support operational use cases such as assistance, interaction, perception, and data interpretation;
  • ​develop practical experience in designing, prototyping, and testing software components within a multidisciplinary engineering team;
  • ​learn how immersive technologies must be adapted, validated, and matured for use in constrained and safety-relevant environments.

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You must be a university student, preferably in your final or second-to-last year of university course at Master's level. In addition, you must be able to prove that you will be enrolled at your university for the entire duration of the internship.

Additional requirements

The working languages of the Agency are English and French. A good knowledge of one of these is required. Knowledge of another ESA Member State language is an asset.

During the interview, your motivation for applying to this role will be explored.

 

Essential Skills:

  • proven experience in Unreal Engine development;
  • intermediate C++ and/or intermediate Python proficiency;
  • interest in extended reality development and machine learning applications;
  • familiarity with version control and collaborative software engineering practices.

 

Desirable Skills:

  • knowledge of computer vision, Bayesian theory, or signal processing;
  • experience with the ESA XR Plugin;
  • experience with prototyping, experimentation, or technical evaluation of interactive systems;
  • experience with popular machine learning computer vision models and/or software.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusiveness 
ESA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics. 

At the Agency we value diversity, and we welcome people with disabilities. Whenever possible, we seek to accommodate individuals with disabilities by providing the necessary support at the workplace. The Human Resources Department can also provide assistance during the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss this further, please contact us via email at ESA.Student.Internships@esa.int.

 

Important Information and Disclaimer
During the recruitment process, the Agency may request applicants to undergo selection tests.

Applicants must be eligible to access information, technology, and hardware which is subject to European or US export control and sanctions regulations.

The information published on ESA’s careers website regarding internship conditions is correct at the time of publication. It is not intended to be exhaustive and may not address all questions you would have. 

 

Nationality 

Please note that applications are only considered from nationals of one of the following States: Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Title: Internal Research Fellow (PostDoc) in AI on board for Synthetic Aperture Radar Missions
description_html:
Location
ESRIN, Frascati, Italy  

Our team and mission

Reporting to the Head of the Explore Office in the ESA Φ-lab, you will work in close cooperation with other staff in the Directorate of Earth Observation Programmes and colleagues from the Directorate of Technology, Engineering and Quality. There may also be collaboration with scientists and engineers in other divisions at ESA. You will be part of the ESA Φ-lab. Our mission is to accelerate the future of Earth observation via transformative innovation* and commercialisation actions strengthening ESA Member States’ world-leading competitiveness. .Our vision is to be the “EO innovation hub”, connecting EO with a growing ecosystem of disruptive and transformative innovation such as AI, ML, quantum computing, edge computing, metamaterials, photonics, etc. Many of the challenges posed by new technologies still need to be tackled at the scientific, application and capability level to deliver maximum value from satellite-derived EO assets for our climate, society, and economy. The Φ-lab will bring together early career and senior researchers from a variety of disciplines across EO and disruptive/transformative innovation to help develop innovative EO solutions.

 

We offer:

•    a stimulating multinational, interdisciplinary and open work environment;
•    access to high-performance computing infrastructure and unparalleled EO and technology expertise;
•    a unique opportunity to work on innovative solutions to address global challenges;
•    freedom and focus to conduct creative research while making an impact in relation to ESA’s strategy;
•    a wide network of relationships and collaboration with top academia, industry and research centres;
•    the opportunity to contribute to the Φ-lab strategy and activities.

 

You are encouraged to visit the ESA website: https://www.esa.int/

Field(s) of activity/research for the traineeship

Main objectives of the Research Fellowship

 

Cognitive cloud computing in space (3CS) is emerging as a key paradigm for future Earth observation systems, enabling coordinated, event-driven operations across heterogeneous space assets through onboard intelligence, distributed computing and inter-satellite communications. By supporting capabilities such as autonomous tip-and-cue, event-based mission replanning, adaptive multi-sensor tasking and distributed information fusion, 3CS aims to significantly improve the responsiveness and autonomy of future EO missions. In this context, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) represents a strategic sensing modality thanks to its all-weather, day-and-night imaging capabilities, providing reliable information to trigger and support coordinated observations in rapidly evolving scenarios such as disasters, maritime surveillance and security monitoring. Recent advances in cognitive SAR have demonstrated the potential of AI methods operating directly on raw or partially processed data for tasks such as learned focusing, adaptive compression and information extraction. However, significant challenges remain, including the computational complexity of SAR processing chains, the limited robustness of current AI approaches, and the difficulty of deploying intelligent processing under stringent onboard resource constraints. In addition, significant exploration is still required to explore novel cognitive SAR and novel mission concepts enabled by onboard SAR processing. This fellowship will address these challenges by developing AI-based methods for onboard SAR data processing operating close to the sensing level, enabling real-time information extraction, event detection, autonomous re-tasking, and cooperative multi-sensor operations for next-generation missions, including Copernicus Sentinel-1 Next Generation, thereby supporting the transition towards autonomous and coordinated EO systems.

 

Research topic of interests include:

  • advanced onboard SAR data processing architectures: target applications include but are not limited to onboard SAR data focusing, and extraction of insight from SAR unfocused data;
  • cognitive SAR: novel mission concepts, applications and in-orbit data processing for cognitive SAR systems;
  • onboard foundation models for SAR data processing: including multimodal foundation models;
  • onboard SAR for 3CS systems: onboard SAR for tip-and-cue systems, in-orbit data fusion, etc.

 

Within your application, please provide a research proposal (no more than five pages) related to onboard AI for SAR missions:

  • Describe the main research questions that you would like to address.
  • Propose a research plan with a clear description of the methodology that you would like to adopt to answer those questions with specific reference to your previous experience and your publications on the topic, the novel concept that you plan to research, and a possible schedule.

.

In particular, you will:

  • undertake advanced research activities, exploring and expanding the use of disruptive/transformative innovation (AI, ML, disruptive computing, etc.) to develop new prototypes for onboard SAR data processing, cognitive SAR, and onboard SAR for 3CS systems. The research may cover a wide range of innovative topics:
    • exploration of innovative methodologies and technologies;
    • the development of novel methods, of new technology implementations, (e.g. ML models), of high-level products;
    • contribution to the development and curation of open data sets and tools enabling the community to develop its own AI for applications and research;
  • support the definition and implementation of rapid prototyping activities, research sprints and open challenges of innovative EO solutions addressing upcoming lab activities and wider strategy;
  • engage with the innovation ecosystem to promote the uptake of new techniques and capture the latest developments in EO and disruptive/transformative innovation;
  • publish the research project outcomes in high-impact journals;
  • drive collaboration within the Φ-lab community and ESA internal teams to promote the uptake of these new techniques and solutions;
  • contribute to the Φ-lab strategy, activities and outreach on disruptive technologies for EO;
  • maintain a continuous dialogue with the scientific community, including major international programmes and initiatives in the field;
  • support the Φ-lab’s daily activities and research network of ESA Graduate Trainees, National Trainees, interns, visiting professors, experts and researchers, as applicable;
  • collaborate closely with ESA’s Φ-lab and avionics and EEE Division for the identification, testing and benchmarking of hardware components for edge computing and learning;
  • conduct research and implement prototypes of onboard AI for SAR;
  • support ESA’s Φ-lab staff with external R&D activities related to onboard AI for SAR.

Technical competencies

Knowledge relevant to the field of research
Research/publication record
Ability to conduct research autonomously
Breadth of exposure coming from past and/or current research/activities
Ability to gather and share relevant information
General interest in space and space research

Behavioural competencies

Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking 

For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook

Education

You should have recently completed (within the past five years), or be close to completion of a PhD in a relevant field such as data science, AI, computer science, remote sensing, machine learning, electronics, embedded systems, aerospace engineering, Earth system science, climate etc., with the subject of your thesis being relevant to the description of the tasks outlined above.

Additional requirements

In addition to your CV and motivation letter, please prepare a research proposal of no more than five pages. When submitting your application, please upload the proposal under the “Research Outline” field in “My Documents.

 

You should have:

  • sound knowledge of themes of interest, such as EO, AI, ML, and technologies in general;
  • knowledge relevant to your research field in SAR signal processing and algorithms;
  • the ability to think outside the box and explore new avenues, with natural curiosity and a passion for new subjects and research areas;
  • experience with one or more general-purpose programming languages, for example Python and general-purpose deep learning frameworks, such as Tensorflow or PyTorch;
  • the interest and ability to share knowledge with other ESA organisational units.

 

The following elements are considered an asset:

  •  Knowledge of onboard AI, edge computing for SAR systems
  • Experience with hardware for edge computing (e.g., FPGAs, TPUs, VPUs and GPUs)

 

You should also have good interpersonal and communication skills and should be able to work in a multi-cultural environment, both independently and as part of a team. Your motivation, overall professional perspective and career goals will also be explored during the later stages of the selection process.

description_text: Location ESRIN, Frascati, Italy Our team and mission Reporting to the Head of the Explore Office in the ESA Φ-lab, you will work in close cooperation with other staff in the Directorate of Earth Observation Programmes and colleagues from the Directorate of Technology, Engineering and Quality. There may also be collaboration with scientists and engineers in other divisions at ESA. You will be part of the ESA Φ-lab. Our mission is to accelerate the future of Earth observation via transformative innovation* and commercialisation actions strengthening ESA Member States’ world-leading competitiveness. .Our vision is to be the “EO innovation hub”, connecting EO with a growing ecosystem of disruptive and transformative innovation such as AI, ML, quantum computing, edge computing, metamaterials, photonics, etc. Many of the challenges posed by new technologies still need to be tackled at the scientific, application and capability level to deliver maximum value from satellite-derived EO assets for our climate, society, and economy. The Φ-lab will bring together early career and senior researchers from a variety of disciplines across EO and disruptive/transformative innovation to help develop innovative EO solutions. We offer: •    a stimulating multinational, interdisciplinary and open work environment; •    access to high-performance computing infrastructure and unparalleled EO and technology expertise; •    a unique opportunity to work on innovative solutions to address global challenges; •    freedom and focus to conduct creative research while making an impact in relation to ESA’s strategy; •    a wide network of relationships and collaboration with top academia, industry and research centres; •    the opportunity to contribute to the Φ-lab strategy and activities. You are encouraged to visit the ESA website: https://www.esa.int/ Field(s) of activity/research for the traineeship Main objectives of the Research Fellowship Cognitive cloud computing in space (3CS) is emerging as a key paradigm for future Earth observation systems, enabling coordinated, event-driven operations across heterogeneous space assets through onboard intelligence, distributed computing and inter-satellite communications. By supporting capabilities such as autonomous tip-and-cue, event-based mission replanning, adaptive multi-sensor tasking and distributed information fusion, 3CS aims to significantly improve the responsiveness and autonomy of future EO missions. In this context, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) represents a strategic sensing modality thanks to its all-weather, day-and-night imaging capabilities, providing reliable information to trigger and support coordinated observations in rapidly evolving scenarios such as disasters, maritime surveillance and security monitoring. Recent advances in cognitive SAR have demonstrated the potential of AI methods operating directly on raw or partially processed data for tasks such as learned focusing, adaptive compression and information extraction. However, significant challenges remain, including the computational complexity of SAR processing chains, the limited robustness of current AI approaches, and the difficulty of deploying intelligent processing under stringent onboard resource constraints. In addition, significant exploration is still required to explore novel cognitive SAR and novel mission concepts enabled by onboard SAR processing. This fellowship will address these challenges by developing AI-based methods for onboard SAR data processing operating close to the sensing level, enabling real-time information extraction, event detection, autonomous re-tasking, and cooperative multi-sensor operations for next-generation missions, including Copernicus Sentinel-1 Next Generation, thereby supporting the transition towards autonomous and coordinated EO systems. Research topic of interests include: advanced onboard SAR data processing architectures: target applications include but are not limited to onboard SAR data focusing, and extraction of insight from SAR unfocused data; cognitive SAR: novel mission concepts, applications and in-orbit data processing for cognitive SAR systems; onboard foundation models for SAR data processing: including multimodal foundation models; onboard SAR for 3CS systems: onboard SAR for tip-and-cue systems, in-orbit data fusion, etc. Within your application, please provide a research proposal (no more than five pages) related to onboard AI for SAR missions: Describe the main research questions that you would like to address. Propose a research plan with a clear description of the methodology that you would like to adopt to answer those questions with specific reference to your previous experience and your publications on the topic, the novel concept that you plan to research, and a possible schedule. . In particular, you will: undertake advanced research activities, exploring and expanding the use of disruptive/transformative innovation (AI, ML, disruptive computing, etc.) to develop new prototypes for onboard SAR data processing, cognitive SAR, and onboard SAR for 3CS systems. The research may cover a wide range of innovative topics: exploration of innovative methodologies and technologies; the development of novel methods, of new technology implementations, (e.g. ML models), of high-level products; contribution to the development and curation of open data sets and tools enabling the community to develop its own AI for applications and research; support the definition and implementation of rapid prototyping activities, research sprints and open challenges of innovative EO solutions addressing upcoming lab activities and wider strategy; engage with the innovation ecosystem to promote the uptake of new techniques and capture the latest developments in EO and disruptive/transformative innovation; publish the research project outcomes in high-impact journals; drive collaboration within the Φ-lab community and ESA internal teams to promote the uptake of these new techniques and solutions; contribute to the Φ-lab strategy, activities and outreach on disruptive technologies for EO; maintain a continuous dialogue with the scientific community, including major international programmes and initiatives in the field; support the Φ-lab’s daily activities and research network of ESA Graduate Trainees, National Trainees, interns, visiting professors, experts and researchers, as applicable; collaborate closely with ESA’s Φ-lab and avionics and EEE Division for the identification, testing and benchmarking of hardware components for edge computing and learning; conduct research and implement prototypes of onboard AI for SAR; support ESA’s Φ-lab staff with external R&D activities related to onboard AI for SAR.
